CL:0000000.name: cell
CL:0000000.def: a material entity of anatomical origin (part of or deriving from an organism) that has as its parts a maximally connected cell compartment surrounded by a plasma membrane.

CL:0000001.name: primary cultured cell
CL:0000001.def: a cultured cell that is freshly isolated from a organismal source, or derives in culture from such a cell prior to the culture being passaged.

CL:0000002.name: obsolete immortal cell line cell
CL:0000002.def: obsolete: a cell line cell that is expected to be capable of an unlimited number of divisions, and is thus able to support indefinite growth/propagation in vitro as part of a immortal cell line.

CL:0000003.name: native cell
CL:0000003.def: a cell that is found in a natural setting, which includes multicellular organism cells 'in vivo' (i.e. part of an organism), and unicellular organisms 'in environment' (i.e. part of a natural environment).

CL:0000004.name: obsolete cell by organism
CL:0000004.def: obsolete: a classification of cells by the organisms within which they are contained.

CL:0000005.name: fibroblast neural crest derived
CL:0000005.def: any fibroblast that is deriived from the neural crest.

CL:0000007.name: early embryonic cell (metazoa)
CL:0000007.def: a cell found in the embryo before the formation of all the gem layers is complete.

CL:0000008.name: migratory cranial neural crest cell
CL:0000008.def: cell that is part of the migratory cranial neural crest population. migratory cranial neural crest cells develop from premigratory cranial neural crest cells and have undergone epithelial to mesenchymal transition and delamination.

CL:0000009.name: obsolete fusiform initial
CL:0000009.def: obsolete. use po:0000079 from plant ontology instead. an elongated cell with approximately wedge-shaped ends, found in the vascular cambium, which gives rise to the elements of the axial system in the secondary vascular tissues.

CL:0000010.name: cultured cell
CL:0000010.def: a cell in vitro that is or has been maintained or propagated as part of a cell culture.

CL:0000011.name: migratory trunk neural crest cell
CL:0000011.def: cell that is part of the migratory trunk neural crest population. migratory trunk neural crest cells develop from premigratory trunk neural crest cells and have undergone epithelial to mesenchymal transition and delamination.

CL:0000014.name: germ line stem cell
CL:0000014.def: a stem cell that is the precursor of gametes.

CL:0000015.name: male germ cell
CL:0000015.def: a germ cell that supports male gamete production. in some species, non-germ cells known as sertoli cells also play a role in spermatogenesis.

CL:0000016.name: male germ line stem cell
CL:0000016.def: a stem cell that is the precursor of male gametes.

CL:0000017.name: spermatocyte
CL:0000017.def: a male germ cell that develops from spermatogonia. the euploid primary spermatocytes undergo meiosis and give rise to the haploid secondary spermatocytes which in turn give rise to spermatids.

CL:0000018.name: spermatid
CL:0000018.def: a male germ cell that develops from the haploid secondary spermatocytes. without further division, spermatids undergo structural changes and give rise to spermatozoa.

CL:0000019.name: sperm
CL:0000019.def: a mature male germ cell that develops from a spermatid.

CL:0000020.name: spermatogonium
CL:0000020.def: an euploid male germ cell of an early stage of spermatogenesis.

CL:0000021.name: female germ cell
CL:0000021.def: female germ cell is a germ cell that supports female gamete production.

CL:0000022.name: female germ line stem cell
CL:0000022.def: a stem cell that is the precursor of female gametes.

CL:0000023.name: oocyte
CL:0000023.def: a female germ cell that has entered meiosis.

CL:0000024.name: oogonial cell
CL:0000024.def: an undifferentiated germ cell that proliferates rapidly and gives rise to oocytes.

CL:0000025.name: egg cell
CL:0000025.def: a female gamete where meiosis has progressed to metaphase ii and is able to participate in fertilization.

CL:0000026.name: invertebrate nurse cell
CL:0000026.def: a germline cell that contributes to the development of the oocyte by transferring cytoplasm directly to oocyte.

CL:0000027.name: smooth muscle cell neural crest derived
CL:0000027.def: a smooth muscle cell derived from the neural crest.

CL:0000031.name: neuroblast (sensu vertebrata)
CL:0000031.def: a cell that will develop into a neuron often after a migration phase.

CL:0000032.name: neuroplacodal cell
CL:0000032.def: a cell of a platelike structure, especially a thickened plate of ectoderm in the early embryo, from which a sense organ develops.

CL:0000033.name: apocrine cell
CL:0000033.def: an exocrine cell characterized by loss of part of the cytoplasm during the process of secretion. the secreted substance is accumulated at the apical end and is either budded off through the plasma membrane producing secreted vesicles or dissolved in the cytoplasm that is lost during secretion.

CL:0000034.name: stem cell
CL:0000034.def: a relatively undifferentiated cell that retains the ability to divide and proliferate throughout life to provide progenitor cells that can differentiate into specialized cells.

CL:0000035.name: single fate stem cell
CL:0000035.def: a stem cell that self-renews as well as give rise to a single mature cell type.

CL:0000037.name: hematopoietic stem cell
CL:0000037.def: a stem cell from which all cells of the lymphoid and myeloid lineages develop, including blood cells and cells of the immune system. hematopoietic stem cells lack cell markers of effector cells (lin-negative). lin-negative is defined by lacking one or more of the following cell surface markers: cd2, cd3 epsilon, cd4, cd5 ,cd8 alpha chain, cd11b, cd14, cd19, cd20, cd56, ly6g, ter119.

CL:0000038.name: erythroid progenitor cell
CL:0000038.def: a progenitor cell committed to the erythroid lineage.

CL:0000039.name: germ line cell
CL:0000039.def: a cell that is within the developmental lineage of gametes and is able to pass along its genetic material to offspring.

CL:0000040.name: monoblast
CL:0000040.def: a myeloid progenitor cell committed to the monocyte lineage. this cell is cd11b-positive, has basophilic cytoplasm, euchromatin, and the presence of a nucleolus.

CL:0000041.name: mature eosinophil
CL:0000041.def: a fully differentiated eosinophil, a granular leukocyte with a nucleus that usually has two lobes connected by one or more slender threads, and cytoplasm containing coarse, round granules that are uniform in size and which can be stained by the dye eosin. cells are also differentiated from other granulocytes by a small nuclear-to-cytoplasm ratio (1:3). this cell type is cd49d-positive.

CL:0000042.name: neutrophilic myeloblast
CL:0000042.def: a myeloblast committed to the neutrophil lineage. this cell type is gata-1 positive, c/ebpa-positive, aml-1-positive, c-myb-positive and has low expression of pu.1 transcription factor.

CL:0000043.name: mature basophil
CL:0000043.def: a fully differentiated basophil, a granular leukocyte with an irregularly shaped, pale-staining nucleus that is partially constricted into two lobes, and with cytoplasm that contains coarse granules of variable size. basophils contain vasoactive amines such as histamine and serotonin, which are released on appropriate stimulation.

CL:0000045.name: obsolete thymus processed stem cell
CL:0000045.def: obsolete (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000046.name: obsolete bursa processed stem cell
CL:0000046.def: obsolete (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000047.name: neural stem cell
CL:0000047.def: an undifferentiated neural cell that originates from the neuroectoderm and has the capacity both to perpetually self-renew without differentiating and to generate multiple central nervous system neuronal and glial cell types.

CL:0000048.name: multi fate stem cell
CL:0000048.def: a stem cell that can give rise to multiple lineages of cells.

CL:0000049.name: common myeloid progenitor
CL:0000049.def: a progenitor cell committed to myeloid lineage, including the megakaryocyte and erythroid lineages.

CL:0000050.name: megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitor cell
CL:0000050.def: a progenitor cell committed to the megakaryocyte and erythroid lineages.

CL:0000051.name: common lymphoid progenitor
CL:0000051.def: a oligopotent progenitor cell committed to the lymphoid lineage.

CL:0000052.name: totipotent stem cell
CL:0000052.def: a stem cell from which all cells of the body can form.

CL:0000055.name: non-terminally differentiated cell
CL:0000055.def: a precursor cell with a limited number of potential fates.

CL:0000056.name: myoblast
CL:0000056.def: a cell that is commited to differentiating into a muscle cell.  embryonic myoblasts develop from the mesoderm. they undergo proliferation, migrate to their various sites, and then differentiate into the appropriate form of myocytes.  myoblasts also occur as transient populations of cells in muscles undergoing repair.

CL:0000057.name: fibroblast
CL:0000057.def: a connective tissue cell which secretes an extracellular matrix rich in collagen and other macromolecules. flattened and irregular in outline with branching processes; appear fusiform or spindle-shaped.

CL:0000058.name: chondroblast
CL:0000058.def: skeletogenic cell that is typically non-terminally differentiated, secretes an avascular, gag rich matrix; is not buried in cartilage tissue matrix, retains the ability to divide, located adjacent to cartilage tissue (including within the perichondrium), and develops from prechondroblast (and thus prechondrogenic) cell.

CL:0000059.name: ameloblast
CL:0000059.def: skeletogenic cell that produces enamel, overlies the odontogenic papilla, and arises from the differentiation of a preameloblast cell.

CL:0000060.name: odontoblast
CL:0000060.def: skeletogenic cell that secretes dentine matrix, is derived from the odontogenic papilla, and develops from a preodontoblast cell.

CL:0000061.name: cementoblast
CL:0000061.def: skeletogenic cell that produces cementum (a bony substance that covers the root of a tooth), is part of the odontogenic papilla, and develops from a precementoblast cell.

CL:0000062.name: osteoblast
CL:0000062.def: skeletogenic cell that secretes osteoid, is capable of producing mineralized (hydroxyapatite) matrix, is located adjacent to or within osteoid tissue, and arises from the transformation of a preosteoblast cell.

CL:0000063.name: obsolete cell by histology
CL:0000063.def: obsolete: a classification of cells by their microscopic appearance.

CL:0000064.name: ciliated cell
CL:0000064.def: a cell that has a filiform extrusion of the cell surface.

CL:0000065.name: ependymal cell
CL:0000065.def: a neurectoderm derived cell that lines the neural lumen.

CL:0000066.name: epithelial cell
CL:0000066.def: a cell that is usually found in a two-dimensional sheet with a free surface. the cell has a cytoskeleton that allows for tight cell to cell contact and for cell polarity where apical part is directed towards the lumen and the basal part to the basal lamina.

CL:0000067.name: ciliated epithelial cell
CL:0000067.def: an epithelial cell that has a cilia.

CL:0000068.name: duct epithelial cell
CL:0000068.def: an epithelial cell that is part of a duct.

CL:0000071.name: blood vessel endothelial cell
CL:0000071.def: an endothelial cell that lines the vasculature.
CL:0000071.synonym: cuboidal endothelial cell of vascular tree

CL:0000074.name: obsolete epithem cell
CL:0000074.def: obsolete. use po:0000066 from plant ontology instead. a cell that constitutes the mesophyll of a hydathode and is located between the xylem endings and the epidermis. proposed to be involved in the retrieval of solutes from the xylem sap.

CL:0000075.name: columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell
CL:0000075.def: a columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell is a cell usually found in a two dimensional sheet with a free surface. columnar/cuboidal epithelial cells take on the shape of a column or cube.

CL:0000077.name: mesothelial cell
CL:0000077.def: a flattened epithelial cell of mesenchymal origin that lines the serous cavity.

CL:0000080.name: circulating cell
CL:0000080.def: a cell which moves among different tissues of the body, via blood, lymph, or other medium.

CL:0000081.name: blood cell
CL:0000081.def: a cell found predominately in the blood.

CL:0000082.name: epithelial cell of lung
CL:0000082.def: an epithelial cell of the lung.

CL:0000083.name: epithelial cell of pancreas
CL:0000083.def: an epithelial cell of the pancreas.

CL:0000084.name: t cell
CL:0000084.def: a type of lymphocyte whose defining characteristic is the expression of a t cell receptor complex.

CL:0000085.name: obsolete germ line stem cell (sensu vertebrata)

CL:0000086.name: obsolete germ line stem cell (sensu nematoda and protostomia)

CL:0000087.name: obsolete male germ line stem cell (sensu nematoda and protostomia)

CL:0000088.name: obsolete female germ line stem cell (sensu nematoda and protostomia)

CL:0000089.name: obsolete male germ line stem cell (sensu vertebrata)

CL:0000090.name: obsolete female germ line stem cell (sensu vertebrata)

CL:0000091.name: kupffer cell
CL:0000091.def: a tissue-resident macrophage of the reticuloendothelial system found on the luminal surface of the hepatic sinusoids involved in erythrocyte clearance. markers include f4/80+, cd11b-low, cd68-positive, sialoadhesin-positive, cd163/srcr-positive. irregular, with long processes including lamellipodia extending into the sinusoid lumen, have flattened nucleus with cytoplasm containing characteristic invaginations of the plasma membrane (vermiform bodies); lie within the sinusoid lumen attached to the endothelial surface; derived from the bone marrow, form a major part of the body's mononuclear phagocyte system.

CL:0000092.name: osteoclast
CL:0000092.def: a specialized phagocytic cell associated with the absorption and removal of the mineralized matrix of bone tissue, which typically differentiates from monocytes. this cell has the following markers: tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase type 5-positive, pu.1-positive, c-fos-positive, nuclear factor nf-kappa-b p100 subunit-positive, tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 11a-positive and macrophage colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor-positive.

CL:0000093.name: obsolete osteochondroclast
CL:0000093.def: obsolete (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000094.name: granulocyte
CL:0000094.def: a leukocyte with abundant granules in the cytoplasm.

CL:0000096.name: mature neutrophil
CL:0000096.def: a fully differentiated neutrophil, a granular leukocyte having a nucleus with three to five lobes connected by slender threads, and cytoplasm containing fine inconspicuous granules and stainable by neutral dyes. they are produced in bone marrow at a rate of 5e10-10e10/day and have a half-life of 6-8 hours. neutrophils are cd15-positive, cd16-positive, cd32-positive, cd43-positive, cd181-positive, and cd182-positive.

CL:0000097.name: mast cell
CL:0000097.def: a cell that is found in almost all tissues containing numerous basophilic granules and capable of releasing large amounts of histamine and heparin upon activation. progenitors leave bone marrow and mature in connective and mucosal tissue. mature mast cells are found in all tissues, except the bloodstream. their phenotype is cd117-high, cd123-negative, cd193-positive, cd200r3-positive, and fceri-high. stem-cell factor (kit-ligand; scf) is the main controlling signal of their survival and development.

CL:0000098.name: sensory epithelial cell
CL:0000098.def: a specialized epithelial cell involved in sensory perception. restricted to special sense organs of the olfactory, gustatory, and vestibulocochlear receptor systems; contain sensory cells surrounded by supportive, non-receptive cells.

CL:0000099.name: interneuron
CL:0000099.def: most generally any neuron which is not motor or sensory. interneurons may also refer to neurons whose axons remain within a particular brain region as contrasted with projection neurons which have axons projecting to other brain regions.

CL:0000100.name: motor neuron
CL:0000100.def: an efferent neuron that passes from the central nervous system or a ganglion toward or to a muscle and conducts an impulse that causes or inhibits movement.

CL:0000101.name: sensory neuron
CL:0000101.def: any neuron having a sensory function; an afferent neuron conveying sensory impulses.

CL:0000103.name: bipolar neuron
CL:0000103.def: a type of interneuron that has two neurites, usually an axon and a dendrite, extending from opposite poles of an ovoid cell body.

CL:0000104.name: multipolar neuron
CL:0000104.def: a neuron with three or more neurites, usually an axon and multiple dendrites.

CL:0000105.name: pseudounipolar neuron
CL:0000105.def: neuron with two neurites that are fused grossly when they protrude from the soma and bifurcate a short distance from the soma.

CL:0000106.name: unipolar neuron
CL:0000106.def: neuron with one neurite that extends from the cell body.

CL:0000107.name: autonomic neuron
CL:0000107.def: a neuron whose cell body is within an autonomic ganglion.

CL:0000108.name: cholinergic neuron
CL:0000108.def: a neuron that uses acetylcholine as a vesicular neurotransmitter.

CL:0000110.name: peptidergic neuron
CL:0000110.def: a neuron that uses neuropeptides as transmitters.

CL:0000113.name: mononuclear phagocyte
CL:0000113.def: a vertebrate phagocyte with a single nucleus.

CL:0000115.name: endothelial cell
CL:0000115.def: an endothelial cell comprises the outermost layer or lining of anatomical structures and can be squamous or cuboidal. in mammals, endothelial cell has vimentin filaments and is derived from the mesoderm.

CL:0000116.name: pioneer neuron
CL:0000116.def: pioneer neurons establish a pathway in the developing central nervous system and then undergo programmed cell death once the adult axons, which follow them, have made connections with the target site. thus, they are a transient cell type involved in axon guidance.

CL:0000118.name: basket cell
CL:0000118.def: basket cells are inhibitory gabaergic interneurons of the brain. in general, dendrites of basket cells are free branching and contain smooth spines. axons are highly branched. the branched axonal arborizations give rise to basket-like structures that surround the soma of the target cell. basket cells form axo-somatic synapses, meaning their synapses target somas of other cells.

CL:0000119.name: cerebellar golgi cell
CL:0000119.def: large intrinsic neuron located in the granule layer of the cerebellar cortex that extends its dendrites into the molecular layer where they receive contact from parallel fibers. the axon of the golgi cell ramifies densely in the granule layer and enters into a complex arrangement with mossy fiber terminals and granule cell dendrites to form the cerebellar glomerulus. llinas, walton and lang. in the synaptic organization of the brain. 5th ed. 2004.

CL:0000120.name: granule cell
CL:0000120.def: a neuron of the vertebrate central nervous system that is small in size. this general class includes small neurons in the granular layer of the cerebellar cortex, cerebral cortex neurons that are not pyramidal cells and small neurons without axons found in the olfactory bulb.

CL:0000121.name: purkinje cell
CL:0000121.def: the output neuron of the cerebellar cortex.

CL:0000122.name: stellate neuron
CL:0000122.def: a neuron that has dendritic processes radiating from the cell body forming a star-like shape.

CL:0000124.name: obsolete glial cell (sensu nematoda and protostomia)

CL:0000125.name: glial cell
CL:0000125.def: a non-neuronal cell of the nervous system. they not only provide physical support, but also respond to injury, regulate the ionic and chemical composition of the extracellular milieu. guide neuronal migration during development, and exchange metabolites with neurons.

CL:0000126.name: macroglial cell
CL:0000126.def: a neuroglial cell of ectodermal origin, i.e., the astrocytes and oligodendrocytes considered together.

CL:0000127.name: astrocyte
CL:0000127.def: a class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system - the largest and most numerous neuroglial cells in the brain and spinal cord. astrocytes (from 'star' cells) are irregularly shaped with many long processes, including those with 'end feet' which form the glial (limiting) membrane and directly and indirectly contribute to the blood-brain barrier. they regulate the extracellular ionic and chemical environment, and 'reactive astrocytes' (along with microglia) respond to injury.

CL:0000128.name: oligodendrocyte
CL:0000128.def: a class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system. form the insulating myelin sheath of axons in the central nervous system.

CL:0000129.name: microglial cell
CL:0000129.def: a central nervous system macrophage found in the parenchyma of the central nervous system. marker include cd11b-positive, f4/80-positive, and cd68-positive.

CL:0000130.name: neuron associated cell (sensu nematoda and protostomia)

CL:0000132.name: corneal endothelial cell
CL:0000132.def: an hexagonal, flattened, mitochondria-rich endothelial cell that forms a monolayer on the posterior surface of the cornea (the corneal endothelium). corneal endothelial cells are derived from the neural crest and are responsible for keeping the cornea transparent by maintaining the tissue in a semi-dry state through the action of their ionic pumps and tight junction barrier.

CL:0000133.name: neurectodermal cell
CL:0000133.def: ectoderm destined to be nervous tissue.

CL:0000134.name: mesenchymal stem cell
CL:0000134.def: a connective tissue cell that normally gives rise to other cells that are organized as three-dimensional masses. in humans, this cell type is cd73-positive, cd90-positive, cd105-positive, cd45-negative, cd34-negative, and mhcii-negative. they may further differentiate into osteoblasts, adipocytes, myocytes, neurons, or chondroblasts in vitro. originally described as residing in the bone marrow, this cell type is now known to reside in many, if not all, adult organs.

CL:0000135.name: fibrocyte
CL:0000135.def: an inactive fibroblast; cytoplasm is sparse, endoplasmic reticulum is scanty with flattened nucleus. term used by some histologists; when fibroblasts become relatively inactive in fiber formation. however, this cell has the potential for fibrogenesis in quiescent connective tissue of the adult, as well as during development, other histologists prefer to use the term fibroblast in all circumstances. these cells represent ~0.5% of peripheral blood leukocytes.

CL:0000136.name: fat cell
CL:0000136.def: a fat-storing cell found mostly in the abdominal cavity and subcutaneous tissue of mammals. fat is usually stored in the form of triglycerides.

CL:0000137.name: osteocyte
CL:0000137.def: a mature osteoblast that has become embedded in the bone matrix. they occupy a small cavity, called lacuna, in the matrix and are connected to adjacent osteocytes via protoplasmic projections called canaliculi.

CL:0000138.name: chondrocyte
CL:0000138.def: skeletogenic cell that is terminally differentiated, secretes an avascular, gag-rich matrix, is embedded in cartilage tissue matrix, retains the ability to divide, and develops from a chondroblast cell.

CL:0000140.name: odontocyte
CL:0000140.def: skeletogenic cell that secretes dentine matrix, is derived from odontogenic papilla. embedded in dentine tissue, and is the transformation of a non-terminally differentiated odontoblast cell.

CL:0000141.name: cementocyte
CL:0000141.def: an osteocytelike cell with numerous processes, trapped in a lacuna in the cement of the tooth.

CL:0000142.name: hyalocyte
CL:0000142.def: a cell occurring in the peripheral part of the vitreous body of the eye that may be responsible for production of hyaluronic acid and collagen.

CL:0000144.name: obsolete cell by function
CL:0000144.def: obsolete: a classification of cells by their primary end goal or behavior.

CL:0000145.name: professional antigen presenting cell
CL:0000145.def: a cell capable of processing and presenting lipid and protein antigens to t cells in order to initiate an immune response.

CL:0000147.name: pigment cell
CL:0000147.def: a pigment cell is a cell that contains pigment granules.

CL:0000148.name: melanocyte
CL:0000148.def: a pigment cell derived from the neural crest. contains melanin-filled pigment granules, which gives a brown to black appearance.

CL:0000150.name: glandular epithelial cell
CL:0000150.def: a specialized epithelial cell that is capable of synthesizing and secreting certain biomolecules.

CL:0000151.name: secretory cell
CL:0000151.def: a cell that specializes in controlled release of one or more substances.

CL:0000152.name: exocrine cell
CL:0000152.def: a cell of an exocrine gland; i.e. a gland that discharges its secretion via a duct.

CL:0000155.name: peptic cell
CL:0000155.def: a cell that is usually basal in position, cuboidal with round nucleus, short microvilli, secretes pepsinogen.

CL:0000156.name: obsolete antibody secreting cell
CL:0000156.def: obsolete: a cell of the lymphoid series that can react with antigen to produce specific cell products called antibodies. various cell subpopulations, often b cells, can be defined, based on the different classes of immunoglobulins that they synthesize.

CL:0000157.name: surfactant secreting cell
CL:0000157.def: a cell that specializes in secretion of surfactant in the alveoli of the lung.

CL:0000158.name: club cell
CL:0000158.def: a non-mucous, epithelial secretory cell that is part of the tracheobronchial tree. a club cell has short microvilli but no cilia. a club cell is able to multiply and differentiate into ciliated cells to regenerate the bronchiolar epithelium and it also protects the tracheobronchial epithelium.

CL:0000160.name: goblet cell
CL:0000160.def: a cell of the epithelial lining that produce and secrete mucins.

CL:0000162.name: parietal cell
CL:0000162.def: a large, oval stomach epithelial cell with a central nucleus; source of gastric acid. secretes hcl.

CL:0000163.name: endocrine cell
CL:0000163.def: a cell of an endocrine gland, ductless glands that secrete substances which are released directly into the circulation and which influence metabolism and other body functions.

CL:0000164.name: enteroendocrine cell
CL:0000164.def: an endocrine cell that is located in the epithelium of the gastrointestinal tract or in the pancreas.

CL:0000165.name: neuroendocrine cell
CL:0000165.def: a neuron that is capable of some hormone secretion in response to neuronal signals.

CL:0000166.name: chromaffin cell
CL:0000166.def: a cell that stores epinephrine secretory vesicles. during times of stress, the nervous system signals the vesicles to secrete their hormonal content. their name derives from their ability to stain a brownish color with chromic salts. characteristically, they are located in the adrenal medulla and paraganglia of the sympathetic nervous system.

CL:0000169.name: type b pancreatic cell
CL:0000169.def: a cell that secretes insulin and is located towards the center of the islets of langerhans.

CL:0000171.name: pancreatic a cell
CL:0000171.def: a type of enteocrine cell found in the periphery of the islets of langerhans that secretes glucagon.

CL:0000173.name: pancreatic d cell
CL:0000173.def: a d cell located in the pancreas. peripherally placed within the islets like type a cells; contains somatostatin.

CL:0000175.name: luteal cell
CL:0000175.def: a progesterone secreting cell in the corpus luteum. the large luteal cells develop from the granulosa cells. the small luteal cells develop from the theca cells.

CL:0000178.name: leydig cell
CL:0000178.def: a leydig cell is a testosterone-secreting cell in the interstitial area, between the seminiferous tubules, in the testis.

CL:0000180.name: estradiol secreting cell
CL:0000180.def: a steroid hormone secreting cell that secretes estradiol.

CL:0000181.name: obsolete metabolising cell
CL:0000181.def: a cell whose primary function is intermediary metabolism.

CL:0000182.name: hepatocyte
CL:0000182.def: the main structural component of the liver. they are specialized epithelial cells that are organized into interconnected plates called lobules. majority of cell population of liver, polygonal in shape, arranged in plates or trabeculae between sinusoids; may have single nucleus or binucleated.

CL:0000183.name: contractile cell
CL:0000183.def: a cell whose primary function is to shorten.

CL:0000185.name: myoepithelial cell
CL:0000185.def: contractile cells resembling smooth muscle cells that are present in glands, notably the mammary gland, and aid in secretion. this cell has long weaving dendritic processes containing myofilament.

CL:0000186.name: myofibroblast cell
CL:0000186.def: an animal cell that has characteristics of both a fibroblast cell and a smooth muscle cell.

CL:0000187.name: muscle cell
CL:0000187.def: a mature contractile cell, commonly known as a myocyte. this cell has as part of its cytoplasm myofibrils organized in various patterns.

CL:0000188.name: cell of skeletal muscle
CL:0000188.def: a somatic cell located in skeletal muscle.

CL:0000189.name: slow muscle cell
CL:0000189.def: a muscle cell that develops tension more slowly than a fast-twitch fiber.

CL:0000190.name: fast muscle cell
CL:0000190.def: a muscle cell that can develop high tension rapidly. it is usually innervated by a single alpha neuron.

CL:0000192.name: smooth muscle cell
CL:0000192.def: a non-striated, elongated, spindle-shaped cell found lining the digestive tract, uterus, and blood vessels. they develop from specialized myoblasts (smooth muscle myoblast).

CL:0000193.name: cardiac muscle cell (sensu arthopoda)
CL:0000193.def: a striated muscle cell of an arthropod heart that participates in heart contraction.

CL:0000196.name: insect flight muscle cell
CL:0000196.def: a muscle cell that is involved in the mechanism of insect flight. this encompasses both, cells that power flight and cells that control flight.

CL:0000197.name: sensory receptor cell
CL:0000197.def: a cell that is capable of detection of a stimulus involved in sensory perception.

CL:0000198.name: pain receptor cell
CL:0000198.def: the peripheral receptor for pain. includes receptors which are sensitive to painful mechanical stimuli, extreme heat or cold, and chemical stimuli. all mammalian nociceptors are free nerve endings.

CL:0000199.name: mechanoreceptor cell
CL:0000199.def: a cell specialized to transduce mechanical stimuli and relay that information centrally in the nervous system.

CL:0000202.name: auditory hair cell
CL:0000202.def: a mechanoreceptor cell of the auditory or vestibular system that is sensitive to auditory stimuli. the accessory sensory structures are arranged so that appropriate stimuli cause movement of the hair-like projections (stereocilia and kinocilia) which relay the information centrally in the nervous system.

CL:0000205.name: thermoreceptor cell
CL:0000205.def: a cellular receptor which mediates the sense of temperature. thermoreceptor cells in vertebrates are mostly located under the skin. in mammals there are separate types of thermoreceptors for cold and for warmth and pain receptor cells which detect cold or heat extreme enough to cause pain.

CL:0000206.name: chemoreceptor cell
CL:0000206.def: a cell specialized to detect chemical substances and relay that information centrally in the nervous system. chemoreceptors may monitor external stimuli, as in taste and olfaction, or internal stimuli, such as the concentrations of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the blood.

CL:0000209.name: taste receptor cell
CL:0000209.def: a specialized cell involved in gustatory sensory perception.

CL:0000210.name: photoreceptor cell
CL:0000210.def: a cell specialized to detect and transduce light.

CL:0000211.name: electrically active cell
CL:0000211.def: a cell whose function is determined by the generation or the reception of an electric signal.

CL:0000212.name: absorptive cell
CL:0000212.def: a cell that takes up and metabolizes substances.

CL:0000213.name: lining cell
CL:0000213.def: a cell within an epithelial cell sheet whose main function is to act as an internal or external covering for a tissue or an organism.

CL:0000214.name: synovial cell
CL:0000214.def: a cell located in the synovial joint.

CL:0000215.name: barrier cell
CL:0000215.def: a cell whose primary function is to prevent the transport of stuff across compartments.

CL:0000216.name: sertoli cell
CL:0000216.def: a supporting cell projecting inward from the basement membrane of seminiferous tubules. they surround and nourish the developing male germ cells and secrete androgen binding protein. their tight junctions with the spermatogonia and spermatocytes provide a blood-testis barrier.

CL:0000218.name: myelinating schwann cell
CL:0000218.def: a neuroglial cell of the peripheral nervous system which forms the insulating myelin sheaths of peripheral axons.

CL:0000219.name: motile cell
CL:0000219.def: a cell that moves by its own activities.

CL:0000221.name: ectodermal cell
CL:0000221.def: a cell of the outer of the three germ layers of the embryo.

CL:0000222.name: mesodermal cell
CL:0000222.def: a cell of the middle germ layer of the embryo.

CL:0000223.name: endodermal cell
CL:0000223.def: a cell of the inner of the three germ layers of the embryo.

CL:0000224.name: obsolete cell by nuclear number
CL:0000224.def: obsolete: a classification of cells by the number of their nuclei.

CL:0000225.name: anucleate cell
CL:0000225.def: a cell that lacks a nucleus.

CL:0000226.name: single nucleate cell
CL:0000226.def: a cell with a single nucleus.

CL:0000228.name: multinucleate cell
CL:0000228.def: a cell with more than one nucleus.

CL:0000229.name: obsolete lymphoblast
CL:0000229.def: obsolete (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000230.name: obsolete t lymphoblast
CL:0000230.def: obsolete (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000231.name: obsolete b lymphoblast
CL:0000231.def: obsolete (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000232.name: erythrocyte
CL:0000232.def: a red blood cell. in mammals, mature erythrocytes are biconcave disks containing hemoglobin whose function is to transport oxygen.

CL:0000233.name: platelet
CL:0000233.def: a non-nucleated disk-shaped cell formed by extrusion from megakaryocytes, found in the blood of all mammals, and mainly involved in blood coagulation.

CL:0000234.name: phagocyte
CL:0000234.def: any cell capable of ingesting particulate matter via phagocytosis.

CL:0000235.name: macrophage
CL:0000235.def: a mononuclear phagocyte present in variety of tissues, typically differentiated from monocytes, capable of phagocytosing a variety of extracellular particulate material, including immune complexes, microorganisms, and dead cells.

CL:0000236.name: b cell
CL:0000236.def: a lymphocyte of b lineage that is capable of b cell mediated immunity.

CL:0000242.name: merkel cell
CL:0000242.def: a modified epidermal cell located in the stratum basale. they are found mostly in areas where sensory perception is acute. merkel cells are closely associated with an expanded terminal bulb of an afferent myelinated nerve fiber.

CL:0000243.name: obsolete glial cell (sensu vertebrata)
CL:0000243.def: a non-neuronal cell of the nervous system. they not only provide physical support, but also respond to injury, regulate the ionic and chemical composition of the extracellular milieu. form the myelin insulation of nervous pathways, guide neuronal migration during development, and exchange metabolites with neurons. neuroglia have high-affinity transmitter uptake systems, voltage-dependent and transmitter-gated ion channels, and can release transmitters, but their role in signaling (as in many other functions) is unclear.

CL:0000244.name: transitional epithelial cell
CL:0000244.def: a cell characteristically found lining hollow organs that are subject to great mechanical change due to contraction and distention; originally thought to represent a transition between stratified squamous and columnar epithelium.

CL:0000245.name: obsolete passage cell
CL:0000245.def: obsolete. use po:0000353 from plant ontology instead. cell in exodermis or endodermis that remains thin walled when the associated cells develop thick secondary walls. has casparian strip in endodermis.

CL:0000247.name: rohon-beard neuron
CL:0000247.def: type of neuron that is a primary mechanosensory cell, with peripheral neurites innervating the skin with free nerve endings.

CL:0000248.name: obsolete microsporocyte
CL:0000248.def: obsolete. use po:0020047 from plant ontology instead. a diploid (2n) cell that undergoes meiosis and forms four haploid (1n) microspores; also called microspore mother cell and, in seed plants, pollen mother cell.

CL:0000250.name: obsolete megaspore
CL:0000250.def: obsolete. use po:0020019 from plant ontology instead. a haploid (1n) spore developing into a female gametophyte in heterosporous plants.

CL:0000252.name: obsolete microspore
CL:0000252.def: obsolete. use po:0020048 from plant ontology instead. a haploid (1n) spore developing into a male gametophyte in heterosporous plants; the uninucleate pollen grain in seed plants.

CL:0000254.name: obsolete egg cell
CL:0000254.def: obsolete. use po:0020094 from plant ontology instead. the female gamete of plants.

CL:0000258.name: obsolete fiber tracheid
CL:0000258.def: obsolete. use po:0000355 from plant ontology instead. a fiber like tracheid in the secondary xylem; commonly thick walled, with pointed ends and bordered pits that have lenticular to slit like apertures.

CL:0000260.name: obsolete mucilage cell
CL:0000260.def: obsolete. use po:0000373 from plant ontology instead. cell containing mucilages or gums or similar carbohydrate material characterized by the property of swelling in water.

CL:0000262.name: obsolete guard mother cell
CL:0000262.def: obsolete. use po:0000351 from plant ontology instead. an epidermal cell that divides to produce the guard cells.

CL:0000264.name: obsolete phloem initial
CL:0000264.def: obsolete. use po:0000400 from plant ontology instead. a cambial cell on the phloem side of the cambial zone that is the source of one or more cells arising by periclinal divisions and differentiating into phloem elements with or without additional divisions in various planes.

CL:0000266.name: obsolete meristemoid
CL:0000266.def: obsolete. use po:0004011 from plant ontology instead. a cell constituting an active locus of meristematic activity in a tissue composed of somewhat older, differentiating cells.

CL:0000268.name: obsolete sieve element
CL:0000268.def: obsolete. consult plant ontology instead. the cell in the phloem tissue concerned with mainly longitudinal conduction of food materials. classified into sieve cell and sieve tube member.

CL:0000270.name: obsolete subsidiary cell
CL:0000270.def: obsolete. use po:0000284 from plant ontology instead. an epidermal cell associated with a stoma and at least morphologically distinguishable from the epidermal cells composing the groundmass of the tissue.

CL:0000272.name: obsolete cambial initial
CL:0000272.def: obsolete, use term from plant ontology. a cell localized in the vascular cambium or phellogen. its periclinal division can contribute cells either to the outside or to the inside of the axis; in vascular cambium, classified into fusiform initials (source of axial cells of xylem and phloem) and ray initials (source of the ray cells).

CL:0000276.name: obsolete sclerenchyma cell
CL:0000276.def: obsolete. use po:0000077 from plant ontology instead. cell variable in form and size, being more or less thick, often lignified, secondary walls. belongs to the category of subcells and may or may not be devoid of protoplast at maturity.

CL:0000277.name: obsolete prestalk i cell
CL:0000277.def: obsolete: initial population of prestalk cells that activate the ecma promoter at the mound stage and that presumably further differentiate into psta and psto cells.

CL:0000278.name: obsolete central cell
CL:0000278.def: obsolete. use po:0020090 from plant ontology instead. obsoleted, use term from plant ontology. a cell containing the two polar nuclei which, after double fertilization, will develop into the endosperm.

CL:0000280.name: obsolete generative cell
CL:0000280.def: obsolete. use po:0020097 from plant ontology instead. the cell that will give rise to the generative nuclei which will participate in fertilization.

CL:0000282.name: obsolete trichome
CL:0000282.def: obsolete. use po:0000282 from plant ontology instead. an outgrowth from the epidermis. trichomes vary in size and complexity and include hairs, scales, and other structures and may be glandular. in arabidopsis, patterning of trichome development is not random but does not appear to be lineage-based like stomata.

CL:0000284.name: obsolete companion cell
CL:0000284.def: obsolete. use po:0000071 from plant ontology instead. a specialized parenchyma cell associated with a sieve-tube member in angiosperm phloem and arising from the same mother cell as the sieve-tube member.

CL:0000286.name: hyphal cell
CL:0000286.def: a cell of a filament of a fungal mycelium.

CL:0000288.name: obsolete synergid
CL:0000288.def: obsolete. use po:0000191 from plant ontology instead. a cell in the micropylar end of the embryo sac associated with the egg in the egg apparatus of angiosperms. plays a vital role in fertilization.

CL:0000290.name: obsolete xylem fiber cell
CL:0000290.def: obsolete. use po:0000274 from plant ontology instead. a fiber of the xylem tissue, two types are recognized in the secondary xylem: fiber tracheids and libriform fibers.

CL:0000292.name: obsolete guard cell
CL:0000292.def: obsolete. use po:0000293 from plant ontology instead. one of a pair of cells flanking the stomatal pore and causing the opening and closing of the pore by changes in turgor.

CL:0000293.name: structural cell
CL:0000293.def: a cell whose primary function is to provide structural support, to provide strength and physical integrity to the organism.

CL:0000294.name: obsolete sieve cell
CL:0000294.def: obsolete. consult plant ontology instead. a type of sieve element that has relatively undifferentiated sieve areas (with narrow pores), rather uniform in structure on all walls; that is, there are no sieve plates. typical of gymnosperms and lower vascular plants.

CL:0000295.name: somatotropin secreting cell
CL:0000295.def: a peptide hormone secreting cell that produces growth hormone, somatotropin.

CL:0000296.name: obsolete vegetative cell
CL:0000296.def: obsolete. use po:0020099 from plant ontology instead. cell type formed after the first mitotic division of the microgametophye, the nucleus of this cell migrates to the tip of the pollen tube after germination and disintegrates when the pollen tube penetrates the nucellus.

CL:0000297.name: obsolete socket cell
CL:0000297.def: obsolete. use po:0000115 from plant ontology instead. a cell that surrounds a trichome and provides support for the trichome.

CL:0000298.name: obsolete xylem element
CL:0000298.def: obsolete. use po:0000273 from plant ontology instead. a cell composing the xylem.

CL:0000299.name: obsolete trichoblast
CL:0000299.def: obsoleted. commonly used for a cell in root epidermis that gives rise to a root hair. the daughter cell produced by the asymmetric division of a root epidermal cell that gives rise to a root hair.

CL:0000300.name: gamete
CL:0000300.def: a mature sexual reproductive cell having a single set of unpaired chromosomes.

CL:0000301.name: pole cell
CL:0000301.def: a primordial germ cell of insects. such cells form at the posterior pole of the early embryo.

CL:0000302.name: obsolete igm b cell
CL:0000302.def: obsolete (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000303.name: obsolete igg b cell
CL:0000303.def: obsolete (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000304.name: obsolete iga b cell
CL:0000304.def: obsolete (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000305.name: obsolete ige b cell
CL:0000305.def: obsolete (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000307.name: tracheal epithelial cell
CL:0000307.def: an epithelial cell found in the trachea.

CL:0000312.name: keratinocyte
CL:0000312.def: an epidermal cell which synthesizes keratin and undergoes a characteristic change as it moves upward from the basal layers of the epidermis to the cornified (horny) layer of the skin. successive stages of differentiation of the keratinocytes forming the epidermal layers are basal cell, spinous or prickle cell, and the granular cell.

CL:0000313.name: serous secreting cell
CL:0000313.def: columnar glandular cell with irregular nucleus, copious granular endoplasmic reticulum and supranuclear granules. secretes a watery fluid containing proteins known as serous fluid.

CL:0000315.name: tear secreting cell
CL:0000315.def: a cell secreting tears, the fluid secreted by the lacrimal glands. this fluid moistens the conjunctiva and cornea.

CL:0000316.name: obsolete ray initial
CL:0000316.def: obsolete. use po:0000082 from plant ontology instead. a meristemic ray cell in the vascular cambium that gives rise to ray cells of the secondary xylem and secondary phloem.

CL:0000317.name: sebum secreting cell
CL:0000317.def: a cell secreting sebun, an oily substance secreted by sebaceous glands, composed of keratin, fat, and cellular debris.

CL:0000318.name: sweat secreting cell
CL:0000318.def: a cell secreting sweat, the fluid excreted by the sweat glands of mammals. it consists of water containing sodium chloride, phosphate, urea, ammonia, and other waste products.

CL:0000320.name: obsolete megasporocyte
CL:0000320.def: obsolete. use po:0000431 from plant ontology instead. a diploid (2n) cell that undergoes meiosis and produces four haploid (1n) megaspores; also called megaspore mother cell.

CL:0000322.name: pneumocyte
CL:0000322.def: an epithelial cell that lines the peripheral gas exchange region of the lungs of air-breathing vertebrates.

CL:0000325.name: stuff accumulating cell
CL:0000325.def: a cell that is specialised to accumulate a particular substance(s).

CL:0000330.name: obsolete collenchymal cell
CL:0000330.def: obsolete. use po:0000075 from plant ontology instead. an elongated living cell with unevenly thickened nonlignified primary walls.

CL:0000331.name: obsolete tracheid
CL:0000331.def: obsolete. use po:0000301 from plant ontology instead. a tracheary element of the xylem that has no perforations, as contrasted with a vessel member. may occur in primary and in secondary xylem. may have any kind of secondary wall thickening found in tracheary elements.

CL:0000332.name: obsolete atrichoblast
CL:0000332.def: obsolete, use term from plant ontology. a cell formed after asymmetric division of root epidermal cell that does not give rise to a root hair.

CL:0000333.name: migratory neural crest cell
CL:0000333.def: a cell derived from the specialized ectoderm flanking each side of the embryonic neural plate, which after the closure of the neural tube, forms masses of cells that migrate out from the dorsal aspect of the neural tube to spread throughout the body.

CL:0000335.name: mesenchyme condensation cell
CL:0000335.def: a mesenchymal cell in embryonic development found in a contracting mass and that gives rise to osteoprogenitors.

CL:0000336.name: adrenal medulla chromaffin cell
CL:0000336.def: a cell found within the adrenal medulla that secrete biogenic amine hormones upon stimulation.
CL:0000336.synonym: medullary chromaffin cell of adrenal gland

CL:0000338.name: neuroblast (sensu nematoda and protostomia)
CL:0000338.def: a neural precursor of the central nervous system.

CL:0000339.name: glioblast (sensu vertebrata)
CL:0000339.def: an early neural cell developing from the early ependymal cell of the neural tube.

CL:0000340.name: glioblast (sensu nematoda and protostomia)
CL:0000340.def: a precursor of the central nervous system that gives rise to glial cells only.

CL:0000342.name: pigment cell (sensu vertebrata)
CL:0000342.def: any animal cell containing pigment granules.

CL:0000343.name: visual pigment cell (sensu vertebrata)
CL:0000343.def: a pigment cell that is capable of detecting light stimulus that is involved in visual perception.

CL:0000345.name: dental papilla cell
CL:0000345.def: a mesenchymal cell that is part of a small mass of condensed mesenchyme in the enamel organ; it differentiates into the dentin and dental pulp.

CL:0000346.name: hair follicle dermal papilla cell
CL:0000346.def: a specialized mesenchymal cell that resides in the dermal papilla located at the bottom of hair follicles. this cell plays a pivotal roles in hair formation, growth, and cycling.

CL:0000347.name: scleral cell
CL:0000347.def: a cell of the sclera of the eye.

CL:0000348.name: choroidal cell of the eye
CL:0000348.def: a structural cell that is part of optic choroid.

CL:0000351.name: trophoblast cell
CL:0000351.def: a cell lining the outside of the blastocyst. after binding to the endometrium, trophoblast cells develop into two distinct layers, an inner layer of mononuclear cytotrophoblast cells and an outer layer of continuous multinuclear cytoplasm, the syncytiotrophoblast cells, which form the early fetal-maternal interface.

CL:0000352.name: epiblast cell
CL:0000352.def: a cell of the outer layer of a blastula that gives rise to the ectoderm after gastrulation.

CL:0000353.name: blastoderm cell
CL:0000353.def: an undifferentiated cell produced by early cleavages of the fertilized egg (zygote).

CL:0000355.name: multi-potent skeletal muscle stem cell
CL:0000355.def: a multifate stem cell found in skeletal muscle than can differentiate into many different cell types, including muscle. distinct cell type from satellite cell.

CL:0000358.name: sphincter associated smooth muscle cell
CL:0000358.def: a smooth muscle cell that is part of a sphincter. a sphincter is a typically circular muscle that normally maintains constriction of a natural body passage or orifice and which relaxes as required by normal physiological functioning.

CL:0000359.name: vascular associated smooth muscle cell
CL:0000359.def: a smooth muscle cell associated with the vasculature.

CL:0000360.name: morula cell
CL:0000360.def: a cell of the early embryo at the developmental stage in which the blastomeres, resulting from repeated mitotic divisions of the fertilized ovum (zygote), form a compact cell mass.

CL:0000361.name: gastrula cell
CL:0000361.def: a cell of the embryo in the early stage following the blastula, characterized by morphogenetic cell movements, cell differentiation, and the formation of the three germ layers.

CL:0000362.name: epidermal cell
CL:0000362.def: an epithelial cell of the integument (the outer layer of an organism).

CL:0000363.name: obsolete axial cell
CL:0000363.def: obsolete. use po:0000081 from plant ontology instead. obsolete, use term from the plant ontology. a secondary vascular cell that develops from the fusiform cambial initials and oriented with their longest diameter parallel with the main axis of stem or root. these cells make up the axial system, also known as vertical or longitudinal system.

CL:0000364.name: obsolete ray cell
CL:0000364.def: obsolete. consult plant ontology. a cell that develops from the ray initial and composes all rays (panels of tissue variable in height and width, formed by the ray initials in the vascular cambium and extending radially in the secondary xylem and secondary phloem) in the secondary vascular tissues.

CL:0000365.name: animal zygote
CL:0000365.def: diploid cell produced by the fusion of sperm cell nucleus and egg cell.

CL:0000366.name: obsolete sperm cell (sensu viridiplantae)
CL:0000366.def: obsolete. use po:0000084 from plant ontology instead. male gamete, part of male germ unit.

CL:0000368.name: obsolete myrosin cell
CL:0000368.def: obsolete. use po:0000352 from plant ontology instead. cell containing glucosinolates ('mustard oil glucosides') and myrosinases, enzymes hydrolyzing the glucosinolates. occurs in eleven dicotyledon families, the two largest of which are the brassicaceae and euphorbiaceae.

CL:0000370.name: obsolete transfer cell
CL:0000370.def: obsolete. use po:0000078 from plant ontology instead. parenchyma cell with the wall ingrowth (or invaginations) that increase the surface of the plasmalemma. appears to be specialized for short-distance transfer of solutes.

CL:0000371.name: protoplast
CL:0000371.def: the cell protoplasm after removal of the cell wall.

CL:0000372.name: tormogen cell
CL:0000372.def: an epidermal cell that is part of a cell cluster organ of the insect integument (such as a sensillum) and that secretes a cuticular specialization that forms a socket around the base of a cuticular specialization produced by a trichogen cell.

CL:0000373.name: histoblast
CL:0000373.def: a progenitor cell found in the larval epidermis of insects and that gives rise to the adult abdominal epidermis.

CL:0000374.name: trichogen cell
CL:0000374.def: an epidermal cell that is part of a cell cluster organ of the insect integument (such as a sensillum) and that secretes a cuticular specialization, often in the form of a hair, bristle, peg or scale. the base of this specialization is often surrounded by a socket produced by a closely associated tormogen cell.

CL:0000380.name: thecogen cell
CL:0000380.def: the support cell that makes the thecogen dendritic cap - a cuticle-like matrix around the tip of the eo-dendrite and which encloses the soma of the eo-neuron.

CL:0000382.name: scolopale cell
CL:0000382.def: a cell that is part of a scolopidium and surrounds the dendrite of a scolopidial neuron.

CL:0000387.name: hemocyte (sensu arthropoda)
CL:0000387.def: a blood cell of the circulatory system of arthropods.

CL:0000388.name: tendon cell
CL:0000388.def: an elongated fibrocyte that is part of a tendon. the cytoplasm is stretched between the collagen fibres of the tendon. they have a central cell nucleus with a prominent nucleolus. tendon cells have a well-developed rough endoplasmic reticulum and they are responsible for synthesis and turnover of tendon fibres and ground substance.

CL:0000392.name: crystal cell
CL:0000392.def: a hemocyte that synthesizes and secretes melanins as part of the antimicrobial immune response. it is characterized morphologically by crystal inclusions of phenoloxidases in its cytoplasm, hence its name.

CL:0000393.name: electrically responsive cell
CL:0000393.def: a cell whose function is determined by its response to an electric signal.

CL:0000394.name: plasmatocyte
CL:0000394.def: a phagocytic hemocyte, responsible for the engulfment of small particles, microbes, and apoptotic tissue debris. it may also secretes antimicrobial peptides and contribute to the production and secretion of proteins of the hemolymph.

CL:0000395.name: procrystal cell
CL:0000395.def: a precursor of mature crystal cells.

CL:0000396.name: lamellocyte
CL:0000396.def: a hemocyte found in immuno-stimulated larvae.

CL:0000399.name: obsolete phloem element
CL:0000399.def: obsolete. consult plant ontology instead. obsoleted, not defined prior to obsoletion.

CL:0000400.name: obsolete pavement cell
CL:0000400.def: obsolete. use po:0000332 from plant ontology instead. an epidermal cell with a characteristic convoluted anticlinal cell wall that gives a jigsaw like appearance to the lamina.

CL:0000402.name: cns interneuron
CL:0000402.def: an interneuron that has its cell body in a central nervous system.

CL:0000404.name: electrically signaling cell
CL:0000404.def: a cell that initiates an electrical signal and passes that signal to another cell.

CL:0000407.name: scolopidial ligament cell
CL:0000407.def: a cell that anchors the cell body of a scolopidial neuron to the integument.

CL:0000411.name: caenorhabditis hypodermal cell
CL:0000411.def: an epithelial cell of the hypodermis of caenorhabditis.

CL:0000412.name: polyploid cell
CL:0000412.def: a cell whose nucleus, or nuclei, each contain more than two haploid genomes.

CL:0000413.name: haploid cell
CL:0000413.def: a cell whose nucleus contains a single haploid genome.

CL:0000414.name: obsolete cell by ploidy
CL:0000414.def: obsolete: a classification of cells by the number of haploid genome equivalents of their nucleus or nuclei.

CL:0000415.name: diploid cell
CL:0000415.def: a cell whose nucleus has two haploid genomes.

CL:0000418.name: arcade cell
CL:0000418.def: an epithelial cell found in c. elegans that firmly hold the outer body wall and the lips to the inner cylinder of the pharynx in a manner that keeps these organs from breaking apart, while still giving each organ freedom of movement during feeding.

CL:0000419.name: seam cell
CL:0000419.def: an epithelial fate stem cell found in flatworms.

CL:0000421.name: coelomocyte
CL:0000421.def: a free floating cell, including amebocytes and eleocytes, in the coelom of certain animals, especially annelids.

CL:0000422.name: mitogenic signaling cell
CL:0000422.def: a cell whose primary function is to cause growth by stimulating cell division in its immediate cellular environment.

CL:0000424.name: excretory cell
CL:0000424.def: a cell involved in the elimination of metabolic and foreign toxins, and in maintaining the ionic, acid-base and water balance of biological fluids.

CL:0000425.name: pore cell
CL:0000425.def: forms the terminal part of the cuticle-lined excretory duct of c. elegans.

CL:0000427.name: glr cell
CL:0000427.def: a scaffolding cell type found in c. elegans, this cell plays a supportive role to the muscle arms. may also have an endocrine role.

CL:0000429.name: imaginal disc cell
CL:0000429.def: a columnar epithelial cell that is part of an insect imaginal disc.

CL:0000430.name: xanthophore cell
CL:0000430.def: a pigment cell derived from the neural crest. contains cartenoid pigments in structures called pterinosomes or xanthosomes. this gives an appearance ranging from a golden yellow to orange and red.

CL:0000431.name: iridophore
CL:0000431.def: a pigment cell derived from the neural crest. the cell contains flat light-reflecting platelets, probably of guanine, in stacks called reflecting platelets or iridisomes. the color-generating components produce a silver, gold, or iridescent color.

CL:0000432.name: reticular cell
CL:0000432.def: a fibroblast that synthesizes collagen and uses it to produce reticular fibers, thus providing structural support. reticular cells are found in many organs, including the spleen, lymph nodes and kidneys. subtypes of reticular cells include epithelial, mesenchymal, and fibroblastic reticular cells. fibroblastic reticular cells are involved in directing b cells and t cells to specific regions within a tissue, whereas epithelial and mesenchymal reticular cells are associated with certain areas of the brain.

CL:0000433.name: obsolete functional megaspore
CL:0000433.def: obsolete. use po:0000244 from plant ontology instead. in monosporic and bisporic megasporogenesis: the megaspore(s) that will undergo megagametogenesis.

CL:0000434.name: eccrine cell
CL:0000434.def: a secretory cell that discharges its product without loss of cytoplasm.

CL:0000437.name: gonadtroph
CL:0000437.def: a rounded cell that is usually situated next to sinusoids; secretes follicular stimulating hormone (fsh) and luteinizing hormone (lh).

CL:0000438.name: luteinizing hormone secreting cell
CL:0000438.def: a peptide hormone secreting cell pituitary that produces luteinizing hormone.

CL:0000439.name: prolactin secreting cell
CL:0000439.def: a peptide hormone cell that secretes prolactin.

CL:0000440.name: melanocyte stimulating hormone secreting cell
CL:0000440.def: a cell of the intermediate pituitary that produces melanocyte stimulating hormone.

CL:0000441.name: follicle stem cell (sensu arthropoda)
CL:0000441.def: a stem cell that gives rise to the follicle cells that surround the oocyte in female arthropods.

CL:0000442.name: follicular dendritic cell
CL:0000442.def: a cell with extensive dendritic processes found in the b cell areas (primary follicles and germinal centers) of lymphoid tissue. they are unrelated to the dendritic cell associated with t cells. follicular dendritic cells have fc receptors and c3b receptors, but unlike other dendritic cells, they do not process or present antigen in a way that allows recognition by t cells. instead, they hold antigen in the form of immune complexes on their surfaces for long periods and can present antigen to b cells during an immune response.

CL:0000444.name: obliquely striated muscle cell
CL:0000444.def: a muscle cell in which the fibers are organised into sarcomeres but in which adjacent myofibrils are offset from each other, producing an oblique banding pattern.

CL:0000446.name: chief cell of parathyroid gland
CL:0000446.def: an epithelial cell of the parathyroid gland that is arranged in wide, irregular interconnecting columns; responsible for the synthesis and secretion of parathyroid hormone.

CL:0000448.name: white fat cell
CL:0000448.def: fat cells with light coloration and few mitochondria. they contain a scant ring of cytoplasm surrounding a single large lipid droplet or vacuole.

CL:0000449.name: brown fat cell
CL:0000449.def: a cell from the thermogenic form of adipose tissue found in many species,  particularly in newborns and hibernating mammals, but also in lesser amounts in adults of other mammals including humans. brown fat is capable of rapid liberation of energy and seems to be important in the maintenance of body temperature immediately after birth and upon waking from hibernation.

CL:0000451.name: dendritic cell
CL:0000451.def: a cell of hematopoietic origin, typically resident in particular tissues, specialized in the uptake, processing, and transport of antigens to lymph nodes for the purpose of stimulating an immune response via t cell activation. these cells are lineage negative (cd3-negative, cd19-negative, cd34-negative, and cd56-negative).

CL:0000453.name: langerhans cell
CL:0000453.def: langerhans cell is a conventional dendritic cell that has plasma membrane part cd207. a langerhans cell is a stellate dendritic cell of myeloid origin, that appears clear on light microscopy and has a dark-staining, indented nucleus and characteristic inclusions (birbeck granules) in the cytoplasm; langerhans cells are found principally in the stratum spinosum of the epidermis, but they also occur in other stratified epithelia and have been identified in the lung, lymph nodes, spleen, and thymus.

CL:0000454.name: epinephrine secreting cell
CL:0000454.def: a cell capable of producing epinephrine. epiniphrine is synthesized from norepiniphrine by the actions of the phenylethanolamine n-methyltransferase enzyme, which is expressed in the adrenal glands, androgenic neurons, and in other cell types.

CL:0000455.name: obsolete starch sheath cell
CL:0000455.def: obsolete. use po:0004531 from plant ontology instead. a cell characterized by conspicuous and rather stable accumulation of starch.

CL:0000459.name: noradrenergic cell
CL:0000459.def: a cell capable of producting norepiniphrine. norepiniphrine is a catecholamine with multiple roles including as a hormone and a neurotransmitter. in addition, epiniphrine is synthesized from norepiniphrine by the actions of the phenylethanolamine n-methyltransferase enzyme.

CL:0000462.name: adepithelial cell
CL:0000462.def: a cell of mesodermal origin that is closely associated with the epithelium of an imaginal disc. it is a precursor of some of the insect's adult muscles.

CL:0000463.name: epidermal cell (sensu arthropoda)
CL:0000463.def: an epidermal cell that secretes chitinous cuticle from its apical side.

CL:0000464.name: epidermoblast
CL:0000464.def: an epidermal progenitor cell that arises from neuroectoderm and in turn gives rise to the epidermal sheath of ventral and cephalic regions.

CL:0000465.name: cardioblast (sensu arthropoda)
CL:0000465.def: a precursor of the cells that form the dorsal vessel of arthropods.

CL:0000467.name: adrenocorticotropic hormone secreting cell
CL:0000467.def: a peptide hormone secreting cell that produces adrenocorticotropin, or corticotropin.

CL:0000468.name: neuroglioblast (sensu nematoda and protostomia)
CL:0000468.def: a precursor of the central nervous system that gives rise to both neurons and glial cells.

CL:0000469.name: ganglion mother cell
CL:0000469.def: a neural progenitor cell that is the daughter of a neuroblast (sensu arthopoda).  the progeny of ganglion mother cells develop into neurons, glia and (occasionally) epithelial cells.

CL:0000472.name: obsolete chlorenchyma cell
CL:0000472.def: obsolete. use po:0000076 from plant ontology instead. obsolete, use term from plant ontology. parenchyma cells containing chloroplasts; a component of leaf mesophyll and other green parenchyma tissue.

CL:0000473.name: defensive cell
CL:0000473.def: a cell whose primary function is to protect the organism.

CL:0000474.name: pericardial nephrocyte
CL:0000474.def: an insect renal cell that filters hemolymph and is found with other pericardial nephrocytes in two rows flanking the dorsal vessel.

CL:0000475.name: obsolete degenerate megaspore
CL:0000475.def: obsolete. use po:0000245 from plant ontology instead. in monosporic and bisporic megasporogenesis: the megaspore(s) that do not participate in megagametogenesis.

CL:0000476.name: thyrotroph
CL:0000476.def: a basophil cell of the anterior pituitary that produces thyroid stimulating hormone, thyrotrophin. this cell type is elongated, polygonal and lie in clusters towards the adenohypophyseal center.

CL:0000477.name: follicle cell of egg chamber
CL:0000477.def: a somatic epithelial cell of the insect egg chamber.

CL:0000478.name: oxytocin stimulating hormone secreting cell
CL:0000478.def: a peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes oxytocin stimulating hormone

CL:0000479.name: vasopressin stimulating hormone secreting cell
CL:0000479.def: a peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes vasopressin stimulating hormone

CL:0000480.name: secretin stimulating hormone secreting cell
CL:0000480.def: a peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes secretin stimulating hormone

CL:0000481.name: cholecystokin stimulating hormone secreting cell
CL:0000481.def: a peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes cholecystokin stimulating hormone.

CL:0000482.name: juvenile hormone secreting cell
CL:0000482.def: an endocrine cell that secretes juvenile hormone.

CL:0000483.name: bombesin stimulating hormone secreting cell
CL:0000483.def: a peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes bombesin stimulating hormone.

CL:0000484.name: connective tissue type mast cell
CL:0000484.def: mast cell subtype whose granules contain both the serine proteases tryptase and chymase. these cells are primarily found in connective tissue, such as the peritoneal cavity, skin, and intestinal submucosa. their development is t-cell independent.

CL:0000485.name: mucosal type mast cell
CL:0000485.def: mast cell subtype that contains only the serine protease trypase in its granules. these cells are primarily found in mucosal tissue, such as intestinal mucosa and alveoli. they depend upon t-cells for development of phenotype.

CL:0000486.name: garland cell
CL:0000486.def: a large binucleate cell that forms a 'garland' around the anterior end of the proventriculus (cardia) at its junction with the esophagus in both adults and larvae flies. each cell is surrounded by a basement membrane and there are numerous micro-invaginations (lacunae) extending from the surface into the cytoplasm. at the mouth of each lacuna is a doubled filament forming a specialised filtration system (diaphragm). the filtrate is endocytosed from the lacunae.

CL:0000487.name: oenocyte
CL:0000487.def: a secretory cell of ectodermal origin. this cell may have important functions in fatty acid and hydrocarbon metabolism and is metabolically linked to the fat body and tracheae. this cell is exclusive of arthropods.

CL:0000488.name: visible light photoreceptor cell
CL:0000488.def: a photoreceptor cell that detects visible light.

CL:0000491.name: obsolete cytotoxic t cell
CL:0000491.def: obsolete: a cell responsible for spontaneous cytotoxicity of a variety of tumor cells without prior immunization. these natural killer cells are found in non-immune humans and experimental animals and are thought by some to be the same as killer cells (killing by antibody-dependent cell cytotoxicity), but they can also kill in the absence of antibody.

CL:0000492.name: cd4-positive helper t cell
CL:0000492.def: a cd4-positive, alpha-beta t cell that cooperates with other lymphocytes via direct contact or cytokine release to initiate a variety of immune functions.

CL:0000493.name: obsolete regulatory t cell
CL:0000493.def: obsolete: subpopulation of cd4+ cells which induce cd8+ suppressor t cells to suppress antibody production by b cells. they also stimulate other cellular immune responses.

CL:0000494.name: uv sensitive photoreceptor cell
CL:0000494.def: a photoreceptor cell that detects ultraviolet light.

CL:0000495.name: blue sensitive photoreceptor cell
CL:0000495.def: a photoreceptor cell that is sensitive to blue light.

CL:0000496.name: green sensitive photoreceptor cell
CL:0000496.def: a photoreceptor cell that is sensitive to green light.

CL:0000497.name: red sensitive photoreceptor cell
CL:0000497.def: a photoreceptor cell that is sensitive to red light.

CL:0000498.name: inhibitory interneuron
CL:0000498.def: an interneuron (also called relay neuron, association neuron or local circuit neuron) is a multipolar neuron which connects afferent neurons and efferent neurons in neural pathways. like motor neurons, interneuron cell bodies are always located in the central nervous system (cns).

CL:0000499.name: stromal cell
CL:0000499.def: a connective tissue cell of an organ found in the loose connective tissue. these are most often associated with the uterine mucosa and the ovary as well as the hematopoietic system and elsewhere.

CL:0000500.name: follicular epithelial cell
CL:0000500.def: an epithelial somatic cell associated with a maturing oocyte.

CL:0000501.name: granulosa cell
CL:0000501.def: a supporting cell for the developing female gamete in the ovary of mammals. they develop from the coelomic epithelial cells of the gonadal ridge. granulosa cells form a single layer around the mammalian oocyte in the primordial ovarian follicle and advance to form a multilayered cumulus oophorus surrounding the ovum in the graafian follicle. the major functions of granulosa cells include the production of steroids and lh receptors.

CL:0000502.name: type d enteroendocrine cell
CL:0000502.def: a cell found throughout the gastrointestinal tract and in the pancreas. they secrete somatostatin in both an endocrine and paracrine manner. somatostatin inhibits gastrin, cholecystokinin, insulin, glucagon, pancreatic enzymes, and gastric hydrochloric acid. a variety of substances which inhibit gastric acid secretion (vasoactive intestinal peptide, calcitonin gene-related peptide, cholecystokinin, beta-adrenergic agonists, and gastric inhibitory peptide) are thought to act by releasing somatostatin.

CL:0000503.name: theca cell
CL:0000503.def: a flattened stroma cell forming a sheath or theca outside the basal lamina lining the mature ovarian follicle. thecal interstitial or stromal cells are steroidogenic, and produce primarily androgens which serve as precusors of estrogens in the granulosa cells.

CL:0000504.name: enterochromaffin-like cell
CL:0000504.def: a enteroendocrine cell part of the glands of the gastric mucosa. they produce histamine and peptides such as chromogranins. this cell type respond to gastrin by releasing histamine which acts as a paracrine stimulator of the release of hydrochloric acid from the gastric parietal cells.

CL:0000505.name: substance p secreting cell
CL:0000505.def: a peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes substance p.

CL:0000506.name: enkephalin secreting cell
CL:0000506.def: an endorphine cell that secretes enkephalin.

CL:0000507.name: endorphin secreting cell
CL:0000507.def: a peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes endorphin.

CL:0000508.name: type g enteroendocrine cell
CL:0000508.def: an endocrine cell found in the pyloric gland mucosa (antral mucosa) of the stomach of mammals and responsible for the secretion of gastrin and enkephalin. most abundant in pyloric antrum, pyramidal in form with a narrow apex bearing long microvilli.

CL:0000509.name: gastrin secreting cell
CL:0000509.def: a peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes gastrin.

CL:0000510.name: paneth cell
CL:0000510.def: an epithelial cell found in the basal part of the intestinal glands (crypts of lieberkuhn) including the appendix. paneth cells synthesize and secrete lysozyme and cryptdins. numerous in the deeper parts of the intestinal crypts, particularly in the duodenum, rich in zinc, contain large acidophilic granules, with irregular apical microvilli and prominent membrane-bound vacuoles containing matrix.

CL:0000511.name: androgen binding protein secreting cell
CL:0000511.def: a peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes androgen binding protein.

CL:0000512.name: paracrine cell
CL:0000512.def: a paracrine cell is a secretory cell that secretes an agonist into intercellular spaces in which it diffuses to a target cell other than that which produced it.

CL:0000513.name: cardiac muscle myoblast
CL:0000513.def: a precursor cell destined to differentiate into cardiac muscle cell.

CL:0000514.name: smooth muscle myoblast
CL:0000514.def: a precursor cell destined to differentiate into smooth muscle myocytes.

CL:0000515.name: skeletal muscle myoblast
CL:0000515.def: a myoblast that differentiates into skeletal muscle fibers.

CL:0000516.name: perineuronal satellite cell
CL:0000516.def: a non-neuronal cell that surrounds the neuronal cell bodies of the ganglia.

CL:0000517.name: macrophage derived foam cell
CL:0000517.def: a type of foam cell derived from a macrophage containing lipids in small vacuoles and typically seen in atherolosclerotic lesions, as well as other conditions.

CL:0000518.name: phagocyte (sensu vertebrata)
CL:0000518.def: a phagocyte in vertebrates that is able to phagocytosis.

CL:0000519.name: phagocyte (sensu nematoda and protostomia)
CL:0000519.def: a phagocyte from organisms in the nematoda or protostomia clades.

CL:0000522.name: obsolete spore
CL:0000522.def: obsolete: the reproductive structure of bacteria, fungi and cryptograms.

CL:0000523.name: mononuclear cytotrophoblast cell
CL:0000523.def: a cell from the inner layer of the trophoblast of the early mammalian embryo that gives rise to the outer surface and villi of the chorion. mononuclear crytoblasts fuse to give rise to a multinuclear cytotrophoblast.

CL:0000524.name: spheroplast
CL:0000524.def: a cell, usually of bacteria or yeast, which has partially lost its cell wall.

CL:0000525.name: syncytiotrophoblast cell
CL:0000525.def: a cell from the outer syncytial layer of the trophoblast of an early mammalian embryo, directly associated with the maternal blood supply. it secretes hcg in order to maintain progesterone secretion and sustain a pregnancy.

CL:0000526.name: afferent neuron
CL:0000526.def: a neuron which conveys sensory information centrally from the periphery.

CL:0000527.name: efferent neuron
CL:0000527.def: a neuron which sends impulses peripherally to activate muscles or secretory cells.

CL:0000528.name: nitrergic neuron
CL:0000528.def: a nerve cell where transmission is mediated by nitric oxide.

CL:0000530.name: primary neuron (sensu teleostei)
CL:0000530.def: a neuron that develops during the early segmentation stages in teleosts, before the neural tube is formed.

CL:0000531.name: primary sensory neuron (sensu teleostei)
CL:0000531.def: a primary neuron (sensu teleostei) that has a sensory function.

CL:0000533.name: primary motor neuron (sensu teleostei)
CL:0000533.def: a primary neuron (sensu teleostei) that has a motor function.

CL:0000534.name: primary interneuron (sensu teleostei)
CL:0000534.def: a primary neuron (sensu teleostei) that is neither a sensory neuron or a motor neuron.

CL:0000535.name: secondary neuron (sensu teleostei)
CL:0000535.def: a neuron of teleosts that develops later than a primary neuron, typically during the larval stages.

CL:0000536.name: secondary motor neuron (sensu teleostei)
CL:0000536.def: a secondary neuron (sensu teleostei) that has a motor function.

CL:0000537.name: obsolete antipodal cell
CL:0000537.def: obsolete. use po:0020093 from plant ontology instead. obsolete, use term from plant ontology. a cell located at the chalazal end of the mature embryo sac in angiosperms.

CL:0000538.name: obsolete epidermal initial
CL:0000538.def: obsolete. use po:0000349 from plant ontology instead. a relatively unspecialized cell that will give rise to specialized cell types of the epidermis.

CL:0000539.name: obsolete idioblast
CL:0000539.def: obsolete: a cell in a tissue that markedly differs in form, size, or contents from other cells in the same tissue.

CL:0000540.name: neuron
CL:0000540.def: the basic cellular unit of nervous tissue. each neuron consists of a body, an axon, and dendrites. their purpose is to receive, conduct, and transmit impulses in the nervous system.

CL:0000541.name: melanoblast
CL:0000541.def: a cell that originates from the neural crest and differentiates into a pigment cell.

CL:0000542.name: lymphocyte
CL:0000542.def: a lymphocyte is a leukocyte commonly found in the blood and lymph that has the characteristics of a large nucleus, a neutral staining cytoplasm, and prominent heterochromatin.

CL:0000543.name: obsolete sieve tube member
CL:0000543.def: obsolete. use po:0000289 from plant ontology instead. one of the series of cellular components of a sieve tube. it shows a more or less pronounced differentiation between sieve plates (wide pores) and lateral sieve areas (narrow pores). also sieve tube element and the obsolete sieve tube segment.

CL:0000545.name: t-helper 1 cell
CL:0000545.def: a cd4-positive, alpha-beta t cell that has the phenotype t-bet-positive, cxcr3-positive, ccr6-negative, and is capable of producing interferon-gamma.

CL:0000546.name: t-helper 2 cell
CL:0000546.def: a cd4-positive, alpha-beta t cell that has the phenotype gata-3-positive, cxcr3-negative, ccr6-negative, and is capable of producing interleukin-4.

CL:0000547.name: proerythroblast
CL:0000547.def: an immature, nucleated erythrocyte occupying the stage of erythropoeisis that follows formation of erythroid progenitor cells. this cell is cd71-positive, has both a nucleus and a nucleolus, and lacks hematopoeitic lineage markers.

CL:0000548.name: animal cell
CL:0000548.def: a native cell that is part of some metazoa.

CL:0000549.name: basophilic erythroblast
CL:0000549.def: a nucleated immature erythrocyte, having cytoplasm generally similar to that of the earlier proerythroblast but sometimes even more basophilic, and usually regular in outline. the nucleus is still relatively large, but the chromatin strands are thicker and more deeply staining, giving a coarser appearance; the nucleoli have disappeared. this cell is cd71-positive and lacks hematopoeitic lineage markers.

CL:0000550.name: polychromatophilic erythroblast
