PATO:0005018.name: mesiodistally compressed
PATO:0005018.def: a quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being compressed from the side facing the midline of the jaw to the side opposite the midline.

PATO:0005019.name: curved lingually
PATO:0005019.def: a curvature quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being curved towards the tongue.

PATO:0005020.name: irregularly shaped
PATO:0005020.def: a shape quality inhering on a bearer by virtue of a bearer's shape lacking in pattern or uniformity; for example, it may have sides of different lengths, different curvatures, or unequal angles.

PATO:0005021.name: unicuspidate
PATO:0005021.def: cuspidate quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's possessing a single cusp.

PATO:0005022.name: uniform diameter
PATO:0005022.def: a diameter that remains constant throughout the extent of an entity.

PATO:0005023.name: parasagittal orientation
PATO:0005023.def: an orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer having a position that is in the parasagittal plane.

PATO:0005024.name: longitudinal orientation
PATO:0005024.def: an orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer having a position that is directed along the longitudinal or anterior-posterior axis.

PATO:0010000.name: maximally connected
PATO:0010000.def: a structural quality inhering in the bearer by virtue of the bearer consisting of a single, maximally connected structure.

PATO:0010001.name: disconnected
PATO:0010001.def: a structural quality inhering in the bearer by virtue of the bearer consisting of multiple structures lacking any physical connection to each other.

PATO:0010002.name: propagation velocity
PATO:0010002.def: the velocity of spatial propagation of a process. examples include the velocity of propagation of an action potential along an axon.

PATO:0010003.name: increased propagation velocity
PATO:0010003.def: a propagation velocity that is higher than normal.

PATO:0010004.name: decreased propagation velocity
PATO:0010004.def: a propagation velocity that is lower than normal.

PATO:0010005.name: spatial distribution of a process
PATO:0010005.def: a physical quality of a process that is its spatial distribution. for example, bone mineralization follows stereotypical spatial distribution patterns during development, which may be altered in some phenotypes.

PATO:0010006.name: cell morphology
PATO:0010006.def: a quality of a single cell inhering in the bearer by virtue of the bearer's size or shape or structure.

PATO:0015001.name: absence due to degeneration
PATO:0015001.def: absence due to a degenerative process.

PATO:0015002.name: process efficacy
PATO:0015002.def: the ability of a process to produce its output.

PATO:0015003.name: decreased efficacy
PATO:0015003.def: a decrease in the ability of a process to produce its output.

PATO:0015004.name: increased efficacy
PATO:0015004.def: a increase in the ability of a process to produce its output.

PATO:0015006.name: polymeric
PATO:0015006.def: a quality inhering in a structure by virtue of it consisting of many of repeated, similar or identical subunits, arranged in some orderly array.

PATO:0015007.name: prominence
PATO:0015007.def: a quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the degree to which the bearers stands out or projects beyond a surface or line.

PATO:0015008.name: distensibility
PATO:0015008.def: a quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the extent to which the bearer is capable of being stretched or swollen.

PATO:0015009.name: humidity
PATO:0015009.def: a quality inhering in air by virtue of the partial pressure exerted by the bearer's water vapour content.

PATO:0015012.name: quality of a plasma
PATO:0015012.def: a physical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's exhibiting the physical characteristics of an entity consisting of roughly equal proportions of positively and negatively charged particles, having neither a defined volume nor defined shape, having internal magnetic fields, and being electrically conductive.

PATO:0015013.name: degree of illumination
PATO:0015013.def: the degree to which the bearer is exposed to visible light.

PATO:0015016.name: stepped
PATO:0015016.def: having a shape or form that resembles a step of a stairway (e.g., a ledge or offset margin).

PATO:0015017.name: quality of a colloid
PATO:0015017.def: a physical quality inhering in an entity by virtue of a portion of the bearer's molecular or polymolecular constituents present in one phase being dispersed in a portion of the bearer's constituents present in another phase.

PATO:0015018.name: quality of an aerosol
PATO:0015018.def: a physical quality inhering in an entity by virtue of the bearer's solid or liquid constituents being suspended in a gas.

PATO:0015019.name: c-shaped
PATO:0015019.def: a concave 3-d shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped in the form of the letter c.

PATO:0015020.name: j-shaped
PATO:0015020.def: a concave 3-d shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped in the form of the letter j.

PATO:0015021.name: combustibility
PATO:0015021.def: the propensity of a material to undergo combustion. combustion encompasses smouldering and flaming combustion. combustibility is usually applied to solids.

PATO:0015026.name: stability
PATO:0015026.def: quality, state, or degree of being stable.

PATO:0015029.name: quality of a suspension
PATO:0015029.def: a physical quality inhering in an entity by virtue of the bearer's solid or liquid constituents being transiently dispersed in a solid, liquid, or gas before settling due to gravity or centrifugal forces.

PATO:0015030.name: plume-shaped
PATO:0015030.def: a shape that ineres in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's mass being distributed in a feather-like fashion.

PATO:0015031.name: contamination
PATO:0015031.def: the presence of a constituent, impurity, or some other undesirable element that spoils, corrupts, infects, makes unfit, or makes inferior a material, physical body, natural environment, place of human occupancy, or other material entity.

PATO:0020000.name: genotypic sex
PATO:0020000.def: a biological sex quality inhering in an individual based upon genotypic composition of sex chromosomes.

PATO:0020001.name: male genotypic sex
PATO:0020001.def: a biological sex quality inhering in an individual based upon genotypic composition that confers the capability for an organism to differentiate male gonads.

PATO:0020002.name: female genotypic sex
PATO:0020002.def: a biological sex quality inhering in an individual or a population based upon genotypic composition that confers the capability for an organism to differentiate female gonads.

PATO:0025000.name: potability
PATO:0025000.def: a physical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's disposition to being fit to be used as a safe means of hydration.

PATO:0025001.name: non-potable
PATO:0025001.def: a physical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer not being suitable for use as a safe means of hydration.

PATO:0025002.name: potable
PATO:0025002.def: a physical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer being suitable for use as a safe means of hydration.

PATO:0030000.name: anteriorized
PATO:0030000.def: a malformed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's gross morphology containing what are normally anterior structures and missing some or all of what are normally posterior structures.

PATO:0030001.name: dorsalized
PATO:0030001.def: a malformed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's gross morphology containing what are normally dorsal structures and missing some or all of what are normally ventral structures.

PATO:0030002.name: posteriorized
PATO:0030002.def: a malformed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's gross morphology containing what are normally posterior structures and missing some or all of what are normally anterior structures.

PATO:0030003.name: ventralized
PATO:0030003.def: a malformed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's gross morphology containing what are normally ventral structures and missing some or all of what are normally dorsal structures.

PATO:0030004.name: partially anteriorized
PATO:0030004.def: an anteriorized quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's gross morphology containing what are normally anterior structures and missing some but not all of what are normally posterior structures.

PATO:0030005.name: partially dorsalized
PATO:0030005.def: a dorsalized quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's gross morphology containing what are normally dorsal structures and missing some but not all of what are normally ventral structures.

PATO:0030006.name: partially posteriorized
PATO:0030006.def: a posteriorized quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's gross morphology containing what are normally posterior structures and missing some but not all of what are normally anterior structures.

PATO:0030007.name: partially ventralized
PATO:0030007.def: a ventralized quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's gross morphology containing what are normally ventral structures and missing some but not all of what are normally dorsal structures.

PATO:0030008.name: dorso-anteriorized
PATO:0030008.def: a malformed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's gross morphology containing what are normally dorso-anterior structures and missing some or all of what are normally ventro-posterior structures.

PATO:0030009.name: partially dorso-anteriorized
PATO:0030009.def: a dorso-anteriorized quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's gross morphology containing what are normally dorso-anterior structures and missing some but not all of what are normally ventro-posterior structures.

PATO:0030010.name: wholly dorso-anteriorized
PATO:0030010.def: a dorso-anteriorized quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's gross morphology containing only what are normally dorso-anterior structures.

PATO:0030011.name: ventro-posteriorized
PATO:0030011.def: a malformed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's gross morphology containing what are normally ventro-posterior structures and missing some or all of what are normally dorso-anterior structures.

PATO:0030012.name: partially ventro-posteriorized
PATO:0030012.def: a ventro-posteriorized quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's gross morphology containing what are normally ventro-posterior structures and missing some but not all of what are normally dorso-anterior structures.

PATO:0030013.name: wholly ventro-posteriorized
PATO:0030013.def: a ventro-posteriorized quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's gross morphology containing only what are normally ventro-posterior structures.

PATO:0040000.name: heterotaxic
PATO:0040000.def: an oriented quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being abnormally placed or arranged.

PATO:0040002.name: position originates from
PATO:0040002.def: a positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of some aspect of that bearer beginning from a position on another entity.

PATO:0040003.name: pathogenicity
PATO:0040003.def: the ability of a pathogen to produce an infectious disease or disorder in an another organism.

PATO:0040004.name: plush
PATO:0040004.def: a texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being covered or partially covered with hair that has increased thickness and softness.

PATO:0040005.name: posteroventral orientation
PATO:0040005.def: an orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer having a position that is directed posteroventrally.

PATO:0040006.name: crown like
PATO:0040006.def: a shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a shape like a crown.

PATO:0040007.name: shell shaped
PATO:0040007.def: a shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a shape like a shell.

PATO:0040008.name: fringed
PATO:0040008.def: a shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having an ornamental border consisting of short straight or twisted threads or strips hanging from cut or raveled edges or from a separate band.

PATO:0040009.name: bowl shaped
PATO:0040009.def: a concave 3-d shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped in the form of a bowl.

PATO:0040010.name: mobile relative to
PATO:0040010.def: mobility relative to a second entity.

PATO:0040011.name: immobile relative to
PATO:0040011.def: immobility relative to a second entity.

PATO:0040012.name: plug shaped
PATO:0040012.def: a shape that is in the form of a plug, being tube-like and expanded on one end.

PATO:0040013.name: dorsomedial orientation
PATO:0040013.def: an orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer having a position that is directed dorsomedially.

PATO:0040014.name: band shaped
PATO:0040014.def: a shape that is in the form of a narrow strip encircling an object.

PATO:0040015.name: trough shaped
PATO:0040015.def: a concave 3-d shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's shape resembling that of a trough, being narrow, long, and boxlike in shape.

PATO:0040016.name: pentagonal
PATO:0040016.def: a shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having five angles and five sides.

PATO:0040017.name: dysplastic growth
PATO:0040017.def: a growth quality of occurrent in which the growth of an organism, structure or group of organisms is abnormal.

PATO:0040019.name: fibrotic
PATO:0040019.def: fibrosis is the formation of excess fibrous connective tissue in an organ or tissue in a reparative or reactive process.

PATO:0040020.name: spayed female
PATO:0040020.def: female quality of being incapable to reproduce because of functional loss of the ovaries and/or uterus from surgical removal.

PATO:0040021.name: unpaired
PATO:0040021.def: the bearer of this quality has_part n=1 of the indicated entity type, where n is bilaterally paired for a comparable organism..

PATO:0040022.name: flared
PATO:0040022.def: a shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer being expanded laterally and or opened outward in shape.

PATO:0040023.name: distomedial orientation
PATO:0040023.def: an orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer having a position that is directed distomedially, ie, pertaining to an inside aspect, but also farther away from the center of the body.

PATO:0040024.name: bilaterally paired
PATO:0040024.def: the bearer of this quality has_part n=2 of the indicated entity type, where n is unpaired for a comparable organism.

PATO:0040025.name: lesioned
PATO:0040025.def: a structural quality which is held by a bearer where a localized pathological or traumatic structural change, damage, deformity, or discontinuity of tissue, organ, or body part is present.

PATO:0040026.name: structurally discontinuous
PATO:0040026.def: a structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being marked by interruptions or gaps.

PATO:0040027.name: doubled haploid
PATO:0040027.def: a ploidy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's haploid cells undergo chromosome doubling.

PATO:0040028.name: parous
PATO:0040028.def: an organismal quality of having successfully reproduced.

PATO:0040029.name: shaded
PATO:0040029.def: a physical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of that bearer being shielded from visible light.

PATO:0040030.name: decreased width and length
PATO:0040030.def: a width and length quality which is relatively small, where both width and length are decreased.

PATO:0040031.name: increased width and length
PATO:0040031.def: a width and length quality that is relatively large, where both width and length are increased.

PATO:0040032.name: increased linear velocity
PATO:0040032.def: a distance traveled in a specific time that is relatively high.

PATO:0040033.name: decreased linear velocity
PATO:0040033.def: a distance traveled in a specific time that is relatively low.

PATO:0040034.name: fractured
PATO:0040034.def: a broken quality where an entity is cracked or broken, usually a bone.

PATO:0040035.name: transversely fractured
PATO:0040035.def: a fractured quality where the fracture traverses the bone perpendicular to the axis of the bone.

PATO:0040036.name: impact-fractured
PATO:0040036.def: a fractured quality in which one of the fragments is driven into another fragment.

PATO:0040037.name: linearly fractured
PATO:0040037.def: a fractured quality where the fracture runs parallel to the long axis of a bone.

PATO:0040038.name: obliquely fractured
PATO:0040038.def: a fractured quality where the fracture occurs at a plane oblique to the long axis of the bone.

PATO:0040039.name: spirally fractured
PATO:0040039.def: a fractured quality that occurs when torque (a rotating force) is applied along the axis of a bone.

PATO:0040040.name: compression-fractured
PATO:0040040.def: a fractured quality that is caused by a loss of bone mass (osteoporosis) that occurs as part of aging.

PATO:0040041.name: avulsion fractured
PATO:0040041.def: a fractured quality in which the fragment of bone tears away from the main mass of bone as a result of physical trauma.

PATO:0040042.name: decreased proportionality to
PATO:0040042.def: a proportionality quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's decreased magnitude in respect to a related entity.

PATO:0040043.name: increased proportionality to
PATO:0040043.def: a proportionality quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's increased magnitude in respect to a related entity.

PATO:0040044.name: ruptured
PATO:0040044.def: a structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's components being torn, typically used for soft tissues or membranes.

PATO:0040045.name: population growth rate
PATO:0040045.def: the rate or speed of the change in in number of a population.

PATO:0040046.name: single organismal growth rate
PATO:0040046.def: the rate or speed of the change in size of an individual entity.

PATO:0040047.name: fragmented
PATO:0040047.def: existing or functioning as though broken into separate parts; disorganized; disunified.

PATO:0040048.name: erythematous
PATO:0040048.def: red due to increase blood circulation in a defined area.

PATO:0040049.name: male with dsd
PATO:0040049.def: a biological sex quality inhering in an individual or a population who are otherwise male of a non-hermaphroditic species who has ambiguous or atypical congenital development of the reproductive system.

PATO:0040050.name: diandrous
PATO:0040050.def: a phenotypic sex quality inhering in a  plant organism or a population of plants in which the flowers have two stamens.

PATO:0040051.name: monandrous
PATO:0040051.def: a phenotypic sex quality inhering in a  plant organism or a population of plants in which the flowers have only one stamen.

PATO:0040052.name: protogynous
PATO:0040052.def: a sequential hermaphroditic quality whereby organisms start out as female and change to male at a later life stage.

PATO:0040053.name: protandrous
PATO:0040053.def: a sequential hermaphroditic quality whereby organisms start out as male and change to female at a later life stage.

PATO:0040054.name: protogynous hermaphroditism
PATO:0040054.def: a protogynous quality whereby organisms start out as female and change to hermaphrodite at a later life stage.

PATO:0040055.name: protandrous hermaphroditism
PATO:0040055.def: a protandrous quality whereby organisms start out as male and change to hermaphrodite at a later life stage.

PATO:0040056.name: female with dsd
PATO:0040056.def: a biological sex quality inhering in an individual or a population who are otherwise female of a non-hermaphroditic species who has ambiguous or atypical congenital development of the reproductive system.

PATO:0040057.name: population process quality
PATO:0040057.def: a quality inhering in a process by virtue of that process having a population or part of a population, where population is defined as a collection of individuals from the same taxonomic class distinguished by one or more characteristics, as participants.

PATO:0040058.name: absence of physical object
PATO:0040058.def: a quality denoting the lack of a physical entity or object, such as a chemical.

PATO:0040059.name: absent process
PATO:0040059.def: a quality denoting the lack of a process or function.

PATO:0040060.name: absence of anatomical entity
PATO:0040060.def: a quality denoting the lack of an anatomical entity or cellular component.

PATO:0040070.name: thermoplastic
PATO:0040070.def: a physical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's disposition to deform by heating.

PATO:0040071.name: nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio
PATO:0040071.def: a quality inhering in a cell by virtue of the ratio between the volume of its nucleus and the volume of its cytoplasm.

PATO:0040072.name: high nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio
PATO:0040072.def: a quality inhering in a cell by virtue of the cell having a high nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio.

PATO:0045076.def: a variability of rate which is relatively normal or average

PATO:0045077.def: a variability of size which is relatively normal or average

PATO:0045078.name: normal variability of temperature
PATO:0045078.def: a variability of temperature which is relatively normal or average

PATO:0045079.name: normal velocity
PATO:0045079.def: a velocity which is relatively normal or average

PATO:0045080.name: normal virulence
PATO:0045080.def: a virulence which is relatively normal or average

PATO:0045081.name: normal viscosity
PATO:0045081.def: a viscosity which is relatively normal or average

PATO:0045082.name: normal waxiness
PATO:0045082.def: a waxiness which is relatively normal or average

PATO:0045083.name: normal wetness
PATO:0045083.def: a wetness which is relatively normal or average

PATO:0045084.name: normal duration
PATO:0045084.def: a duration quality of a process which is relatively normal.

PATO:0045085.name: normal duration of temperature
PATO:0045085.def: a duration quality of temperature quality of a process which is relatively normal.

PATO:0045086.name: normal occurrence
PATO:0045086.def: an occurrence which is relatively normal.

PATO:0045087.name: normal frequency
PATO:0045087.def: a frequency which is relatively normal.

PATO:0045088.name: normal sensitivity of a process
PATO:0045088.def: a sensitivity of a process which is relatively normal.

PATO:0045089.name: normal sensitivity of a process to oxygen
PATO:0045089.def: a sensitivity of occurrent to oxygen which is relatively normal.

PATO:0045090.name: cardinal direction
PATO:0045090.def: the four cardinal directions or cardinal points are the directions north, east, south, and west, commonly denoted by their initials, n, e, s, w. east and west are at right angles to north and south, with east being in the clockwise direction of rotation from north and west being directly opposite east.

PATO:0045091.name: north
PATO:0045091.def: north is one of the four compass points or cardinal directions. it is the opposite of south and is perpendicular to east and west.

PATO:0045092.name: east
PATO:0045092.def: east is one of the four cardinal directions or points of the compass. it is the opposite direction from west.

PATO:0045093.name: south
PATO:0045093.def: south is one of the four cardinal directions or compass points. south is the polar opposite of north and is perpendicular to east and west.

PATO:0045094.name: west
PATO:0045094.def: west is one of the four cardinal directions or points of the compass. it is the opposite direction from east.

PATO:0050000.name: rate of occurence
PATO:0050000.def: the number of repeated events per unit time, occurring in a repeating series. (e.g. the number of heart beats occurring over 1 minute)

PATO:0050001.name: rate of continuous process
PATO:0050001.def: the rate of output of a continuous process. example include: growth rate, cell migration rate, enzyme reaction rate.

PATO:0055001.name: decreased spatial extent of a process
PATO:0055001.def: a spatial distribution of a process in which the process occupies a smaller length, area, or volume than the reference process. for example, heterochromatin may form over a shorter length of a chromosome in a mutant than in wild type.

PATO:0055002.name: increased spatial extent of a process
PATO:0055002.def: a spatial distribution of a process in which the process occupies a greater length, area, or volume than the reference process. for example, heterochromatin may form over a shorter length of a chromosome in a mutant than in wild type.

PATO:0055003.name: increased rate of occurrence
PATO:0055003.def: a rate of occurrence that is relatively high.

PATO:0055004.name: decreased rate of occurrence
PATO:0055004.def: a rate of occurrence that is relatively low.

PATO:0055005.name: increased rate of continuous process
PATO:0055005.def: a rate of output of a continuous process that is relatively high.

PATO:0055006.name: decreased rate of continuous process
PATO:0055006.def: a rate of output of a continuous process that is relatively low.

PATO:0060001.name: sex-specific
PATO:0060001.def: a quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being present in one sex and absent from the other in members of the same species.

PATO:0060002.name: male-specific
PATO:0060002.def: a quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being present in males and absent from females in members of the same species.

PATO:0060003.name: female-specific
PATO:0060003.def: a quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being present in females and absent from males in members of the same species.

PATO:0065001.name: lysed
PATO:0065001.def: the breakdown, disintegration, destruction of an entity due to the breaking of cell membranes by any means.

PATO:0065002.name: patchy pigmentation
PATO:0065002.def: a degree of pigmentation quality that is diversified with patches, or irregularity.

PATO:0070000.name: sequential hermaphrodite
PATO:0070000.def: a hermaphroditic quality that inheres in a population or organism where an organism changes is a different sexes during different life stages.

PATO:0070001.name: neurogliaform morphology
PATO:0070001.def: a cell morphology that inheres in neurons which have a small round soma, a large number of short, smooth, or slightly beaded primary dendrites that give rise to only a few secondary branches, and a branched axon that establishes a dense axonal mesh with thin shafts.

PATO:0070002.name: basket cell morphology
PATO:0070002.def: a cell morphology that inheres in multipolar neurons with densely branched terminal axonal arborizations that form basket-like structures surrounding and synapsing to the somas of target cells.

PATO:0070003.name: small basket cell morphology
PATO:0070003.def: a basket cell morphology that inheres in neurons with axonal arbors composed of frequent, short, curvy axonal branches that tend to be near their somata and within the same layer.

PATO:0070004.name: large basket cell morphology
PATO:0070004.def: a basket cell morphology that inheres in neurons that are large, and typically ascend to give rise to many long horizontally and vertically projecting axon collaterals that traverse neighboring columns and can extend through all cortical layers.

PATO:0070005.name: nest basket cell morphology
PATO:0070005.def: a basket cell morphology that inheres in neurons which have simpler dendritic arbors (compared to small or large basket cell morphology), and an axonal plexus of intermediate density, composed of a few long, smooth axonal branches.

PATO:0070006.name: cortical bipolar morphology
PATO:0070006.def: a cell morphology that inheres in neurons which have two principal dendrites that emerge from the soma and begin to branch some distance from it, have few spines, and branch in narrow fields. this is in contrast to bitufted morphology where branching occurs close to the soma.

PATO:0070007.name: martinotti morphology
PATO:0070007.def: a cell morphology that inheres in neurons which are large and non-spiny, with dendrites radiating in a multipolar or bitufted pattern, often favouring the descending side, and axons that ascend directly from the superficial side of the soma, and travel upward without branching.

PATO:0070008.name: t martinotti morphology
PATO:0070008.def: a martinotti cell morphology that inheres in neurons which have axons that form a horizontal ramification, making it t-shaped.

PATO:0070009.name: fan martinotti morphology
PATO:0070009.def: a martinotti cell morphology that inheres in neurons which have axons that form a fan-like plexus.

PATO:0070010.name: stellate morphology
PATO:0070010.def: a cell morphology that inheres in neurons that have dendritic processes radiating from the cell body forming a star-like shape.

PATO:0070011.name: chandelier cell morphology
PATO:0070011.def: a cell morphology that inheres in neurons which are small and round, and make highly specialized synapses with the axon initial segments of pyramidal neurons, wrapping them with candle-shaped synaptic 'cartridges'.

PATO:0070012.name: bitufted cell morphology
PATO:0070012.def: a cell morphology that inheres in neurons which have two clusters of primary dendrites that originate directly and extend from opposite ends of the soma, and axons that form a plexus which spreads widely. compared to the narrow vertical axonal projection of bipolar morphology, and the 'horse-tail' axonal cluster of double boquet cells, bitufted morphology has wide horizontal axonal spans, and branching that occur close to the soma. their vertical projection is also less extensive and crosses mostly to neighboring layers.

PATO:0070013.name: spiny stellate cell morphology
PATO:0070013.def: a cell morphology that inheres in neurons which have spiny basal dendrites and resemble pyramidal cells but lose their apical dendrites as they mature. their axons nearly always emerge from the descending side of the soma, but often recurve and ascend with arc-like collaterals.

PATO:0070015.name: pyramidal family morphology
PATO:0070015.def: a cell morphology that inheres in neurons which have a pyramidal shaped soma, a single axon, a large apical dendrite and multiple basal dendrites.

PATO:0070016.name: horizontal pyramidal morphology
PATO:0070016.def: a pyramidal family morphology that inheres in neurons which have an apical tree which is oriented parallel to the pia.

PATO:0070017.name: standard pyramidal morphology
PATO:0070017.def: a pyramidal family morphology that inheres in neurons which have a standard pyramidal shape with its apical dendrite aligned vertically.

PATO:0070018.name: tufted pyramidal morphology
PATO:0070018.def: a pyramidal cell morphology that inheres in neurons which have a distinct tuft formation, distal from the soma.

PATO:0070019.name: untufted pyramidal morphology
PATO:0070019.def: a pyramidal cell morphology that inheres in neurons which lack a clear tuft formation but extend to large radial distances.

PATO:0070020.name: stellate pyramidal morphology
PATO:0070020.def: a pyramidal cell morphology that inheres in neurons which lack a tuft formation but extend to small radial distances forming a star-like shape.

PATO:0070021.name: inverted pyramidal morphology
PATO:0070021.def: a pyramidal cell morphology that inheres in neurons which have an apical tree which is oriented towards the white matter.

PATO:0070025.name: unipolar neuron morphology
PATO:0070025.def: a cell morphology that inheres in neurons with only one process, a neurite, that extends from the cell body. the neurite then branches to form dendritic and axonal processes.

PATO:0070026.name: multipolar neuron morphology
PATO:0070026.def: a cell morphology that inheres in neurons which possess three or more neurites, usually a single axon and many dendrites and dendritic branches.

PATO:0070027.name: bitufted dendrite cell morphology
PATO:0070027.def: a cell morphology that inheres in neurons with dendrites that are bidirectional, emerging from opposite ends of the soma, with the two arbors extending in radial or tangential directions.

PATO:0070028.name: extratelencephalic projecting
PATO:0070028.def: a neuron projection quality that is a characteristic of neurons whose soma is located in the telencephalon and that project to structures outside the telencephalon

PATO:0070029.name: corticothalamic projecting
PATO:0070029.def: a neuron projection quality that is a characteristic of neurons with soma in the cerebral cortex and projections to the thalamus.

PATO:0070030.name: near projecting
PATO:0070030.def: a neuron projection quality that is a characteristic of neurons with projections that terminate locally rather than distantly.

PATO:0070031.name: corticomedulla projecting
PATO:0070031.def: a neuron projection quality that is a characteristic of neurons that project to the medulla oblongata from other brain regions.

PATO:0070033.name: neuron projection quality
PATO:0070033.def: a physical quality inhering in a neuron by virtue of the relative location of its soma and the regions to which it projects and makes synaptic contacts in.

PATO:0070034.name: intratelencephalic projecting
PATO:0070034.def: a neuron projection quality that is a characteristic of neurons with both soma and projections entirely within the telencephalon.

PATO:0070036.name: dendrite quality
PATO:0070036.def: a quality inhering in a neuron's dendrites by virtue of the bearer's physical composition.

PATO:0070038.name: spiny dendrite quality
PATO:0070038.def: a dendrite quality inhering in a neuron by virtue of the bearer's dendrite having spines.

PATO:0070039.name: tufted dendrite quality
PATO:0070039.def: a dendrite quality inhering in a neuron by virtue of the bearer's dendrite having a terminal tuft.

PATO:0070040.name: aspiny dendrite quality
PATO:0070040.def: a dendrite quality inhering in a neuron by virtue of the bearer's dendrite having few or no recognizable dendritic spines.

PATO:0070041.name: varicose dendrite quality
PATO:0070041.def: a dendrite quality inhering in a neuron by virtue of the bearer's dendrite having numerous swellings or varicosities along their length.

PATO:0070042.name: retinal bipolar morphology
PATO:0070042.def: a cell morphology that inheres in retinal neurons which have two principal fibres, an axon and a dendrite, that emerge from opposite end the soma.

PATO:0070044.name: anatomical structure quality
PATO:0070044.def: a quality of continuant that exist at the anatomical level of organisation and anything under it. this includes, but is not limited to, cells , tissues, and components.

PATO:0070045.name: anatomical histological quality
PATO:0070045.def: a quality inhering in an anotomical structure by virtue of its capacity to be stained by specific histological dyes.

PATO:0070046.name: neutrophillic
PATO:0070046.def: an affinity inhering in an anatomical structure by virtue of the bearer exhibiting a molecular interaction that stains and colors, pale-pink, with wright-giemsa stain.

PATO:0070047.name: polychromatophilic
PATO:0070047.def: an affinity inhering in an anatomical structure by virtue of the bearer exhibiting a molecular interaction for both basic and acid stains under specific ph conditions.

PATO:0070059.name: rusty
PATO:0070059.def: a texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being covered by iron oxide as a result of oxidation.

PATO:0070060.name: quality of interaction of a substance with electromagnetic radiation
PATO:0070060.def: a quality of a substance on which or through which electromagnetic radiation impinges or traverses with respect to radiation. this substance quality changes the quality of the incident radiation with respect to any of: intensity, direction, scatter and wavelength.

PATO:0070061.name: double bouquet morphology
PATO:0070061.def: a cell morphology that inheres in neurons with bitufted dendritic morphology but with the special feature of a tight fascicular axonal cylinder that resembles a 'horse tail'.

PATO:0070062.name: bistratified dendrite cell morphology
PATO:0070062.def: a cell morphology that inheres in neurons with dendrites that stratify at two and only two locations.

PATO:0070063.name: monostratified dendrite cell morphology
PATO:0070063.def: a cell morphology that inheres in neurons with dendrites that stratify at one and only one location.

PATO:0070064.name: dendritic field size
PATO:0070064.def: a 3-d extent quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the spatial region that is defined by the maximal span of the bearer's dendritic arbor.

PATO:0080001.name: quality of a fluid
PATO:0080001.def: a physical quality inhering in an entity exhibiting the physical charachteristics of a material that flows under applied force.

PATO:0085001.name: salinity
PATO:0085001.def: an osmolarity quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the total amount of ionic salts dissolved in the bearer.

PATO:0095001.name: organismal area to mass ratio
PATO:0095001.def: quotient (or ratio) of surface area of an organism divided by the mass of the same organism

PATO:0095002.name: cursorial
PATO:0095002.def: an organismal quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's morphological and physiological adaptation for running.

PATO:0095003.name: fossorial
PATO:0095003.def: an organismal quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's morphological and physiological adaptation for digging and living underground.

PATO:0095004.name: arboreal
PATO:0095004.def: an organismal quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's morphological and physiological adaptation for living in trees.

PATO:0095005.name: crepuscular
PATO:0095005.def: a quality of a process that happens during dawn and dusk.

PATO:0095006.name: nocturnal
PATO:0095006.def: a quality of a process that happens during the hours of darkness.

PATO:0095007.name: diurnal
PATO:0095007.def: a quality of a process that happens during the hours of daylight.

PATO:0095008.name: migratory
PATO:0095008.def: an organismal quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's morphological and physiological adaptation for participating in long-distance movement of conspecifics, usually on a seasonal basis.

PATO:0095009.name: anecic
PATO:0095009.def: an organismal quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's ability to burrow more than 20 cm deep into the soil and make permanent, vertical burrows.

UBERON:0000000.name: processual entity
UBERON:0000000.def: an occurrent [span:occurrent] that exists in time by occurring or happening, has temporal parts and always involves and depends on some entity.

UBERON:0000002.name: uterine cervix
UBERON:0000002.def: lower, narrow portion of the uterus where it joins with the top end of the vagina.

UBERON:0000003.name: naris
UBERON:0000003.def: orifice of the olfactory system. the naris is the route by which odorants enter the olfactory system[mah].

UBERON:0000004.name: nose
UBERON:0000004.def: the olfactory organ of vertebrates, consisting of nares, olfactory epithelia and the structures and skeletal framework of the nasal cavity.

UBERON:0000006.name: islet of langerhans
UBERON:0000006.def: the clusters of hormone-producing cells that are scattered throughout the pancreas.

UBERON:0000007.name: pituitary gland
UBERON:0000007.def: the pituitary gland is an endocrine gland that secretes hormones that regulate many other glands [go]. an endocrine gland located ventral to the diencephalon and derived from mixed neuroectodermal and non neuroectodermal origin [zfin].

UBERON:0000009.name: submucosa
UBERON:0000009.def: a layer of dense irregular connective tissue that lines organs and supports the mucosa, as well as joins the mucosa to the bulk of underlying smooth muscle. [wp,unvetted].

UBERON:0000010.name: peripheral nervous system
UBERON:0000010.def: a major division of the nervous system that contains nerves which connect the central nervous system (cns) with sensory organs, other organs, muscles, blood vessels and glands.

UBERON:0000011.name: parasympathetic nervous system
UBERON:0000011.def: the parasympathetic nervous system is one of the two divisions of the vertebrate autonomic nervous system. parasympathetic nerves emerge cranially as pre ganglionic fibers from oculomotor, facial, glossopharyngeal and vagus and from the sacral region of the spinal cord. most neurons are cholinergic and responses are mediated by muscarinic receptors. the parasympathetic system innervates, for example: salivary glands, thoracic and abdominal viscera, bladder and genitalia[go].

UBERON:0000012.name: somatic nervous system
UBERON:0000012.def: part of peripheral nervous system that includes the somatic parts of the cranial and spinal nerves and their ganglia and the peripheral sensory receptors.

UBERON:0000013.name: sympathetic nervous system
UBERON:0000013.def: the sympathetic nervous system is one of the two divisions of the vertebrate autonomic nervous system (the other being the parasympathetic nervous system). the sympathetic preganglionic neurons have their cell bodies in the thoracic and lumbar regions of the spinal cord and connect to the paravertebral chain of sympathetic ganglia. innervate heart and blood vessels, sweat glands, viscera and the adrenal medulla. most sympathetic neurons, but not all, use noradrenaline as a post-ganglionic neurotransmitter [go].
UBERON:0000013.synonym: sympathetic part of autonomic division of nervous system

UBERON:0000014.name: zone of skin
UBERON:0000014.def: any portion of the organ that covers that body and consists of a layer of epidermis and a layer of dermis.

UBERON:0000015.name: non-material anatomical boundary
UBERON:0000015.def: a non-material anatomical entity of two dimensions. anatomical boundaries are contiguous structures.

UBERON:0000016.name: endocrine pancreas
UBERON:0000016.def: the part of the pancreas that is part of the endocrine system and is made up of islet cells, which produce insulin, glucagon and somatostatin.

UBERON:0000017.name: exocrine pancreas
UBERON:0000017.def: the part of the pancreas that is part of the exocrine system and which produces and store zymogens of digestive enzymes, such as chymotrypsinogen and trypsinogen in the acinar cells [go].

UBERON:0000018.name: compound eye
UBERON:0000018.def: a light sensing organ composed of ommatidia.

UBERON:0000019.name: camera-type eye
UBERON:0000019.def: an organ of sight that includes the camera-type eyeball and supporting structures such as the lacrimal apparatus, the conjunctiva, the eyelid.

UBERON:0000020.name: sense organ
UBERON:0000020.def: an organ that is capable of transducing sensory stimulus to the nervous system.

UBERON:0000021.name: cutaneous appendage
UBERON:0000021.def: anatomical projection that protrudes from the skin. examples: hair, nail, feather, claw, hoof, horn, wattle, spur, beak, antler, bristle and some scales.

UBERON:0000022.name: feather
UBERON:0000022.def: one of the epidermal growths that form the distinctive outer covering, or plumage, on birds. feathers are formed in tiny follicles in the epidermis, or outer skin layer, that produce keratin proteins.

UBERON:0000023.name: wing
UBERON:0000023.def: appendage that is shaped in order to produce lift for flight through the air.

UBERON:0000024.name: forelimb wing
UBERON:0000024.def: forelimb that is used to produce lift for flight through the air.

UBERON:0000025.name: tube
UBERON:0000025.def: any hollow cylindrical anatomical structure containing a lumen through which substances are transported.

UBERON:0000026.name: appendage
UBERON:0000026.def: major subdivision of an organism that protrudes from the body[dos, caro].

UBERON:0000029.name: lymph node
UBERON:0000029.def: any of the rounded masses of lymphoid tissue that are surrounded by a capsule of connective tissue, are distributed along the lymphatic vessels, and contain numerous lymphocytes which filter the flow of lymph.

UBERON:0000030.name: lamina propria
UBERON:0000030.def: a thin layer of loose connective tissue which lies beneath the epithelium and together with the epithelium constitutes the mucosa[wp]. the lamina propria contains capillaries and a central lacteal (lymph vessel) in the small intestine, as well as lymphoid tissue. lamina propria also contains glands with the ducts opening on to the mucosal epithelium, that secrete mucus and serous secretions.

UBERON:0000031.name: lamina propria of trachea
UBERON:0000031.def: a lamina propria that is part of a respiratory airway.

UBERON:0000033.name: head
UBERON:0000033.def: the head is the anterior-most division of the body [go].

UBERON:0000035.name: primary ovarian follicle
UBERON:0000035.def: an ovarian follicle that has one layer of granulosa cells.

UBERON:0000036.name: secondary ovarian follicle
UBERON:0000036.def: a maturing ovarian follicle that has two more more layers of granulosa cells, up to the onset of antrum formation.

UBERON:0000037.name: tertiary ovarian follicle
UBERON:0000037.def: a follicle that has reached the most mature stage of folliculogenesis, characterized by the presence of the antrum.

UBERON:0000038.name: follicular fluid
UBERON:0000038.def: the fluid surrounding the ovum and granulosa cells in the ovarian follicle.

UBERON:0000039.name: follicular antrum
UBERON:0000039.def: region of ovarian follicle filled with follicular fluid.

UBERON:0000040.name: leydig's organ
UBERON:0000040.def: a hemopoietic organ found in elasmobranchs. along with the spleen and special tissue around the gonads, this structure produces red blood cells and it is nestled along the top and bottom of the esophagus.

UBERON:0000041.name: odontode scale
UBERON:0000041.def: multi-tissue structure composed of enameloid, dentine surrounding a pulp cavity, and bone of attachment anchoring the element into the dermis[vsao].

UBERON:0000042.name: serous membrane
UBERON:0000042.def: multi-tissue structure that is comprised of a secretory epithelial layer (mesothelium) and a connective tissue layer.

UBERON:0000043.name: tendon
UBERON:0000043.def: dense regular connective tissue that connects muscle to bone[vsao].

UBERON:0000044.name: dorsal root ganglion
UBERON:0000044.def: sensory ganglia located on the dorsal spinal roots within the vertebral column. the spinal ganglion cells are pseudounipolar. the single primary branch bifurcates sending a peripheral process to carry sensory information from the periphery and a central branch which relays that information to the spinal cord or brain. (msh) * ganglion found on the posterior root of each spinal nerve, composed of the unipolar nerve cell bodies of the sensory neurons of the nerve. (csp).
UBERON:0000044.synonym: spinal ganglion part of peripheral nervous system

UBERON:0000045.name: ganglion
UBERON:0000045.def: a biological tissue mass, most commonly a mass of nerve cell bodies.

UBERON:0000046.name: stemma
UBERON:0000046.def: eye-spots which may be set into a pit to reduce the angles of light that enters and affects the eyespot, to allow the organism to deduce the angle of incoming light.

UBERON:0000047.name: simple eye
UBERON:0000047.def: an eye with one concave chamber. note that 'simple' does not imply a reduced level of complexity or acuity.

UBERON:0000048.name: pinhole eye
UBERON:0000048.def: simple eye that has a small aperture (which may be adjustable) and deep pit. it is only found in the nautiloids.

UBERON:0000049.name: spherical lensed eye
UBERON:0000049.def: simple eye that consists of a lens of one refractive index.

UBERON:0000050.name: simple eye with multiple lenses
UBERON:0000050.def: simple eye that has two or more lenses. some marine organisms bear more than one lens; for instance the copeopod pontella has three. the outer has a parabolic surface, countering the effects of spherical aberration while allowing a sharp image to be formed. copilla's eyes have two lenses, which move in and out like a telescope.

UBERON:0000051.name: fornix of vagina
UBERON:0000051.def: the deepest portions of the vagina, extending into the recesses created by the vaginal portion of cervix[wp,unvetted].

UBERON:0000052.name: fornix of brain
UBERON:0000052.def: a c-shaped bundle of fibres (axons) in the brain, and carries signals from the hippocampus to the mammillary bodies and septal nuclei. it is typically divided into the columns (crus), body, commissure and the pre-commissural and post-commissural fornix (mm).

UBERON:0000053.name: macula lutea
UBERON:0000053.def: an oval area in the retina, usually located temporal to the posterior pole of the eye and slightly below the level of the optic disk. it is characterized by the presence of a yellow pigment diffusely permeating the inner layers, contains the fovea centralis in its center, and provides the best phototopic visual acuity. it is devoid of retinal blood vessels, except in its periphery, and receives nourishment from the choriocapillaris of the choroid. (from cline et al., dictionary of visual science, 4th ed).

UBERON:0000054.name: macula
UBERON:0000054.def: thickened areas of the saccule or utricle where the termination of the vestibular nerve occurs[mesh,modified].

UBERON:0000055.name: vessel
UBERON:0000055.def: a tubular structure that contains, conveys body fluid, such as blood or lymph.

UBERON:0000056.name: ureter
UBERON:0000056.def: muscular duct that propels urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder, or related organs.

UBERON:0000057.name: urethra
UBERON:0000057.def: the fibromuscular tubular canal through which urine is discharged from the bladder to the exterior via the external urinary meatus; in males, the urethra is joined by the ejaculatory ducts and serves as a passageway for semen during ejaculation, as well as a canal for urine during voiding; in females, the urethra is shorter and emerges above the vaginal opening.

UBERON:0000058.name: duct
UBERON:0000058.def: a tubular structure that transports secreted or excreted substances.

UBERON:0000059.name: large intestine
UBERON:0000059.def: a subdivision of the digestive tract that connects the small intestine to the cloaca or anus. lacks or has few villi[kardong].

UBERON:0000060.name: anatomical wall
UBERON:0000060.def: organ component adjacent to an organ cavity and which consists of a maximal aggregate of organ component layers.

UBERON:0000061.name: anatomical structure
UBERON:0000061.def: material anatomical entity that is a single connected structure with inherent 3d shape generated by coordinated expression of the organism's own genome.

UBERON:0000062.name: organ
UBERON:0000062.def: anatomical structure that performs a specific function or group of functions [wp].

UBERON:0000063.name: organ subunit
UBERON:0000063.def: a part of an organ that constitutes a distinct modular sub-unit. in some cases, the organ may also contain other sub-units of identical or similar types, in other cases this may be a distinct entity.

UBERON:0000064.name: organ part
UBERON:0000064.def: a multicellular structure that is a part of an organ.

UBERON:0000065.name: respiratory tract
UBERON:0000065.def: anatomical structure that is part of the respiratory system. in mammals consists of upper and lower tracts.

UBERON:0000066.name: fully formed stage
UBERON:0000066.def: the stage of development at which the animal is fully formed, including immaturity and maturity. includes both sexually immature stage, and adult stage.

UBERON:0000067.name: obsolete embryo stage part
UBERON:0000067.def: a stage that is part of the embryo stage.

UBERON:0000068.name: embryo stage
UBERON:0000068.def: a life cycle stage that starts with fertilization and ends with the fully formed embryo.

UBERON:0000069.name: larval stage
UBERON:0000069.def: a distinct juvenile stage many animals undergo before metamorphosis into adults. animals with indirect development such as insects, amphibians, or cnidarians typically have a larval phase of their life cycle.

UBERON:0000070.name: pupal stage
UBERON:0000070.def: a life cycle stage of holometabolous insects in which the organism is a pupa and starts with the larval-pupal apolysis and ends with pupal-adult apolysis.

UBERON:0000071.name: death stage
UBERON:0000071.def: end of the life of an organism.

UBERON:0000072.name: proximo-distal subdivision of respiratory tract
UBERON:0000072.def: an section of a respiratory tract.

UBERON:0000073.name: regional part of nervous system
UBERON:0000073.def: any part or collection of parts of the central or peripheral nervous system. parts may span both cns and pns.

UBERON:0000074.name: renal glomerulus
UBERON:0000074.def: a capillary tuft which forms a close network with the visceral epithelium (podocytes) and the mesangium to form the filtration barrier and is surrounded by bowman's capsule in nephrons of the vertebrate kidney[go].

UBERON:0000075.name: subdivision of skeletal system
UBERON:0000075.def: anatomical cluster consisting of the skeletal elements and articular elements that are part of an individual subdivision of the organism.

UBERON:0000076.name: external ectoderm
UBERON:0000076.def: the surface (external) layer of ectoderm which begins to proliferate shortly after separation from the neuroectoderm.

UBERON:0000077.name: mixed endoderm/mesoderm-derived structure
UBERON:0000077.def: an anatomical structure that develops from the endoderm and the mesoderm.

UBERON:0000078.name: mixed ectoderm/mesoderm/endoderm-derived structure
UBERON:0000078.def: an anatomical structure that develops from the ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm.

UBERON:0000079.name: male reproductive system
UBERON:0000079.def: the organs associated with producing offspring in the gender that produces spermatozoa.

UBERON:0000080.name: mesonephros
UBERON:0000080.def: the second stage of the kidney. it serves as the main excretory organ of aquatic vertebrates and as a temporary embryonic kidney in higher vertebrates. it is composed of the mesonephric duct (also called the wolffian duct), mesonephric tubules, and associated capillary tufts. a single tubule and its associated capillary tuft is called a mesonephric excretory unit; these units are similar in structure and function to nephrons of the adult kidney. the mesonephros is derived from intermediate mesoderm in the vertebrate embryo.

UBERON:0000081.name: metanephros
UBERON:0000081.def: in mammals, the metanephros is the excretory organ of the fetus, which develops into the mature kidney and is formed from the rear portion of the nephrogenic cord. the metanephros is an endocrine and metabolic organ that filters the blood and excretes the end products of body metabolism in the form of urine[go].

UBERON:0000082.name: adult mammalian kidney
UBERON:0000082.def: a kidney at the most advanced stage of development in a mammal.

UBERON:0000083.name: mesonephric tubule
UBERON:0000083.def: a mesonephric tubule is an epithelial tube that is part of the mesonephros[go]. genital ridge that is next to the mesonephros[wp].

UBERON:0000084.name: ureteric bud
UBERON:0000084.def: an epithelial swelling on the wolffian duct that elongates to invade the adjacent metanephric mesenchyme[mp].

UBERON:0000085.name: morula
UBERON:0000085.def: a spherical embryonic mass of blastomeres formed before the blastula and resulting from cleavage of the fertilized ovum.

UBERON:0000086.name: zona pellucida
UBERON:0000086.def: a glycoprotein membrane surrounding the plasma membrane of an oocyte. it is a vital constitutive part of the latter, external but not extraneous to it. the zona pellucida first appears in multilaminar primary oocytes.

UBERON:0000087.name: inner cell mass
UBERON:0000087.def: a mass of cells that develop into the body of the embryo and some extraembryonic tissues.

UBERON:0000088.name: trophoblast
UBERON:0000088.def: the mesectodermal cell layer arising from the trophectoderm that erodes the uterine mucosa and contributes to the formation of the placenta.

UBERON:0000090.name: blastocele
UBERON:0000090.def: fluid-filled central region of a blastocyst.

UBERON:0000091.name: bilaminar disc
UBERON:0000091.def: a flattened, almost circular bilaminar plate of cells formed when the inner cell mass (aka embryoblast) forms two epithelial layers, each of a distinct lineage, separated by an extracellular basement membrane: the external (dorsal) layer is called the epiblast and the internal (ventral) layer is called the hypoblast (aka primitive endoderm); together, they compose the bilaminar embryonic disc.

UBERON:0000092.name: post-embryonic stage
UBERON:0000092.def: stage succeeding embryo, including mature structure.

UBERON:0000093.name: sulcus
UBERON:0000093.def: a depression or fissure in the surface of an organ.

UBERON:0000094.name: membrane organ
UBERON:0000094.def: nonparenchymatous organ that primarily consists of dense connective tissue organized into a sheet which interconnects two or more organs, separates two or more body spaces from one another, or surrounds an organ or body part. examples: interosseous membrane of forearm, obturator membrane, tympanic membrane, fibrous pericardium, fascia lata, dura mater. [fma].

UBERON:0000095.name: cardiac neural crest
UBERON:0000095.def: portion of neural crest that develops from the dorsal neural tube. it overlaps the vagal neural crest and migrates to populate the pharyngeal arches 3, 4 and 6 (producing structures in the head) and to the heart, forming connective tissue that separates the great vessels of the heart. [wikipedia].

UBERON:0000100.name: blastopore
UBERON:0000100.def: the orifice of invagination of the endomesodermal cells during the embryonic stages of an organism.

UBERON:0000101.name: lobe of lung
UBERON:0000101.def: a lung lobe is one of the rounded projections that compose the lung[go].

UBERON:0000102.name: lung vasculature
UBERON:0000102.def: the lung vasculature is composed of the tubule structures that carry blood or lymph in the lungs[go].

UBERON:0000103.name: obsolete life cycle stage boundary
UBERON:0000103.def: instant starting or ending a life cycle stage. these can be arbitrary/fiat.

UBERON:0000104.name: life cycle
UBERON:0000104.def: an entire span of an organism's life. in metazoans, commences with the zygote stage and ends with the death of the organism.

UBERON:0000105.name: life cycle stage
UBERON:0000105.def: a spatiotemporal region encompassing some part of the life cycle of an organism.

UBERON:0000106.name: zygote stage
UBERON:0000106.def: a stage at which the organism is a single cell produced by means of sexual reproduction.

UBERON:0000107.name: cleavage stage
UBERON:0000107.def: the first few specialized divisions of an activated animal egg; stage consisting of division of cells in the early embryo. the zygotes of many species undergo rapid cell cycles with no significant growth, producing a cluster of cells the same size as the original zygote. the different cells derived from cleavage are called blastomeres and form a compact mass called the morula. cleavage ends with the formation of the blastula.

UBERON:0000108.name: blastula stage
UBERON:0000108.def: an early stage of embryonic development in animals. it is produced by cleavage of a fertilized ovum and consists of a spherical layer of around 128 cells surrounding a central fluid-filled cavity called the blastocoel. the blastula follows the morula and precedes the gastrula in the developmental sequence.

UBERON:0000109.name: gastrula stage
UBERON:0000109.def: a stage defined by complex and coordinated series of cellular movements that occurs at the end of cleavage during embryonic development of most animals. the details of gastrulation vary from species to species, but usually result in the formation of the three primary germ layers, ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm.

UBERON:0000110.name: neurula stage
UBERON:0000110.def: staged defined by the formation of a tube from the flat layer of ectodermal cells known as the neural plate. this will give rise to the central nervous system.

UBERON:0000111.name: organogenesis stage
UBERON:0000111.def: a stage at which the ectoderm, endoderm, and mesoderm develop into the internal organs of the organism.

UBERON:0000113.name: post-juvenile adult stage
UBERON:0000113.def: the stage of being a sexually mature adult animal.

UBERON:0000114.name: lung connective tissue
UBERON:0000114.def: the connective tissue located between the respiratory (airway and alveolar) epithelium, the capillary endothelium and pleural mesothelium; it contains basement membrane composed of collagen, elastin, proteoglycans, and fibronectin.

UBERON:0000115.name: lung epithelium
UBERON:0000115.def: the epithelial layer of the lung.

UBERON:0000116.name: lung saccule
UBERON:0000116.def: primitive gas exchange portion of the lung composed of type i and type ii cells[go].

UBERON:0000117.name: respiratory tube
UBERON:0000117.def: a tube in the respiratory system. examples: bronchus, bronchiole, trachea.

UBERON:0000118.name: lung bud
UBERON:0000118.def: structure derived from foregut that becomes a lung[go].

UBERON:0000119.name: cell layer
UBERON:0000119.def: portion of tissue, that consists of single layer of cells connected to each other by cell junctions. examples: layer of glial cells; epithelium.

UBERON:0000120.name: blood brain barrier
UBERON:0000120.def: cell layer consisting of lining cells that separates the central nervous system and the bloodstream. the bbb may consist of endothelial cells or glial cells. an endothelial barrier may have arisen independently several times during evolution. in bichir and lungfish the barrier is formed by brain endothelial cells, while in sturgeon it is formed by a complex perivascular glial sheath, but with no detectable tight junctions.

UBERON:0000121.name: perineurium
UBERON:0000121.def: a layer of thin, concentrically arranged cells with interspersed collagen that lies within the epineurium. the perineurium is a component of the blood–nerve barrier and is essential for protecting axons and their associated schwann cells from ionic flux, toxins and infection.

UBERON:0000122.name: neuron projection bundle
UBERON:0000122.def: a fasciculated bundle of neuron projections (go:0043005), largely or completely lacking synapses.

UBERON:0000123.name: endoneurium
UBERON:0000123.def: the loose connective tissue within the perineurium that continues into nerve fascicles and surrounds individual fibers. (nolte, j. the human brain 3rd edition).

UBERON:0000124.name: epineurium
UBERON:0000124.def: a loose connective tissue sheath surrounding each peripheral nerve. composed mainly of colagen and fibroblasts, it forms a substantial covering over nerve trunks, then thins to an incomplete layer around smaller branches near their terminations. the epineurium is continuous centrally with the dura. peripherally, it usually ends near the termination of a nerve fiber, but it may continue as the capsule of meissner corpuscles and a few other encapsulated endings. nolte, j. the human brain 3rd edition.

UBERON:0000125.name: neural nucleus
UBERON:0000125.def: a spatially aggregated collection of nerve cell bodies in the cns, consisting of one or more subpopulations that share cell type, chemical phenotype, and connections, and including nearby cells that share the same cell type, chemical phenotype, and connections. (cumbo).

UBERON:0000126.name: cranial nerve nucleus
UBERON:0000126.def: nucleus that receives projections from or contains neurons that send projections through one of the cranial nerves.

UBERON:0000127.name: facial nucleus
UBERON:0000127.def: the group of motor neurons residing in the pons that innervate the muscles of facial expression.

UBERON:0000128.name: olivary body
UBERON:0000128.def: prominent oval structure in the medulla oblongata, present in pairs, the lower portion of the brainstem. they contain the olivary nuclei.

UBERON:0000130.name: transverse foramen
UBERON:0000130.def: foramen that pierces the transverse processes of the seven cervical vertebrae. in the upper six vertebrae, the foramen gives passage to the vertebral artery, vertebral vein, and a plexus of sympathetic nerves. the seventh foramen lacks the artery, but contains the vein and sympathetic nerves.

UBERON:0000144.name: trochlea of humerus
UBERON:0000144.def: the medial portion of the articular surface of the humerus is named the trochlea, and presents a deep depression between two well-marked borders; it is convex from before backward, concave from side to side, and occupies the anterior, lower, and posterior parts of the extremity. it is directly inferior to the most prominent anterior humeral fossia, the coronoid fossia. it articulates with the ulna.

UBERON:0000151.name: pectoral fin
UBERON:0000151.def: paired fin that is located in the thoracic region of the body.

UBERON:0000152.name: pelvic fin
UBERON:0000152.def: paired fin located in the abdominal position of the body.

UBERON:0000155.name: theca cell layer
UBERON:0000155.def: a layer of the ovarian follicle that consists of theca cells.

UBERON:0000156.name: theca externa
UBERON:0000156.def: the theca externa is the outer layers of the theca folliculi. it contains abundant collagen and is mainly supportive.

UBERON:0000157.name: theca interna
UBERON:0000157.def: theca interna cells express receptors for luteinizing hormone, which when activated will stimulate the production of androstenedione from cholesterol by the enzyme desmolase. androstenedione ultimately gives the granulosa cells the precursor substrate for estrogen manufacturing.

UBERON:0000159.name: anal canal
UBERON:0000159.def: the terminal part of the large intestine, continuous proximally with the rectum and distally terminates with the anus.

UBERON:0000160.name: intestine
UBERON:0000160.def: segment of the alimentary canal extending from the stomach to the anus and, in humans and other mammals, consists of two segments, the small intestine and the large intestine.

UBERON:0000161.name: orifice
UBERON:0000161.def: anatomical conduit that connects two adjacent body spaces (or a body space with the space surrounding the organism)[fma,modified].

UBERON:0000162.name: cloaca
UBERON:0000162.def: common chamber into which the intestines and excretory system opens. arises during development in all vertebrates, but in many it becomes subdivided, lost or incorporated into other structures.

UBERON:0000163.name: embryonic cloaca
UBERON:0000163.def: endoderm-lined chamber that develops as pouch-like dilation of the caudal end of the hindgut and receives the allantois ventrally and two mesonephric ducts laterally; caudally it ends blindly at the cloacal membrane formed by the union of proctodeal (anal pit) ectoderm and cloacal endoderm, with no intervening mesoderm[mp].

UBERON:0000164.name: primitive urogenital sinus
UBERON:0000164.def: the ventral part of the cloaca remaining after septation of the rectum, which further develops into part of the bladder, part of the prostatic part of the male urethra and the urethra and vestibule in females.

UBERON:0000165.name: mouth
UBERON:0000165.def: the proximal portion of the digestive tract, containing the oral cavity and bounded by the oral opening. in vertebrates, this extends to the pharynx and includes gums, lips, tongue and parts of the palate. typically also includes the teeth, except where these occur elsewhere (e.g. pharyngeal jaws) or protrude from the mouth (tusks).

UBERON:0000166.name: oral opening
UBERON:0000166.def: the orifice that connects the mouth to the exterior of the body.

UBERON:0000167.name: oral cavity
UBERON:0000167.def: anatomical cavity at the start of the digestive tract that that is enclosed by the mouth. the boundaries and contents vary depending on the species. in vertebrates, the boundaries are the oral opening, the cheeks, the palate and (if present) the palatoglossal arch - if this is not present then the mouth and pharynx form the oropharyngeal cavity. the buccal cavity contains the teeth, tongue and palate (when present).

UBERON:0000168.name: proximal-distal subdivision of colon
UBERON:0000168.def: a section dividing a colon along a proximal-distal axis.

UBERON:0000170.name: pair of lungs
UBERON:0000170.def: the pair of anatomical structures comprised of a left lung and right lung.

UBERON:0000171.name: respiration organ
UBERON:0000171.def: organ that functions in gaseous exchange between an organism and its environment. in plants, microorganisms, and many small animals, air or water makes direct contact with the organism's cells or tissue fluids, and the processes of diffusion supply the organism with dioxygen (o2) and remove carbon dioxide (co2). in larger animals the efficiency of gaseous exchange is improved by specialized respiratory organs, such as lungs and gills, which are ventilated by breathing mechanisms.

UBERON:0000172.name: vomit
UBERON:0000172.def: a bodily fluid consisting of the expulsed contents of the stomach disgorged through the mouth or nose that happens as a result of a vomit reflex.

UBERON:0000173.name: amniotic fluid
UBERON:0000173.def: amniotic fluid is a bodily fluid consisting of watery liquid surrounding and cushioning a growing fetus within the amnion. it allows the fetus to move freely without the walls of the uterus being too tight against its body. buoyancy is also provided. the composition of the fluid changes over the course of gestation. initially, amniotic fluid is similar to maternal plasma, mainly water with electrolytes. as the fetus develops, proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, phospholipids originating from the lungs, fetal cells, and urea are deposited in the fluid.

UBERON:0000174.name: excreta
UBERON:0000174.def: a portion of organism substance that is the product of an excretion process that will be eliminated from the body. an excretion process is elimination by an organism of the waste products that arise as a result of metabolic activity.

UBERON:0000175.name: pleural effusion
UBERON:0000175.def: pleural effusion is a bodily fluid that is produced in exess and accumulates in the pleural cavity, the fluid-filled space that surrounds the lungs. excessive amounts of such fluid can impair breathing by limiting the expansion of the lungs during inhalation.

UBERON:0000176.name: oronasal secretion
UBERON:0000176.def: a bodily fluid secreted from the body via the mouth or nose.

UBERON:0000177.name: pus
UBERON:0000177.def: pus is a bodily fluid consisting of a whitish-yellow or yellow substance produced during inflammatory responses of the body that can be found in regions of pyogenic bacterial infections. pus is produced from the dead and living cells which travel into the intercellular spaces around the affected cells.

UBERON:0000178.name: blood
UBERON:0000178.def: a fluid that is composed of blood plasma and erythrocytes.

UBERON:0000179.name: haemolymphatic fluid
UBERON:0000179.def: circulating fluid that is part of the hemolymphoid system. blood, lymph, interstitial fluid or its analogs.

UBERON:0000180.name: lateral lumbar region of abdomen
UBERON:0000180.def: a region of the posterior torso (lower back) beneath the ribs and above the ilium.

UBERON:0000199.name: neck of radius
UBERON:0000199.def: the narrow part of the shaft of the radius just below the head.

UBERON:0000200.name: gyrus
UBERON:0000200.def: a ridge on the cerebral cortex. it is generally surrounded by one or more sulci .

UBERON:0000201.name: endothelial blood brain barrier
UBERON:0000201.def: a blood brain barrier that is composed of endothelial cells.

UBERON:0000202.name: glial blood brain barrier
UBERON:0000202.def: a blood brain barrier composed of glial cells.

UBERON:0000203.name: pallium
UBERON:0000203.def: dorsal part (roof region) of the telencephalon[go].

UBERON:0000204.name: ventral part of telencephalon
UBERON:0000204.def: ventral part (base region) of the telencephalon.

UBERON:0000205.name: papula
UBERON:0000205.def: a thin protuberance on the surface of the body of an echinoderm containing diverticula of the water vascular system lined by ciliated peritoneum. along with tube feet, provide the principle gas exchange surfaces..

UBERON:0000206.name: pharyngeal gill
UBERON:0000206.def: a gill that develops in the walls of the pharynx along a series of gill slits opening to the exterior. in fish, the gills are located on both sides of the pharynx.

UBERON:0000207.name: compound eye corneal lens
UBERON:0000207.def: a chitinous extracellular secretion of the four underlying cone cells and the pigment cells.

UBERON:0000209.name: tetrapod frontal bone
UBERON:0000209.def: the bone forming the forehead and roof of the eye orbit.

UBERON:0000210.name: tetrapod parietal bone
UBERON:0000210.def: in humans: bone forming side and roof of cranium. each bone is irregularly quadrilateral in form, and has two surfaces, four borders, and four angles.

UBERON:0000211.name: ligament
UBERON:0000211.def: dense regular connective tissue connecting two or more adjacent skeletal elements or supporting an organ.

UBERON:0000212.name: toilet claw
UBERON:0000212.def: a specialized claw or nail on the foot of certain primates, used for personal grooming.

UBERON:0000218.name: vertebral arch of axis
UBERON:0000218.def: a neural arch that is part of a vertebral bone 2.

UBERON:0000220.name: atlanto-occipital joint
UBERON:0000220.def: the atlanto-occipital joint (articulation between the atlas and the occipital bone) consists of a pair of condyloid joints. the atlanto-occipital joint is a synovial joint. the ligaments connecting the bones are: two articular capsules; posterior atlantoöccipital membrane; anterior atlantoöccipital membrane; lateral atlantoöccipital.

UBERON:0000221.name: supraauricular point
UBERON:0000221.def: a craniometric point on the posterior root of the zygomatic process of the temporal bone directly above the auricular point.

UBERON:0000301.name: amniotic cavity
UBERON:0000301.def: a closed space between the embryo and the amnion which contains the amniotic fluid and is formed by the fusion of the parts of the anterior and posterior amniotic folds.

UBERON:0000303.name: adductor longus
UBERON:0000303.def: an adductor muscle that attaches to the hip and femur. in humans, it is a part of the adductor group of the thigh, that as the name suggests adducts the thigh. the adductor longus muscle forms the medial wall of the femoral triangle[wp, generalized].

UBERON:0000304.name: tendon sheath
UBERON:0000304.def: a layer of membrane around a tendon. it has 2 layers: synovial sheath + fibrous tendon sheath.

UBERON:0000305.name: amnion
UBERON:0000305.def: the thin innermost layer of the extraembryonic membranes that contains the amniotic fluid; the membrane forms a closed sac in which the embryo and later, the fetus, is suspended and protected.

UBERON:0000307.name: blastula
UBERON:0000307.def: organism at the blastula stage - an early stage of embryonic development in animals. it is produced by cleavage of a fertilized ovum and consists of a spherical layer of around 128 cells surrounding a central fluid-filled cavity called the blastocoel. the blastula follows the morula and precedes the gastrula in the developmental sequence.

UBERON:0000309.name: body wall
UBERON:0000309.def: the external portion of an animal body derived from ectoderm and mesoderm layers that encloses the body cavity.

UBERON:0000310.name: breast
UBERON:0000310.def: the upper ventral region of the torso of an organism.

UBERON:0000311.name: extensor muscle
UBERON:0000311.def: a skeletal muscle whose contraction extends or stretches a body part.

UBERON:0000313.name: portion of cartilage tissue in tibia

UBERON:0000314.name: cecum mucosa
UBERON:0000314.def: a mucosa that is part of a cecum [automatically generated definition].
UBERON:0000314.synonym: organ mucosa of intestinum crassum caecum

UBERON:0000315.name: subarachnoid space
UBERON:0000315.def: the space between the arachnoid and pia mater.

UBERON:0000316.name: cervical mucus
UBERON:0000316.def: a substance produced by the cervix and endocervical glands[bto]. thick acidic mucus that blocks the cervical os after mestruation[wp]. this 'infertile' mucus blocks spermatozoa from entering the uterus.

UBERON:0000317.name: colonic mucosa
UBERON:0000317.def: mucosa that is part of a colon. the mucosa of the colon is lined by a simple columnar epithelium with a thin brush border and numerous goblet cells.

UBERON:0000319.name: cytotrophoblast
UBERON:0000319.def: the inner layer of the trophoblast, interior to the syncytiotrophoblast in an embryo. it serves to anchor the embryonic chorion to the maternal endometrium. cytotrophoblasts are stem cells in the chorionic villi. during differentiation, mononuclear cytotrophoblast fuse together into the multinucleated syncytiotrophoblasts. the primary villi has only the cytotrophoblast as an axe. [wp,unvetted].

UBERON:0000320.name: duodenal mucosa
UBERON:0000320.def: a mucosa that is part of a duodenum [automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0000323.name: late embryo
UBERON:0000323.def: an embryo that is at the late embryonic stage; this stage covers late steps of the embryogenesis with a fully formed embryo still developing before birth or egg hatching.

UBERON:0000325.name: gastric gland
UBERON:0000325.def: the branched tubular glands found in the mucosa of the fundus and body of the stomach which contain parietal cells that secrete hydrochloric acid and zymogenic cells that produce pepsin.

UBERON:0000326.name: pancreatic juice
UBERON:0000326.def: pancreatic juice is slightly alkaline and contains numerous enzymes and inactive enzyme precursors including alpha-amylase, chymotrypsinogen, lipase, procarboxypeptidase, proelastase, prophospholipase a2, ribonuclease, and trypsinogen. its high concentration of bicarbonate ions helps to neutralize the acid from the stomach.

UBERON:0000328.name: gut wall
UBERON:0000328.def: the wall of the digestive tract. this encompasses all parts of the digestive tract with the exception of the lumen (cavity).

UBERON:0000329.name: hair root
UBERON:0000329.def: the enlarged basal part of a hair within the skin[bto]. the root of the hair ends in an enlargement, the hair bulb, which is whiter in color and softer in texture than the shaft, and is lodged in a follicular involution of the epidermis called the hair follicle. [wikipedia].

UBERON:0000331.name: ileal mucosa
UBERON:0000331.def: a mucosa that is part of a ileum [automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0000332.name: yellow bone marrow
UBERON:0000332.def: bone marrow in which the fat cells predominate in the meshes of the reticular network.

UBERON:0000333.name: intestinal gland
UBERON:0000333.def: a gland that is part of the intestinal mucosa. examples include the intestinal crypts, duodenal gland[cjm].

UBERON:0000341.name: throat
UBERON:0000341.def: in anatomy, the throat is the anterior part of the neck, in front of the vertebral column. it consists of the pharynx and larynx. an important feature of the throat is the epiglottis, a flap which separates the esophagus from the trachea and prevents inhalation of food or drink. the throat contains various blood vessels, various pharyngeal muscles, the trachea (windpipe) and the esophagus. the hyoid bone and the clavicle are the only bones located in the throat of mammals. it is sometimes considered a synonym for fauces. [wp,unvetted].

UBERON:0000344.name: mucosa
