MONDO:0000232.def: a spotted fever that has material basis in rickettsia honei, which is transmitted by cayenne ticks (amblyomma cajennense). the infection has symptom mild spotted fever, has symptom eschar and has symptom adenopathy.

MONDO:0000233.name: japanese spotted fever
MONDO:0000233.def: a spotted fever that has material basis in rickettsia japonica, which is transmitted by ticks (dermacentor taiwanensis and haemaphysalis flava). the infection has symptom fever, has symptom eschars, has symptom regional adenopathy, and has symptom rash on extremities.

MONDO:0000234.name: rickettsia parkeri spotted fever
MONDO:0000234.def: a spotted fever that has material basis in rickettsia parkeri, which is transmitted by gulf coast tick (amblyomma maculatum). the infection has symptom fever, has symptom headache, has symptom eschar, and has symptom rash.

MONDO:0000236.name: oropharyngeal anthrax
MONDO:0000236.def: a anthrax infection that involves the oropharynx.

MONDO:0000238.name: obsolete pestis minor
MONDO:0000238.def: obsolete. a mild form of bubonic plague characterized by symptoms such as mild fever and lymphadenitis.

MONDO:0000239.name: adiaspiromycosis
MONDO:0000239.def: adiaspiromycosis is a rare fungal infection in the lung and is caused by inhalation of spores of the saprophytic soil fungus chrysosporium parvum var crescens (previously known as emmonsia crescens).

MONDO:0000240.name: invasive aspergillosis
MONDO:0000240.def: an aspergillosis that is a serious fungal infection of the lung with pneumonia caused by aspergillus, which spreads to other parts of the body through bloodstream in patients with acute leukemia and recipients of tissue transplants. clinical symptoms include pulmonary nodules and hemorrhage.

MONDO:0000241.name: keshan disease
MONDO:0000241.def: a congestive cardiomyopathy caused by a combination of dietary deficiency of selenium and the presence of a mutated strain of coxsackievirus.
MONDO:0000241.synonym: enlarged heart and poor heart function

MONDO:0000242.name: tinea barbae
MONDO:0000242.def: a dermatophytosis that involves the beard.

MONDO:0000243.name: ectothrix infectious disease
MONDO:0000243.def: a dermatophyte infection of the hair that infects the hair surface.

MONDO:0000244.name: endothrix infectious disease
MONDO:0000244.def: a dermatophyte infection of the hair that nvade the hair shaft and internalize into the hair cell.

MONDO:0000245.name: tinea imbricata
MONDO:0000245.def: a tinea corporis that results in fungal infection located in skin, has material basis in trichophyton concentricum, which is characterized by ring-like growth in overlapping circles that may have an autosomal dominant genetic predisposition.

MONDO:0000247.name: obsolete hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
MONDO:0000247.def: obsolete. a rare but potentially life-threatening disorder characterized by the proliferation of histiocytes and macrophages and phagocytosis of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. it may be inherited or secondary, due to infections, autoimmune disorders, or underlying malignancies. signs and symptoms include fever, lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and pancytopenia.

MONDO:0000248.name: dengue shock syndrome
MONDO:0000248.def: a dengue disease that involves the most severe form of dengue fever, has material basis in dengue virus [ncbitaxon:12637] with four serotypes (dengue virus 1, 2, 3 and 4), which are transmitted by aedes mosquito bite. the infection has symptom easy bruising, has symptom blood spots, has symptom bleeding gums, and has symptom nosebleeds. it is accompanied by circulatory collapse, involves hypotension, narrow pulse pressure (less than or equal to 20mm hg), or frank shock. the shock occurs after two to six days of symptoms, followed by collapse, weak pulse, and blueness around the mouth.

MONDO:0000249.name: secretory diarrhea
MONDO:0000249.def: watery voluminous diarrhea resulting from an imbalance between ion and water secretion and absorption.

MONDO:0000250.name: osmotic diarrheal disease
MONDO:0000250.def: a diarrhea that results from the presence of osmotically active, poorly absorbed solutes in the bowel lumen that inhibit normal water and electrolyte absorption.

MONDO:0000251.name: diarrheal disease secondary to altered bowel motility
MONDO:0000251.def: a diarrhea that results from either increased or decreased motility in the bowel.

MONDO:0000252.name: inflammatory diarrhea
MONDO:0000252.def: an diarrhea (disease) involving a pathogenic inflammatory response in the intestinal mucosa.

MONDO:0000253.name: piedra
MONDO:0000253.def: either of two diseases resulting from fungal infection of the hair shafts. black piedra occurs mainly in and on the hairs of the scalp and is caused by piedraia hortae; white piedra occurs in and on the hairs of the scalp, beard, mustache and genital areas and is caused by trichosporon species.

MONDO:0000254.name: cutaneous mycosis
MONDO:0000254.def: a mycosis that involves the integument and its appendages, including hair and nails. infection may involve the stratum corneum or deeper layers of the epidermis.

MONDO:0000255.name: subcutaneous mycosis
MONDO:0000255.def: a mycosis that involves subcutaneous tissue. there are three general types of subcutaneous mycoses: chromoblastomycosis, mycetoma, and sporotrichosis.

MONDO:0000256.name: systemic mycosis
MONDO:0000256.def: a mycosis that involves the lungs, abdominal viscera, bones and or central nervous system.

MONDO:0000261.name: adenoiditis
MONDO:0000261.def: an inflammatory disease involving a pathogenic inflammatory response in the pharyngeal tonsil.

MONDO:0000262.name: otomycosis
MONDO:0000262.def: fungus infection of the external ear, usually by aspergillus species

MONDO:0000263.name: laryngotracheitis
MONDO:0000263.def: an inflammation of both larynx and trachea.

MONDO:0000265.name: aspiration pneumonia
MONDO:0000265.def: a type of lung inflammation resulting from the aspiration of food, liquid, or gastric contents into the upper respiratory tract.

MONDO:0000266.name: pulmonary aspergilloma
MONDO:0000266.def: a aspergillosis that involves the lung.

MONDO:0000270.name: lower respiratory tract disorder
MONDO:0000270.def: a disease involving the lower respiratory tract.
MONDO:0000270.synonym: lower respiratory tract disease or disorder

MONDO:0000271.name: tuberculous salpingitis
MONDO:0000271.def: an urogenital tuberculosis involving a pathogenic inflammatory response in the fallopian tube.

MONDO:0000273.name: kunjin virus infectous disease
MONDO:0000273.def: a west nile encephalitis that results in infection located in brain, has material basis in kunjin virus, a subtype of west nile virus, which is transmitted by culex annulirostris mosquito bite. the infection has symptom fever, has symptom rigor, has symptom headache, has symptom confusion, and has symptom lethargy.

MONDO:0000275.name: obsolete monogenic disease
MONDO:0000275.def: obsolete. a genetic disease that is the result of one or more abnormal alleles and may be dominant (a single copy of the abnormal allele is sufficient to give rise to the disease), semi-dominant, or recessive (requiring both copies of the gene to have an abnormal allele).

MONDO:0000276.name: powassan encephalitis
MONDO:0000276.def: a disease caused by infection with powassan virus.

MONDO:0000282.name: whitewater arroyo hemorrhagic fever
MONDO:0000282.def: a viral infectious disease that is a hemorrhagic fever, has material basis in whitewater arroyo virus, which is transmitted by white-throated woodrats (neotoma albigula). the infection has symptom fever, has symptom headache, has symptom myalgia, and has symptom hemorrhagic manifestations.

MONDO:0000283.name: hantavirus hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, seoul virus type

MONDO:0000284.name: hantavirus hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, puumala virus type

MONDO:0000286.name: epstein-barr virus hepatitis
MONDO:0000286.def: a viral hepatitis that results in inflammation, located in liver, has material basis in human herpesvirus 4 and has symptom headache, has symptom fatigue, has symptom fever, has symptom abdominal pain, has symptom nausea, and has symptom jaundice.

MONDO:0000290.name: primary amebic meningoencephalitis
MONDO:0000290.def: a infectious disease involving the naegleria fowleri.

MONDO:0000291.name: granulomatous amebic encephalitis
MONDO:0000291.def: granulomatous amebic encephalitis is a life-threatening infection of the brain caused by the free-living amoebae acanthamoeba spp., balamuthia mandrillaris and sappinia pedata. acanthamoeba species, are commonly found in lakes, swimming pools, tap water, and heating and air conditioning units. the disease affects immunocompromised peple and is very serious. symptoms include mental status changes, loss of coordination, fever, muscular weakness or partial paralysis affecting one side of the body, double vision, sensitivity to light and other neurologic problems. the diagnosis is difficult and is often made at advanced stages. tests useful in the diagnosis include brain scans, biopsies, or spinal taps and in disseminated disease, biopsy of the involved sites and testing by the laboratory experts. early diagnosis is important for the prognosis. no single drug is effective; hence multiple antibiotics are needed for successful treatment. a combination of surgical and medical interventions involving multiple specialty experts is required to prevent death and morbidity in survivors.

MONDO:0000292.name: philophthalmiasis
MONDO:0000292.def: a disease caused by infection with philophthalmus.

MONDO:0000293.name: coenurosis
MONDO:0000293.def: a parasitic infection that develops in the intermediate hosts of some tapeworm species (taenia multiceps, t. serialis, t. brauni, or t. glomerata) and are caused by the coenurus, the larval stage of these worms. this disease occurs mainly in sheep and other ungulates, but occasionally can occur in humans too by accidental ingestion of worms' eggs.

MONDO:0000294.name: mesocestoidiasis
MONDO:0000294.def: an disease or disorder caused by infection with mesocestoides.

MONDO:0000295.name: acanthocephaliasis
MONDO:0000295.def: an disease or disorder caused by infection with acanthocephala.

MONDO:0000297.name: baylisascariasis
MONDO:0000297.def: an infection that is caused by the raccoon nematode baylisascaris procyonis, which is transmitted by the ingestion of embryonated eggs in contaminated soil; symptoms depend on larval migration sites (visceral organs, eye, or brain) provoking severe inflammatory responses.

MONDO:0000298.name: dioctophymiasis
MONDO:0000298.def: a disease caused by infection with dioctophyme renale.

MONDO:0000299.name: thelaziasis
MONDO:0000299.def: a disease caused by infection with thelazia.

MONDO:0000301.name: ophthalmomyiasis
MONDO:0000301.def: an myiasis caused by infection with oestrus ovis.

MONDO:0000302.name: basidiobolomycosis
MONDO:0000302.def: a disease caused by infection with basidiobolus.

MONDO:0000304.name: penicilliosis
MONDO:0000304.def: a disease caused by infection with talaromyces marneffei.

MONDO:0000306.name: trichosporonosis
MONDO:0000306.def: fungal infections caused by trichosporon that may become systemic especially in an immunocompromised host. clinical manifestations range from superficial cutaneous infections to systemic lesions in multiple organs.

MONDO:0000307.name: parasitic ichthyosporea infectious disease
MONDO:0000307.def: a disease caused by infection with ichthyosporea.

MONDO:0000308.name: primary systemic mycosis
MONDO:0000308.def: a systemic mycosis that arises from infection in an immunologically normal host.

MONDO:0000309.name: aniseikonia
MONDO:0000309.def: a condition in which the ocular image of an object as seen by one eye differs in size and shape from that seen by the other.

MONDO:0000310.name: alkhurma hemorrhagic fever
MONDO:0000310.def: a disease caused by infection with alkhumra hemorrhagic fever virus.
MONDO:0000310.synonym: alkhumra hemorrhagic fever virus infectious disease

MONDO:0000313.name: hypophosphatemia
MONDO:0000313.def: lower than normal levels of phosphates in the circulating blood.

MONDO:0000315.name: commensal bacterial infectious disease
MONDO:0000315.def: a bacterial infectious disease that results in infection by bacteria which are part of the normal human flora when one or more of the defense mechanisms designed to restrict them from the usually sterile internal tissues are breached by accident, by intent (surgery), or by an underlying metabolic or an infectious disorder.

MONDO:0000320.name: glandular tularemia
MONDO:0000320.def: a tularemia that involves the lymph node.

MONDO:0000321.name: typhoidal tularemia
MONDO:0000321.def: a tularemia that results in bacteremia and has symptom fever, has symptom chills, has symptom myalgia, has symptom malaise, and has symptom weight loss.

MONDO:0000322.name: obsolete carrion disease
MONDO:0000322.def: obsolete. a disease caused by infection with bartonella bacilliformis.

MONDO:0000327.name: buruli ulcer disease
MONDO:0000327.def: a cutaneous infection caused by mycobacterium ulcerans. it presents with painless nodular swelling of the skin, leading to the formation of necrotizing ulcers.

MONDO:0000328.name: hyperphosphatemia
MONDO:0000328.def: abnormally high level of phosphate in the blood.

MONDO:0000330.name: endemic typhus
MONDO:0000330.def: a bacterial infection caused by rickettsia typhi.

MONDO:0000331.name: rickettsia helvetica spotted fever
MONDO:0000331.def: a disease caused by infection with rickettsia helvetica.

MONDO:0000332.name: sennetsu fever
MONDO:0000332.def: a disease caused by infection with neorickettsia sennetsu.

MONDO:0000333.name: early congenital syphilis
MONDO:0000333.def: a congenital syphilis that is manifested between 0 and 2 years old.

MONDO:0000334.name: multinodular goiter
MONDO:0000334.def: nodular goiter characterized by more than one discrete tissue mass.

MONDO:0000335.name: parenchymatous neurosyphilis
MONDO:0000335.def: a tertiary neurosyphilis that results when chronic meningoencephalitis causes destruction of cortical parenchyma. the infection has symptom irritability, has symptom difficulty concentrating, has symptom deterioration of memory, has symptom defective judgment, has symptom headaches, has symptom insomnia, has symptom fatigue, and has symptom lethargy.

MONDO:0000336.name: meningovascular neurosyphilis
MONDO:0000336.def: a tertiary neurosyphilis that results in inflammation located in arteries of the brain or located in arteries of spinal cord. the infection has symptom headache, has symptom neck stiffness, has symptom dizziness, has symptom behavioral abnormalities, has symptom poor concentration, has symptom memory loss, has symptom lassitude, has symptom insomnia, has symptom blurred vision, has symptom weakness and wasting of shoulder-girdle and arm muscles, has symptom slowly progressive leg weakness with urinary or fecal incontinence or both, and has symptom paralysis of the legs due to thrombosis of spinal arteries.

MONDO:0000337.name: exanthema subitum
MONDO:0000337.def: an infection that is due to human herpesvirus (hhv) types 6 or 7; it is characterized by 3-5 days of high fever followed by the acute onset of a rosy, pink, non-pruritic, macular rash that is predominantly on the neck and trunk.

MONDO:0000339.name: spinal polio
MONDO:0000339.def: a paralytic poliomyelitis in which the site of paralysis is the spinal cord.

MONDO:0000340.name: bulbospinal polio
MONDO:0000340.def: a paralytic poliomyelitis in which the site of paralysis is the bulbospinal tract.

MONDO:0000341.name: paralytic poliomyelitis
MONDO:0000341.def: a poliomyelitis that results in destruction located in motor neurons of central nervous system, has material basis in human poliovirus 1, has material basis in human poliovirus 2, or has material basis in human poliovirus 3, which are transmitted by ingestion of food or water contaminated with feces, or transmitted by direct contact with the oral secretions. the infection has symptom loss of reflexes, has symptom muscle spasms, and has symptom acute flaccid paralysis.

MONDO:0000342.name: o'nyong'nyong fever
MONDO:0000342.def: an disease or disorder caused by infection with o'nyong-nyong virus.

MONDO:0000343.name: barmah forest virus disease
MONDO:0000343.def: a disease caused by infection with barmah forest virus.

MONDO:0000344.name: ross river fever
MONDO:0000344.def: a disease caused by infection with ross river virus.

MONDO:0000345.name: oropouche fever
MONDO:0000345.def: a disease caused by infection with oropouche virus.

MONDO:0000346.name: hantavirus hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, dobrava-belgrade virus type

MONDO:0000351.name: disorder of methionine catabolism
MONDO:0000351.def: an inherited metabolic disease that is has its basis in the disruption of methionine catabolic process.
MONDO:0000351.synonym: rare inborn error of methionine catabolic process

MONDO:0000355.name: ullrich congenital muscular dystrophy
MONDO:0000355.def: ullrich congenital muscular dystrophy (ucmd) is characterized by early-onset, generalized and slowly progressive muscle weakness, multiple proximal joint contractures, marked hypermobility of the distal joints and normal intelligence.

MONDO:0000359.name: spondylocostal dysostosis
MONDO:0000359.def: spondylocostal dysplasia is a rare genetic disorder characterized by defects of the bones of the spine (vertebrae) and abnormalities of the ribs. ribs can be fused or missing in chaotic patterns. these malformations are present at birth (congenital).

MONDO:0000363.name: gummatous syphilis
MONDO:0000363.def: a tertiary syphilis that is characterized by granulomatous lesions, called gummas, which are characterized by a center of necrotic tissue with a rubbery texture. they form in the liver, bones, and testes but may affect any organ.

MONDO:0000365.name: primary congenital glaucoma
MONDO:0000365.def: primary congenital glaucoma (pcg) is characterized by elevated intraocular pressure (iop), enlargement of the globe (buphthalmos), edema, and opacification of the cornea with rupture of descemet's membrane (haab's striae), thinning of the anterior sclera and iris atrophy, anomalously deep anterior chamber, and structurally normal posterior segment except for progressive glaucomatous optic atrophy. symptoms include photophobia, blepharospasm, and excessive tearing. typically, the diagnosis is made in the first year of life. depending on when treatment is instituted, visual acuity may be reduced and/or visual fields may be restricted. in untreated individuals, blindness invariably occurs.

MONDO:0000367.name: taeniasis
MONDO:0000367.def: a parasitic infection caused by tapeworms of the genus taenia. humans are infected by eating undercooked or raw meat of infected animals. it is usually an asymptomatic infection and patients may become aware of the infection by noticing segments of the tapeworm in their feces. if symptoms are present, they include nausea, abdominal pain, indigestion, constipation, or diarrhea.

MONDO:0000368.name: extrapulmonary tuberculosis
MONDO:0000368.def: a tuberculosis that occurs at body sites other than the lung.

MONDO:0000369.name: abdominal tuberculosis
MONDO:0000369.def: an extrapulmonary tuberculosis that is located in gastrointestinal tract, located in peritoneum, located in omentum, located in mesentery, located in liver, located in spleen or located in pancreas.

MONDO:0000371.name: oral cavity carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0000371.def: a in situ carcinoma that involves the oral cavity.

MONDO:0000372.name: pharynx carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0000372.def: stage 0 carcinoma of the pharynx according to the american joint committee on cancer, 6th, 7th, and 8th editions.

MONDO:0000373.name: gall bladder carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0000373.def: a carcinoma in situ involving a gall bladder.

MONDO:0000374.name: bile duct carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0000374.def: a carcinoma in situ involving a bile duct.

MONDO:0000375.name: bronchus carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0000375.def: a carcinoma in situ involving a bronchus.

MONDO:0000376.name: respiratory system cancer
MONDO:0000376.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the respiratory system

MONDO:0000377.name: malignant leydig cell tumor
MONDO:0000377.def: a leydig cell tumor characterized by large tumor size, the presence of cytologic atypia, increased mitotic activity, necrosis, and vascular invasion. approximately 10% of the testicular leydig cell tumors show malignant characteristics and metastasize. leydig cell tumors of the ovary follow a benign clinical course.

MONDO:0000378.name: malignant sertoli cell tumor
MONDO:0000378.def: a sertoli cell tumor of the testis or the ovary which metastasizes to another anatomic site.

MONDO:0000379.name: malignant sertoli-leydig cell tumor
MONDO:0000379.def: a malignant form of sertoli-leydig cell tumor.

MONDO:0000380.name: paranasal sinus carcinoma
MONDO:0000380.def: a malignant epithelial neoplasm arising in the paranasal sinus.
MONDO:0000380.synonym: squamous cell carcinoma of paranasal sinus

MONDO:0000381.name: infiltrating renal pelvis transitional cell carcinoma
MONDO:0000381.def: a infiltrating urothelial carcinoma that involves the renal pelvis.

MONDO:0000382.name: respiratory system benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000382.def: a benign neoplasm that involves the respiratory system.

MONDO:0000383.name: benign reproductive system neoplasm
MONDO:0000383.def: a non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the male or female reproductive system. representative examples include benign prostate phyllodes tumor, benign sertoli cell tumor, uterine corpus leiomyoma, and benign ovarian serous tumor.

MONDO:0000384.name: bladder benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000384.def: a benign abnormal growth of the cells that comprise the bladder.

MONDO:0000385.name: benign digestive system neoplasm
MONDO:0000385.def: a non-metastasizing neoplasm arising from any part of the digestive system.

MONDO:0000386.name: digestive system neuroendocrine tumor, grade 1/2
MONDO:0000386.def: a well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor arising from the digestive system. it is characterized by the presence of cells with features similar to those of the normal endocrine cells of the digestive system. the neoplastic cells express immunohistochemical evidence of neuroendocrine differentiation and hormones. there is mild to moderate nuclear atypia and less than 20 mitoses per 10 hpf. it includes well-differentiated endocrine tumors or carcinoid tumors and well-differentiated endocrine carcinomas.

MONDO:0000387.name: hypochromic microcytic anemia
MONDO:0000387.def: anemia in which the circulating rbcs are smaller than the usual size of rbcs (microcytic) and have decreased red color (hypochromic).

MONDO:0000390.name: vitelliform macular dystrophy
MONDO:0000390.def: a rare genetic disorder characterized by macular degeneration in the retina resulting in progressive loss of central vision with retention of the peripheral vision.

MONDO:0000393.name: partial fetal alcohol syndrome
MONDO:0000393.def: a fetal alcohol spectrum disorder that results in most, but not all, of the growth deficiency and/or craniofacial features of fetal alcohol syndrome including central nervous system dysfunction due to prenatal alcohol exposure.

MONDO:0000395.name: alcohol-related birth defect
MONDO:0000395.def: a physical or cognitive mental abnormality caused by maternal alcohol consumption and its toxic effect on the developing embryo during pregnancy.

MONDO:0000396.name: spastic cerebral palsy
MONDO:0000396.def: a form of cerebral palsy wherein spasticity is the exclusive impairment present.

MONDO:0000397.name: ataxic cerebral palsy
MONDO:0000397.def: a form of cerebral palsy caused by damage to cerebellar structures.

MONDO:0000400.name: mixed cerebral palsy
MONDO:0000400.def: a subtype of cerebral palsy characterized by both the tight muscle tone of spastic cerebral palsy and the writhing, involuntary muscle movements of athetoid cerebral palsy.

MONDO:0000401.name: obsolete congenital bile acid synthesis defect

MONDO:0000402.name: small cell carcinoma
MONDO:0000402.def: a neuroendocrine carcinoma composed of small malignant cells which are often said to resemble \"oat cells\

MONDO:0000405.name: anal canal cancer
MONDO:0000405.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the anal canal

MONDO:0000407.name: malignant pleural solitary fibrous tumor
MONDO:0000407.def: a malignant form of pleural solitary fibrous tumor.

MONDO:0000408.name: fetal alcohol spectrum disorder
MONDO:0000408.def: a group of disorders caused by a prenatal exposure to maternal consumption of alcohol leading to a range of behavioral, cognitive and neurological deficits in the offspring. it is characterized by physical growth problems, distinct facies, and varying psycho-neurological issues.

MONDO:0000409.name: chorioamnionitis
MONDO:0000409.def: a morphologic finding indicating inflammation of the fetal sac membranes. it is characterized by neutrophilic infiltration of the amnion and chorion.

MONDO:0000410.name: funisitis
MONDO:0000410.def: an acute inflammation of the umbilical cord. it is characterized by the presence of polymorphonuclear cells migrating from the fetal umbilical cord vessels through the umbilical cord towards the bacteria containing amniotic fluid.

MONDO:0000411.name: electroclinical syndrome
MONDO:0000411.def: an epilepsy syndrome that is a group of clinical entities showing a cluster of electro-clinical characteristics, classified according to age at onset, cognitive and developmental antecedents and consequences, motor and sensory examinations, eeg features, provoking or triggering factors, and patterns of seizure occurrence with respect to sleep.

MONDO:0000412.name: neonatal period electroclinical syndrome
MONDO:0000412.def: an electroclinical syndrome with onset in the neonatal period less than 44 weeks of gestational age.

MONDO:0000413.name: infancy electroclinical syndrome
MONDO:0000413.def: an electroclinical syndrome with onset in infancy occurring between birth and one year of age.

MONDO:0000414.name: childhood electroclinical syndrome
MONDO:0000414.def: a electroclinical syndrome that occurs during childhood.

MONDO:0000415.name: adolescence-adult electroclinical syndrome
MONDO:0000415.def: an electroclinical syndrome with onset in adolescence and adulthood.

MONDO:0000416.name: obsolete variable age at onset electroclinical syndrome

MONDO:0000417.name: early onset absence epilepsy
MONDO:0000417.def: a childhood electroclinical syndrome characterized by the occurrence of typical absence seizures starting between the age of four and ten years.

MONDO:0000420.name: obsolete cerebral folate receptor alpha deficiency

MONDO:0000421.name: inborn serine deficiency
MONDO:0000421.def: an inherited metabolic disease that is has its basis in the disruption of l-serine biosynthetic process.
MONDO:0000421.synonym: rare inborn error of l-serine biosynthetic process

MONDO:0000424.name: inborn vitamin b12 deficiency
MONDO:0000424.def: low serum levels of vitamin b12 (cobalamin) due to poor intestinal absorption, decreased dietary intake, or increased physiologic requirement.
MONDO:0000424.synonym: rare inborn error of cobalamin metabolic process

MONDO:0000429.name: autosomal genetic disease
MONDO:0000429.def: a monogenic disease that is has material basis in a mutation in a single gene on one of the non-sex chromosomes.

MONDO:0000430.name: mature t-cell and nk-cell non-hodgkin lymphoma
MONDO:0000430.def: this type of lymphoma is not frequently seen in the western hemisphere. clinically, with the exception of anaplastic large cell lymphoma, mature t- and nk-cell lymphomas are among the most aggressive of all hematopoietic neoplasms. representative disease entities include mycosis fungoides, angioimmunoblastic t-cell lymphoma, hepatosplenic t-cell lymphoma, and anaplastic large cell lymphoma.

MONDO:0000432.name: lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma
MONDO:0000432.def: a clonal neoplasm of small b-lymphocytes, lymphoplasmacytoid cells, and plasma cells involving the bone marrow, lymph nodes, and the spleen. the majority of patients have a serum igm paraprotein.

MONDO:0000436.name: obsolete t-cell large granular lymphocyte leukemia

MONDO:0000437.name: cerebellar ataxia
MONDO:0000437.def: a neurological syndrome characterized by clumsy and uncoordinated movement of the limbs, trunk, and cranial muscles. it results from pathology in the cerebellum and its connections, or in the proprioceptive sensory pathways.

MONDO:0000438.name: obsolete ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2

MONDO:0000441.name: obsolete x-linked myopathy with excessive autophagy

MONDO:0000447.name: autosomal dominant polycystic liver disease
MONDO:0000447.def: an autosomal dominant inherited condition characterized by many cysts of various sizes scattered throughout the liver.

MONDO:0000448.name: paraganglioma
MONDO:0000448.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm arising from paraganglia located along the sympathetic or parasympathetic nerves. infrequently, it may arise outside the usual distribution of the sympathetic and parasympathetic paraganglia. tumors arising from the adrenal gland medulla are called pheochromocytomas. morphologically, paragangliomas usually display a nesting (zellballen) growth pattern. there are no reliable morphologic criteria to distinguish between benign and malignant paragangliomas. the only definitive indicator of malignancy is the presence of regional or distant metastases.

MONDO:0000450.name: secondary progressive multiple sclerosis
MONDO:0000450.def: a multiple sclerosis with a clinical course characterized by a progressive accumulation of neurological disability, independent of relapses, following an initial relapsing-remitting (rr) phase.

MONDO:0000451.name: primary progressive multiple sclerosis
MONDO:0000451.def: a multiple sclerosis that is characterized by steady worsening of neurologic functioning, without any distinct relapses or periods of remission. the rate of progression may vary over time, with occasional plateaus or temporary improvements, but the progression is continuous.

MONDO:0000452.name: progressive relapsing multiple sclerosis
MONDO:0000452.def: a multiple sclerosis that is characterized by steadily worsening symptoms and attacks during periods of remission with disease progression from the onset.

MONDO:0000453.name: short qt syndrome
MONDO:0000453.def: a genetic disease of the electrical system of the heart that consists of a constellation of signs and symptoms, consisting of a short qt interval on an ekg (< 300 ms) that does not significantly change with heart rate, tall and peaked t waves, and a structurally normal heart. short qt syndrome appears to be inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern, and a few affected families have been identified
MONDO:0000453.synonym: ventricular arrhythmia associated with short qt syndrome

MONDO:0000455.name: cone dystrophy
MONDO:0000455.def: an inherited ocular disorder characterized by the loss of cone cells, the photoreceptors responsible for both central and color vision.

MONDO:0000456.name: cerebral creatine deficiency syndrome
MONDO:0000456.def: creatine deficiency syndrome (cds) comprises a group of inborn errors of creatine metabolism, characterized by a global developmental delay, intellectual disability and associated neurological (seizures, movement disorders, myopathy) and behavioral manifestions. cds includes two creatine biosynthesis disorders; guanidinoacetate methyltransferase deficiency and l- arginine: glycine amidinotransferase deficiency, as well as x-linked creatine transporter deficiency.

MONDO:0000457.name: classical glioblastoma
MONDO:0000457.def: a molecular subtype of glioblastoma characterized by lack of p53 mutations, chromosome 7 amplifications or deletions, and high levels of egfr amplification.

MONDO:0000458.name: proneural glioblastoma
MONDO:0000458.def: a molecular subtype of glioblastoma that is associated with younger age at presentation and is characterized by p53 mutations and pdgfra amplifications.

MONDO:0000459.name: mesenchymal glioblastoma
MONDO:0000459.def: a molecular subtype of glioblastoma characterized by the presence of nf1 mutations.

MONDO:0000460.name: neural glioblastoma
MONDO:0000460.def: a molecular subtype of glioblastoma characterized by the expression of the neural markers nefl, gabra1, syt1, and slc12a5.

MONDO:0000462.name: eye adnexa disorder
MONDO:0000462.def: a disease involving the ocular adnexa.

MONDO:0000463.name: ochoa syndrome
MONDO:0000463.def: ochoa syndrome is characterized by the association of severe voiding dysfunction and a characteristic facial expression.

MONDO:0000465.name: atrioventricular block
MONDO:0000465.def: a heart block that is initiated in the atrioventricular node.

MONDO:0000466.name: first-degree atrioventricular block
MONDO:0000466.def: a disorder characterized by an electrocardiographic finding of prolonged pr interval for a specific population. for adults one common threshold is a pr interval greater than 0.20 seconds.

MONDO:0000467.name: second-degree atrioventricular block
MONDO:0000467.def: intermittent failure of atrial electrical impulse conduction to the ventricles.

MONDO:0000468.name: third-degree atrioventricular block
MONDO:0000468.def: a disorder characterized by an electrocardiographic finding of complete failure of atrial electrical impulse conduction to the ventricles. this is manifested on the ecg by disassociation of atrial and ventricular rhythms. the atrial rate must be faster than the ventricular rate. (cdisc)

MONDO:0000469.name: sinoatrial node disorder
MONDO:0000469.def: a disease involving the sinoatrial node.

MONDO:0000471.name: tricuspid valve disorder
MONDO:0000471.def: a disease involving the tricuspid valve.

MONDO:0000473.name: arterial disorder
MONDO:0000473.def: an impairment of the structure or function of the blood vessels which carry blood away from the heart.

MONDO:0000477.name: focal dystonia
MONDO:0000477.def: a dystonia that is localized to a specific part of the body.

MONDO:0000478.name: multifocal dystonia
MONDO:0000478.def: a dystonia that involves two or more unrelated body parts.

MONDO:0000479.name: segmental dystonia
MONDO:0000479.def: a dystonia that affects two or more adjacent parts of the body.

MONDO:0000480.name: anismus
MONDO:0000480.def: a focal dystonia of the pelvic floor muscles during attempted defecation.

MONDO:0000481.name: cervical dystonia
MONDO:0000481.def: cervical dystonia is a neurological condition characterized by excessive pulling of the muscles of the neck and shoulder resulting in abnormal movements of the head (dystonia).most commonly, the head turns to one side or the other.tilting sideways, or to the back or front may also occur.the turning or tilting movements may be accompanied by shaking movement (tremor) and/or soreness of the muscles of the neck and shoulders.cervical dystonia can occur at any age, but most cases occur in middle age. it often begins slowly and usually reaches a plateau over a few months or years. the cause of cervical dystonia is often unknown. in some cases there is a family history. several genes have been associated with cervical dystonia, including gnal, thap1, ciz1, and ano3. other cases may be linked to an underlying disease (e.g. parkinson disease), neck trauma, or certain medications. treatment may include local injections of botulinum toxin, pain medications, benzodiazepines (anti-anxiety medications), anticholinergics,physical therapy, or surgery.

MONDO:0000482.name: focal hand dystonia
MONDO:0000482.def: a focal dystonia that affects a single muscle or small group of muscles in the hand resulting from involuntary muscular contractions.

MONDO:0000483.name: oculogyric crisis
MONDO:0000483.def: a focal dystonia that is characterized by a prolonged involuntary upward deviation of the eyes.

MONDO:0000485.name: spasmodic dystonia
MONDO:0000485.def: a chronic voice disorder characterized by momentary periods of uncontrolled spasms of the muscles of the larynx.

MONDO:0000486.name: craniofacial dystonia
MONDO:0000486.def: a focal dystonia that is characterized as dystonia that affects the muscles of the head, face, and neck.

MONDO:0000487.name: hemidystonia
MONDO:0000487.def: a multifocal dystonia that involves the arm and leg on the same side of the body.

MONDO:0000488.name: periampullary adenoma
MONDO:0000488.def: a adenoma that involves the periampullary region of duodenum.

MONDO:0000489.name: diabetic encephalopathy
MONDO:0000489.def: a brain disease that is characterized by functional impairment of cognition, cerebral signal conduction, neurotransmission and synaptic plasticity, and underlying structural pathology associated with diabetes.

MONDO:0000490.name: glomerulosclerosis
MONDO:0000490.def: a hardening of the kidney glomerulus caused by scarring of the blood vessels.

MONDO:0000491.name: limb ischemia
MONDO:0000491.def: a ischemia that involves the limb.

MONDO:0000494.name: renal fibrosis
MONDO:0000494.def: a final common manifestation of a wide variety of chronic kidney diseases characterized by glomerulosclerosis and tubulointerstitial fibrosis.

MONDO:0000495.name: oppositional defiant disorder
MONDO:0000495.def: a behavior disorder characterized by a persistent pattern of defiant, disobedient, and hostile behavior towards authority figures, manifested by a frequent loss of temper, arguing, becoming angry or vindictive, or other negativistic behaviors.

MONDO:0000496.name: hemorrhagic cystitis
MONDO:0000496.def: inflammation of the bladder resulting in bloody urine.

MONDO:0000497.name: pyometritis
MONDO:0000497.def: inflammation of uterine musculature associated with pus in the uterine cavity.

MONDO:0000498.name: arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy
MONDO:0000498.def: an anterior ischemic neuropathy that is the cause of vision loss that occurs in temporal arteritis (aka giant cell arteritis)

MONDO:0000500.name: tongue squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0000500.def: a squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the tongue. it usually presents as a painful ulcerated or nodular lesion. the size of the tumor and the status of the lymph nodes are the most important factors that determine prognosis.

MONDO:0000501.name: obsolete jensen syndrome
MONDO:0000501.synonym: syndrome of opticoacoustic nerve atrophy with dementia

MONDO:0000502.name: villous adenoma
MONDO:0000502.def: an epithelial neoplasm morphologically characterized by the presence of a villous architectural pattern. most often it occurs in the large intestine, small intestine, and the stomach in which the neoplastic epithelial cells show dysplastic features. it may also arise in the urinary bladder, urethra, and vagina.

MONDO:0000503.name: lung adenocarcinoma in situ
MONDO:0000503.def: a localized non-invasive adenocarcinoma of the lung measuring 3 cm or less. it is characterized by a pure lepidic growth pattern and the lack of stromal, vascular, or pleural invasion.
MONDO:0000503.synonym: stage 0 adenosquamous lung carcinoma ajcc v7

MONDO:0000507.name: inclusion body myopathy with paget disease of bone and frontotemporal dementia
MONDO:0000507.def: inclusion body myopathy with paget disease of bone and frontotemporal dementia (ibmpfd) is a multisystem degenerative genetic disorder characterized by adult-onset proximal and distal muscle weakness (clinically resembling limb-girdle muscular dystrophy); early-onset paget disease of bone, manifesting with bone pain, deformity and enlargement of the long-bones; and premature frontotemporal dementia, manifesting first with dysnomia, dyscalculia and comprehension deficits followed by progressive aphasia, alexia, and agraphia. as the disease progresses, muscle weakness begins to affect the other limbs and respiratory muscles, ultimately resulting in respiratory or cardiac failure.

MONDO:0000508.name: syndromic intellectual disability
MONDO:0000508.def: a intellectual disability that is part of a larger syndrome.

MONDO:0000509.name: non-syndromic intellectual disability
MONDO:0000509.def: an intellectual disability that is not part of a larger syndrome.

MONDO:0000510.name: synucleinopathy
MONDO:0000510.def: a neurodegenerative disease that is characterized by the abnormal accumulation of aggregates of alpha-synuclein protein in neurons, nerve fibers or glial cells. [url:http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/synucleinopathies ]

MONDO:0000513.name: bone ameloblastoma
MONDO:0000513.def: a ameloblastoma that involves the bone tissue.

MONDO:0000514.name: bone squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0000514.def: a squamous cell carcinoma that involves the bone tissue.

MONDO:0000515.name: bone chondrosarcoma
MONDO:0000515.def: a chondrosarcoma (disease) that involves the bone tissue.

MONDO:0000516.name: phalanx chondroma
MONDO:0000516.def: a chondroma that involves the phalanx.

MONDO:0000517.name: brain stem medulloblastoma
MONDO:0000517.def: a medulloblastoma that involves the brainstem.

MONDO:0000518.name: sacrum chordoma
MONDO:0000518.def: a chordoma (disease) that involves the fused sacrum.

MONDO:0000519.name: corpus callosum oligodendroglioma
MONDO:0000519.def: a oligodendroglioma that involves the corpus callosum.

MONDO:0000520.name: parietal lobe ependymal tumor
MONDO:0000520.def: an ependymal tumor affecting the parietal lobe of the brain.

MONDO:0000521.name: salivary gland carcinoma
MONDO:0000521.def: a carcinoma that arises from the major or minor salivary glands. representative examples include carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma, adenocarcinoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma, and mucoepidermoid carcinoma.

MONDO:0000524.name: mixed extragonadal germ cell cancer
MONDO:0000524.def: a mixed germ cell cancer that is located in areas of the body other than the ovary or testicle.

MONDO:0000525.name: cecum villous adenoma
MONDO:0000525.def: a neoplasm that arises from the glandular epithelium of the cecal mucosa. it is characterized by a villous architectural pattern. the neoplastic glandular cells have dysplastic features.

MONDO:0000526.name: obsolete appendix carcinoid tumor
MONDO:0000526.def: obsolete. a carcinoid tumor (disease) that involves the vermiform appendix.

MONDO:0000527.name: colon adenoma
MONDO:0000527.def: an adenoma that arises from the colon. the group of colonic adenomas includes tubular, villous, and tubulovillous adenomas, traditional serrated adenomas, sessile serrated adenomas/polyps, and familial adenomatous polyposis.

MONDO:0000530.name: rectum adenoma
MONDO:0000530.def: an adenoma that arises from the rectum. the group of rectal adenomas includes tubular, villous, and tubulovillous adenomas, traditional serrated adenomas, sessile serrated adenomas/polyps, and familial adenomatous polyposis.

MONDO:0000531.name: bronchus mucoepidermoid carcinoma
MONDO:0000531.def: a mucoepidermoid carcinoma that involves the bronchus.

MONDO:0000532.name: lung combined type small cell adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0000532.def: a lung combined type small cell carcinoma that has material basis in epithelial tissue of glandular origin.

MONDO:0000534.name: trachea mucoepidermoid carcinoma
MONDO:0000534.def: a mucoepidermoid carcinoma that involves the trachea.

MONDO:0000535.name: tonsil squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0000535.def: a squamous cell carcinoma that involves the tonsil.

MONDO:0000536.name: pharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0000536.def: a squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the pharynx.

MONDO:0000538.name: obsolete spindle epithelial tumor with thymus-like differentiation tumor

MONDO:0000539.name: striated muscle rhabdoid tumor
MONDO:0000539.def: a rhabdoid tumor that involves the striated muscle tissue.

MONDO:0000540.name: small intestinal neuroendocrine tumor g1
MONDO:0000540.def: a well differentiated, low grade neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid tumor) that arises from the small intestine. the mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 hpf and/or the ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent.
MONDO:0000540.synonym: small intestine neuroendocrine tumor, well differentiated, low grade

MONDO:0000541.name: jejunal adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0000541.def: a adenocarcinoma that involves the jejunum.

MONDO:0000543.name: ovarian melanoma
MONDO:0000543.def: a melanoma (disease) that involves the ovary.

MONDO:0000544.name: mucosal melanoma
MONDO:0000544.def: a melanoma that arises from a mucosal site.

MONDO:0000545.name: sublingual gland adenoid cystic carcinoma
MONDO:0000545.def: a adenoid cystic carcinoma that involves the sublingual gland.

MONDO:0000546.name: obsolete parotid gland adenoid cystic carcinoma

MONDO:0000548.name: ovarian clear cell cancer
MONDO:0000548.def: an invasive malignant neoplasm that arises from the ovary and is characterized by a predominance of clear and hobnail malignant epithelial cells.

MONDO:0000549.name: cervical neuroblastoma
MONDO:0000549.def: a relatively uncommon neuroblastoma that is found in the neck.

MONDO:0000550.name: extra-adrenal sympathetic paraganglioma
MONDO:0000550.def: a benign or malignant sympathetic paraganglioma arising from paraganglia outside the adrenal gland. clinical symptoms are related to secretion of catecholamines. representative examples include the superior and inferior paraaortic and bladder paragangliomas.

MONDO:0000551.name: retroperitoneal neuroblastoma
MONDO:0000551.def: a neuroblastoma that involves the retroperitoneal space.

MONDO:0000552.name: breast lobular carcinoma
MONDO:0000552.def: an adenocarcinoma of the breast arising from the lobules. this is a relatively uncommon carcinoma, represents approximately 10% of the breast adenocarcinomas and is often bilateral or multifocal.

MONDO:0000553.name: uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma
MONDO:0000553.def: a endometrial carcinoma (disease) that involves the body of uterus.
MONDO:0000553.synonym: endometrial carcinoma (disease) of body of uterus

MONDO:0000554.name: endocervical adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0000554.def: an adenocarcinoma that arises from the endocervix. it is the most common type of endocervical adenocarcinoma. the neoplastic epithelium shows a pseudostratified architecture and the malignant cells have enlarged, elongated, and hyperchromatic nuclei.

MONDO:0000564.name: obsolete cerebellar ataxia, mental retardation and dysequlibrium syndrome

MONDO:0000565.name: infective endocarditis
MONDO:0000565.def: infective endocarditis (ie) is an infection of the inner lining of the heart chambers (endocardium) and valves. this condition is sometimes called 'endocarditis,' although it is important to distinguish it from non-infective endocarditis. ie is caused bybacteria, fungi, or other germs invading the bloodstream and attaching to the heart. ie can damagethe heart and cause serious and sometimes fatal complications. it can develop quickly or slowly depending on what type of germ is causing it and whether there is an underlying heart problem. common symptoms of ie are fever and other flu-like symptoms, but signs and symptoms can vary. it can also cause problems in many other parts of the body besides the heart. ie is typically treated with antibiotics for several weeks; some individuals may need heart surgery to repair or replace heart valves or remove infected heart tissue.

MONDO:0000568.name: autoimmune disorder of central nervous system
MONDO:0000568.def: a hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease that involves the central nervous system.
MONDO:0000568.synonym: central nervous system hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease

MONDO:0000569.name: autoimmune disorder of endocrine system
MONDO:0000569.def: a hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease that involves the endocrine system.
MONDO:0000569.synonym: endocrine system hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease

MONDO:0000570.name: obsolete severe combined immunodeficiency due to artemis deficiency

MONDO:0000572.name: recombinase activating gene 1 deficiency
MONDO:0000572.def: a severe combined immunodeficiency that is the result of a mutation on chromosome 6 rag1 gene involving genetic rearrangement of both the t- and b-lymphocyte receptor genes.

MONDO:0000573.name: recombinase activating gene 2 deficiency
MONDO:0000573.def: a severe combined immunodeficiency that is the result of a mutation on chromosome 6 rag2 gene involving genetic rearrangement of both the t- and b-lymphocyte receptor genes.

MONDO:0000577.name: congenital anemia
MONDO:0000577.def: anemia, the cause of which is present at birth.

MONDO:0000584.name: b cell linker protein deficiency
MONDO:0000584.def: a hypobammaglobulinemia that is a b cell deficiency that has material basis in a mutation in a cytoplasmic linker or adaptor protein that plays a critical role in b cell development, the b cell linker protein (blnk) gene. mutations in this gene cause hypoglobulinemia and absent b cells, a disease in which the pro- to pre-b-cell transition is developmentally blocked. the blnk gene is associated with intracellular calcium mobilization, essential for cell activation.

MONDO:0000586.name: autoimmune disorder of exocrine system
MONDO:0000586.def: a hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease that involves the exocrine system.
MONDO:0000586.synonym: exocrine system hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease

MONDO:0000587.name: autoimmune disease of ear, nose and throat
MONDO:0000587.def: an autoimmune form of otorhinolaryngologic disease.

MONDO:0000588.name: autoimmune disorder of gastrointestinal tract
MONDO:0000588.def: a hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease that involves the alimentary part of gastrointestinal system.
MONDO:0000588.synonym: autoimmune disease of alimentary part of gastrointestinal system

MONDO:0000589.name: autoimmune disorder of musculoskeletal system
MONDO:0000589.def: a hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease that involves the musculoskeletal system.
MONDO:0000589.synonym: musculoskeletal system hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease

MONDO:0000590.name: autoimmune disorder of peripheral nervous system
MONDO:0000590.def: a hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease that involves the peripheral nervous system.
MONDO:0000590.synonym: peripheral nervous system hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease

MONDO:0000591.name: intrinsic cardiomyopathy
MONDO:0000591.def: a cardiomyopathy that is due to abnormalities in heart muscle cells.

MONDO:0000592.name: specific developmental disorder
MONDO:0000592.def: a developmental disorder of mental health that categorizes specific learning disabilities and developmental disorders affecting coordination.

MONDO:0000593.name: obsolete autoimmune disease of skin and connective tissue

MONDO:0000594.name: pervasive developmental disorder
MONDO:0000594.def: a category of developmental disorders characterized by impaired communication and socialization skills. the impairments are incongruent with the individual's developmental level or mental age. these disorders can be associated with general medical or genetic conditions.

MONDO:0000595.name: sexual and gender identity disorders
MONDO:0000595.def: a category of psychiatric disorders characterized by a disturbance in sexual desire and in the psychophysiological changes that make up the sexual response cycle.

MONDO:0000596.name: paraphilic disorder
MONDO:0000596.def: disorders that include recurrent, intense sexually arousing fantasies, sexual urges, or behaviors generally involving nonhuman objects, suffering of oneself or partners, or children or other nonconsenting partners. (from dsm-v)

MONDO:0000597.name: munchausen by proxy
MONDO:0000597.def: a factitious disorder that involves a care giver's deliberate exaggeration, fabrication, and/or induce physical, psychological, behavioral, and/or mental health problems in others.

MONDO:0000598.name: aphasia
MONDO:0000598.def: a language disorder that involves an acquired impairment of any laguage modality such as producting or comprehending spoken or written language.

MONDO:0000599.name: writing disorder
MONDO:0000599.def: a learning disability that involves impaired written language ability such as impairments in handwriting, spelling, organization of ideas, and composition.

MONDO:0000600.name: nosophobia
MONDO:0000600.def: a specific phobia that involves an irrational fear of contracting a disease.

MONDO:0000601.name: obsolete autoimmune disorder of urogenital tract
MONDO:0000601.def: obsolete. a hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease that involves the genitourinary system.
MONDO:0000601.synonym: genitourinary system hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease

MONDO:0000602.name: autoimmune disorder of blood
MONDO:0000602.def: a hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease that involves the blood.
MONDO:0000602.synonym: blood hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease

MONDO:0000603.name: autoimmune disorder of cardiovascular system
MONDO:0000603.def: a hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease that involves the cardiovascular system.
MONDO:0000603.synonym: cardiovascular system hypersensitivity reaction type ii disease

MONDO:0000605.name: hypersensitivity reaction disease
MONDO:0000605.def: an immune system disease that has basis in dysregulation of the hypersensitivity reaction, an inflammatory response to an exogenous environmental antigen or an endogenous antigen initiated by the adaptive immune system.

MONDO:0000607.name: primary cutaneous t-cell non-hodgkin lymphoma
MONDO:0000607.def: a t-cell non-hodgkin lymphoma arising from the skin. representative examples include mycosis fungoides and primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma.
MONDO:0000607.synonym: t-cell non-hodgkin's lymphoma of the skin

MONDO:0000609.name: obsolete sideroblastic anemia with spinocerebellar ataxia

MONDO:0000610.name: marantic endocarditis
MONDO:0000610.def: formation of a non-infectious thrombus, referred to as vegetation, on previously undamaged endocardium. it usually occurs as a complication of connective-tissue diseases and cancers because of the associated hypercoagulable state (see thrombophilia).

MONDO:0000611.name: pre-malignant neoplasm
MONDO:0000611.def: a disease of cellular proliferation that results in abnormal growths in the body, which do not invade or destroy the surrounding tissue but, given enough time, will transform into a cancer.

MONDO:0000612.name: lymphatic system cancer
MONDO:0000612.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the lymphatic part of lymphoid system
MONDO:0000612.synonym: malignant neoplasm of lymphatic part of lymphoid system

MONDO:0000620.name: breast benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000620.def: a non-metastasizing neoplasm arising from the breast parenchyma.

MONDO:0000621.name: immune system cancer
MONDO:0000621.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the immune system

MONDO:0000624.name: benign female reproductive system neoplasm
MONDO:0000624.def: a non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the female reproductive system. representative examples include uterine corpus leiomyoma, endocervical polyp, and benign ovarian germ cell tumor.

MONDO:0000625.name: benign male reproductive system neoplasm
MONDO:0000625.def: a non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the male reproductive system. representative examples include benign prostate phyllodes tumor, benign sertoli cell tumor, seminal vesicle cystadenoma, and epididymal adenomatoid tumor.

MONDO:0000626.name: vestibular gland benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000626.def: a benign neoplasm that involves the vestibular gland.

MONDO:0000627.name: benign endocrine neoplasm
MONDO:0000627.def: a non-metastasizing, functioning or non-functioning neoplasm that arises from an endocrine organ. representative examples include thyroid gland follicular adenoma and parathyroid gland adenoma.

MONDO:0000628.name: central nervous system organ benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000628.def: a benign neoplasm that involves the central nervous system.

MONDO:0000629.name: cardiovascular organ benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000629.def: a benign neoplasm that involves the cardiovascular system.

MONDO:0000630.name: immune system organ benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000630.def: a benign neoplasm that involves the immune organ.

MONDO:0000631.name: bone benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000631.def: a neoplasm that arises from the bone or articular cartilage and does not invade adjacent tissues or metastasize to other anatomic sites.

MONDO:0000632.name: uterine benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000632.def: a non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the uterine corpus or the cervix. representative examples include leiomyoma, adenomyoma, and endocervical polyp.

MONDO:0000633.name: sensory organ benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000633.def: a benign neoplasm that involves the sense organ.

MONDO:0000634.name: thoracic benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000634.def: a non-metastasizing neoplasm arising from any of the organs of the thoracic cavity. representative examples include pleural adenomatoid tumor, chest wall lipoma, mediastinal schwannoma, and lung hamartoma.
MONDO:0000634.synonym: thoracic segment of trunk benign neoplasm

MONDO:0000636.name: musculoskeletal system benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000636.def: a benign neoplasm that involves the musculoskeletal system.

MONDO:0000637.name: musculoskeletal system cancer
MONDO:0000637.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the musculoskeletal system

MONDO:0000638.name: benign glioma
MONDO:0000638.def: a form of glioma without malignant characteristics.

MONDO:0000639.name: cartilage cancer
MONDO:0000639.def: a cancer involving a cartilage tissue.

MONDO:0000640.name: central nervous system primitive neuroectodermal neoplasm
MONDO:0000640.def: a neuroectodermal tumor that involves the central nervous system.
MONDO:0000640.synonym: primitive neuroectodermal tumour of central nervous system

MONDO:0000641.name: obsolete cerebellar medulloblastoma
MONDO:0000641.def: obsolete. a cerebellum cancer that begins in the lower part of the brain on the floor of the skull.

MONDO:0000642.name: brain meningioma
MONDO:0000642.def: a meningioma (disease) that involves the brain.

MONDO:0000643.name: vulvar benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000643.def: a non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the vulva. representative examples include cellular angiofibroma, melanocytic nevus, nodular hidradenoma, and bartholin gland adenoma.

MONDO:0000644.name: cervical benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000644.def: a non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the cervix. representative examples include squamous papilloma, endocervical polyp, and rhabdomyoma.

MONDO:0000645.name: fallopian tube benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000645.def: a non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the fallopian tube. representative examples include papilloma, adenofibroma, and leiomyoma.

MONDO:0000646.name: ovarian benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000646.def: a non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the ovary. representative examples include serous cystadenoma, mucinous cystadenoma, clear cell adenofibroma, benign brenner tumor, thecoma, and fibroma.

MONDO:0000647.name: benign vaginal neoplasm
MONDO:0000647.def: a non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the vagina. representative examples include squamous papilloma and melanocytic nevus.

MONDO:0000648.name: nervous system benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000648.def: abnormal growth of cells in the nervous system without evidence of malignant characteristics. unlike other organ systems, tumors in the central nervous system can have benign histological characteristics but still have life threatening effects due to their location within the neuraxis (e.g., brainstem gliomas).

MONDO:0000649.name: sensory system cancer
MONDO:0000649.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the sensory system

MONDO:0000650.name: peritoneal benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000650.def: a non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the peritoneal cavity. representative examples include adenomatoid tumor and disseminated peritoneal leiomyomatosis.

MONDO:0000651.name: obsolete thoracic disorder
MONDO:0000651.def: obsolete. a non-neoplastic or neoplastic disorder that affects the thorax and/or the organs of the thoracic cavity. representative examples include pleural infection, mediastinitis, thymoma, mediastinal lymphoma, and pleural mesothelioma.
MONDO:0000651.synonym: thoracic segment of trunk disease or disorder

MONDO:0000652.name: integumentary system benign neoplasm
MONDO:0000652.def: a benign neoplasm that involves the integumental system.

MONDO:0000653.name: integumentary system cancer
MONDO:0000653.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the integumental system

MONDO:0000654.name: benign connective and soft tissue neoplasm
MONDO:0000654.def: a non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the connective and soft tissue. representative examples include lipoma, leiomyoma, fibroma, and osteoma.

MONDO:0000659.name: delta-heavy chain disease
MONDO:0000659.def: a heavy chain disease that results from an overproduction of delta antibody (igd).

MONDO:0000660.name: akinetopsia
MONDO:0000660.def: an agnosia that is a loss of motion perception.

MONDO:0000661.name: alexithymia
MONDO:0000661.def: an agnosia that is a deficiency in understanding, processing, or describing emotions.

MONDO:0000662.name: amusia
MONDO:0000662.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to recognize musical notes, rhythms, and intervals.

MONDO:0000663.name: anosognosia
MONDO:0000663.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to gain feedback about one's own condition or impairments.

MONDO:0000664.name: apperceptive agnosia
MONDO:0000664.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to distinguish visual shapes.

MONDO:0000665.name: apraxia
MONDO:0000665.def: apraxia is a neurological disorder characterized by the inability to perform tasks or movements, despite having the desire and physical ability to perform them. it is caused by damage to the brain, especially the parietal lobe, and can arise from many diseases, tumors, a stroke, or traumatic brain injury. in some cases it is present from birth. there are several types of apraxia, which may occur alone or together. these include: buccofacial or orofacial apraxia is the inability to carry out facial movements on demand. this may include licking the lips, sticking out the tongue, whistling, coughing, or winking. ideational apraxia is the inability to carryout learned, complex tasks with multiple, sequential movements. this may include dressing, eating, and bathing. ideomotor apraxia is the inability to perform a learned task (such as using a tool) or communicate using gestures (like waving good-bye). limb-kinetic apraxia is the inability to make fine, precise movements with an arm or leg. this may include buttoning a shirt or tying a shoe. verbal apraxia is difficulty coordinating mouth and speech movements. verbal apraxia may be acquired or present from birth. constructional apraxia is the inability to copy, draw, or construct simple figures. oculomotor apraxia is difficulty moving the eyes on command. treatment of apraxia may include physical, speech, or occupational therapy. if apraxia occurs as a symptom of another disorder, treatment should be directed to the underlying condition.

MONDO:0000666.name: associative visual agnosia
MONDO:0000666.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to recognize visual scenes or classes of objects but retain the abilty to describe them.

MONDO:0000667.name: auditory agnosia
MONDO:0000667.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to distinguishing environmental and non-verbal auditory cues including difficulty distinguishing speech from non-speech sounds even though hearing is usually normal.

MONDO:0000668.name: autotopagnosia
MONDO:0000668.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to orient parts of the body.

MONDO:0000669.name: color agnosia
MONDO:0000669.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to recognize a color, while being able to perceive or distinguish it.

MONDO:0000670.name: cortical deafness
MONDO:0000670.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to perceive any auditory information but whose hearing is intact.

MONDO:0000671.name: finger agnosia
MONDO:0000671.def: an agnosia characterized by an inabilty to distinguish, name, or recognize the fingers

MONDO:0000672.name: form agnosia
MONDO:0000672.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to perceive a whole object while perceiving only parts of details.

MONDO:0000673.name: integrative agnosia
MONDO:0000673.def: agnosia characterized by the inability to integrate perceptual wholes within knowledge.

MONDO:0000674.name: mirror agnosia
MONDO:0000674.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to acknowledge objects in the neglected field that are visible when a mirror reflects the object visible in the non-neglected field.

MONDO:0000675.name: pain agnosia
MONDO:0000675.def: loss of the ability to perceive and process pain.

MONDO:0000676.name: phonagnosia
MONDO:0000676.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to recognize familiar voices.

MONDO:0000677.name: semantic agnosia
MONDO:0000677.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to visually recognize an object while maintaining the use of non-visual sensory systems such as feeling, tapping, smelling, rocking or flicking the object to recognize the object.

MONDO:0000678.name: simultanagnosia
MONDO:0000678.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to recgonize a whole image or scene while retianing the ability to recognize objects or details in their visual field one at a time.

MONDO:0000679.name: social emotional agnosia
MONDO:0000679.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to perceive facial expression, body language and intonation, rendering them unable to non-verbally perceive people's emotions and limiting that aspect of social interaction.

MONDO:0000680.name: astereognosia
MONDO:0000680.def: an agnosia that is the loss of the ability to recognize objects by touch based on its texture, size and weight.

MONDO:0000681.name: tactile agnosia
MONDO:0000681.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to recognize or identify objects by touch alone.

MONDO:0000682.name: time agnosia
MONDO:0000682.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to comprehend the succession and duration of events.

MONDO:0000683.name: topographical agnosia
MONDO:0000683.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to rely on visual cues to guide them directionally due to the inability to recognize objects.

MONDO:0000684.name: verbal auditory agnosia
MONDO:0000684.def: an agnosia that is a loss of the ability to recognizing spoken words as semantically meaningful.

MONDO:0000685.name: visual agnosia
MONDO:0000685.def: an inability to recognize or interpret objects by sight.

MONDO:0000686.name: alexia without agraphia
MONDO:0000686.def: loss of the power to comprehend written materials despite preservation of the ability to write (i.e., alexia without agraphia). this condition is generally attributed to lesions that 'disconnect' the visual cortex of the non-dominant hemisphere from language centers in the dominant hemisphere. this may occur when a dominant visual cortex injury is combined with underlying white matter lesions that involve crossing fibers from the occipital lobe of the opposite hemisphere. (from adams et al., principles of neurology, 6th ed, p483)

MONDO:0000687.name: diffuse alopecia areata
MONDO:0000687.def: an alopecia areata that involves diffuse loss of hair over the whole scalp.

MONDO:0000688.name: inborn organic aciduria
MONDO:0000688.def: an inherited disorder that affects the metabolism of any acidic compound containing carbon in a covalent linkage.
MONDO:0000688.synonym: rare inborn error of organic acid metabolic process

MONDO:0000689.name: obsolete survival motor neuron spinal muscular atrophy

MONDO:0000690.name: body dysmorphic disorder
MONDO:0000690.def: preoccupations with appearance or self-image causing significant distress or impairment in important areas of functioning.

MONDO:0000693.name: bipolar ii disorder
MONDO:0000693.def: a bipolar disorder that is characterized by at least one hypomanic episode and at least one major depressive episode; with this disorder, depressive episodes are more frequent and more intense than manic episodes.

MONDO:0000694.name: seasonal affective disorder
MONDO:0000694.def: a syndrome characterized by depressions that recur annually at the same time each year, usually during the winter months. other symptoms include anxiety, irritability, decreased energy, increased appetite (carbohydrate cravings), increased duration of sleep, and weight gain. sad (seasonal affective disorder) can be treated by daily exposure to bright artificial lights (phototherapy), during the season of recurrence.

MONDO:0000698.name: gamma-amino butyric acid metabolism disorder
MONDO:0000698.def: an amino acid metabolic disorder characterized by impairment of the gaba catabolic pathway.

MONDO:0000700.name: familial hemiplegic migraine
MONDO:0000700.def: a migraine disorder characterized by individual and family history of aura that includes motor weakness.

MONDO:0000701.name: ischemic colitis
MONDO:0000701.def: inflammation of the colon due to colonic ischemia resulting from alterations in systemic circulation or local vasculature.

MONDO:0000702.name: microscopic colitis
MONDO:0000702.def: inflammation of the colon that is only apparent by microscopic examination.

MONDO:0000703.name: collagenous colitis
MONDO:0000703.def: a type of microscopic colitis of unknown etiology. it is characterized by the presence of collagen deposits in the lamina propria of the colonic mucosa. patients present with chronic watery diarrhea. colonoscopy reveals normal-appearing mucosa. the diagnosis is made with the microscopic examination of the colonic biopsy samples.

MONDO:0000704.name: lymphocytic colitis
MONDO:0000704.def: microscopic colitis characterized by the accumulation of lymphocytes in the colonic epithelium and lamina propria. patients present with chronic watery diarrhea. colonoscopy reveals normal colonic mucosa. the diagnosis is made with the microscopic examination of the colonic biopsy samples.

MONDO:0000705.name: clostridium difficile colitis
MONDO:0000705.def: a bacterial infection of the colon secondary to infection with clostridium difficile bacteria. this infection generally results from the loss of normal gut flora secondary to recent antibiotic use, and manifests as copious watery stools, with associated abdominal pain and myalgia. c. difficile is the most common cause of pseudomembranous colitis, and can progress to toxic megacolon if left untreated.

MONDO:0000706.name: chemical colitis
MONDO:0000706.def: a colitis caused by the introduction of harsh chemicals to the colon by an enema or other procedure. chemical colitis can resemble ulcerative colitis, infectious colitis and pseudomembranous colitis endoscopically.

MONDO:0000707.name: diversion colitis
MONDO:0000707.def: a colitis which can occur as a complication of ileostomy or colostomy.

MONDO:0000709.name: crohn ileitis
MONDO:0000709.def: an crohn disease involving a pathogenic inflammatory response in the ileum.

MONDO:0000710.name: gastroduodenal crohn disease
MONDO:0000710.def: an inflammatory bowel disease characterized by inflammation located in stomach and located in duodenum, has symptom nausea, has symptom vomiting, has symptom weight loss and has symptom loss of appetite.

MONDO:0000715.name: lymph node adenoid cystic carcinoma
MONDO:0000715.def: a adenoid cystic carcinoma that involves the lymph node.

MONDO:0000716.name: agraphia
MONDO:0000716.def: an acquired writing disorder causing a loss in the ability to communicate through writing, either due to some motor dysfunction or the inability to spell.

MONDO:0000721.name: xanthinuria
MONDO:0000721.def: a metabolic metabolic disorder characterized by excess urinary excretion of the purine base xanthine.

MONDO:0000722.name: non-syndromic synpolydactyly
MONDO:0000722.def: a synpolydactyly that is not part of a larger syndrome.

MONDO:0000723.name: stutter disorder
MONDO:0000723.def: a speech disorder characterized by frequent sound or syllable repetitions, sound prolongations, or other dysfluencies that are inappropriate for the individual's age.

MONDO:0000724.name: specific language impairment
MONDO:0000724.def: a language disorder characterized by difficulty in language acquisition despite otherwise normal development and in the absence of any obvious explanatory factors.

MONDO:0000726.name: idiopathic scoliosis
MONDO:0000726.def: a scoliosis with no known cause.

MONDO:0000727.name: scapuloperoneal myopathy
MONDO:0000727.def: a muscular dystrophy which begins at the lower legs and affects the shoulder region earlier and more severely than distal arm.

MONDO:0000728.name: ptosis
MONDO:0000728.def: the drooping of the upper eyelid.

MONDO:0000732.name: combined oxidative phosphorylation deficiency
MONDO:0000732.def: a mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder in which multiple mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes.

MONDO:0000736.name: dyschromatosis universalis hereditaria
MONDO:0000736.def: a pigmentation disease characterized by reticulate hyper- and hypo-pigmentated macules in a generalized distribution.

MONDO:0000740.name: adenoid hypertrophy
MONDO:0000740.def: an upper respiratory tract disease characterized by the unusual growth of the adenoid tonsil; has symptom snoring, has symptom hyponasality, has symptom otitis media with effusion, has symptom mouth breathing.

MONDO:0000741.name: angular cheilitis
MONDO:0000741.def: inflammation of the skin at the corners of the mouth characterized by redness, fissures or crusts.

MONDO:0000743.name: oral hairy leukoplakia
MONDO:0000743.def: an epithelial hyperplasia of the oral cavity mucosa associated with epstein-barr virus and found almost exclusively in persons with hiv infection. the lesion consists of a white patch that is often corrugated or hairy.

MONDO:0000744.name: lung abscess
MONDO:0000744.def: a bacterial, fungal or parasitic abscess that develops in the lung parenchyma. causes include aspiration pneumonia, necrotizing pneumonia, necrotizing malignant tumors, and wegener's granulomatosis.

MONDO:0000745.name: cardiac arrest
MONDO:0000745.def: cessation of breathing and/or cardiac function.

MONDO:0000746.name: obsolete inguinal hernia
MONDO:0000746.def: obsolete. the protrusion of a sac-like structure containing fibroadipose tissue through an abnormal opening in the inguinal region.

MONDO:0000747.name: obsolete umbilical hernia
MONDO:0000747.def: obsolete. a congenital defect in the muscles of the abdominal wall that results in the intestines and other abdominal organs developing outside the abdominal wall covered in a sac.

MONDO:0000748.name: mastoiditis
MONDO:0000748.def: inflammation of the mucosal lining of the mastoid antrum and mastoid air cell system of the mastoid process.

MONDO:0000749.name: breast abscess
MONDO:0000749.def: a breast disease characterized by a collection of pus in the breast.

MONDO:0000750.name: dental abscess
MONDO:0000750.def: a tooth disease characterized by a localized collection of pus associated with a tooth.

MONDO:0000751.name: cervical polyp
MONDO:0000751.def: a polyp that arises from the surface of the cervix.

MONDO:0000754.name: anal fistula
MONDO:0000754.def: a pathologic tract that connects an opening in the anal canal to the perianal skin. in the vast majority of cases there is a history of perianal abscess.

MONDO:0000755.name: ectopic pregnancy
MONDO:0000755.def: an abnormal pregnancy in which the conception is implanted outside the endometrial cavity.

MONDO:0000756.name: parameningeal embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma
MONDO:0000756.def: an embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma located in the parameningeal region.

MONDO:0000757.name: glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis
MONDO:0000757.def: an osteoporosis caused by chronic glucocorticoid use. glucocorticoids impair the replication, differentiation and function of osteoblasts and induce the apoptosis of mature osteoblasts and osteocytes; the also favor osteoclastogenesis leading to an increase in bone resorption.

MONDO:0000758.name: bacillary angiomatosis
MONDO:0000758.def: a condition that is caused by infection with bartonella, and which is characterized by vascular proliferation, usually in immunocompromised individuals.

MONDO:0000761.name: syndrome caused by partial chromosomal deletion
MONDO:0000761.def: a chromosomal disorder consisting of the absence of a part of a chromosome.

MONDO:0000762.name: syndrome caused by partial chromosomal duplication
MONDO:0000762.def: a chromosomal disorder consisting of the presence of a part of a chromosome in more copies than in a regular genome.

MONDO:0000764.name: epithelial-stromal tgfbi dystrophy
MONDO:0000764.def: any corneal dystrophy (disease) in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the tgfbi gene.

MONDO:0000766.name: corneal endothelial dystrophy
MONDO:0000766.def: a corneal dystrophy (disease) that involves the corneal epithelium.

MONDO:0000769.name: obsolete chicken egg allergy
MONDO:0000769.def: obsolete. an egg allergy triggered by gallus gallus eggs.

MONDO:0000770.name: obsolete shellfish allergy
MONDO:0000770.def: obsolete. allergic reaction to shellfish or shellfish products.

MONDO:0000771.name: allergic respiratory disease
MONDO:0000771.def: a respiratory system disease with a basis in a pathological type i hypersensitivity reaction.

MONDO:0000773.name: obsolete timothy grass allergy
MONDO:0000773.def: obsolete. a allergy involving a phleum pratense.

MONDO:0000774.name: autoimmune neuropathy
MONDO:0000774.def: an autoimmune form of peripheral neuropathy.

MONDO:0000775.name: drug allergy
MONDO:0000775.def: immunologically mediated adverse reactions to medicinal substances used legally or illegally.

MONDO:0000776.name: obsolete metal allergy
MONDO:0000776.def: obsolete. a allergy involving a metal allergen.

MONDO:0000777.name: gastrointestinal allergy
MONDO:0000777.def: a allergic disease that involves the digestive tract.

MONDO:0000778.name: obsolete fruit allergy
MONDO:0000778.def: obsolete. a food allergy triggered by a plant fruit product.

MONDO:0000779.name: obsolete apple allergy
MONDO:0000779.def: obsolete. a allergy involving a malus domestica.

MONDO:0000780.name: obsolete apricot allergy
MONDO:0000780.def: obsolete. a allergy involving a prunus armeniaca.

MONDO:0000781.name: obsolete cherry allergy
MONDO:0000781.def: obsolete. a fruit allergy triggered by prunus avium plant fruit food product.

MONDO:0000782.name: obsolete indian plum allergy
MONDO:0000782.def: obsolete. a fruit allergy triggered by ziziphus mauritiana plant fruit food product.

MONDO:0000783.name: obsolete orange allergy
MONDO:0000783.def: obsolete. a fruit allergy triggered by citrus sinensis plant fruit food product.

MONDO:0000784.name: obsolete melon allergy
MONDO:0000784.def: obsolete. a fruit allergy triggered by cucumis melo plant fruit food product.

MONDO:0000785.name: obsolete peach allergy
MONDO:0000785.def: obsolete. a allergy involving a prunus persica.

MONDO:0000786.name: obsolete plum allergy
MONDO:0000786.def: obsolete. a allergy involving a prunus domestica.

MONDO:0000787.name: obsolete tomato allergy
MONDO:0000787.def: obsolete. a allergy involving a solanum lycopersicum.

MONDO:0000789.name: obsolete atlantic cod allergy
MONDO:0000789.def: obsolete. a allergy involving a gadus morhua.

MONDO:0000790.name: obsolete atlantic salmon allergy
MONDO:0000790.def: obsolete. a allergy involving a salmo salar.

MONDO:0000791.name: obsolete carp allergy
MONDO:0000791.def: obsolete. a allergy involving a cyprinus carpio.

MONDO:0000793.name: obsolete rainbow trout allergy
MONDO:0000793.def: obsolete. a allergy involving a oncorhynchus mykiss.

MONDO:0000794.name: obsolete beta-lactam allergy
MONDO:0000794.def: obsolete. a allergy involving a beta-lactam.

MONDO:0000796.name: obsolete cow milk allergy
MONDO:0000796.def: obsolete. a allergy involving cow mile.
