MONDO:0004462.def: a mucinous cystic neoplasm that arises from the extrahepatic bile ducts.
MONDO:0004462.synonym: extrahepatic bile duct mucinous cystic neoplasm

MONDO:0004463.name: cellular phase chronic idiopathic myelofibrosis
MONDO:0004463.def: primary myelofibrosis characterized by bone marrow hypercellularity and the presence of atypical megakaryocytes. there is no increase in the percentage of myeloblasts and no significant increase in reticulin or collagen fibrosis in the bone marrow.

MONDO:0004464.name: nephrogenic adenoma of the urethra
MONDO:0004464.def: a metaplastic lesion of the urothelium found in the urethra. it is characterized by the presence of aggregates of cuboidal or hobnail cells and represents a reaction of the urothelium to injury caused by instrumentation, surgery or calculi.

MONDO:0004465.name: periampullary adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0004465.def: an adenocarcinoma that arises from the periampullary region.

MONDO:0004467.name: mature gastric teratoma
MONDO:0004467.def: a benign teratoma that arises from the stomach.

MONDO:0004468.name: anal canal paget disease
MONDO:0004468.def: paget disease involving the squamous epithelium of the anal canal.
MONDO:0004468.synonym: paget's disease of the anal canal

MONDO:0004471.name: bacterial arthritis
MONDO:0004471.def: the inflammation of one or more joints caused by a bacterial infection within the joint space. symptoms include pain, stiffness, and decreased range of motion in the affected joint.

MONDO:0004472.name: breast columnar cell mucinous carcinoma
MONDO:0004472.def: an invasive breast adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of tall columnar neoplastic cells that contain intracytoplasmic mucin. grossly, cystic changes are not identified.

MONDO:0004473.name: epiglottis cancer
MONDO:0004473.def: a malignant neoplasm that affects the epiglottis. the vast majority of cases are squamous cell carcinomas.

MONDO:0004474.name: gallbladder lymphoma
MONDO:0004474.def: a lymphoma that arises from the gallbladder, with the bulk of the tumor located at this site.

MONDO:0004475.name: thymus clear cell carcinoma
MONDO:0004475.def: a rare, usually aggressive, primary thymic carcinoma, characterized by the presence of carcinoma cells with clear cytoplasm.

MONDO:0004476.name: obsolete thymus sarcomatoid carcinoma
MONDO:0004476.def: obsolete. a rare, usually aggressive, primary thymic carcinoma, characterized by the presence of tumor cells morphologically resembling soft tissue sarcoma.

MONDO:0004477.name: adrenal gland ganglioneuroblastoma
MONDO:0004477.def: a ganglioneuroblastoma arising from the adrenal gland.

MONDO:0004478.name: pregerminal center chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma
MONDO:0004478.def: a recently recognized variant of chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (cll/sll) that lacks somatic hypermutations of the immunoglobulin heavy chain (igh) genes, implying pregerminal center b-cell origin. microarray gene expression profiling studies have demonstrated the expression of zap-70 gene (syk family tyrosine kinase) in this subset of cll/cll. patients with this variant of cll/sll have an unfavorable prognosis compared to those with somatic hypermutations of the igh genes, with a median survival of approximately 6-8 years.
MONDO:0004478.synonym: pregerminal center chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma

MONDO:0004479.name: malignant childhood germ cell neoplasm
MONDO:0004479.def: a malignant germ cell tumor that occurs during childhood.

MONDO:0004480.name: obsolete pancreatic invasive intraductal papillary-mucinous carcinoma

MONDO:0004481.name: pancreatic intraductal papillary-mucinous neoplasm with an associated invasive carcinoma
MONDO:0004481.def: a pancreatic intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm characterized by the presence of a focal or multifocal invasive carcinomatous component. the invasive carcinoma is either colloid or ductal adenocarcinoma.

MONDO:0004482.name: fibroosseous pseudotumor of the digits
MONDO:0004482.def: a non-neoplastic soft tissue disorder characterized by the localized formation of reactive fibrous and bone tissues. it usually occurs in the subcutaneous tissue of the proximal phalanx. less frequently, it involves the toe. it presents with swelling and pain of the affected area. the prognosis is excellent. however, incomplete excision may lead to the re-growth of the lesion.

MONDO:0004483.name: thyroid gland oncocytic adenoma
MONDO:0004483.def: a thyroid gland adenoma composed of large cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm and large nuclei with prominent nucleoli.

MONDO:0004484.name: gallbladder melanoma
MONDO:0004484.def: a melanoma that arises from the gallbladder.

MONDO:0004485.name: interstitial myocarditis
MONDO:0004485.def: inflammation of the heart characterized by infiltration of the interstitial tissues by inflammatory cells, histiocytes, and the formation of granulomas. giant cells are often present.

MONDO:0004486.name: endocervical type cervical adenomyoma
MONDO:0004486.def: an adenomyoma that arises from the cervix and is characterized by the presence of endocervical mucinous glands and a smooth muscle cell component. there is no atypia or significant mitotic activity present.

MONDO:0004487.name: endometrial type cervical adenomyoma
MONDO:0004487.def: an adenomyoma that arises from the cervix and is characterized by the presence of endometrial type glands and endometrial stroma, surrounded by smooth muscle. there is no evidence of atypia.

MONDO:0004488.name: cervical atypical polypoid adenomyoma
MONDO:0004488.def: an adenomyoma that arises from the cervix and is characterized by the presence of a glandular component exhibiting architectural complexity.

MONDO:0004489.name: fallopian tube gestational choriocarcinoma
MONDO:0004489.def: a malignant trophoblastic tumor that arises from the fallopian tube during pregnancy.
MONDO:0004489.synonym: gestational choriocarcinoma of the fallopian tube

MONDO:0004490.name: gestational uterine corpus choriocarcinoma
MONDO:0004490.def: a gestational choriocarcinoma that involves the body of uterus.
MONDO:0004490.synonym: gestational choriocarcinoma of body of uterus

MONDO:0004491.name: uterine corpus choriocarcinoma
MONDO:0004491.def: an aggressive malignant tumor arising from trophoblastic cells in the uterus during pregnancy. approximately half of the cases develop from a complete hydatidiform mole. there is often marked elevation of human chorionic gonadotropin (hcg) in the blood. choriocarcinomas disseminate rapidly through the hematogenous route; the lungs are most frequently affected.

MONDO:0004492.name: mediastinitis
MONDO:0004492.def: an inflammatory process affecting the mediastinum.

MONDO:0004493.name: testicular yolk sac tumor, papillary pattern
MONDO:0004493.def: a yolk sac tumor that arises from the testis and is characterized by the presence of numerous papillary structures that are lined by cells with prominent nucleoli.
MONDO:0004493.synonym: testicular yolk sac tumor, papillary pattern

MONDO:0004494.name: testicular yolk sac tumor, hepatoid pattern
MONDO:0004494.def: a yolk sac tumor that arises from the testis and is characterized by the presence of hepatoid cells collections.
MONDO:0004494.synonym: testicular yolk sac tumor, hepatoid pattern

MONDO:0004495.name: myotonic cataract
MONDO:0004495.def: a cataract occurring as a sequela of myotonic dystrophy.

MONDO:0004496.name: myocarditis
MONDO:0004496.def: myocarditis is a condition that is characterized by inflammation of the heart muscle (myocardium). some affected people have no noticeable symptoms of the condition. when present, signs and symptoms may include chest pain, abnormal heartbeat, shortness of breath, fatigue, signs of infection (i.e. fever, headache, sore throat, diarrhea), and leg swelling. myocarditis can be caused by a variety of factors including infections (viral, bacterial, parasitic, and fungal), allergic reactions to certain medications, and exposure to certain chemicals. it can also be associated with other inflammatory conditions such as lupus, wegener's granulomatosis, giant cell arteritis and takayasu's arteritis. most cases occur sporadically in people with no family history of the condition. treatment aims to address the underlying cause of the condition. medications and rarely, a heart transplant may be needed if the heart muscle becomes weak.

MONDO:0004497.name: tertiary syphilis
MONDO:0004497.def: a stage of syphilis that occurs fifteen to thirty years after the initial infection; it can include gumma formation and cardiovascular or central nervous system involvement (neurosyphilis).

MONDO:0004498.name: sacral spinal canal and spinal cord meningioma
MONDO:0004498.def: a meningioma that arises from the meninges of the sacral region of the spinal cord.

MONDO:0004499.name: lung hilum carcinoma
MONDO:0004499.def: a lung carcinoma arising from the hilum of the lung.

MONDO:0004500.name: lung superior sulcus carcinoma
MONDO:0004500.def: a carcinoma originating from the apical lung. most superior sulcus lung carcinomas are bronchogenic carcinomas. this carcinoma may be associated with pancoast syndrome. lt is also known as pancoast tumor.

MONDO:0004501.name: fallopian tube cystadenofibroma
MONDO:0004501.def: a rare, benign, asymptomatic neoplasm that arises from the fallopian tube. the tumors are round and solitary and contain connective tissue and cystic structures lined by serous-type epithelium. the majority of cases are incidental findings during operation for an unrelated gynecologic disorder.

MONDO:0004503.name: upper clivus meningioma
MONDO:0004503.def: a meningioma that affects the upper clivus.

MONDO:0004504.name: penile urethral cancer
MONDO:0004504.def: a urethra cancer that involves the penis.

MONDO:0004505.name: central breast papilloma
MONDO:0004505.def: a benign papillary neoplasm that arises in a large duct of the breast. it is characterized by the presence of a fibrovascular core that is lined by benign epithelial and myoepithelial proliferations. patients usually present with nipple discharge.

MONDO:0004506.name: microscopic breast papilloma
MONDO:0004506.def: a benign papillary neoplasm that arises in a terminal ductal lobular unit. it is characterized by the presence of a fibrovascular core that is lined by benign epithelial and myoepithelial proliferations. peripheral breast papillomas are often multiple and are usually found microscopically. patients are often asymptomatic.

MONDO:0004507.name: atypical breast papilloma
MONDO:0004507.def: an intraductal papilloma of the breast characterized by the presence of focal epithelial atypia.

MONDO:0004508.name: periapical periodontitis
MONDO:0004508.def: inflammation of the periapical tissue. it includes general, unspecified, or acute nonsuppurative inflammation. chronic nonsuppurative inflammation is periapical granuloma. suppurative inflammation is periapical abscess.

MONDO:0004509.name: intrahepatic biliary papillomatosis
MONDO:0004509.def: a non-invasive, papillary epithelial neoplasm that arises from the epithelium of the intrahepatic bile ducts.

MONDO:0004510.name: inflammatory liposarcoma
MONDO:0004510.def: a rare morphologic variant of well differentiated liposarcoma occurring most often in the retroperitoneum. it is characterized by the presence of a predominant inflammatory infiltrate composed of lymphoplasmacytic aggregates.

MONDO:0004511.name: lower clivus meningioma
MONDO:0004511.def: a meningioma that affects the lower clivus.

MONDO:0004512.name: meningeal melanomatosis
MONDO:0004512.def: a meningeal melanoma with secondary diffuse meningeal spread. (who)

MONDO:0004513.name: adult pleomorphic rhabdomyosarcoma
MONDO:0004513.def: an aggressive rhabdomyosarcoma occurring in adults. the neoplasm is characterized by the presence of bizarre round, spindle, and polygonal cells. clinical presentation includes a rapidly enlarging painful mass usually in the lower extremities.

MONDO:0004514.name: chronic rhinitis
MONDO:0004514.def: chronic inflammation of the nasal cavity mucosa. it may lead to post-nasal drip resulting in chronic sore throat and chronic cough.

MONDO:0004517.name: ureter tuberculosis
MONDO:0004517.def: a tuberculosis that involves the ureter.

MONDO:0004518.name: anterior urethra cancer
MONDO:0004518.def: a malignant neoplasm that affects the portion of the urethra that is close to the outside of the body.
MONDO:0004518.synonym: malignant tumour of the anterior urethra

MONDO:0004519.name: synovial angioma
MONDO:0004519.def: a rare hemangioma arising from synovium lining surfaces.

MONDO:0004520.name: intratubular embryonal carcinoma
MONDO:0004520.def: stage 0 includes: ptis, n0, m0, s0. ptis: intratubular germ cell neoplasia (carcinoma in situ). n0: regional lymph node metastasis. m0: no distant metastasis. s0: marker study levels within normal limits. (ajcc 6th and 7th eds.)
MONDO:0004520.synonym: stage 0 testicular embryonal carcinoma ajcc v7

MONDO:0004521.name: adult epithelioid sarcoma
MONDO:0004521.def: an epithelioid sarcoma occurring in adults.

MONDO:0004522.name: peritonitis
MONDO:0004522.def: inflammation of the peritoneum due to infection by bacteria or fungi. causes include liver disease, perforation of the gastrointestinal tract or biliary tract, and peritoneal dialysis. patients usually present with abdominal pain and tenderness, fever, chills, and nausea and vomiting. it is an emergency medical condition that requires prompt medical attention and treatment.

MONDO:0004523.name: clear cell squamous cell skin carcinoma
MONDO:0004523.def: a squamous cell carcinoma of the skin with a prominent clear cell component.
MONDO:0004523.synonym: clear cell squamous cell skin carcinoma

MONDO:0004524.name: thyroid gland atypical follicular adenoma
MONDO:0004524.def: a thyroid gland adenoma with increased cellularity and nuclear atypia. there is no capsular or vascular invasion. the clinical course is benign.

MONDO:0004525.name: scabies
MONDO:0004525.def: a contagious skin infection that is caused by the burrowing parasitic mite, sarcoptes scabiei, and is characterized by intense itching and small, raised red spots in the area of the mite burrows.

MONDO:0004526.name: mixed endometrial stromal and smooth muscle tumor
MONDO:0004526.def: a benign or malignant mesenchymal neoplasm of the uterine corpus. representative examples include leiomyoma, leiomyosarcoma, and endometrial stromal sarcoma.

MONDO:0004527.name: congenital granular cell tumor
MONDO:0004527.def: an instance of granular cell tumor that is present from birth.

MONDO:0004528.name: lymph node palisaded myofibroblastoma
MONDO:0004528.def: a myofibroblastoma arising from the inguinal lymph nodes. it is characterized by the presence of nuclear palisading.
MONDO:0004528.synonym: palisaded myofibroblastoma of the lymph node

MONDO:0004529.name: non-ossifying fibromyxoid tumor
MONDO:0004529.def: a rare soft tissue tumor of uncertain lineage characterized by the presence of neoplastic spindle to round cells forming cords in a fibromyxoid stroma. metaplastic bone formation is not present.

MONDO:0004530.name: early invasive cervical adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0004530.def: a cervical adenocarcinoma with minimal stromal invasion. the risk of local lymph node metastasis is insignificant and the prognosis is excellent.

MONDO:0004531.name: sclerosing adenosis of breast
MONDO:0004531.def: breast adenosis characterized by the proliferation of acini, a lobulated architectural pattern, and stromal sclerosis. the luminal epithelial and myopepithelial cells are preserved. microcalcifications and foci of apocrine metaplasia may be present.

MONDO:0004532.name: auditory system cancer
MONDO:0004532.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the auditory system

MONDO:0004533.name: perineural angioma
MONDO:0004533.def: a hemangioma arising from perineural tissues.

MONDO:0004534.name: microglandular adenosis of breast
MONDO:0004534.def: a rare variant of breast adenosis characterized by the proliferation of small round glands in a collagenous stroma. the epithelial cells are cuboidal and there are no myopepithelial cells present. there is no evidence of atypia.

MONDO:0004535.name: childhood choriocarcinoma of the ovary
MONDO:0004535.def: a non-gestational choriocarcinoma that arises from the ovary and occurs in children.

MONDO:0004536.name: obsolete villoglandular variant cervical mucinous adenocarcinoma

MONDO:0004537.name: intestinal variant cervical mucinous adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0004537.def: a cervical mucinous adenocarcinoma that resembles the large intestinal adenocarcinoma.

MONDO:0004538.name: endocervical type cervical mucinous adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0004538.def: a cervical mucinous adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of malignant glandular cells that resemble those of the endocervix.

MONDO:0004539.name: aortic malignant tumor
MONDO:0004539.def: a cancer that involves the aorta.

MONDO:0004540.name: epithelioid malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor
MONDO:0004540.def: a rare variant of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor composed predominantly or exclusively of epithelioid cells.
MONDO:0004540.synonym: malignant epithelioid tumour of the peripheral nerve sheath

MONDO:0004541.name: pseudoglandular variant testicular seminoma
MONDO:0004541.def: a morphologic variant of testicular seminoma characterized by the presence of seminoma cells arranged in pseudoglandular patterns and few lymphocytes.

MONDO:0004542.name: cervical adenosquamous carcinoma, glassy cell variant
MONDO:0004542.def: a poorly differentiated variant of adenosquamous carcinoma that arises from the cervix. it is characterized by the presence of large malignant cells with ground glass cytoplasm and stromal eosinophilic infiltrates.
MONDO:0004542.synonym: glassy cell variant cervical adenosquamous carcinoma

MONDO:0004543.name: enteric pattern testicular yolk sac tumor
MONDO:0004543.def: a yolk sac tumor that arises from the testis and is characterized by the presence of immature glands.
MONDO:0004543.synonym: testicular yolk sac tumor, enteric pattern

MONDO:0004544.name: chordoid meningioma
MONDO:0004544.def: a who grade ii, usually recurring meningioma characterized by the predominance of tissues that are histologically similar to chordoma.

MONDO:0004545.name: adult malignant schwannoma
MONDO:0004545.def: a malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor occurring during adulthood.

MONDO:0004546.name: lumbar plexus neoplasm
MONDO:0004546.def: a neoplasm (disease) that involves the lumbar nerve plexus.

MONDO:0004547.name: reticular pattern testicular yolk sac tumor
MONDO:0004547.def: a yolk sac tumor that arises from the testis and is characterized by the presence of a meshwork of small vacuolated cells resulting in a honeycomb appearance.
MONDO:0004547.synonym: testicular yolk sac tumor, reticular pattern

MONDO:0004548.name: adult type testicular granulosa cell tumor
MONDO:0004548.def: a rare sex cord-stromal tumor that arises from the testis in adults. gynecomastia is present in approximately a quarter of the patients. several morphologic patterns have been identified and include insular, gyriform, trabecular, pseudosarcomatous, and solid. metastases occur in approximately twenty percent of the cases.
MONDO:0004548.synonym: adult type testicular granulosa cell tumor

MONDO:0004549.name: cork-handlers' disease
MONDO:0004549.def: an extrinsic allergic alveolitis caused by inhalation of cork dust containing the antigens produced by the fungus penicillium glabrum. the symptoms include dyspnea, wheezing cough, fever and asthenia.

MONDO:0004550.name: malignant cornea melanoma
MONDO:0004550.def: a melanoma within the cornea of the eye.

MONDO:0004551.name: meckel diverticulitis
MONDO:0004551.def: inflammation of a congenital diverticulum of the lower intestine.

MONDO:0004552.name: microinvasive cervical squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0004552.def: a cervical squamous cell carcinoma with minimal stromal invasion. the risk of lymph node metastasis is low.
MONDO:0004552.synonym: early invasive cervical squamous cell carcinoma

MONDO:0004555.name: kidney angiomyolipoma
MONDO:0004555.def: an angiomyolipoma arising from the kidney.

MONDO:0004556.name: carcinoma arising in nasal papillomatosis
MONDO:0004556.def: a rare squamous cell carcinoma that either arises from or is associated with the presence of inverted papilloma in the nose.

MONDO:0004557.name: congenital fibrosarcoma
MONDO:0004557.def: a fibrosarcoma that occurs in infants. it shares identical morphologic features with adult fibrosarcoma but carries the t(12;15)(p13;q25) translocation that results in etv6-ntrk3 gene fusion. it usually affects the superficial and deep soft tissues of the extremities. the prognosis is generally much more favorable than for adult fibrosarcoma, and it rarely metastasizes.

MONDO:0004558.name: thyroid gland macrofollicular adenoma
MONDO:0004558.def: a thyroid gland adenoma composed of large size follicles.

MONDO:0004559.name: malignant glandular tumor of peripheral nerve sheath
MONDO:0004559.def: a variant of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor characterized by the presence of glandular epithelium.
MONDO:0004559.synonym: malignant glandular tumour of the peripheral nerve sheath

MONDO:0004561.name: retinal melanoma
MONDO:0004561.def: a melanoma affecting the retinal portion of the eye. --2003

MONDO:0004562.name: breast apocrine carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004562.def: a ductal breast carcinoma in situ, characterized by the presence of neoplastic epithelial cells with apocrine differentiation.
MONDO:0004562.synonym: apocrine carcinoma in situ of the breast

MONDO:0004564.name: thyroid malformation
MONDO:0004564.def: an anatomic abnormality of the thyroid gland.

MONDO:0004565.name: intestinal obstruction
MONDO:0004565.def: blockage of the normal flow of the intestinal contents within the bowel.

MONDO:0004566.name: postgastrectomy syndrome
MONDO:0004566.def: sequelae of gastrectomy from the second week after operation on. include recurrent or anastomotic ulcer, postprandial syndromes (dumping syndrome and late postprandial hypoglycemia), disordered bowel action, and nutritional deficiencies.

MONDO:0004567.name: ileus
MONDO:0004567.def: decrease in peristalsis in the absence of a mechanical bowel obstruction.

MONDO:0004568.name: paralytic ileus
MONDO:0004568.def: an ileus caused by abdominal or pelvic surgery, infections, disorders that affect the muscles and nerves, and medications. signs and symptoms include those of intestinal obstruction.

MONDO:0004570.name: intestinal volvulus
MONDO:0004570.def: twisting of a loop of bowel that results in intestinal obstruction.

MONDO:0004572.name: cyclothymic disorder
MONDO:0004572.def: an affective disorder characterized by periods of depression and hypomania. these may be separated by periods of normal mood.

MONDO:0004573.name: ariboflavinosis
MONDO:0004573.def: a dietary deficiency of riboflavin causing a syndrome chiefly marked by cheilitis, angular stomatitis, glossitis associated with a purplish red or magenta-colored tongue that may show fissures, corneal vascularization, dyssebacia, and anemia. (dorland, 27th ed)

MONDO:0004574.name: pyridoxine deficiency anemia
MONDO:0004574.def: deficiency of vitamin b6. it is usually caused by alcoholism, malabsorption, or as a side effect of medications. signs and symptoms include stomatitis, glossitis, dermatitis, peripheral neuropathy, irritability, seizures, and anemia.

MONDO:0004575.name: choline deficiency disease
MONDO:0004575.def: a condition produced by a deficiency of choline in animals. choline is known as a lipotropic agent because it has been shown to promote the transport of excess fat from the liver under certain conditions in laboratory animals. combined deficiency of choline (included in the b vitamin complex) and all other methyl group donors causes liver cirrhosis in some animals. unlike compounds normally considered as vitamins, choline does not serve as a cofactor in enzymatic reactions. (from saunders dictionary & encyclopedia of laboratory medicine and technology, 1984)

MONDO:0004577.name: corneal ulcer
MONDO:0004577.def: area of epithelial tissue loss from corneal surface; associated with inflammatory cells in the cornea and anterior chamber.

MONDO:0004579.name: retinoschisis
MONDO:0004579.def: an inherited or acquired disorder characterized by splitting of the retina into two layers. it results in loss of vision.

MONDO:0004582.name: rheumatic myocarditis
MONDO:0004582.def: inflammation of the myocardium in acute rheumatic heart disease.

MONDO:0004583.name: transient retinal arterial occlusion
MONDO:0004583.def: a partial, temporary occlusion of the retinal artery.

MONDO:0004585.name: polyhydramnios
MONDO:0004585.def: an excess quantity of amniotic fluid in the amniotic sac as compared to normal values. typically associated with an amniotic fluid index (afi) of greater than or equal to 25 cm or a single maximum vertical pocket (mvp) of greater than 8 cm.

MONDO:0004586.name: rheumatoid lung disease
MONDO:0004586.def: rheumatoid lung disease is a group of lung problems related to rheumatoid arthritis.

MONDO:0004587.name: hereditary night blindness
MONDO:0004587.def: an instance of night blindness that is caused by an inherited modification of the individual's genome.

MONDO:0004588.name: night blindness
MONDO:0004588.def: inability to see clearly in dim light.

MONDO:0004591.name: impetigo herpetiformis
MONDO:0004591.def: an impetigo that is characterized as a form of severe pustular psoriasis occurring in pregnancy.

MONDO:0004592.name: impetigo
MONDO:0004592.def: a contagious bacterial cutaneous infection that affects children and is usually caused by staphylococcus aureus. it usually presents in the face with honey colored scabs.

MONDO:0004593.name: bartholin duct cyst
MONDO:0004593.def: distension of the bartholin gland duct caused by an accumulation of mucus in the duct, usually as a result of obstruction of the gland duct orifice.

MONDO:0004596.name: cor pulmonale
MONDO:0004596.def: hypertrophy and dilation of the right ventricle of the heart that is caused by pulmonary hypertension. this condition is often associated with pulmonary parenchymal or vascular diseases, such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and pulmonary embolism.

MONDO:0004597.name: pulmonary embolism and infarction
MONDO:0004597.def: localized necrosis of lung tissue caused by obstruction of the arterial blood supply, most often due to pulmonary embolism.

MONDO:0004598.name: acute cor pulmonale
MONDO:0004598.def: a form of acute right heart failure produced by a sudden increase in resistance to blood flow in the pulmonary circulation.

MONDO:0004599.name: barbiturate abuse
MONDO:0004599.def: a substance abuse that involves the recurring use of barbiturate drugs despite negative consequences.

MONDO:0004601.name: ulcer of lower limbs
MONDO:0004601.def: ulcer of lower limbs is a chronic ulcer of skin where the ulcer is not a decubitus ulcer.

MONDO:0004604.name: hodgkin's lymphoma, lymphocytic-histiocytic predominance
MONDO:0004604.def: a subtype of classical hodgkin lymphoma with scattered hodgkin and reed-sternberg cells and a nodular or less often diffuse cellular background consisting of small lymphocytes and with an absence of neutrophils and eosinophils. (who, 2008)

MONDO:0004607.name: vallecula cancer
MONDO:0004607.def: a cancer involving a epiglottic vallecula.

MONDO:0004608.name: oropharynx cancer
MONDO:0004608.def: a primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm that affects the oropharynx.
MONDO:0004608.synonym: primary malignant neoplasm of lateral wall of oropharynx

MONDO:0004609.name: herpes simplex infectious disease
MONDO:0004609.def: a group of acute infections caused by herpes simplex virus type 1 or type 2 that is characterized by the development of one or more small fluid-filled vesicles with a raised erythematous base on the skin or mucous membrane. it occurs as a primary infection or recurs due to a reactivation of a latent infection. (dorland, 27th ed.)

MONDO:0004611.name: soft palate cancer
MONDO:0004611.def: a primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm that affects the soft palate.

MONDO:0004612.name: malignant histiocytosis
MONDO:0004612.def: distinctive neoplastic disorders of histiocytes. included are malignant neoplasms of macrophages and dendritic cells.

MONDO:0004613.name: acute intestinal ischemia
MONDO:0004613.def: ischemia of the intestine that is rapid in onset.

MONDO:0004614.name: chronic monocytic leukemia
MONDO:0004614.def: form of leukemia characterized by an uncontrolled proliferation of the myeloid lineage and their precursors (myeloid progenitor cells) in the bone marrow and other sites.

MONDO:0004615.name: upper gum cancer
MONDO:0004615.def: a cancer involving a gingiva of upper jaw.

MONDO:0004616.name: herpetic whitlow
MONDO:0004616.def: a painful blister of the periungual skin that is caused by herpes simplex virus type 1 or 2.

MONDO:0004617.name: recurrent hypersomnia
MONDO:0004617.def: disorders characterized by hypersomnolence during normal waking hours that may impair cognitive functioning. subtypes include primary hypersomnia disorders (e.g., idiopathic hypersomnolence; narcolepsy; and kleine-levin syndrome) and secondary hypersomnia disorders where excessive somnolence can be attributed to a known cause (e.g., drug affect, mental disorders, and sleep apnea syndrome). (from j neurol sci 1998 jan 8;153(2):192-202; thorpy, principles and practice of sleep medicine, 2nd ed, p320)

MONDO:0004619.name: measles
MONDO:0004619.def: a highly contagious viral infection caused by the measles virus. symptoms appear 8-12 days after exposure and include a rash, cough, fever and muscle pains that can last 4-7 days. measles vaccines are available to provide prophylaxis, usually combined with mumps and rubella vaccines (mmr).

MONDO:0004620.name: hodgkin's lymphoma, lymphocytic depletion
MONDO:0004620.def: a diffuse subtype of classical hodgkin lymphoma which is rich in hodgkin and reed-sternberg cells and/or depleted in non-neoplastic lymphocytes. (who, 2008)

MONDO:0004621.name: upper lip cancer
MONDO:0004621.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the upper lip.

MONDO:0004624.name: uvula cancer
MONDO:0004624.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the palatine uvula.

MONDO:0004627.name: duodenitis
MONDO:0004627.def: acute or chronic inflammation of the duodenum. causes include bacterial and viral infections and gastroesophageal reflux disease. symptoms include vomiting and abdominal pain.

MONDO:0004631.name: tongue cancer
MONDO:0004631.def: a malignant neoplasm affecting the tongue. the vast majority of cases are carcinomas.

MONDO:0004632.name: obsolete hodgkin's granuloma
MONDO:0004632.def: obsolete. an obsolete term referring to hodgkin lymphoma.
MONDO:0004632.synonym: hodgkin's granuloma, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites

MONDO:0004633.name: hodgkin's lymphoma, mixed cellularity
MONDO:0004633.def: a subtype of classical hodgkin lymphoma with scattered reed-sternberg and hodgkin cells in a diffuse or vaguely nodular mixed inflammatory background without nodular sclerosing fibrosis. (who, 2008)

MONDO:0004635.name: postcricoid region cancer
MONDO:0004635.def: a primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm that affects the postcricoid region.
MONDO:0004635.synonym: malignant tumour of the postcricoid area

MONDO:0004636.name: lip carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004636.def: a in situ carcinoma that involves the lip.

MONDO:0004637.name: aryepiglottic fold cancer
MONDO:0004637.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the aryepiglottic fold.
MONDO:0004637.synonym: malignant tumour aryepiglottic fold - hypopharyngeal aspect

MONDO:0004638.name: lymphosarcoma
MONDO:0004638.def: an antiquated term that refers to a non-hodgkin lymphoma composed of small and medium sized lymphocytes.

MONDO:0004639.name: perinatal necrotizing enterocolitis
MONDO:0004639.def: a fulminating disease of neonates in which there is extensive mucosal ulceration, pseudomembrane formation, submucosal hemorrhage, and necrosis usually of the right colon, cecum, terminal ileum, and appendix, possibly due to perinatal intestinal ischemia and bacterial invasion. progression can lead to necrosis, perforation and/or scarring of the intestinal tract.

MONDO:0004640.name: alcoholic gastritis
MONDO:0004640.def: inflammation of the stomach resulting from alcohol ingestion.
MONDO:0004640.synonym: alcoholic gastritis, without mention of hemorrhage

MONDO:0004641.name: skin carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004641.def: a in situ carcinoma that involves the zone of skin.
MONDO:0004641.synonym: zone of skin in situ carcinoma

MONDO:0004642.name: tonsillar pillar cancer
MONDO:0004642.def: a cancer that involves the tonsillar pillar.

MONDO:0004643.name: myeloid leukemia
MONDO:0004643.def: a clonal proliferation of myeloid cells and their precursors in the bone marrow, peripheral blood, and spleen. when the proliferating cells are immature myeloid cells and myeloblasts, it is called acute myeloid leukemia. when the proliferating myeloid cells are neutrophils, it is called chronic myelogenous leukemia.

MONDO:0004645.name: cheek mucosa cancer
MONDO:0004645.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the buccal mucosa.
MONDO:0004645.synonym: malignant tumour of the buccal mucosa

MONDO:0004646.name: decubitus ulcer
MONDO:0004646.def: death of tissue due to external pressure.

MONDO:0004647.name: in situ carcinoma
MONDO:0004647.def: a malignant epithelial neoplasm which is confined to the epithelial layer without evidence of further tissue invasion.

MONDO:0004648.name: vascular dementia
MONDO:0004648.def: a degenerative vascular disorder affecting the brain. it is caused by the blockage of the blood supply to the brain. it is manifested with decline of memory and cognitive functions.

MONDO:0004649.name: anaerobic pneumonia
MONDO:0004649.def: a pneumonia caused by anaerobic bacteria.

MONDO:0004650.name: malignant carotid body paraganglioma
MONDO:0004650.def: a carotid body paraganglioma that metastasizes to other anatomic sites.
MONDO:0004650.synonym: malignant tumour of the carotid body

MONDO:0004651.name: smallpox
MONDO:0004651.def: a condition that is caused by infection with variola, and that is characterized by small, raised bumps.

MONDO:0004652.name: bacterial pneumonia
MONDO:0004652.def: acute infection of the lung parenchyma caused by bacteria (e.g., streptococcus pneumoniae, haemophilus influenzae, chlamydia pneumoniae, mycoplasma pneumoniae, and legionella pneumophila). signs and symptoms include productive cough, fever, chills, shortness of breath, and chest pain.
MONDO:0004652.synonym: pneumonia due to other gram-negative bacteria

MONDO:0004653.name: atypical chronic myeloid leukemia, bcr-abl1 negative
MONDO:0004653.def: a myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by the principal involvement of the neutrophil series with leukocytosis and multilineage dysplasia. the neoplastic cells do not have a philadelphia chromosome or the bcr/abl fusion gene. (who, 2001)

MONDO:0004656.name: rubella
MONDO:0004656.def: a viral infection caused by the rubella virus. it is initially manifested with flu-like symptoms that last one or two days, followed by the development of a characteristic red rash which lasts from one to five days. the rash first appears in the neck and face. it subsequently spreads to the rest of the body.

MONDO:0004658.name: breast carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004658.def: a in situ carcinoma that involves the breast.

MONDO:0004659.name: eye carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004659.def: a carcinoma in situ involving a eye.
MONDO:0004659.synonym: stage 0 eyeball of camera-type eye carcinoma

MONDO:0004660.name: lung carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004660.def: a carcinoma in situ involving a lung.

MONDO:0004661.name: trachea carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004661.def: a carcinoma that arises from the tracheal mucosa and is confined to the epithelial layer without evidence of further tissue invasion.

MONDO:0004662.name: heterophyiasis
MONDO:0004662.def: an infection that is caused by the intestinal fluke heterophyes heterophyes, which is most commonly found in asia, the middle east, and africa, and which is transmitted via consumption of contaminated raw or undercooked fish. symptoms typically range from asymptomatic to intermittent abdominal pain and diarrhea, with occasional ectopic infection.

MONDO:0004663.name: colon carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004663.def: a in situ carcinoma that involves the colon.

MONDO:0004664.name: helminthiasis
MONDO:0004664.def: a parasitic infection characterized by the infestation with worms, mainly in the intestine.

MONDO:0004665.name: nodular sclerosis classical hodgkin lymphoma
MONDO:0004665.def: a subtype of classical hodgkin lymphoma characterized by collagen bands that surround at least one nodule, and hodgkin and reed-sternberg cells with lacunar type morphology. (who, 2008)

MONDO:0004666.name: metagonimiasis
MONDO:0004666.def: an infection that is most commonly caused by the intestinal fluke metagonimus yokogawai, which is most commonly found in the far east, and which is transmitted via consumption of contaminated raw or undercooked fish. symptoms typically range from asymptomatic to intermittent abdominal pain and diarrhea, with occasional ectopic infection.

MONDO:0004667.name: sublingual gland cancer
MONDO:0004667.def: a rare malignant neoplasm that arises from the sublingual gland. the majority are carcinomas.

MONDO:0004668.name: fascioliasis
MONDO:0004668.def: a parasitic infection that is caused by liver flukes, usually fasciola hepatica, of sheep, goats, and cattle. humans become infected by eating uncooked, infested aquatic vegetation (classically watercress). adult flukes inhabit the bile ducts, gallbladder, and occasionally ectopic sites. symptoms arise secondary to inflammatory response or obstruction.

MONDO:0004669.name: salivary gland cancer
MONDO:0004669.def: a primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm that affects the major or minor salivary glands. representative examples include carcinoma, lymphoma, and sarcoma.

MONDO:0004670.name: lupus erythematosus
MONDO:0004670.def: an autoimmune, connective tissue chronic inflammatory disorder affecting the skin, joints, kidneys, lungs, heart, and the peripheral blood cells. it is more commonly seen in women than men. variants include discoid and systemic lupus erythematosus.

MONDO:0004671.name: penis carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004671.def: a in situ carcinoma that involves the penis.

MONDO:0004672.name: fasciolopsiasis
MONDO:0004672.def: a small bowel infection that is caused by fasciolopsis buski, which is endemic in the far east and southeast asia, and which is transmitted via the consumption of raw or undercooked aquatic plants. the spectrum of manifestations range from asymptomatic to intestinal symptoms from local invasion or allergic response.

MONDO:0004673.name: lower lip cancer
MONDO:0004673.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the lower lip.

MONDO:0004674.name: chorioretinitis
MONDO:0004674.def: inflammation of the distal posterior uveal tract (choroid) and its structural and vascular attachments to the retina. it is usually caused by infection and though rare, it is clinically significant due to its most serious sequela: loss of vision.

MONDO:0004675.name: mitochondrial encephalomyopathy
MONDO:0004675.def: a heterogenous group of disorders characterized by alterations of mitochondrial metabolism that result in muscle and nervous system dysfunction. these are often multisystemic and vary considerably in age at onset (usually in the first or second decade of life), distribution of affected muscles, severity, and course. (from adams et al., principles of neurology, 6th ed, pp984-5)

MONDO:0004677.name: tinea nigra
MONDO:0004677.def: a superficial mycosis that is a superficial fungal infection of the skin characterized by brown to black macules which usually occur on the palmar aspects of hands and occasionally the plantar and other surfaces of the skin, caused by hortaea werneckii, which is a common saprophytic fungus believed to occur in soil, compost, humus and on wood in humid tropical and sub-tropical regions.

MONDO:0004678.name: dermatophytosis
MONDO:0004678.def: a common fungal infection of the stratum corneum of the skin, hair, or nails by a dermatophyte. it is characterized by itching, inflammation, redness of the skin, small papular vesicles, central clearing, fissures, scaling, and/or hair loss in the affected area.

MONDO:0004681.name: learning disability
MONDO:0004681.def: a group of disorders that affect a person's ability to learn or process specific types of information which is in contrast to his/her apparent level of intellect.

MONDO:0004682.name: retromolar area cancer
MONDO:0004682.def: a malignant form of neoplasm of retromolar area.

MONDO:0004684.name: plantar fibromatosis
MONDO:0004684.def: a superficial fibromatosis arising from soft tissue of the plantar regions. it is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped fibroblasts, hypercellularity, and an infiltrative growth pattern.
MONDO:0004684.synonym: superficial fibromatosis of plantar part of pes

MONDO:0004685.name: waldeyer's ring cancer
MONDO:0004685.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the tonsillar ring.

MONDO:0004689.name: inborn metal metabolism disorder
MONDO:0004689.def: an inherited metabolic disorder that involves metabolic disturbances in the processing or distribution of dietary minerals.

MONDO:0004690.name: tonsillar fossa cancer
MONDO:0004690.def: a cancer involving a tonsillar fossa.

MONDO:0004691.name: autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
MONDO:0004691.def: autosomal dominant form of polycystic kidney disease.

MONDO:0004693.name: squamous carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004693.def: a malignant epithelial neoplasm confined to the squamous epithelium, without invasion of the underlying tissues.

MONDO:0004694.name: hepatopulmonary syndrome
MONDO:0004694.def: hepatopulmonary syndrome (hps) is a lung disease characterized by widening of arteries and veins (dilatation) in the lungs in people who have chronic liver disease. because of the dilated vases, the workload of the heart increases and the blood pumped to the body does not have enough oxygen, leading to a decreased level of oxygen in the blood (hypoxemia). the normal diameter of the lung vessels ranges between 8 and 15 μm whereas when in hps rises to between 15 and 500 μm. while many people with hps don't have any obvious problems, the main reported symptom is shortness of breath (dyspnea) that is worse when standing or sitting up, and is relieved when lying down (platypnea). symptoms related to chronic liver disease (generally cirrhosis) include small red spots on the skin (spider angiomas) and abnormal vascular dilatations. some other symptoms that have been described are infections in the brain (brain abscesses), brain bleeding and an increased number of red blood cells in the blood (polycythemia). there is currently no effective medication for hps. oxygen therapy may improve the breathing in some cases. liver transplant is an efficient treatment which improves the symptoms, even in severe cases.

MONDO:0004695.name: liver lymphoma
MONDO:0004695.def: a rare lymphoma that arises from the liver and the bulk of the tumor is located in the liver. the most frequent types of lymphoma that arise from the liver are diffuse large b-cell lymphoma and mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma.

MONDO:0004696.name: larynx carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004696.def: a in situ carcinoma that involves the larynx.

MONDO:0004697.name: esophageal leukoplakia
MONDO:0004697.def: a rare condition that usually affects the middle-to-distal esophagus in middle-aged and elderly people. there is usually a history of tobacco smoking or alcohol intake. dysphagia is the presenting symptom. morphologically, the lesions are well-demarcated and are characterized by epithelial hyperplasia, thickened basal layer, prominent granular cell layer, and hyperorthokeratosis. in a minority of patients this condition is associated with adjacent high-grade squamous dysplasia and/or squamous cell carcinoma.

MONDO:0004698.name: intestine carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004698.def: a carcinoma in situ involving a intestine.

MONDO:0004699.name: gastrointestinal lymphoma
MONDO:0004699.def: a non-hodgkin or hodgkin lymphoma that arises from any part of the digestive system, with the bulk of the disease localized to that site.

MONDO:0004700.name: parotid gland cancer
MONDO:0004700.def: a primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm involving the parotid gland. representative examples include carcinoma, malignant mixed tumor, and non-hodgkin lymphoma.

MONDO:0004701.name: uterine polyp
MONDO:0004701.def: a benign protruding lesion arising either from the endometrial cavity (endometrial polyp) or the endocervix (endocervical polyp). it may occasionally recur following complete resection.

MONDO:0004702.name: uterine cervix leukoplakia
MONDO:0004702.def: the presence of whitish patches on the mucosal surface of the cervix. histologic examination reveals hyperkeratosis. in a minority of cases, underlying dysplasia or carcinoma in situ is present.

MONDO:0004703.name: bladder carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004703.def: also known as carcinoma in situ of the urinary bladder or high grade intraurothelial neoplasia, this is a flat lesion of the transitional cell epithelium characterized by severe cytologic atypia. this lesion is confined to the urothelium, and is a precursor of invasive transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder. stage 0is includes: tis, n0, m0. tis: carcinoma in situ: \"flat tumor\". n0: no regional lymph node metastasis. m0: no distant metastasis. (ajcc 6th and 7th eds.)

MONDO:0004705.name: liver solitary fibrous tumor
MONDO:0004705.def: a solitary fibrous tumor that arises from the liver. it affects females more frequently than males. signs and symptoms include the presence of an abdominal mass and abdominal discomfort.

MONDO:0004707.name: anal canal carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004707.def: a carcinoma in situ involving a anal canal.

MONDO:0004708.name: esophagus carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004708.def: stage 0 includes: for squamous cell carcinoma: tis (hgd), n0, m0, g1, gx, tumor location: any. for adenocarcinoma: tis (hgd), n0, m0, g1, gx. tis: high-grade dysplasia. n0: no regional lymph node metastasis. m0: no distant metastasis. g1: well differentiated. gx: grade cannot be assessed-stage grouping as g1. tumor location: location of the primary cancer site is defined by the position of the upper (proximal) edge of the tumor in the esophagus. (ajcc 7th ed.)

MONDO:0004709.name: occipital lobe neoplasm
MONDO:0004709.def: a neoplasm involving a occipital lobe.

MONDO:0004710.name: uterus carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004710.def: a carcinoma in situ involving a uterus.

MONDO:0004712.name: herpes simplex dermatitis
MONDO:0004712.def: localized rash characterized by grouped vesicles or pustules on an erythematous base that is caused by herpes simplex virus infection.

MONDO:0004713.name: lower gum cancer
MONDO:0004713.def: a cancer involving a gingiva of lower jaw.

MONDO:0004714.name: atrophic muscular disease
MONDO:0004714.def: a group of primary or secondary disorders affecting the muscles. it is characterized by an abnormal reduction in the muscle volume and atrophy. the atrophy may be caused by diseases of the muscle tissues or diseases of the peripheral nerves.

MONDO:0004715.name: liver carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004715.def: a carcinoma in situ involving a liver.

MONDO:0004716.name: stomach carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004716.def: a in situ carcinoma that involves the stomach.

MONDO:0004717.name: peliosis hepatis
MONDO:0004717.def: a vascular disease of the liver characterized by the occurrence of multiple blood-filled cysts or cavities. the cysts are lined with endothelial cells; the cavities lined with hepatic parenchymal cells (hepatocytes). peliosis hepatis has been associated with use of anabolic steroids (anabolic agents) and certain drugs.

MONDO:0004719.name: hard palate cancer
MONDO:0004719.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the hard palate.
MONDO:0004719.synonym: malignant tumour of the hard palate

MONDO:0004720.name: variola minor infection
MONDO:0004720.def: a orthopoxvirus that causes a milder clinical syndrome than smallpox.

MONDO:0004723.name: liver leiomyoma
MONDO:0004723.def: a benign smooth muscle neoplasm arising from the liver. it is characterized by the presence of spindle cells with cigar-shaped nuclei, interlacing fascicles, and a whorled pattern.

MONDO:0004724.name: submandibular gland cancer
MONDO:0004724.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the submandibular gland.

MONDO:0004725.name: rectum carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004725.def: a in situ carcinoma that involves the rectum.

MONDO:0004726.name: liver inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor
MONDO:0004726.def: a multinodular intermediate fibroblastic neoplasm arising from the liver. it is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped fibroblasts and myofibroblasts, and a chronic inflammatory infiltrate composed of eosinophils, lymphocytes and plasma cells.

MONDO:0004727.name: vestibule of mouth cancer
MONDO:0004727.def: a cancer that involves the oral opening.

MONDO:0004729.name: dyskinesia of esophagus
MONDO:0004729.def: disorders affecting the motor function of the upper esophageal sphincter; lower esophageal sphincter; the esophagus body, or a combination of these parts. the failure of the sphincters to maintain a tonic pressure may result in gastric reflux of food and acid into the esophagus (gastroesophageal reflux). other disorders include hypermotility (spastic disorders) and markedly increased amplitude in contraction (nutcracker esophagus).

MONDO:0004730.name: speech disorder
MONDO:0004730.def: a term referring to disorders characterized by the disruption of normal speech. it includes stuttering, lisps, dysarthria and voice disorders.

MONDO:0004731.name: central sleep apnea syndrome
MONDO:0004731.def: a broad classification of disorders which includes 6 subtypes (primary central sleep apnea, central sleep apnea due to cheyne-stokes breathing pattern, central sleep apnea due to medical condition not cheyne-stokes, central sleep apnea due to high-altitude periodic breathing, central sleep apnea due to drug or substance and primary sleep apnea of infancy) that are each characterized by interruptions in breathing while asleep. it is caused by improper signaling from the brainstem to respiratory muscles and is triggered by either hypoventilation or hyperventilation. in adults, this disorder may arise following a stroke, congestive heart failure, trauma, infection or the use of narcotic medications. it is more common in older males and may present as a co-morbid condition to obesity. clinical signs include snoring, insomnia or hypersomnia, difficulty concentrating and fatigue. recurrent episodes of hypoxia/hypoxemia have long-term detrimental effects on cardiovascular health.

MONDO:0004732.name: kidney carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0004732.def: a carcinoma in situ involving a kidney.

MONDO:0004733.name: pyriform sinus cancer
MONDO:0004733.def: a primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm that affects the pyriform sinus.
MONDO:0004733.synonym: malignant tumour of the pyriform sinus

MONDO:0004736.name: inborn disorder of amino acid metabolism
MONDO:0004736.def: an inherited disorder that affects the metabolism of the amino acids. representative examples include alkaptonuria, homocystinuria, tyrosinemia, and phenylketonuria.
MONDO:0004736.synonym: rare inborn error of cellular amino acid metabolic process

MONDO:0004737.name: homocystinuria
MONDO:0004737.def: an autosomal recessive inherited metabolic disorder caused by mutations in the cbs, mthfr, mtr, and mtrr genes. it is characterized by abnormalities in the methionine metabolism and is associated with deficiency of cystathionine synthase. it results in the accumulation of homocysteine in the serum. it may affect the cardiovascular, musculoskeletal and the central nervous systems.

MONDO:0004739.name: urea cycle disorder
MONDO:0004739.def: a genetic inborn error of metabolism characterized by the deficiency of one of the enzymes necessary for the urea cycle. it results in accumulation of ammonia in the body.

MONDO:0004741.name: tyrosinemia
MONDO:0004741.def: an autosomal recessive inherited metabolic disorder caused by mutations in the fah, hpd, and tat genes. it is characterized by deficiency of one of the enzymes that are involved in the metabolism of tyrosine. it results in elevated blood tyrosine levels and accumulation of tyrosine and its byproducts in the liver, kidney, nervous system and other organs.

MONDO:0004742.name: primary cerebellar degeneration
MONDO:0004742.def: a heterogenous group of degenerative syndromes marked by progressive cerebellar dysfunction either in isolation or combined with other neurologic manifestations. sporadic and inherited subtypes occur. inheritance patterns include autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive, and x-linked.

MONDO:0004743.name: hyperhomocysteinemia
MONDO:0004743.def: a serious metabolic condition caused by mutations in the mthfr gene, medications, or nutritional deficiency. it results in increased levels of homocysteine in the blood. patients with this condition are at an increased risk for recurrent blood clots formation and cardiovascular accidents.

MONDO:0004745.name: priapism
MONDO:0004745.def: persistent and usually painful erection that lasts for at least four hours in the absence of physical or psychological stimulation, which can be caused by hematologic disorders, including sickle cell disease and leukemia, spinal cord injuries, and medications.

MONDO:0004746.name: myopathy of extraocular muscle
MONDO:0004746.def: a myopathy that involves the extra-ocular muscle.

MONDO:0004747.name: cleft lip
MONDO:0004747.def: a congenital abnormality consisting of one or more clefts (splits) in the upper lip, which may be accompanied by a cleft palate; it is the result of the failure of the embryonic parts of the lip to fuse.

MONDO:0004749.name: myocardium cancer
MONDO:0004749.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the myocardium.

MONDO:0004750.name: language disorder
MONDO:0004750.def: a category of disorders characterized by an impairment in the development of an individual's language capabilities, which is in contrast to his/her non-verbal intellect.

MONDO:0004751.name: disease of orbital part of eye adnexa
MONDO:0004751.def: diseases of the bony orbit and contents except the eyeball.

MONDO:0004752.name: neurofibroma of the heart
MONDO:0004752.def: a rare neurofibroma that affects the heart.

MONDO:0004754.name: rectal prolapse
MONDO:0004754.def: protrusion of the rectum through the anus.

MONDO:0004755.name: monieziasis
MONDO:0004755.def: infection of ruminants with tapeworms of the genus moniezia.

MONDO:0004756.name: nasal cavity neoplasm
MONDO:0004756.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the nasal cavity. representative examples of benign neoplasms include schneiderian papilloma and salivary gland-type adenoma. representative examples of malignant neoplasms include carcinoma and lymphoma.

MONDO:0004757.name: chronic ethmoidal sinusitis
MONDO:0004757.def: inflammation of the ethmoid sinus that typically lasts beyond eight weeks. it is caused by infections, allergies, and the presence of sinus polyps or a deviated septum. signs and symptoms include headache, nasal discharge, swelling in the face, dizziness, and breathing difficulties.

MONDO:0004758.name: scotoma
MONDO:0004758.def: a localized defect in the visual field bordered by an area of normal vision. this occurs with a variety of eye diseases (e.g., retinal diseases and glaucoma); optic nerve diseases, and other conditions.
MONDO:0004758.synonym: sector or arcuate visual field defects

MONDO:0004763.name: carotid artery dissection
MONDO:0004763.def: spontaneous or traumatic separation of the layers of the carotid artery wall. it manifests with headache, neck pain, temporary vision loss, and/or ischemic stroke.

MONDO:0004765.name: intrinsic asthma
MONDO:0004765.def: an asthma that is triggered by factors not related to allergies such as anxiety, stress, exercise, cold air, dry air, hyperventilation, smoke, viruses, chemical irritants, autonomic imbalance, hormonal deficiencies and psychogenic influences. it is characterized by airway obstruction and inflammation that is at least partially reversible with medication. the symptoms include coughing, wheezing, shortness of breath or rapid breathing, and chest tightness.

MONDO:0004766.name: status asthmaticus
MONDO:0004766.def: an acute exacerbation of asthma, characterized by inadequate response to initial bronchodilators.

MONDO:0004767.name: vesiculitis
MONDO:0004767.def: an inflammatory disease involving a pathogenic inflammatory response in the seminal vesicle.

MONDO:0004768.name: keratoconjunctivitis
MONDO:0004768.def: inflammation of both the cornea and the conjunctiva.

MONDO:0004769.name: orbital plasma cell granuloma
MONDO:0004769.def: a nonspecific tumor-like inflammatory lesion in the orbit of the eye. it is usually composed of mature lymphocytes; plasma cells; macrophages; leukocytes with varying degrees of fibrosis. orbital pseudotumors are often associated with inflammation of the extraocular muscles (orbital myositis) or inflammation of the lacrimal glands (dacryoadenitis).

MONDO:0004770.name: exophthalmos
MONDO:0004770.def: the anterior displacement of the eye within the orbit, giving a bulging appearance.

MONDO:0004773.name: iridocyclitis
MONDO:0004773.def: an inflammation of the iris and the ciliary body

MONDO:0004774.name: gonococcal iridocyclitis
MONDO:0004774.def: an iridocyclitis (disease) caused by infection with neisseria gonorrhoeae.

MONDO:0004777.name: acute laryngitis
MONDO:0004777.def: an acute inflammatory process affecting the larynx. it is caused by bacteria, viruses, or vocal strain. signs and symptoms include sore throat, cough, swallowing difficulties, and hoarseness.

MONDO:0004778.name: epididymo-orchitis
MONDO:0004778.def: a disorder involving inflammation of the epididymis and testes.

MONDO:0004779.name: epididymitis
MONDO:0004779.def: inflammation of the epididymis. its clinical features include enlarged epididymis, a swollen scrotum; pain; pyuria; and fever. it is usually related to infections in the urinary tract, which likely spread to the epididymis through either the vas deferens or the lymphatics of the spermatic cord.

MONDO:0004781.name: acute myocardial infarction
MONDO:0004781.def: necrosis of the myocardium, as a result of interruption of the blood supply to the area. it is characterized by a severe and rapid onset of symptoms that may include chest pain, often radiating to the left arm and left side of the neck, dyspnea, sweating, and palpitations.

MONDO:0004782.name: diabetes insipidus
MONDO:0004782.def: a disorder characterized by excretion of large amounts of urine, accompanied by excessive thirst. causes include deficiency of antidiuretic hormone or failure of the kidneys to respond to antidiuretic hormone. it may also be drug-related.

MONDO:0004784.name: allergic asthma
MONDO:0004784.def: a asthma with a basis in a pathological type i hypersensitivity reaction.

MONDO:0004785.name: blepharitis
MONDO:0004785.def: inflammation of the eyelids near the eyelashes.

MONDO:0004786.name: chronic cholangitis
MONDO:0004786.def: cholangitis that is persistent and long-standing.

MONDO:0004787.name: cervical mullerian papilloma
MONDO:0004787.def: a rare, benign, papillary neoplasm that arises from the cervix. it is characterized by the presence of a fibrovascular core covered by mucinous epithelial cells.

MONDO:0004788.name: cervix squamous papilloma
MONDO:0004788.def: a papilloma that arises from the squamous epithelium of the cervix.

MONDO:0004789.name: cholangitis
MONDO:0004789.def: an acute or chronic inflammatory process affecting the biliary tract.

MONDO:0004790.name: fatty liver disease
MONDO:0004790.def: a reversible condition wherein large vacuoles of triglyceride fat accumulate in liver cells via the process of steatosis.

MONDO:0004792.name: cancer of isthmus of fallopian tube
MONDO:0004792.def: a cancer that involves the uberon:0016632.
MONDO:0004792.synonym: malignant neoplasm of isthmus of fallopian tube

MONDO:0004795.name: otitis externa
MONDO:0004795.def: inflammation of the anatomical structures of the outer ear and ear canal secondary to an infectious process. bacterial etiology is most common, but fungal infection is also possible. symptoms include erythema, edema, and pain.

MONDO:0004796.name: infectious meningitis
MONDO:0004796.def: inflammation of the meninges of the brain and/or spinal cord caused by an infectious agent (viral, bacterial, or fungal). symptoms include headache, fever, vomiting, neck stiffness, photophobia, confusion, and seizures.

MONDO:0004797.name: mononeuritis of lower limb
MONDO:0004797.def: a mononeuritis simplex that involves the hindlimb.

MONDO:0004802.name: pulmonary eosinophilia
MONDO:0004802.def: a condition characterized by infiltration of the lung with eosinophils due to inflammation or other disease processes. major eosinophilic lung diseases are the eosinophilic pneumonias caused by infections, allergens, or toxic agents.

MONDO:0004804.name: dacryoadenitis
MONDO:0004804.def: inflammation and enlargement of the lacrimal gland.

MONDO:0004806.name: chronic eosinophilic pneumonia
MONDO:0004806.def: chronic inflammatory disorder of the lungs characterized by the presence of eosinophils in the interalveolar septa and alveolar spaces and peripheral blood eosinophilia. chest x-rays reveal peripheral infiltrates. approximately half of the patients have history of asthma or atopic disease. signs and symptoms include fever, dyspnea, cough, and weight loss. following treatment with corticosteroids, the eosinophilic infiltrates in the lungs disappear, resulting in dramatic clinical improvement.

MONDO:0004813.name: tuberculous pneumothorax
MONDO:0004813.def: a pneumothorax in which air enters into the pleural cavity.

MONDO:0004815.name: osteosclerotic plasma cell myeloma
MONDO:0004815.def: a plasma cell neoplasm associated with osteosclerotic and fibrotic changes in the bone trabeculae. often, the lymph nodes show changes resembling the plasma cell variant of castleman disease. it is often part of poems syndrome which is characterized by polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, monoclonal gammopathy, and skin changes.

MONDO:0004816.name: refractory plasma cell neoplasm
MONDO:0004816.def: a plasma cell neoplasm that is resistant to treatment.

MONDO:0004817.name: non-secretory plasma cell myeloma
MONDO:0004817.def: a rare type of multiple myeloma in which the plasma cells synthesize but do not secrete immunoglobulins. as a result, none of the immunoglobulins appear out of the normal range. the symptoms are generally the same with those of immunoglobulin-secreting myeloma; however, the incidence of renal insufficiency is lower in non-secretory myeloma. the diagnosis can be missed because of the absence of monoclonal immunoglobulin in the serum or urine.

MONDO:0004820.name: peripheral nerve schwannoma
MONDO:0004820.def: a benign, usually encapsulated slow growing tumor of the peripheral nervous system composed of schwann cells. it recurs infrequently and only rare cases associated with malignant transformation have been reported.

MONDO:0004821.name: nasopharyngeal disorder
MONDO:0004821.def: a non-neoplastic or neoplastic disorder that affects the nasopharynx. representative examples include nasopharyngitis, angiofibroma, and carcinoma.

MONDO:0004822.name: bronchiectasis
MONDO:0004822.def: segmental, irreversible dilation of the bronchial tree resulting in the accumulation of secretions which leads to obstruction. the most common cause is bacterial infection.

MONDO:0004824.name: neonatal candidiasis
MONDO:0004824.def: a fungal infection by any of the candida species in a newborn infant up to 28 days old.

MONDO:0004827.name: esophagus squamous cell papilloma
MONDO:0004827.def: a rare neoplasm arising from the distal third of the esophagus. morphologically, it is characterized by the presence of fibrovascular cores covered by mature stratified squamous epithelium. progression to squamous cell carcinoma is extremely rare.
MONDO:0004827.synonym: squamous cell papilloma of the oesophagus

MONDO:0004828.name: lower urinary tract calculus
MONDO:0004828.def: a urolithiasis that involves the lower urinary tract.

MONDO:0004829.name: krukenberg carcinoma
MONDO:0004829.def: metastatic signet-ring cell carcinoma to the ovary. the primary site is the gastrointestinal tract or breast.

MONDO:0004831.name: proliferative fasciitis
MONDO:0004831.def: a rapidly growing, poorly circumscribed, mass-forming proliferation that arises from the subcutaneous tissues. it is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped fibroblasts, round ganglion-like cells, myxoid to collagenous stroma formation, and high mitotic activity. it recurs only rarely following local excision and does not metastasize.

MONDO:0004832.name: esophagus leiomyoma
MONDO:0004832.def: a benign smooth muscle neoplasm arising from the lower part of the esophagus. it is the most common mesenchymal neoplasm of the esophagus. dysphagia is a frequent clinical symptom.

MONDO:0004833.name: plantar fasciitis
MONDO:0004833.def: inflammation of the thick tissue on the bottom of the foot (plantar fascia) causing heel pain. the plantar fascia (also called plantar aponeurosis) are bands of fibrous tissue extending from the calcaneal tuberosity to the toes. the etiology of plantar fasciitis remains controversial but is likely to involve a biomechanical imbalance. though often presenting along with heel spur, they do not appear to be causally related.

MONDO:0004834.name: ischemic fasciitis
MONDO:0004834.def: a reactive, painless lesion which is characterized by a pseudosarcomatous proliferation of fibroblasts and myofibroblasts usually in the deep subcutaneous tissue. it occurs mainly around the limb girdles, sacral region, and greater trochanter. it affects mainly elderly patients and sometimes is associated with physical immobility. local excision is usually curative.

MONDO:0004835.name: necrotizing fasciitis
MONDO:0004835.def: necrotizing fasciitis is a serious infection of the skin, the tissue just beneath the skin (subcutaneous tissue), and the tissue that covers internal organs (fascia). necrotizing fasciitis can be caused by several different types of bacteria, and the infection can arise suddenly and spread quickly. early signs include flu-like symptoms and redness and pain around the infection site. a prompt diagnosis and treatment are essential.if the infection is not treated promptly, it can lead to multiple organ failure and death. treatment typically includes intravenous (iv) antibiotics and surgery to remove infected and dead tissue.

MONDO:0004836.name: intravascular fasciitis
MONDO:0004836.def: a rare self-limiting, rapidly growing, non-encapsulated benign neoplasm that arises from the vessels. it is characterized by the presence of plump spindle-shaped fibroblasts, multinucleated osteoclast-like giant cells, chronic inflammatory infiltrate, red blood cell extravasation, and high mitotic activity.

MONDO:0004837.name: neurofibroma of the esophagus
MONDO:0004837.def: a non-metastasizing encapsulated neoplasm arising from nerves in the esophagus. morphologically, it is characterized by the presence of fibroblasts and schwann cells.

MONDO:0004841.name: kidney hypertrophy
MONDO:0004841.def: global enlargement of the renal parenchyma in one or both kidneys.

MONDO:0004842.name: stomatitis
MONDO:0004842.def: inflammation of the oral mucosa due to local or systemic factors.

MONDO:0004843.name: pathologic nystagmus
MONDO:0004843.def: involuntary movements of the eyeballs. the presence or absence of nystagmus is often used in the diagnosis of a variety of neurological and visual disorders.

MONDO:0004844.name: oral mucosa leukoplakia
MONDO:0004844.def: a white patch or plaque on the oral mucosa that cannot be characterized clinically or pathologically as any other disease. the diagnosis of leukoplakia is one of exclusion; other conditions such as candidiasis, lichen planus, leukoedema, etc., must be ruled out before a diagnosis of leukoplakia can be made. leukoplakia may be a premalignant condition.

MONDO:0004845.name: aphthous stomatitis
MONDO:0004845.def: a recurrent disease of the oral mucosa of unknown etiology. it is characterized by small white ulcerative lesions, single or multiple, round or oval, lasting for 7-14 days and healing without scarring.

MONDO:0004846.name: placental abruption
MONDO:0004846.def: vaginal bleeding preceding the 20th week of gestation.

MONDO:0004847.name: senile cataract
MONDO:0004847.def: a cataract with no obvious cause occurring in persons over 50 years old.

MONDO:0004848.name: ulcerative stomatitis
MONDO:0004848.def: inflammation of the mouth mucosa associated with the presence of ulcers.

MONDO:0004849.name: pulmonary emphysema
MONDO:0004849.def: a subcategory of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (copd). it occurs in people who smoke and suffer from chronic bronchitis. it is characterized by inflation of the alveoli, alveolar wall damage, and reduction in the number of alveoli, resulting in difficulty breathing.

MONDO:0004854.name: ophthalmia neonatorum
MONDO:0004854.def: inflammation of the conjunctiva in a newborn due to chemical or infectious causes. aseptic conjunctivitis is often related to the use of prophylactic medications for infectious conjunctivitis. septic conjunctivitis is related to perinatal exposure to microorganisms.

MONDO:0004855.name: tenosynovitis
MONDO:0004855.def: inflammation of the synovial lining of a tendon sheath. causes include trauma, tendon stress, bacterial disease (gonorrhea, tuberculosis), rheumatic disease, and gout. common sites are the hand, wrist, shoulder capsule, hip capsule, hamstring muscles, and achilles tendon. the tendon sheaths become inflamed and painful, and accumulate fluid. joint mobility is usually reduced.

MONDO:0004857.name: tendinitis
MONDO:0004857.def: inflammation of a tendon, usually resulting from an overuse injury. it is characterized by swelling of the tendon, tenderness around the inflamed tendon, and pain while moving the affected area of the body.

MONDO:0004858.name: occlusion of gallbladder
MONDO:0004858.def: blockage of the normal flow of the contents of the gallbladder.

MONDO:0004860.name: vitreous disorder
MONDO:0004860.def: a disease involving the vitreous humor.

MONDO:0004864.name: acute allergic mucoid otitis media
MONDO:0004864.def: a blue drum syndrome caused by an allergen.

MONDO:0004865.name: blue drum syndrome
MONDO:0004865.def: a acute transudative otitis media involving thick, viscid and mucuslike fluid effusion due to which the drum appears blue in color.

MONDO:0004866.name: eustachian tube disorder
MONDO:0004866.def: a disease involving the pharyngotympanic tube.

MONDO:0004867.name: upper respiratory tract disorder
MONDO:0004867.def: a disease involving the upper respiratory tract.
MONDO:0004867.synonym: upper respiratory tract disease or disorder

MONDO:0004868.name: biliary tract disorder
MONDO:0004868.def: a disease involving the biliary tree.

MONDO:0004869.name: pelvic varices
MONDO:0004869.def: a varicose disease that involves the pelvic region of trunk.
MONDO:0004869.synonym: varicose disease of pelvic region of trunk

MONDO:0004872.name: hemorrhoid
MONDO:0004872.def: dilated veins in the anal canal.

MONDO:0004873.name: internal hemorrhoid
MONDO:0004873.def: a hemorrhoid which originates above the dentate line.

MONDO:0004875.name: xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis
MONDO:0004875.def: cholecystitis that is characterized by nodules containing lipid.

MONDO:0004876.name: myocardial stunning
MONDO:0004876.def: prolonged dysfunction of the myocardium after a brief episode of severe ischemia, with gradual return of contractile activity.

MONDO:0004880.name: bowel dysfunction
MONDO:0004880.def: any disease in which the causes of the disease is a perturbation of the lower digestive tract leading to its dysfunction.

MONDO:0004881.name: myositis fibrosa
MONDO:0004881.def: a form of myositis that is characterized by the formation of connective tissue within the muscle.

MONDO:0004882.name: angioid streaks of choroid
MONDO:0004882.def: a angioid streaks that involves the optic choroid.

MONDO:0004884.name: eye degenerative disorder
MONDO:0004884.def: a neurodegenerative disease that involves the eye.
MONDO:0004884.synonym: neurodegenerative disease of eyeball of camera-type eye

MONDO:0004885.name: choroidal sclerosis
MONDO:0004885.def: a neurodegenerative disease that involves the optic choroid.

MONDO:0004891.name: hyperopia
MONDO:0004891.def: a refractive error in which rays of light entering the eye parallel to the optic axis are brought to a focus behind the retina, as a result of the eyeball being too short from front to back. it is also called farsightedness because the near point is more distant than it is in emmetropia with an equal amplitude of accommodation. (dorland, 27th ed)

MONDO:0004892.name: refractive error
MONDO:0004892.def: a defect in the focusing of light on the retina as in astigmatism, myopia, or hyperopia.

MONDO:0004893.name: hypertropia
MONDO:0004893.def: vertical strabismus in which there is permanent upward deviation of the visual axis of one eye.

MONDO:0004896.name: esotropia
MONDO:0004896.def: a form of strabismus in which one or both eyes are deviated medially.

MONDO:0004897.name: hypotropia
MONDO:0004897.def: vertical strabismus in which there is permanent downward deviation of the visual axis of one eye.

MONDO:0004901.name: lingual-facial-buccal dyskinesia
MONDO:0004901.def: syndromes which feature dyskinesias as a cardinal manifestation of the disease process. included in this category are degenerative, hereditary, post-infectious, medication-induced, post-inflammatory, and post-traumatic conditions.

MONDO:0004905.name: intestinal disaccharidase deficiency
MONDO:0004905.def: inherited or acquired disorders of sugar metabolism. deficiencies of lactase, maltase or sucrase-isomaltase usually occur irreversibly and independent of one another. congenital deficiencies are rare whereas acquired deficiencies are more common and may be seen following intestinal mucosal brush-border injury. clinical signs include abdominal cramping, bloating, flatulence and diarrhea following dietary intake of lactose, maltose or sucrose. the clinical course leads to malabsorption of disaccharides which has implications for normal growth and development if manifested at an early age.
MONDO:0004905.synonym: intestinal disaccharide deficiency and disaccharide malabsorption

MONDO:0004907.name: alopecia
MONDO:0004907.def: hair loss usually from the scalp. it may result in bald spots or spread to the entire scalp or the entire epidermis. it may be androgenetic or caused by chemotherapeutic agents, compulsive hair pulling, autoimmune disorders or congenital conditions.

MONDO:0004910.name: mitral valve prolapse
MONDO:0004910.def: a fairly common and often benign valvular heart disorder characterized by redundancy or hooding of mitral valve leaflets so that they prolapse into the left atrium, often causing mitral regurgitation. it is often a symptomless condition but may be marked by varied symptoms (e.g. chest pain, fatigue, dizziness, dyspnea, or palpitations) leading in some cases to endocarditis or ventricular tachycardia.

MONDO:0004911.name: cardiovascular syphilis
MONDO:0004911.def: a tertiary syphilis that is manifested as aneurysm formation in the ascending aorta, caused by chronic inflammatory destruction of the vasa vasorum, insufficiency of the aortic valve, or narrowing of the coronary arteries.

MONDO:0004914.name: celiac artery stenosis from compression by median arcuate ligament of diaphragm
MONDO:0004914.def: a vascular compression syndrome attributed to celiac trunk compression by the median arcuate ligament of the diaphragm, with presentations ranging from completely asymptomatic to myriad gastrointestinal symptoms, including chronic abdominal pain (cap), post-prandial pain, nausea and vomiting, anorexia, early satiety, and subsequently weight loss.
MONDO:0004914.synonym: syndromic disease of median arcuate ligament

MONDO:0004917.name: internal hordeolum
MONDO:0004917.def: a hordeolum that results from infection of a meibomian gland.

MONDO:0004922.name: developmental coordination disorder
MONDO:0004922.def: a disorder characterized by an impairment in the development of an individual's motor coordination skills; this impairment in motor development is not due to a medical condition.

MONDO:0004927.name: dacryocystocele
MONDO:0004927.def: a congenital or acquired mucocele that develops in the lacrimal sac. it is usually the result of nasolacrimal duct abnormalities or obstruction.

MONDO:0004928.name: lymph node disorder
MONDO:0004928.def: any disorder of the lymph nodes.

MONDO:0004933.name: hypoplastic left heart syndrome
MONDO:0004933.def: hypoplastic left heart syndrome (hlhs) refers to the abnormal development of the left-sided cardiac structures, resulting in obstruction to blood flow from the left ventricular outflow tract. in addition, the syndrome includes underdevelopment of the left ventricle, aorta, and aortic arch, as well as mitral atresia or stenosis.

MONDO:0004934.name: periostitis
MONDO:0004934.def: inflammation of the periosteum. the condition is generally chronic, and is marked by tenderness and swelling of the bone and an aching pain. acute periostitis is due to infection, is characterized by diffuse suppuration, severe pain, and constitutional symptoms, and usually results in necrosis. (dorland, 27th ed)

MONDO:0004936.name: uterine inversion
MONDO:0004936.def: a complication of obstetric labor in which the corpus of the uterus is forced completely or partially through the uterine cervix. this can occur during the late stages of labor and is associated with immediate postpartum hemorrhage.

MONDO:0004938.name: substance dependence
MONDO:0004938.def: the psychological or physiological need to take a substance in order to experience its effects or to avoid the effects of its absence.

MONDO:0004939.name: hallucinogen dependence
MONDO:0004939.def: a drug dependence for a hallucinogenic substance.

MONDO:0004941.name: eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome
MONDO:0004941.def: a complex systemic syndrome with inflammatory and autoimmune components that affect the skin, fascia, muscle, nerve, blood vessels, lung, and heart. diagnostic features generally include eosinophilia, myalgia severe enough to limit usual activities of daily living, and the absence of coexisting infectious, autoimmune or other conditions that may induce eosinophilia. biopsy of affected tissue reveals a microangiopathy associated with diffuse inflammation involving connective tissue. (from spitzer et al., j rheumatol suppl 1996 oct;46:73-9; blackburn wd, semin arthritis rheum 1997 jun;26(6):788-93)
MONDO:0004941.synonym: syndrome with inflammatory and autoimmune components that affect the skin, fascia, muscle, nerve, blood vessels, lung, and heart

MONDO:0004942.name: orbit lymphoma
MONDO:0004942.def: a lymphoma that arises from the structures of the orbit. representative examples include mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma, follicular lymphoma, and diffuse large b-cell lymphoma.

MONDO:0004943.name: orbit sarcoma
MONDO:0004943.def: a malignant soft tissue neoplasm that arises from the structures of the orbit. the majority of the cases are rhabdomyosarcomas.
