MONDO:0005933.def: a malignant neoplasm of the lung composed of tubular structures and immature mesenchymal elements, which may differentiate towards skeletal and smooth muscle, cartilage or a combination of muscle and cartilage. this is a nodular tumor found in the periphery of the lung. it can occur at any age. the prognosis is related to the stage of the disease at the time of resection. pulmonary blastoma is divided into two subtypes: epithelial predominant and biphasic.

MONDO:0005936.name: recurrent pneumonia
MONDO:0005936.def: infections with nontuberculous mycobacteria (atypical mycobacteria): m. kansasii, m. marinum, m. scrofulaceum, m. flavescens, m. gordonae, m. obuense, m. gilvum, m. duvali, m. szulgai, m. intracellulare (see mycobacterium avium complex;), m. xenopi (littorale), m. ulcerans, m. buruli, m. terrae, m. fortuitum (minetti, giae), m. chelonae.

MONDO:0005937.name: rem sleep behavior disorder
MONDO:0005937.def: a disorder characterized by episodes of vigorous and often violent motor activity during rem sleep (sleep, rem). the affected individual may inflict self injury or harm others, and is difficult to awaken from this condition. episodes are usually followed by a vivid recollection of a dream that is consistent with the aggressive behavior. this condition primarily affects adult males. (from adams et al., principles of neurology, 6th ed, p393)
MONDO:0005937.synonym: rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder

MONDO:0005938.name: renal tuberculosis
MONDO:0005938.def: infection of the kidney due to mycobacteria.

MONDO:0005939.name: reoviridae infectious disease
MONDO:0005939.def: infections produced by reoviruses, general or unspecified.

MONDO:0005940.name: respirovirus infectious disease
MONDO:0005940.def: infections with viruses of the genus respirovirus, family paramyxoviridae. host cell infection occurs by adsorption, via hemagglutinin, to the cell surface.

MONDO:0005941.name: retroperitoneal cancer
MONDO:0005941.def: a primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm involving the retroperitoneum. the vast majority of cases are carcinomas, lymphomas, or sarcomas.

MONDO:0005942.name: reye syndrome
MONDO:0005942.def: an acute and potentially fatal metabolic disorder characterized by cerebral edema, fatty liver and hypoglycemia. it occurs primarily in children and has been associated with the use of aspirin for the treatment of viral infections. however, it can also occur in the absence of aspirin use.

MONDO:0005943.name: rhabditida infectious disease
MONDO:0005943.def: infections with nematodes of the order rhabditida.

MONDO:0005944.name: rhabdoviridae infectious disease
MONDO:0005944.def: virus diseases caused by rhabdoviridae. important infections include rabies; ephemeral fever; and vesicular stomatitis.

MONDO:0005945.name: rhinoscleroma
MONDO:0005945.def: a granulomatous disease caused by klebsiella rhinoscleromatis infection. despite its name, this disease is not limited to the nose and nasopharynx but may affect any part of the respiratory tract, sometimes with extension to the lip and the skin.

MONDO:0005946.name: rhinosporidiosis
MONDO:0005946.def: chronic, localized granulomatous infection of mucocutaneous tissues, especially the nose, and characterized by hyperplasia and the development of polyps. it is found in humans and other animals and is caused by the mesomycetozoean organism rhinosporidium seeberi.

MONDO:0005947.name: rickettsial pneumonia
MONDO:0005947.def: pneumonia caused by infection with bacteria of the family rickettsiaceae.

MONDO:0005949.name: roseolovirus infectious disease
MONDO:0005949.def: infection with roseolovirus, the most common in humans being exanthema subitum, a benign disease of infants and young children.

MONDO:0005950.name: salmonella gastroenteritis
MONDO:0005950.def: poisoning caused by ingestion of food harboring species of salmonella. conditions of raising, shipping, slaughtering, and marketing of domestic animals contribute to the spread of this bacterium in the food supply.

MONDO:0005952.name: scarlet fever
MONDO:0005952.def: a streptococcal infection, mainly occurring among children, that is characterized by a red skin rash, sore throat, and fever.

MONDO:0005953.name: scirrhous adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0005953.def: an infiltrating adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of desmoplastic stromal reaction.

MONDO:0005954.name: screw worm infectious disease
MONDO:0005954.def: infection with larvae of the blow fly cochliomyia hominivorax (callitroga americanum), a common cause of disease in livestock in the southern and southwestern u.s.a.

MONDO:0005956.name: septicemic plague
MONDO:0005956.def: a plague in which the bacteria have entered the bloodstream.

MONDO:0005957.name: setariasis
MONDO:0005957.def: infection with nematodes of the genus setaria. this condition is usually seen in cattle and equines and is of little pathogenic significance, although migration of the worm to the eye may lead to blindness.

MONDO:0005959.name: sick building syndrome
MONDO:0005959.def: a group of symptoms that are two- to three-fold more common in those who work in large, energy-efficient buildings, associated with an increased frequency of headaches, lethargy, and dry skin. clinical manifestations include hypersensitivity pneumonitis (alveolitis, extrinsic allergic); allergic rhinitis (rhinitis, allergic, perennial); asthma; infections, skin eruptions, and mucous membrane irritation syndromes. current usage tends to be less restrictive with regard to the type of building and delineation of complaints. (from segen, dictionary of modern medicine, 1992)

MONDO:0005960.name: silicosis
MONDO:0005960.def: silicosis is a respiratory disease caused by breathing in (inhaling) silica dust. there are three types of silicosis: simple chronic silicosis, the most common type of silicosis, results from long-term exposure (usually more than 20years) to low amounts of silica dust. simple chronic silicosismay causepeople to have difficulty breathing. accelerated silicosis occurs after 5 to 15 yearsof exposure of higher levels of silica.swelling of the lungsand other symptoms occur faster in this type of silicosis than in the simple chronic form. acute silicosis results from short-term exposure (weeks or months) of large amounts of silica.the lungs become very inflamed and can fill with fluid, causing severe shortness of breath and low blood oxygen levels. a cough, weight loss, and fatigue may also be present. acute silicosis progresses rapidly and can be fatal within months. people who work in jobs where they are exposed to silica dust (mining, quarrying, construction, sand blasting, stone cutting) are at risk of developing this condition.

MONDO:0005961.name: sinusitis
MONDO:0005961.def: an acute or chronic inflammatory process affecting the mucous membranes of any sinus cavity.

MONDO:0005962.name: skeletal tuberculosis
MONDO:0005962.def: tuberculosis of the bones or joints.

MONDO:0005963.name: sparganosis
MONDO:0005963.def: a condition resulting from infection with the second stage larvae of the parasite spirometra.

MONDO:0005964.name: sphenoid sinusitis
MONDO:0005964.def: an acute or chronic inflammatory process affecting the mucous membrane of the sphenoid sinus.

MONDO:0005966.name: spleen cancer
MONDO:0005966.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the spleen

MONDO:0005967.name: splenic tuberculosis
MONDO:0005967.def: infection of the spleen with species of mycobacterium.

MONDO:0005968.name: sporotrichosis
MONDO:0005968.def: the commonest and least serious of the deep mycoses, characterized by nodular lesions of the cutaneous and subcutaneous tissues. it is caused by inhalation of contaminated dust or by infection of a wound.

MONDO:0005969.name: st. louis encephalitis
MONDO:0005969.def: a viral encephalitis caused by the st. louis encephalitis virus (encephalitis virus, st. louis), a flavivirus. it is transmitted to humans and other vertebrates primarily by mosquitoes of the genus culex. the primary animal vectors are wild birds and the disorder is endemic to the midwestern and southeastern united states. infections may be limited to an influenza-like illness or present as an aseptic meningitis or encephalitis. clinical manifestations of the encephalitic presentation may include seizures, lethargy, myoclonus, focal neurologic signs, coma, and death. (from adams et al., principles of neurology, 6th ed, p750)
MONDO:0005969.synonym: st. louis encephalitis virus infectious encephalitis

MONDO:0005970.name: staphylococcal pneumonia
MONDO:0005970.def: pneumonia caused by infections with bacteria of the genus staphylococcus, usually with staphylococcus aureus.

MONDO:0005971.name: staphyloenterotoxemia
MONDO:0005971.def: food poisoning that is caused by staphylococcal infection.

MONDO:0005972.name: streptococcal pneumonia
MONDO:0005972.def: a febrile disease caused by streptococcus pneumoniae.

MONDO:0005973.name: strongylida infectious disease
MONDO:0005973.def: infections with nematodes of the order strongylida.

MONDO:0005974.name: strongyloidiasis
MONDO:0005974.def: an infection that is caused by nematodes of the genus strongyloides, most commonly strongyloides stercoralis, which is a soil-transmitted helminth, and which is characterized by a variety of gastrointestinal, dermatologic, and, occasionally, pulmonary manifestations. the worm's autoinfective life cycle can lead to hyper-infection and life-threatening dissemination in immunocompromised hosts decades after initial infection.

MONDO:0005975.name: suppurative otitis media
MONDO:0005975.def: inflammation of the middle ear with purulent discharge.

MONDO:0005976.name: syphilis
MONDO:0005976.def: a contagious bacterial infection caused by the spirochete treponema pallidum. it is a sexually transmitted disorder, although it can also be transmitted from the mother to the fetus in utero. typically, it is initially manifested with a single sore which heals without treatment. if the infection is left untreated, the initial stage is followed by skin rash and mucous membrane lesions. a late stage follows, which is characterized by damage of the internal organs, including the nervous system.

MONDO:0005977.name: tabes dorsalis
MONDO:0005977.def: a form of neurosyphilis characterized by slowly progressive degeneration of the spinal cord. signs and symptoms include pain, ataxia, loss of coordination, personality changes, blindness, urinary incontinence, dementia, and degeneration of the joints.

MONDO:0005978.name: theileriasis
MONDO:0005978.def: infection of cattle, sheep, or goats with protozoa of the genus theileria. this infection results in an acute or chronic febrile condition.

MONDO:0005979.name: thoracic outlet syndrome
MONDO:0005979.def: a syndrome resulting from the compression of the blood vessels or nerves in the space between the clavicle and first rib (thoracic outlet). it is caused by car accident injuries or repetitive job or sport-related injuries. signs and symptoms include pain in the shoulders and neck, numbness in the fingers, and weakening grip.

MONDO:0005980.name: tick infestation
MONDO:0005980.def: infestations with soft-bodied (argasidae) or hard-bodied (ixodidae) ticks.

MONDO:0005981.name: tick paralysis
MONDO:0005981.def: paralysis caused by a neurotropic toxin secreted by the salivary glands of ticks.

MONDO:0005982.name: tinea infection
MONDO:0005982.def: a skin infection caused by a fungus.

MONDO:0005983.name: tinea favosa
MONDO:0005983.def: a severe, chronic fungal skin infection, usually of the scalp, characterized by the development of thick, yellow cup-shaped crusts and scarring over hair follicles.

MONDO:0005984.name: tinea pedis
MONDO:0005984.def: dermatological pruritic lesion in the feet, caused by trichophyton rubrum, t. mentagrophytes, or epidermophyton floccosum.

MONDO:0005985.name: togaviridae infectious disease
MONDO:0005985.def: virus diseases caused by the togaviridae.

MONDO:0005986.name: torovirus infectious disease
MONDO:0005986.def: infections with viruses of the genus torovirus, family coronaviridae.

MONDO:0005987.name: toxascariasis
MONDO:0005987.def: infections with nematodes of the genus toxascaris.

MONDO:0005988.name: toxocariasis
MONDO:0005988.def: a parasitic infection caused by worms found in domestic animals. in humans nematode larvae enter the portal system from the small intestine and disseminate in visceral organs causing inflammatory reactions. signs and symptoms include eosinophilia, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and lung infections.

MONDO:0005989.name: toxoplasmosis
MONDO:0005989.def: a parasitic disease contracted by the ingestion or fetal transmission of toxoplasma gondii.

MONDO:0005990.name: tracheitis
MONDO:0005990.def: a tracheal disease which involves bacterial infection of the trachea often caused by staphylococcus aureus and streptococci that follows a recent viral upper respiratory infection. the symptoms include barking croup cough, loud squeaking noise while breathing, scratchy feeling in the throat, high fever, and production of large amounts of pus-filled secretions.

MONDO:0005991.name: trench fever
MONDO:0005991.def: an intermittent fever characterized by intervals of chills, fever, and splenomegaly each of which may last as long as 40 hours. it is caused by bartonella quintana and transmitted by the human louse.

MONDO:0005993.name: trichomonas vaginitis urogenital infection
MONDO:0005993.def: a sexually transmitted parasitic infection caused by trichomonas vaginalis. symptoms include vaginal discharge, vaginal odor, vaginal itching, and discomfort during intercourse.

MONDO:0005994.name: trichostrongyloidiasis
MONDO:0005994.def: infection by roundworms of the superfamily trichostrongyloidea, including the genera trichostrongylus; ostertagia; cooperia, haemonchus; nematodirus, hyostrongylus, and dictyocaulus.

MONDO:0005995.name: trichostrongylosis
MONDO:0005995.def: infestation with nematode worms of the genus trichostrongylus. humans become infected by swallowing larvae, usually with contaminated food or drink, although the larvae may penetrate human skin.

MONDO:0005996.name: trichuriasis
MONDO:0005996.def: an infection that is caused by the nematode trichuris trichiura, a soil-transmitted helminth, which is transmitted via food and/or water contaminated with the eggs of the worm. symptoms are usually mild and include abdominal pain, diarrhea, fatigue, and possibly anemia secondary to blood loss in diarrhea.

MONDO:0005997.name: tricuspid valve stenosis
MONDO:0005997.def: narrowing or stricture of the tricuspid orifice of the heart.

MONDO:0005998.name: trombiculiasis
MONDO:0005998.def: infestation with mites of the genus trombiculidae, whose larvae carry the rickettsial agent of scrub typhus.

MONDO:0005999.name: tuberculous empyema
MONDO:0005999.def: an empyema resulting from infection by mycobacterium tuberculosis.

MONDO:0006000.name: tuberculous peritonitis
MONDO:0006000.def: a form of peritonitis seen in patients with tuberculosis, characterized by lesion either as a miliary form or as a pelvic mass on the peritoneal surfaces. most patients have ascites, abdominal swelling, abdominal pain, and other systemic symptoms such as fever; weight loss; and anemia.

MONDO:0006001.name: urinary schistosomiasis
MONDO:0006001.def: a bladder infection that occurs as a manifetation of a systemic infection with one or more species of the parasitic worms of the schistosoma type; this can progress to bladder cancer in time.

MONDO:0006002.name: urogenital tuberculosis
MONDO:0006002.def: a general term for mycobacterium infections of any part of the urogenital system in either the male or the female.

MONDO:0006003.name: uterine corpus cancer
MONDO:0006003.def: a malignant neoplasm involving the body of uterus.

MONDO:0006004.name: vasomotor rhinitis
MONDO:0006004.def: inflammation in the nasal cavity mucosa that results from the abnormal regulation of the blood flow in the nose. it may be caused by temperature fluctuations, air pollution, strong odors, and tobacco smoke. it results in chronic nasal congestion, sneezing, and running nose.

MONDO:0006005.name: venezuelan equine encephalitis
MONDO:0006005.def: a condition caused by infection by the venezuelan equine encephalitis virus, which is characterized by headache, fever, myalgia, nausea, and vomiting.

MONDO:0006006.name: verrucous carcinoma
MONDO:0006006.def: a well differentiated squamous cell carcinoma characterized by a papillary growth pattern, acanthosis, mild cytologic atypia, and pushing tumor margins. the most commonly affected anatomic sites are the oral cavity, nasal cavity, larynx, esophagus, anus, vagina, vulva, and the plantar region of the foot.

MONDO:0006007.name: vesicoureteral reflux
MONDO:0006007.def: abnormal flow of urine from the urinary bladder back into the ureters.

MONDO:0006008.name: vestibular neuronitis
MONDO:0006008.def: idiopathic inflammation of the vestibular nerve, characterized clinically by the acute or subacute onset of vertigo; nausea; and imbalance. the cochlear nerve is typically spared and hearing loss and tinnitus do not usually occur. symptoms usually resolve over a period of days to weeks. (adams et al., principles of neurology, 6th ed, p304)

MONDO:0006010.name: salmonid viral hemorrhagic septicemia
MONDO:0006010.def: a systemic infection of various salmonid and a few nonsalmonid fishes caused by viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (see novirhabdovirus),

MONDO:0006011.name: viral hepatitis
MONDO:0006011.def: an acute or chronic inflammation of the liver parenchyma caused by viruses. representative examples include hepatitis a, b, and c, cytomegalovirus hepatitis, and herpes simplex hepatitis.

MONDO:0006012.name: viral pneumonia
MONDO:0006012.def: inflammation of the lung parenchyma that is caused by a viral infection.

MONDO:0006013.name: visna disease
MONDO:0006013.def: demyelinating leukoencephalomyelitis of sheep caused by the visna-maedi virus. it is similar to but not the same as scrapie.

MONDO:0006014.name: vulvovaginal candidiasis
MONDO:0006014.def: infection of the vulva and vagina with a fungus of the genus candida. it is a disease associated with hiv infection.

MONDO:0006015.name: waterhouse-friderichsen syndrome
MONDO:0006015.def: a serious disorder characterized by massive adrenal gland hemorrhage secondary to a bacterial infection, most often neisseria meningitidis infection. it is manifested with decreased blood pressure, shock, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and adrenocortical insufficiency.

MONDO:0006018.name: wissler syndrome
MONDO:0006018.def: a rheumatic syndrome of possibly allergic origin, usually affecting children and adolescents, and characterized by high fever, exanthema, arthralgia, leukocytosis, and increased sedimentation rate.

MONDO:0006019.name: yaws
MONDO:0006019.def: an endemic, infectious, nonvenereal disease in humans that presents mainly in children younger than 15 years. the disease occurs primarily in warm, humid, tropical areas of africa, asia, south america, and oceania, among poor rural populations where conditions of overcrowding and poor sanitation prevail. infection with treponema pertenue, a subspecies of treponema pallidum, causes the disease.

MONDO:0006021.name: prinzmetal angina
MONDO:0006021.def: a syndrome typically consisting of angina (cardiac chest pain) at rest that occurs in cycles. it is caused by vasospasm, a narrowing of the coronary arteries caused by contraction of the smooth muscle tissue in the vessel walls rather than directly by atherosclerosis (buildup of fatty plaque and hardening of the arteries). for a portion of patients prinzmetal's angina may be a manifestation of vasospastic disorder and is associated with migraine, raynaud's phenomenon or aspirin-induced asthma.

MONDO:0006022.name: acidosis disorder
MONDO:0006022.def: an abnormally high acidity of the blood and other body tissues. acidosis can be either respiratory or metabolic.

MONDO:0006026.name: urinary bladder disorder
MONDO:0006026.def: a disease involving the urinary bladder.

MONDO:0006027.name: breast synovial sarcoma
MONDO:0006027.def: a synovial sarcoma (disease) that involves the breast.

MONDO:0006028.name: cecum adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006028.def: a carcinoma that arises from glandular epithelial cells of the caecum

MONDO:0006029.name: cecum carcinoma
MONDO:0006029.def: a carcinoma that arises from epithelial cells of the caecum

MONDO:0006030.name: chronic cystitis
MONDO:0006030.def: recurrent infections of the urinary bladder.

MONDO:0006033.name: diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
MONDO:0006033.def: a neuroglial tumor that arises from the middle portion of the brain stem. it usually affects children and has a poor prognosis.

MONDO:0006034.name: gastric adenosquamous carcinoma
MONDO:0006034.def: a carcinoma that arises from the stomach and is characterized by the presence of malignant cells with glandular and squamous differentiation.

MONDO:0006035.name: gastric tubular adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006035.def: a variant of gastric adenocarcinoma characterized by prominent dilated or slit-like tubules.

MONDO:0006036.name: granulosa cell tumor
MONDO:0006036.def: a slow-growing, malignant tumor, characterize by the presence of granulosa-like cells and call-exner bodies, that is almost always found in the ovary. in rare cases, it has also been found in the testicle. there are two types of granulosa cell tumor that can be distinguished under the microscope: the adult and the juvenile. the testicular juvenile granulosa cell tumors are perhaps the most common congenital testicular neoplasms.

MONDO:0006037.name: hydrolethalus syndrome
MONDO:0006037.def: hydrolethalus (hls) is a severe fetal malformation syndrome characterized by craniofacial dysmorphic features, central nervous system, cardiac, respiratory tract and limb abnormalities.

MONDO:0006038.name: indeterminate colitis
MONDO:0006038.def: it describes patients in whom a diagnosis of ulcerative colitis or crohn's disease cannot be made based on standard clinical testing, including colonoscopy, imaging, laboratory tests, and biopsy.

MONDO:0006039.name: infectious colitis
MONDO:0006039.def: a viral or bacterial infectious process affecting the large intestine.

MONDO:0006040.name: lactic acidosis
MONDO:0006040.def: metabolic acidosis characterized by the accumulation of lactate in the body. it is caused by tissue hypoxia.

MONDO:0006041.name: lung carcinoid tumor
MONDO:0006041.def: a neuroendocrine neoplasm that arises from the lung. it is characterized by the presence of uniform polygonal cells with small or moderate amount of cytoplasm and inconspicuous nucleoli. the cells are usually arranged in organoid and trabecular patterns. it is classified as typical or atypical carcinoid tumor based on the number of mitotic figures and the absence or presence of necrosis. atypical carcinoid tumors have a worse prognosis.

MONDO:0006042.name: meningeal tuberculosis
MONDO:0006042.def: a bacterial infection of the membranes covering the brain and the spinal cord caused by mycobacterium tuberculosis.

MONDO:0006043.name: metaplastic breast carcinoma
MONDO:0006043.def: a group of invasive breast carcinomas characterized by the presence of an adenocarcinomatous component which is admixed with a dominant component that is composed of squamous cells, spindle cells, or mesenchymal cells.

MONDO:0006044.name: nephrosclerosis
MONDO:0006044.def: hardening of the kidney due to infiltration by fibrous connective tissue (fibrosis), usually caused by renovascular diseases or chronic hypertension. nephrosclerosis leads to renal ischemia.

MONDO:0006045.name: ovarian clear cell adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006045.def: a malignant glandular epithelial neoplasm characterized by the presence of clear and hobnail cells. it is highly associated with ovarian endometriosis, pelvic endometriosis and paraendocrine hypercalcemia.

MONDO:0006046.name: ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006046.def: a malignant serous cystic epithelial neoplasm arising from the ovary. it is characterized by the presence of glandular, papillary, or solid structures. psammoma bodies may be present. in well differentiated cases the malignant epithelial cells resemble the cells of fallopian tube epithelium. in poorly differentiated cases the malignant epithelial cells show anaplastic features.

MONDO:0006047.name: pancreatic adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006047.def: a carcinoma that arises from glandular epithelial cells of the pancreas

MONDO:0006049.name: papillary lung adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006049.def: a morphologic variant of lung adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of papillary structures.

MONDO:0006050.name: pleomorphic breast carcinoma
MONDO:0006050.def: a rare, aggressive, high grade invasive ductal carcinoma, not otherwise specified. it is characterized by the presence of pleomorphic and bizarre malignant cells that constitute more than 50 percent of the malignant cellular infiltrate.

MONDO:0006052.name: pulmonary tuberculosis
MONDO:0006052.def: a bacterial infection that affects the lungs and is caused by mycobacterium tuberculosis. most patients with tuberculosis do not have symptoms (latent tuberculosis) and are not contagious. when signs and symptoms occur (active tuberculosis), patients become contagious. the signs and symptoms include chronic cough with blood-tinged sputum, night sweats, fever, fatigue, and weight loss.

MONDO:0006053.name: renal leiomyoma
MONDO:0006053.def: a leiomyoma that involves the kidney.

MONDO:0006054.name: reproductive system neoplasm
MONDO:0006054.def: a benign or malignant, primary or metastatic neoplasm affecting the male and female reproductive system.

MONDO:0006055.name: sex cord-stromal tumor
MONDO:0006055.def: a neoplasm involving a sex cord.

MONDO:0006056.name: squamous cell breast carcinoma
MONDO:0006056.def: a rare carcinoma that arises from the breast parenchyma and is entirely composed of squamous cells.
MONDO:0006056.synonym: squamous cell carcinoma of the breast

MONDO:0006058.name: wilms tumor
MONDO:0006058.def: an embryonal neoplasm characterized by the presence of epithelial, mesenchymal, and blastema components. the vast majority of cases arise from the kidney. a small number of cases with morphologic features resembling wilms tumor of the kidney have been reported arising from the ovary and the cervix.

MONDO:0006059.name: nasal cavity squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0006059.def: a squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the nasal cavity mucosa. signs and symptoms include nasal fullness and obstruction, pain, epistaxis, and the presence of a nasal mass.
MONDO:0006059.synonym: squamous cell carcinoma of the nasal cavity

MONDO:0006060.name: nasopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0006060.def: a squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the nasopharynx.

MONDO:0006061.name: cervical artery dissection
MONDO:0006061.def: a tear within the wall of any of the arteries of the neck (carotid artery or vertebral artery) and that allows blood to separate the wall layers. by separating a portion of the wall of the artery (a layer of the tunica intima or tunica media), a dissection creates two lumens or passages within the vessel, the native or true lumen, and the \"false lumen\

MONDO:0006066.name: acinar prostate adenocarcinoma, foamy gland variant
MONDO:0006066.def: a variant of acinar prostate adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of malignant cells with abundant xanthomatous appearing cytoplasm.

MONDO:0006067.name: acinar prostate mucinous adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006067.def: a usually aggressive morphologic variant of acinar adenocarcinoma of the prostate gland characterized by the presence of lakes of extracellular mucin. this diagnosis applies when at least 25% of the resected tumor contains extracellular mucin.

MONDO:0006068.name: acth-producing pituitary gland adenoma
MONDO:0006068.def: an adenoma of the pituitary gland that produces corticotropin. the vast majority of cases are associated with cushing disease. clinical manifestations include truncal obesity with thin extremities, thinning of the skin, osteoporosis, and a tendency to bruise easily. silent or hormonally non-functioning acth producing adenomas have also been described. they produce symptoms of a mass-related lesion.

MONDO:0006069.name: acth-producing pituitary gland carcinoma
MONDO:0006069.def: a rare, hormonally functioning or non-functioning pituitary gland adenocarcinoma that produces corticotropin. it may be associated with cushing disease.

MONDO:0006071.name: adenofibroma
MONDO:0006071.def: a benign neoplasm characterized by the presence of connective tissue stroma and epithelial structures. it occurs in the ovary, fallopian tube, uterine corpus, and cervix. cases of adenofibroma of the ovary with low grade malignant potential have also been reported.

MONDO:0006072.name: obsolete adenoid cystic breast carcinoma
MONDO:0006072.def: obsolete. an adenoid cystic carcinoma primarily involving the breast. three morphologic patterns are seen: cribriform, trabecular, and solid. the prognosis is excellent.

MONDO:0006073.name: adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
MONDO:0006073.def: a benign, slow growing neoplasm arising from tooth-forming tissues. the vast majority of cases are intraosseous and most often grow in the maxilla. it is characterized by the presence of odontogenic epithelium which is embedded in a connective tissue stroma. local excision is curative and recurrences are very rare.

MONDO:0006074.name: adenosquamous carcinoma
MONDO:0006074.def: a carcinoma composed of malignant glandular cells and malignant squamous cells.
MONDO:0006074.synonym: mixed adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma

MONDO:0006075.name: adrenal gland myelolipoma
MONDO:0006075.def: a benign soft tissue lesion arising from the adrenal gland. it is composed of mature adipose and hematopoietic/lymphoid tissues.

MONDO:0006076.name: adrenal gland neuroblastoma
MONDO:0006076.def: a neuroblastoma arising from the adrenal gland.

MONDO:0006077.name: adrenal medullary hyperplasia
MONDO:0006077.def: a hyperplasia that involves the adrenal medulla.

MONDO:0006078.name: aids-related primary central nervous system lymphoma
MONDO:0006078.def: a lymphoma (non-hodgkin or hodgkin) arising from the central nervous system and occurring in hiv-positive patients.

MONDO:0006079.name: ameloblastic carcinoma
MONDO:0006079.def: a rare, cytologically malignant ameloblastoma that may metastasize.

MONDO:0006081.name: anal melanoma
MONDO:0006081.def: a melanoma arising from the anus. clinical presentation includes rectal bleeding, tenesmus, pain, and change in bowel habit. the prognosis is usually poor.

MONDO:0006082.name: anal squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0006082.def: a squamous cell carcinoma (scc) arising from the anal canal or the anal margin (perianal skin). human papillomavirus is detected in the majority of cases. homosexual hiv-positive men have an increased risk of developing anal squamous cell carcinoma in comparison to the general male population. symptoms include anal pruritus, discomfort when sitting, pain, change in bowel habit, and bleeding. the prognosis is generally better for anal margin scc than for anal canal scc.
MONDO:0006082.synonym: squamous cell carcinoma of the anus

MONDO:0006083.name: obsolete anaplastic large cell lymphoma, alk-negative

MONDO:0006085.name: angiolipoma
MONDO:0006085.def: a lipoma with prominent vascularity. the vascular tissue is more abundant at the periphery of the tumor and contains fibrin thrombi. it occurs more frequently in younger individuals as a painful subcutaneous nodule, often on the arms.

MONDO:0006086.name: angiomyxoma
MONDO:0006086.def: a benign soft tissue neoplasm characterized by the presence of neoplastic spindle and stellate cells, and vascular proliferation in a myxoid stroma.

MONDO:0006087.name: appendix adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006087.def: a carcinoma that arises from glandular epithelial cells of the vermiform appendix.

MONDO:0006088.name: appendix adenoma
MONDO:0006088.def: a circumscribed neoplasm arising from the glandular epithelium of the appendix. morphologically, it is characterized by a proliferation of neoplastic glandular cells and it is associated with dysplasia. according to the growth pattern, it may be classified as tubular, villous, or tubulovillous. the dysplasia is classified as mild, moderate, or severe.

MONDO:0006090.name: appendix hyperplastic polyp
MONDO:0006090.def: a non-neoplastic polyp that arises from the appendix. it is characterized by the presence of elongated serrated crypts and the absence of atypia or dysplasia.

MONDO:0006091.name: appendix neuroendocrine tumor g1
MONDO:0006091.def: a well differentiated, low grade tumor with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the appendix. the mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 hpf and/or the ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent.
MONDO:0006091.synonym: vermiform appendix neuroendocrine tumor, well differentiated, low grade

MONDO:0006092.name: appendix villous adenoma
MONDO:0006092.def: an adenoma arising from the appendix. it is characterized by the presence of villous epithelial structures and it is associated with dysplasia.

MONDO:0006093.name: ascending colon neuroendocrine tumor g1
MONDO:0006093.def: a well differentiated, low grade neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid tumor) that arises from the ascending colon. the mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 hpf and/or the ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent.
MONDO:0006093.synonym: grade 1 neuroendocrine neoplasm of ascending colon

MONDO:0006094.name: askin tumor
MONDO:0006094.def: a primitive neuroectodermal tumor (small round blue cell tumor) of the thorax which can involve the periosteum, thoracic wall and/or pleura though it spares the lung parenchyma.
MONDO:0006094.synonym: small cell tumour of thoracopulmonary region

MONDO:0006095.name: atypical carcinoid tumor
MONDO:0006095.def: a carcinoid tumor characterized by a high mitotic rate, often associated with the presence of necrosis and nuclear pleomorphism.

MONDO:0006096.name: atypical endometrial hyperplasia
MONDO:0006096.def: an endometrial hyperplasia characterized by cytologic and architectural changes which may lead to endometrial carcinoma. despite the atypical features and possible course, there is debate on whether to consider this a neoplasm. the relationship with endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia is also unclear.

MONDO:0006097.name: atypical lipomatous tumor
MONDO:0006097.def: an intermediate, locally aggressive lipomatous neoplasm. microscopically, the adipose tissue contains large and pleomorphic lipoblasts, and is dissected by fibrous septa containing spindle cells. it requires a wide local excision, may recur locally, but never metastasizes.
MONDO:0006097.synonym: well differentiated liposarcoma of superficial soft tissue

MONDO:0006098.name: atypical lobular breast hyperplasia
MONDO:0006098.def: lobular neoplasia characterized by lobular epithelial proliferation that does not completely fill the lobular unit of the breast.
MONDO:0006098.synonym: atypical lobular hyperplasia of the breast

MONDO:0006101.name: obsolete bartholin gland squamous cell carcinoma

MONDO:0006102.name: basaloid carcinoma
MONDO:0006102.def: a malignant epithelial neoplasm characterized by the presence of neoplastic cells with hyperchromatic nuclei, small amount of cytoplasm, and peripheral nuclear palisading.

MONDO:0006103.name: benign adrenal gland pheochromocytoma
MONDO:0006103.def: a sporadic or familial pheochromocytoma that is confined to the adrenal gland and does not have any metastatic potential. the majority of cases are sporadic, and usually unilateral. familial cases are usually bilateral.

MONDO:0006104.name: benign carotid body paraganglioma
MONDO:0006104.def: a carotid body paraganglioma that is confined to the site of origin, without metastatic potential.

MONDO:0006105.name: benign conjunctival neoplasm
MONDO:0006105.def: abnormal growth of the cells of the conjunctiva without malignant characteristics.

MONDO:0006106.name: benign smooth muscle neoplasm
MONDO:0006106.def: a benign mesenchymal neoplasm arising from smooth muscle tissue.

MONDO:0006107.name: benign thyroid gland neoplasm
MONDO:0006107.def: a benign neoplasm arising from the thyroid gland.

MONDO:0006108.name: bile duct adenoma
MONDO:0006108.def: a benign, well-demarcated polypoid neoplasm arising from the bile duct epithelium. according to the growth pattern, it is classified as tubular, papillary, or tubulopapillary. adenomas arising from the extrahepatic bile ducts usually produce symptoms related to biliary obstruction.

MONDO:0006109.name: malignant biphasic mesothelioma
MONDO:0006109.def: a malignant neoplasm arising from mesothelial cells in the pleura. it is characterized by the presence of neoplastic epithelioid cells and sarcomatoid features.

MONDO:0006111.name: bladder flat intraepithelial lesion
MONDO:0006111.def: a non-papillary neoplasm of the urinary bladder, whose classification categories include low-grade intraurothelial neoplasia and urothelial carcinoma in situ.

MONDO:0006112.name: bladder inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor
MONDO:0006112.def: a multinodular intermediate fibroblastic neoplasm arising from the bladder. it is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped fibroblasts and myofibroblasts, and a chronic inflammatory infiltrate composed of eosinophils, lymphocytes and plasma cells.

MONDO:0006113.name: obsolete bladder small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma

MONDO:0006115.name: blast phase chronic myelogenous leukemia, bcr-abl1 positive
MONDO:0006115.def: an advanced phase of chronic myelogenous leukemia. it is characterized by: 1. the presence of blasts in the peripheral blood or bone marrow that are at least 20% of the peripheral blood white cells or of the nucleated cells in the bone marrow respectively, or 2. an extramedullary proliferation of blasts, and/or 3. when there are large aggregates and clusters of blasts in the bone marrow biopsy specimen (adapted from who, 2001).

MONDO:0006116.name: breast carcinoma by gene expression profile
MONDO:0006116.def: a header term that includes the following breast carcinoma subtypes determined by gene expression profiling: luminal a breast carcinoma, luminal b breast carcinoma, her2 positive breast carcinoma, basal-like breast carcinoma, triple-negative breast carcinoma, and normal breast-like subtype of breast carcinoma.
MONDO:0006116.synonym: breast carcinoma by gene expression profile

MONDO:0006117.name: breast diffuse large b-cell lymphoma
MONDO:0006117.def: a diffuse large b-cell lymphoma that arises from the breast. it is the most common type of primary breast lymphoma.
MONDO:0006117.synonym: diffuse large b-cell lymphoma of breast

MONDO:0006118.name: breast fibrosis
MONDO:0006118.def: breast fibrocystic change characterized by the prominence of fibrotic changes in the parenchyma.

MONDO:0006119.name: breast mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma
MONDO:0006119.def: an extranodal marginal zone b-cell lymphoma of mucosa associated lymphoid tissue that arises from the breast as a primary tumor.

MONDO:0006120.name: c-cell hyperplasia
MONDO:0006120.def: neoplastic or reactive proliferation of the c-cells in the thyroid gland. the neoplastic c-cell hyperplasia is associated with familial medullary thyroid gland carcinoma and multiple endocrine neoplasia type ii and iib. morphologically, it is characterized by the presence of clusters of intrafollicular c-cells with atypical cytologic features. the reactive c-cell hyperplasia is also known as physiological or secondary c-cell hyperplasia and it is associated with conditions that cause hypercalcemia (e.g., hyperparathyroidism).

MONDO:0006121.name: calcifying fibrous tumor
MONDO:0006121.def: a benign well-circumscribed paucicellular lesion arising from the soft tissues. it is characterized by the presence of fibroblasts, lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates, collagenous stroma formation, psammoma bodies, and dystrophic calcifications.

MONDO:0006122.name: calcifying nested epithelial stromal tumor of the liver
MONDO:0006122.def: a rare malignant tumor that arises from the liver and occurs in children. it is characterized by the presence of nested epithelioid and spindle cells. desmoplasia, calcifications, and bone formation may also be present.

MONDO:0006123.name: cardiac rhabdomyoma
MONDO:0006123.def: a well circumscribed benign tumor arising from cardiac muscle. it usually affects children and may be present in the fetus. depending on tumor location and size, cardiac, respiratory, and hemodynamic parameters may be affected. there is an association between cardiac rhabdomyoma and tuberous sclerosis.

MONDO:0006126.name: cecum neuroendocrine tumor g1
MONDO:0006126.def: a well differentiated, low grade neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid tumor) that arises from the cecum. the mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 hpf and/or the ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent.

MONDO:0006128.name: central nervous system anaplastic large cell lymphoma
MONDO:0006128.def: an anaplastic large cell lymphoma that affects the brain, meninges, or spinal cord.
MONDO:0006128.synonym: primary cns anaplastic large cell lymphoma

MONDO:0006130.name: central nervous system neoplasm
MONDO:0006130.def: a benign or malignant, primary or metastatic neoplasm that affects the brain, meninges, or spinal cord. representative examples of primary neoplasms include astrocytoma, oligodendroglioma, ependymoma, and meningioma. representative examples of metastatic neoplasms include carcinoma and leukemia.

MONDO:0006131.name: cerebellar liponeurocytoma
MONDO:0006131.def: a rare, who grade ii cerebellar neoplasm which shows consistent neuronal, variable astrocytic and focal lipomatous differentiation. it occurs in adults, has a low proliferative potential and usually has a favorable prognosis. (adapted from who)

MONDO:0006132.name: cervical adenoid basal carcinoma
MONDO:0006132.def: a rare low grade carcinoma that arises from the cervix. it is characterized by the presence of nests of basaloid cells with focal glandular formations.

MONDO:0006133.name: cervical adenoid cystic carcinoma
MONDO:0006133.def: a rare carcinoma that arises from the cervix. it is characterized by the presence of cystic spaces surrounded by palisaded epithelial cells. the cystic spaces contain eosinophilic hyaline material or mucin. nuclear pleomorphism, necrotic changes, and a high mitotic rate are also present.

MONDO:0006134.name: cervical adenosquamous carcinoma
MONDO:0006134.def: an uncommon carcinoma arising from the cervix. it is composed of malignant glandular epithelial cells and malignant squamous epithelial cells.

MONDO:0006135.name: cervical clear cell adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006135.def: a rare morphologic variant of cervical adenocarcinoma composed of clear and hobnail cells. it is associated with in utero exposure to diethylstilbestrol (des).

MONDO:0006137.name: cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2/3
MONDO:0006137.def: a neoplastic process in the cervix characterized by morphologic features of both moderate and severe intraepithelial neoplasia.

MONDO:0006138.name: cervical large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
MONDO:0006138.def: a rare, aggressive neuroendocrine carcinoma that arises from the cervix and is characterized by the presence of malignant cells with abundant cytoplasm, large nuclei, and prominent nucleoli.

MONDO:0006139.name: cervical metaplasia
MONDO:0006139.def: metaplastic changes in the cervical glandular or squamous epithelium.

MONDO:0006140.name: cervical mucinous adenocarcinoma, minimal deviation variant
MONDO:0006140.def: a rare, extremely well differentiated cervical mucinous adenocarcinoma in which most of the neoplastic glands cannot be distinguished from the normal endocervical glands.
MONDO:0006140.synonym: cervical mucinous adenocarcinoma, minimal deviation variant

MONDO:0006141.name: cervical villoglandular adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006141.def: a cervical adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of a prominent villoglandular pattern.

MONDO:0006142.name: cervical small cell carcinoma
MONDO:0006142.def: a small cell carcinoma arising from the cervix.

MONDO:0006143.name: cervical squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0006143.def: a squamous cell carcinoma arising from the cervical epithelium. it usually evolves from a precancerous cervical lesion. increased numbers of sexual partners and human papillomavirus (hpv) infection are risk factors for cervical squamous cell carcinoma. the following histologic patterns have been described: conventional squamous cell carcinoma, papillary squamous cell carcinoma, transitional cell carcinoma, lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma, verrucous carcinoma, condylomatous carcinoma and spindle cell carcinoma. survival is most closely related to the stage of disease at the time of diagnosis.

MONDO:0006144.name: cervical wilms tumor
MONDO:0006144.def: an embryonal neoplasm arising from the cervix with morphologic features resembling wilms tumor of the kidney.

MONDO:0006145.name: chondroid chordoma
MONDO:0006145.def: a slow-growing malignant bone tumor arising from the remnants of the notochord and occurring in the base of the skull. the tumor is characterized by a lobulated growth pattern, myxoid stroma formation, and the presence of physaliphorous cells and cartilage.

MONDO:0006146.name: chondroid hamartoma
MONDO:0006146.def: a hamartoma that is characterized by the presence of chondroid elements.

MONDO:0006147.name: obsolete chronic eosinophilic leukemia, not otherwise specified

MONDO:0006149.name: clear cell papillary cystadenoma
MONDO:0006149.def: a benign cystic glandular epithelial neoplasm characterized by the presence of neoplastic clear or hobnail cells which form papillary structures. there is no evidence of stromal invasion.

MONDO:0006150.name: colon burkitt lymphoma
MONDO:0006150.def: a rare burkitt lymphoma that arises from the colon.

MONDO:0006151.name: colon dysplasia
MONDO:0006151.def: a morphologic finding indicating the presence of dysplastic glandular epithelial cells in the colonic mucosa. there is no evidence of invasion.

MONDO:0006152.name: colon inflammatory polyp
MONDO:0006152.def: a non-neoplastic polypoid lesion in the colon. it may arise in a background of inflammatory bowel disease or colitis. it is characterized by the presence of a distorted epithelium, inflammation, and fibrosis.

MONDO:0006153.name: colon juvenile polyp
MONDO:0006153.def: a non-neoplastic hamartomatous polyp that arises from the colon. it is characterized by the presence of tortuous and cystically dilated glands, edematous changes, and inflammation.

MONDO:0006154.name: colon mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma
MONDO:0006154.def: an extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue that arises from the colon.

MONDO:0006155.name: colon neuroendocrine tumor g1
MONDO:0006155.def: a well differentiated, low grade neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid tumor) that arises from the colon. the mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 hpf and/or the ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent.

MONDO:0006156.name: colon sessile serrated adenoma/polyp
MONDO:0006156.def: a polyp that arises from the colon. it is characterized by the presence of serrated glands and the absence of generalized dysplasia. some authors have suggested that it is a precursor lesion for some colonic adenocarcinomas with microsatellite instability.

MONDO:0006157.name: colorectal adenosquamous carcinoma
MONDO:0006157.def: an unusual colorectal carcinoma characterized by the presence of glandular and squamous carcinomatous components. the two carcinomatous components may be admixed within the tumor, or the two may appear separately in different areas.

MONDO:0006158.name: colorectal diffuse large b-cell lymphoma
MONDO:0006158.def: a diffuse large b-cell lymphoma that arises from the colon or rectum.
MONDO:0006158.synonym: diffuse large b-cell lymphoma of colorectum

MONDO:0006159.name: colorectal gastrointestinal stromal tumor
MONDO:0006159.def: a gastrointestinal stromal tumor that arises from the colon or rectum. the majority of cases have spindle cell morphology. gastrointestinal stromal tumors of the colon are usually advanced upon detection and tend to have a poor prognosis; gastrointestinal stromal tumors of the rectum usually have an aggressive clinical course.

MONDO:0006160.name: colorectal hamartoma
MONDO:0006160.def: a non-neoplastic, hamartomatous polyp that arises from the colon and rectum. this group includes the juvenile polyp, peutz-jeghers polyp, and cowden-associated polyp.

MONDO:0006161.name: colorectal juvenile polyp
MONDO:0006161.def: a non-neoplastic hamartomatous polyp that arises from the colon and rectum. it is characterized by the presence of tortuous and cystically dilated glands, edematous changes, and inflammation.

MONDO:0006162.name: colorectal neuroendocrine tumor g1
MONDO:0006162.def: a well differentiated, low grade neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid tumor) that arises from the colon or rectum. the mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 hpf and/or the ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent.

MONDO:0006163.name: colorectal serrated adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006163.def: a rare, invasive colorectal adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of a malignant infiltrate with serrated glandular architecture.

MONDO:0006164.name: colorectal sessile serrated adenoma/polyp
MONDO:0006164.def: a polyp that arises from the colon or rectum. it is characterized by the presence of serrated glands and the absence of generalized dysplasia. some authors have suggested that it is a precursor lesion for some colorectal adenocarcinomas with microsatellite instability.

MONDO:0006165.name: colorectal squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0006165.def: a very rare colorectal carcinoma characterized by the presence of a malignant squamous cell infiltrate.

MONDO:0006166.name: columnar cell hyperplasia of the breast
MONDO:0006166.def: a columnar cell lesion characterized by the presence of enlarged terminal ductal lobular units with dilated acini. the acini are lined by more than two layers of columnar epithelial cells. prominent apical cytoplasmic snouts are present. secretions are often present in the lumina of the dilated acini.

MONDO:0006167.name: combined lung carcinoma
MONDO:0006167.def: a lung carcinoma characterized by the presence of large or small neuroendocrine carcinoma cells in combination with malignant glandular or squamous epithelial cells.

MONDO:0006169.name: complex endometrial hyperplasia
MONDO:0006169.def: a hyperplasia characterized by excessive proliferation of endometrial cells, resulting in the formation of complex epithelial structures. epithelial atypia may be present or absent.

MONDO:0006172.name: conjunctival nevus
MONDO:0006172.def: a benign melanocytic neoplasm that arises from the conjunctiva.

MONDO:0006173.name: conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0006173.def: a low-grade squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the conjunctiva. it is the most common primary malignant tumor that arises from the conjunctiva. it usually affects older white males. excessive exposure to sunlight is a risk factor. patients may present with a mass, red eye, or pain.
MONDO:0006173.synonym: squamous cell carcinoma of the conjunctiva

MONDO:0006174.name: cortisol-producing adrenal cortex adenoma
MONDO:0006174.def: an adenoma of the adrenal cortex that produces cortisol. it may be associated with cushing syndrome. clinical presentation includes weight gain, round face, easy bruising, muscle weakness, emotional changes, hirsutism, and hypertension.

MONDO:0006176.name: cribriform carcinoma
MONDO:0006176.def: a carcinoma characterized by the presence of a cribriform architectural pattern. representative examples include the intraductal cribriform breast carcinoma and invasive cribriform breast carcinoma.

MONDO:0006178.name: dedifferentiated solitary fibrous tumor
MONDO:0006178.def: a solitary fibrous tumor characterized by the presence of areas of abrupt transition to high grade sarcoma.

MONDO:0006179.name: desmoplastic ameloblastoma
MONDO:0006179.def: an ameloblastoma with prominent desmoplastic stroma that causes compression of the neoplastic epithelial islands.

MONDO:0006180.name: digestive system adenoma
MONDO:0006180.def: a sporadic or less frequently familial neoplasm, arising from the glandular epithelium of the stomach, small intestine, biliary tract, colon, and rectum. it is a polypoid or flat circumscribed lesion. morphologically, it is characterized by a proliferation of neoplastic glandular cells and it is associated with dysplasia. according to the growth pattern, it may be classified as tubular, villous, or tubulovillous. the dysplasia is classified as mild, moderate, or severe. the frequency of malignant transformation depends on the size of the lesion and the degree of dysplasia. larger adenomas with severe dysplastic changes (sometimes called carcinoma in situ) carry a higher risk of progressing to invasive adenocarcinoma. gastrointestinal adenomas may present as solitary or multifocal lesions. familial adenomas tend to be multifocal and carry a higher risk of malignant transformation.

MONDO:0006181.name: digestive system carcinoma
MONDO:0006181.def: a malignant neoplasm that arises from the epithelium of any part of the digestive system. representative examples include colorectal carcinoma, esophageal carcinoma, and pancreatic carcinoma.

MONDO:0006182.name: digestive system mixed adenoneuroendocrine carcinoma
MONDO:0006182.def: a carcinoma that arises from the digestive system and is characterized by the presence of a malignant glandular epithelial component and a malignant neuroendocrine component. at least 30% of either component should be present for the diagnosis to be made.

MONDO:0006183.name: disseminated peritoneal leiomyomatosis
MONDO:0006183.def: a rare, benign process that affects the peritoneal cavity and is characterized by the formation of multiple small nodules that are composed of well differentiated smooth muscle. it usually affects adults in their late reproductive years. most patients are asymptomatic. the tumor nodules may regress spontaneously.

MONDO:0006184.name: ductal breast carcinoma in situ and lobular carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0006184.def: the co-existence of ductal and lobular carcinoma in situ in the breast, without evidence of stromal invasion.
MONDO:0006184.synonym: non-invasive ductal with non-invasive lobular breast carcinoma

MONDO:0006185.name: obsolete ductal or ductular proliferation
MONDO:0006185.def: obsolete. a morphologic finding indicating the presence of typical or atypical proliferation of biliary epithelial cells in the portal tracts of the liver.

MONDO:0006186.name: duodenal adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006186.def: a carcinoma that arises from glandular epithelial cells of the duodenum.

MONDO:0006187.name: duodenal villous adenoma
MONDO:0006187.def: a neoplasm that arises from the glandular epithelium of the duodenum. it is characterized by a villous architectural pattern. the neoplastic glandular cells have dysplastic features.

MONDO:0006188.name: ebv-positive t-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of childhood
MONDO:0006188.def: an epstein-barr virus-associated mature t-cell lymphoproliferative group of disorders affecting children. it occurs with increased frequency in asians and native americans. it includes the systemic ebv-positive t-cell lymphoma of childhood and the hydroa vacciniforme-like lymphoma.
MONDO:0006188.synonym: ebv-positive t-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of childhood

MONDO:0006189.name: eccrine porocarcinoma
MONDO:0006189.def: a carcinoma with eccrine differentiation arising from the sweat glands. it may arise de novo or as a malignant transformation of a pre-existing poroma. it usually grows in the legs, buttocks, feet, and trunk and usually presents as an ulcerative plaque. it is characterized by the presence of intraepidermal and dermal nests of malignant epithelial cells. it may recur after excision and metastasize to the lymph nodes and less frequently to distal anatomic sites.

MONDO:0006190.name: endolymphatic sac tumor
MONDO:0006190.def: an aggressive epithelial neoplasm arising from the temporal bone. it is characterized by the presence of a papillary pattern, and has been described as an adenoma or carcinoma in the literature. there is disagreement regarding its relationship to endolymphatic sac tumor.

MONDO:0006191.name: endometrial clear cell adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006191.def: a clear cell adenocarcinoma that involves the endometrium.

MONDO:0006192.name: endometrial endometrioid adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006192.def: a primary endometrial adenocarcinoma composed of neoplastic cells that form complex glandular patterns associated with budding and branching of the neoplastic glands. the neoplastic glands resemble those of the normal endometrium and may or may not be associated with sheet-like proliferation of malignant cells. endometrioid adenocarcinoma is the most commonly seen morphologic variant of endometrial adenocarcinoma.

MONDO:0006193.name: endometrial hyperplasia without atypia
MONDO:0006193.def: simple or complex endometrial hyperplasia characterized by the absence of epithelial atypia.

MONDO:0006194.name: obsolete endometrial mucinous adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006194.def: obsolete. a primary, usually low grade adenocarcinoma of the endometrium in which the majority of the malignant epithelial cells contain abundant intracytoplasmic mucin.

MONDO:0006195.name: endometrial polyp
MONDO:0006195.def: a benign nodular lesion protruding above the surface of the endometrium. it is composed of a fibrous stroma that contains thick-walled blood vessels and dilated endometrial glands. polypectomy is the treatment of choice. only few cases with recurrence have been reported.

MONDO:0006196.name: endometrial serous adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006196.def: a high grade, aggressive adenocarcinoma arising from the endometrium. it is characterized by the presence of complex papillary patterns with cellular budding. atypical mitoses, necrosis, and psammoma bodies may be present. it is classified as type ii endometrial carcinoma and it is not associated with endometrial hyperplasia. it tends to invade deeply into the myometrium and spreads into the lymphatic vessels. patients frequently present with spread of the tumor beyond the uterus at the time of diagnosis. the prognosis is usually poor.

MONDO:0006197.name: endometrial small cell carcinoma
MONDO:0006197.def: a primary carcinoma of the endometrium that is similar to the small cell carcinoma of the lung, histologically.

MONDO:0006198.name: endometrial squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0006198.def: a primary carcinoma of the endometrium characterized by the presence of malignant squamous cells.
MONDO:0006198.synonym: squamous cell carcinoma of the endometrium

MONDO:0006199.name: endometrial undifferentiated carcinoma
MONDO:0006199.def: a primary carcinoma of the endometrium characterized by the presence of malignant cells that lack evidence of differentiation.

MONDO:0006200.name: epithelioid cell uveal melanoma
MONDO:0006200.def: a uveal melanoma characterized by the presence of malignant large epithelioid melanocytes.

MONDO:0006201.name: ethmoid sinus adenoid cystic carcinoma
MONDO:0006201.def: an adenoid cystic carcinoma that affects the ethmoid sinus.
MONDO:0006201.synonym: adenoid cystic carcinoma of the ethmoid sinus

MONDO:0006202.name: extrahepatic bile duct adenosquamous carcinoma
MONDO:0006202.def: a carcinoma that arises from the extrahepatic bile ducts. it is characterized by the presence of glandular and squamous malignant epithelial components.

MONDO:0006203.name: extrahepatic bile duct squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0006203.def: a carcinoma that arises from the extrahepatic bile ducts. it is composed entirely by malignant squamous epithelial cells.
MONDO:0006203.synonym: squamous cell carcinoma of the bile duct

MONDO:0006205.name: obsolete extraskeletal ewing sarcoma/peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor

MONDO:0006206.name: fallopian tube carcinoma
MONDO:0006206.def: a carcinoma that arises from epithelial cells of the fallopian tube.

MONDO:0006207.name: fallopian tube carcinosarcoma
MONDO:0006207.def: a carcinosarcoma that arises from the fallopian tube. it usually affects postmenopausal women and presents with abdominal pain, abdominal distension or genital bleeding. the prognosis is usually poor.
MONDO:0006207.synonym: fallopian tube malignant mixed mullerian tumour

MONDO:0006208.name: fallopian tube serous adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006208.def: a serous adenocarcinoma that arises from the fallopian tube. it is usually a high grade invasive adenocarcinoma.

MONDO:0006209.name: fibroblastic neoplasm
MONDO:0006209.def: a benign, intermediate, or malignant mesenchymal neoplasm characterized by the presence of neoplastic fibroblasts.

MONDO:0006210.name: fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma
MONDO:0006210.def: a distinctive type of liver cell carcinoma that arises in non-cirrhotic livers and is seen predominantly in young patients. the tumor cells are polygonal and deeply eosinophilic, and are embedded in a fibrous stroma. the prognosis is similar to classical hepatocellular carcinoma that arises in non-cirrhotic livers, and better than hepatocellular carcinoma that arises in cirrhotic livers.
MONDO:0006210.synonym: polygonal cell type hepatocellular carcinoma with fibrous stroma

MONDO:0006211.name: fibrous hamartoma of infancy
MONDO:0006211.def: a poorly circumscribed neoplasm arising from the soft tissues in infants. it is characterized by the presence of bland fibroblastic spindle cells, collagenous stroma formation, primitive mesenchymal round cells, and mature fat cells. these components combined form a distinct organoid pattern.

MONDO:0006212.name: flat urothelial hyperplasia
MONDO:0006212.def: a type of hyperplasia that is characterized by a marked thickening of the urinary tract epithelium. there is no evidence of cytologic atypia. -- 2003

MONDO:0006213.name: floor of mouth mucoepidermoid carcinoma
MONDO:0006213.def: a mucoepidermoid carcinoma of the oral cavity that arises from the floor of the mouth.
MONDO:0006213.synonym: mucoepidermoid carcinoma of the floor of mouth

MONDO:0006214.name: follicular variant thyroid gland papillary carcinoma
MONDO:0006214.def: a nonencapsulated variant of papillary carcinoma of the thyroid gland characterized by the predominance of follicular structures. the malignant follicular cells display the nuclear features that characterize the papillary adenocarcinomas of the thyroid gland.

MONDO:0006215.name: gallbladder adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006215.def: a carcinoma that arises from glandular epithelial cells of the gall bladder.

MONDO:0006216.name: gallbladder adenoma
MONDO:0006216.def: a polypoid epithelial neoplasm that arises from the gallbladder. according to the neoplastic growth pattern, it is classified as tubular, tubulopapillary, or papillary.

MONDO:0006217.name: gallbladder adenosquamous carcinoma
MONDO:0006217.def: a carcinoma that arises from the gallbladder. it is characterized by the presence of glandular and squamous malignant epithelial components.

MONDO:0006218.name: gallbladder biliary intraepithelial neoplasia
MONDO:0006218.def: a neoplastic, non-invasive lesion that affects the gallbladder epithelium. it is characterized by the presence of atypical epithelial cells with an increased nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio, nuclear hyperchromasia, and loss of nuclear polarity.

MONDO:0006219.name: gallbladder small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
MONDO:0006219.def: an aggressive, high-grade and poorly differentiated carcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the gallbladder. it is characterized by the presence of malignant small cells.
MONDO:0006219.synonym: small cell carcinoma of the gallbladder

MONDO:0006220.name: gallbladder squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0006220.def: a carcinoma that arises from the gallbladder. it is composed entirely by malignant squamous epithelial cells.

MONDO:0006221.name: gastric adenoma
MONDO:0006221.def: a neoplastic polyp that arises from the stomach. this category includes intestinal-type adenomatous polyps, gastric-type adenomas, and fundic gland polyps.

MONDO:0006222.name: gastric choriocarcinoma
MONDO:0006222.def: a malignant germ cell tumor that arises from the stomach. it is characterized by the presence of syncytiotrophoblast and cytotrophoblast cellular components. it is often associated with lymph node and hematogenous metastases.

MONDO:0006223.name: gastric diffuse large b-cell lymphoma
MONDO:0006223.def: an extranodal diffuse large b-cell lymphoma that arises from the stomach with the bulk of the mass located in the stomach.
MONDO:0006223.synonym: primary gastric diffuse large b-cell lymphoma

MONDO:0006224.name: gastric hamartomatous polyp
MONDO:0006224.def: a non-neoplastic polyp that arises from the stomach and is characterized by the presence of connective tissue stroma overgrowth and cystic formations.

MONDO:0006225.name: gastric mantle cell lymphoma
MONDO:0006225.def: a mantle cell lymphoma that affects the stomach. it may arise as a solitary mass or it may be a component of multifocal lymphomatous polyposis of the gastrointestinal tract. it usually has an aggressive clinical course.

MONDO:0006226.name: gastric mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma
MONDO:0006226.def: a low grade, indolent b-cell lymphoma, usually associated with helicobacter pylori infection. morphologically it is characterized by a dense mucosal atypical lymphocytic (centrocyte-like cell) infiltrate with often prominent lymphoepithelial lesions and plasmacytic differentiation. approximately 40% of gastric malt lymphomas carry the t(11;18)(q21;q21). such cases are resistant to helicobacter pylori therapy.

MONDO:0006227.name: gastric neuroendocrine tumor g1
MONDO:0006227.def: a well differentiated, low grade neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid tumor) that arises from the stomach. the vast majority of cases arise from the corpus-fundus region. the mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 hpf and/or the ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent. it may be associated with autoimmune chronic atrophic gastritis, multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1, or it may be sporadic.
MONDO:0006227.synonym: stomach neuroendocrine tumor, well differentiated, low grade

MONDO:0006228.name: gastric papillary adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006228.def: a variant of gastric adenocarcinoma with exophytic growth and elongated finger-like processes lined by cylindrical or cuboidal cells supported by fibrovascular connective tissue cores.

MONDO:0006229.name: gastric small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
MONDO:0006229.def: an aggressive, high-grade and poorly differentiated carcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the stomach. it is characterized by the presence of malignant small cells.

MONDO:0006230.name: gastric squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0006230.def: a rare carcinoma of the stomach resembling squamous cell carcinomas arising elsewhere in the body.

MONDO:0006231.name: gastrointestinal hamartoma
MONDO:0006231.def: a non-neoplastic, hamartomatous polyp that arises from the stomach, small intestine, and large intestine. this group includes the juvenile polyps and peutz-jeghers polyps.

MONDO:0006232.name: giant cell tumor of soft tissue
MONDO:0006232.def: a painless, well circumscribed tumor arising in soft tissue, usually of the upper and lower extremities. morphologically, it is characterized by a multinodular growth pattern. the cellular infiltrate is composed of mononuclear round or oval cells and multinucleated osteoclast-like giant cells, in a rich vascular stroma. it rarely metastasizes.

MONDO:0006233.name: gonadal teratoma
MONDO:0006233.def: a teratoma that arises from the testis or ovary.

MONDO:0006234.name: grade iii prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia
MONDO:0006234.def: high grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia characterized by the presence of severe architectural and cytologic abnormalities.

MONDO:0006235.name: granular cell tumor
MONDO:0006235.def: an unusual benign or malignant neoplasm characterized by the presence of neoplastic large polygonal cells with granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm which contains abundant lysosomes. it was originally thought to be a tumor originating from muscle cells and was named granular cell myoblastoma. subsequent studies have suggested a derivation from schwann cells. it affects females more often than males and it usually presents as a solitary mass. a minority of patients have multiple tumors. it can arise from many anatomic sites including the posterior pituitary gland, skin, oral cavity, esophagus, stomach, heart, mediastinum, and breast.

MONDO:0006236.name: obsolete granular cell tumor of the neurohypophysis

MONDO:0006237.name: granulocytic sarcoma
MONDO:0006237.def: a tumor mass composed of myeloblasts, neutrophils and neutrophil precursors. granulocytic sarcoma is the most common type of myeloid sarcoma. (who, 2001)

MONDO:0006238.name: growth hormone-producing pituitary gland adenoma
MONDO:0006238.def: an adenoma of the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland that produces growth hormone. the vast majority of cases are hormonally functioning and are associated with either gigantism or acromegaly.

MONDO:0006239.name: head and neck paraganglioma
MONDO:0006239.def: a benign or malignant extra-adrenal paraganglioma arising from paraganglia in the head and neck. representative examples include the carotid body and jugulotympanic paragangliomas.
MONDO:0006239.synonym: paraganglioma of the head and neck

MONDO:0006241.name: hepatic granuloma
MONDO:0006241.def: a granuloma located in the liver.

MONDO:0006243.name: hepatoid adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006243.def: an adenocarcinoma with morphologic characteristics similar to hepatocellular carcinoma, arising from an anatomic site other than the liver.

MONDO:0006244.name: her2 positive breast carcinoma
MONDO:0006244.def: a biologic subset of breast carcinoma defined by high expression of her2, grb7, and trap100, and by lack of expression of estrogen receptor (er).

MONDO:0006245.name: hidradenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006245.def: a carcinoma with apocrine and less often eccrine differentiation, arising from the sweat glands. it usually presents as a solitary slow growing nodule in the dermis or subcutaneous tissues. it is characterized by a nodular growth pattern and it is often associated with necrotic changes.

MONDO:0006246.name: high grade surface osteosarcoma
MONDO:0006246.def: a usually aggressive high grade malignant bone-forming mesenchymal neoplasm arising from the surface of the bone.

MONDO:0006247.name: histiocytic and dendritic cell neoplasm
MONDO:0006247.def: rare tumors that affect the hematopoietic and lymphoid tissues. the cells of origin are the histiocytes and accessory cells. they can occur at any age and show no significant variations in geographical distribution. this category includes the histiocytic sarcoma, langerhans cell histiocytosis, langerhans cell sarcoma, interdigitading dendritic cell sarcoma/tumor, follicular dendritic cell sarcoma/tumor, and dendritic cell sarcoma, not otherwise specified. (who, 2001)

MONDO:0006248.name: hydatidiform mole
MONDO:0006248.def: a gestational trophoblastic disorder characterized by marked enlargement of the chorionic villi, hyperplasia of the villous trophoblastic cells and hydropic changes.

MONDO:0006249.name: hyperplastic polyp
MONDO:0006249.def: a polyp found mainly in the stomach and colon. microscopically, it is characterized by elongated, serrated crypts lined by proliferative epithelium. hyperplastic polyps are traditionally considered non-neoplastic, but ras mutation is common, clonality has been demonstrated and biochemical abnormalities and epidemiological associations that occur in colorectal adenomas and carcinomas have been found (who tumors of the digestive system, 2000).

MONDO:0006250.name: ileal neuroendocrine tumor g1
MONDO:0006250.def: a well differentiated, low grade neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid tumor) that arises from the ileum. the mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 hpf and/or the ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent.
MONDO:0006250.synonym: ileum neuroendocrine tumor, well differentiated, low grade

MONDO:0006253.name: obsolete infiltrating bladder urothelial carcinoma sarcomatoid variant

MONDO:0006254.name: intestinal type adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0006254.def: an adenocarcinoma arising from epithelium which has undergone intestinal metaplasia. representative examples include gastric, gallbladder, and ampulla of vater intestinal type adenocarcinomas.

MONDO:0006255.name: intimal sarcoma
MONDO:0006255.def: a malignant neoplasm arising from the large blood vessels. it is characterized by the presence of tumor cells that grow within the lumen of the blood vessels. the intraluminal tumor growth may result in vascular obstruction and spread of tumor emboli to peripheral organs. the prognosis is usually poor.

MONDO:0006256.name: invasive breast carcinoma
MONDO:0006256.def: a carcinoma that infiltrates the breast parenchyma. the vast majority are adenocarcinomas arising from the terminal ductal lobular unit (tdlu). often, the invasive adenocarcinoma co-exists with ductal or lobular carcinoma in situ. it is the most common carcinoma affecting women.

MONDO:0006257.name: jejunal neuroendocrine tumor g1
MONDO:0006257.def: a well differentiated, low grade neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid tumor) that arises from the jejunum. the mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 hpf and/or the ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent.
MONDO:0006257.synonym: jejunum neuroendocrine tumor, well differentiated, low grade

MONDO:0006258.name: juvenile polyp
MONDO:0006258.def: a non-neoplastic hamartomatous polyp that arises from the stomach and intestinal tract. it is characterized by the presence of tortuous and cystically dilated glands, edematous changes, and inflammation.

MONDO:0006260.name: kidney medullary carcinoma
MONDO:0006260.def: a type of renal carcinoma affecting mostly young african-americans. it is located in the medulla of the kidney, and follows an aggressive clinical course. most reported cases have shown metastatic disease at the time of diagnosis.

MONDO:0006262.name: lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma
MONDO:0006262.def: a adenoid cystic carcinoma that involves the lacrimal gland.

MONDO:0006264.name: laryngeal adenoid cystic carcinoma
MONDO:0006264.def: a rare adenoid cystic carcinoma of the larynx. it usually arises from the supraglottic or subglottic area. it is characterized by slow progression and late distant metastases.

MONDO:0006265.name: laryngeal small cell carcinoma
MONDO:0006265.def: a rare carcinoma that arises from the larynx. it is characterized by the presence of small neuroendocrine cells. it metastasizes early and has an aggressive clinical course.
MONDO:0006265.synonym: small cell carcinoma of the larynx

MONDO:0006266.name: leydig cell tumor
MONDO:0006266.def: a sex cord-stromal tumor occurring in the testis and rarely in the ovary. it is predominantly or completely composed of leydig cells which may contain crystals of reinke. in males it usually presents as a painless testicular enlargement and it may be associated with gynecomastia and decreased libido. the majority of the cases have a benign clinical course. approximately 10% of the cases have a malignant clinical course and metastasize. in females it may be associated with androgenic manifestations and it follows a benign clinical course.

MONDO:0006267.name: liver cavernous hemangioma
MONDO:0006267.def: a hemangioma with cavernous vascular spaces arising from the liver. it is the most frequent benign tumor of the liver and usually affects young females.

MONDO:0006268.name: liver diffuse large b-cell lymphoma
MONDO:0006268.def: a rare diffuse large b-cell lymphoma that arises from the liver and the bulk of the tumor is located in the liver.
MONDO:0006268.synonym: primary liver diffuse large b-cell lymphoma

MONDO:0006270.name: lobular breast carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0006270.def: a non-invasive adenocarcinoma of the breast characterized by a proliferation of monomorphic cells completely filling the lumina. the overall lobular architecture is preserved. it is frequently multifocal (90% in some series) and bilateral. it seldom becomes invasive; however there is an increased risk of infiltrating ductal adenocarcinoma.
MONDO:0006270.synonym: non-invasive lobular carcinoma of the breast

MONDO:0006271.name: low grade central osteosarcoma
MONDO:0006271.def: a low grade osteosarcoma arising from the medullary portion of the bone. it affects the long bones and is characterized by the presence of fibroblastic stroma and osteoid production. pain and swelling are the usual sign and symptom. the prognosis is more favorable than conventional osteosarcoma.

MONDO:0006272.name: low grade fibromyxoid sarcoma
MONDO:0006272.def: a low grade, late-metastasizing variant of fibrosarcoma characterized by alternating fibrous and myxoid areas and a whorling growth pattern. the neoplastic cells have a spindle morphology, and lack hyperchromasia or significant nuclear atypia. approximately 40% of cases show the focal presence of collagen rosettes. a t(7;16)(q33;p11) translocation has been identified in the majority of cases, associated with the presence of fus-creb3l2 fusion protein. rare cases carry the t(11;16)(p11;p11) translocation which is associated with the presence of the fus-creb3l1 fusion protein.

MONDO:0006273.name: low grade fibromyxoid sarcoma with giant collagen rosettes
MONDO:0006273.def: a low grade fibromyxoid sarcoma characterized by the presence of prominent collagen rosettes.
MONDO:0006273.synonym: hyalinizing spindle cell tumour with giant rosettes

MONDO:0006274.name: low grade vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia
MONDO:0006274.def: an intraepithelial lesion of the vulvar squamous epithelium that represents the clinical and morphological manifestation of a productive hpv infection. low grade refers to the associated low risk of concurrent or future cancer. (who, 2014)

MONDO:0006275.name: lung giant cell carcinoma
MONDO:0006275.def: a morphologic variant of lung sarcomatoid carcinoma characterized by the presence of mononuclear and multinucleated pleomorphic neoplastic giant cells that lack cohesion.

MONDO:0006276.name: lung inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor
MONDO:0006276.def: an intermediate fibroblastic neoplasm arising from the lung. it is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped fibroblasts and myofibroblasts, and a chronic inflammatory infiltrate composed of eosinophils, lymphocytes and plasma cells.

MONDO:0006277.name: lung lymphangioleiomyomatosis
MONDO:0006277.def: lymphangiomyomatosis involving the lungs and local lymph nodes. patients usually present with chylous pleural effusion. the clinical course is variable. patients with resectable lesions usually have a favorable clinical outcome. patients with diffuse lesions usually have a progressive clinical course.

MONDO:0006278.name: lung papilloma
MONDO:0006278.def: a benign papillary neoplasm that arises endobronchially. it is classified as squamous cell, glandular, or mixed squamous cell and glandular papilloma. patients usually present with signs and symptoms of bronchial obstruction.

MONDO:0006279.name: lung sarcomatoid carcinoma
MONDO:0006279.def: a rare, aggressive, poorly differentiated, non-small cell lung carcinoma characterized by the presence of a sarcomatoid component often associated with giant cell differentiation. there is a male to female ratio of 4:1. clinical symptoms include cough, hemoptysis, chest pain, progressive dyspnea and fever secondary to recurrent pneumonia. cigarette smoking is a major risk factor.
