MONDO:0013056.def: a rare mitochondrial substrate carrier disorder characterized by severe muscular hypotonia, seizures (with or without episodic apnea) beginning in the first year of life, and arrested psychomotor development (affecting mainly motor skills). severe spasticity with hyperreflexia has also been reported. global cerebral hypomyelination is a characteristic imaging feature of this disease.

MONDO:0013058.name: cystic leukoencephalopathy without megalencephaly
MONDO:0013058.def: cystic leukoencephalopathy without megalencephaly is characterized by non-progressive leukoencephalopathy, bilateral cysts in the anterior part of the temporal lobe, cerebral white matter anomalies and severe psychomotor impairment. less than 50 patients have been described in the literature so far. inheritance is most likely autosomal recessive.

MONDO:0013059.name: aicardi-goutieres syndrome 5
MONDO:0013059.def: any aicardi-goutieres syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the samhd1 gene.

MONDO:0013060.name: autosomal recessive parkinson disease 14
MONDO:0013060.def: a rare neurodegenerative disease usually presenting before the age of 30 and which is characterized by dystonia, l-dopa-responsive parkinsonism, pyramidal signs and rapid cognitive decline.

MONDO:0013061.name: myofibrillar myopathy 6
MONDO:0013061.def: selcen type muscular dystrophy is characterized by progressive limb and axial muscle weakness associated with cardiomyopathy and severe respiratory insufficiency during adolescence. the disease manifests during childhood and progresses rapidly.

MONDO:0013062.name: long qt syndrome 12
MONDO:0013062.def: any long qt syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the snta1 gene.

MONDO:0013063.name: ventricular fibrillation, paroxysmal familial, 2
MONDO:0013063.def: any ventricular fibrillation in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the dpp6 gene.

MONDO:0013064.name: multiple synostoses syndrome 3
MONDO:0013064.def: any multiple synostoses syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the fgf9 gene.

MONDO:0013065.name: premature ovarian failure 7
MONDO:0013065.def: any primary ovarian failure in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the nr5a1 gene.
MONDO:0013065.synonym: primary ovarian failure caused by mutation in nr5a1

MONDO:0013067.name: cataract 34 multiple types
MONDO:0013067.def: any cataract (disease) in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the foxe3 gene.

MONDO:0013069.name: autosomal recessive optic atrophy, opa7 type
MONDO:0013069.synonym: optic atrophy 7 with or without auditory neuropathy

MONDO:0013071.name: emery-dreifuss muscular dystrophy 4, autosomal dominant
MONDO:0013071.def: any autosomal dominant emery-dreifuss muscular dystrophy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the syne1 gene.
MONDO:0013071.synonym: syne1 autosomal dominant emery-dreifuss muscular dystrophy

MONDO:0013072.name: emery-dreifuss muscular dystrophy 5, autosomal dominant
MONDO:0013072.def: any autosomal dominant emery-dreifuss muscular dystrophy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the syne2 gene.
MONDO:0013072.synonym: syne2 autosomal dominant emery-dreifuss muscular dystrophy

MONDO:0013073.name: palmoplantar keratoderma, nonepidermolytic, focal 1
MONDO:0013073.def: any nonepidermolytic palmoplantar keratoderma in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the krt16 gene.

MONDO:0013074.name: encephalocraniocutaneous lipomatosis
MONDO:0013074.def: a rare neoplastic syndrome characterized by the presence of unilateral lipomas of the cranium, face and neck, and ipsilateral cerebral malformations.

MONDO:0013078.name: type 1 diabetes mellitus 24
MONDO:0013078.def: an inherited susceptibility or predisposition to developing type 1 diabetes mellitus that has material basis in mutation of the locus at chromosome 10q23.31.

MONDO:0013081.name: lymphoproliferative syndrome 1
MONDO:0013081.def: a condition of decreased or absent presence or activity of il2-inducible t-cell kinase. deficiency of this protein is associated with lymphoproliferative syndrome 1, an autosomal recessive primary immunodeficiency characterized by onset in early childhood of epstein-barr virus (ebv)-associated immune dysregulation, manifest as lymphoma, lymphomatoid granulomatosis, hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, hodgkin disease, and/or hypogammaglobulinemia..

MONDO:0013082.name: hirschsprung disease-ganglioneuroblastoma syndrome
MONDO:0013082.def: a rare, genetic, developmental defect during embryogenesis syndrome characterized by total or partial colonic aganglionosis associated with peripheral, usually multifocal, neuroblastic tumors (ganglioneuroblastoma, neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroma). congenital central hypoventilation syndrome, with variable severity of respiratory compromise, cardiovascular and ophthalmologic symptoms, consistent with autonomic nervous system dysfunction, is occasionally associated.

MONDO:0013083.name: neuroblastoma, susceptibility to, 3
MONDO:0013083.def: any neuroblastoma in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the alk gene.

MONDO:0013087.name: bronchiectasis with or without elevated sweat chloride 2
MONDO:0013087.def: any bronchiectasis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the scnn1a gene.

MONDO:0013089.name: schizophrenia 13
MONDO:0013089.def: a schizophrenia that has material basis in a mutation on chromosome 15q13.

MONDO:0013090.name: chromosome 19q13.11 deletion syndrome
MONDO:0013090.def: the 19q13.11 microdeletion is characterized by several major features including pre and postnatal growth retardation, slender habitus, severe postnatal feeding difficulties, microcephaly, intellectual deficit with speech disturbance, hypospadias and ectodermal dysplasia presented by scalp aplasia, thin and sparse hair, eyebrows and eyelashes, thin and dry skin and dysplasic nails.

MONDO:0013091.name: glycogen storage disease ixc
MONDO:0013091.def: a liver phk deficiency caused by variants in the phkg2 gene
MONDO:0013091.synonym: phkg2-related glycogen storage disease type ix

MONDO:0013092.name: glioma susceptibility 2
MONDO:0013092.def: any malignant glioma in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the pten gene.

MONDO:0013093.name: glioma susceptibility 3
MONDO:0013093.def: any malignant glioma in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the brca2 gene.
MONDO:0013093.synonym: malignant glioma caused by mutation in brca2

MONDO:0013098.name: noise induced hearing loss
MONDO:0013098.def: a condition in which a person loses the ability to hear due to exposure to high intensity sound.

MONDO:0013099.name: combined pituitary hormone deficiencies, genetic form
MONDO:0013099.def: congenital hypopituitarism is characterized by multiple pituitary hormone deficiency, including somatotroph, thyrotroph, lactotroph, corticotroph or gonadotroph deficiencies, due to mutations of pituitary transcription factors involved in pituitary ontogenesis. congenital hypopituitarism is rare compared with the high incidence of hypopituitarism induced by pituitary adenomas, transsphenoidal surgery or radiotherapy.

MONDO:0013103.name: epilepsy, idiopathic generalized, susceptibility to, 10
MONDO:0013103.def: an inherited susceptibility or predisposition to developing epilepsy, idiopathic generalized, in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the gabrd gene.

MONDO:0013107.name: dermatitis, atopic, 7
MONDO:0013107.def: an inherited susceptibility or predisposition to developing atopic dermatitis that is associated with variation in the region 11q13.5.

MONDO:0013110.name: neurodegenerative syndrome due to cerebral folate transport deficiency
MONDO:0013110.synonym: neurodegenerative syndrome due to cerebral folate transport deficiency

MONDO:0013111.name: acute infantile liver failure due to synthesis defect of mtdna-encoded proteins
MONDO:0013111.def: acute infantile liver failure due to mtdna-encoded proteins synthesis defect is a very rare mitochondrial respiratory chain deficiency described in fewer than 10 infants, primarily of middle eastern descent, and characterized clinically by transient but life-threatening liver failure with elevated liver enzymes, jaundice, vomiting, coagulopathy, hyperbilirubinemia, and lactic acidemia.

MONDO:0013112.name: bronchiectasis with or without elevated sweat chloride 3
MONDO:0013112.def: any bronchiectasis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the scnn1g gene.

MONDO:0013113.name: metaphyseal anadysplasia 2
MONDO:0013113.def: any metaphyseal anadysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the mmp9 gene.

MONDO:0013114.name: autosomal dominant nonsyndromic hearing loss 50
MONDO:0013114.def: an autosomal dominant nonsyndromic deafness that is characterized postlingual onset in the second decade of life with flat progressive hearing loss and has material basis in mutation in the mirn96 gene on chromosome 7q32.

MONDO:0013115.name: rin2 syndrome
MONDO:0013115.def: rin2 syndrome, formerly known as macrocephaly, alopecia, cutis laxa and scoliosis (macs) syndrome, is a very rare inherited connective tissue disorder characterized by macrocephaly, sparse scalp hair, soft-redundant and hyperextensible skin, joint hypermobility, and scoliosis. patients have progressive facial coarsening with downslanted palpebral fissures, upper eyelid fullness/infraorbital folds, thick/everted vermillion, gingival overgrowth and abnormal position of the teeth. rarer manifestations such as abnormal high-pitched voice, bronchiectasis, hypergonadotropic hypergonadism and brachydactyly have also been reported.

MONDO:0013116.name: congenital cataract-progressive muscular hypotonia-hearing loss-developmental delay syndrome
MONDO:0013116.synonym: myopathy, mitochondrial progressive, with congenital cataract, hearing loss, and developmental delay

MONDO:0013117.name: progressive external ophthalmoplegia with mitochondrial dna deletions, autosomal dominant 5
MONDO:0013117.def: any progressive external ophthalmoplegia with mitochondrial dna deletions in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the rrm2b gene.
MONDO:0013117.synonym: rrm2b progressive external ophthalmoplegia with mitochondrial dna deletions

MONDO:0013118.name: nijmegen breakage syndrome-like disorder
MONDO:0013118.def: nijmegen breakage syndrome-like disorder is a rare, genetic multiple congenital anomalies/dysmorphic syndrome characterized by growth retardation, short stature, developmental delay, intellectual disability, craniofacial dysmorphism (i.e. severe microcephaly, sloping forehead, prominent eyes, broad nasal ridge, hypoplastic nasal septum, epicanthal folds), spontaneous chromosomal instability, cellular hypersensitivity to ionizing radiation and radioresistant dna synthesis, without severe infections, immunodeficiency or cancer predisposition. additional reported features include mild spasticity, slight and nonprogressive ataxia, hyperopia, multiple pigmented nevi, widely spaced nipples, and clinodactyly.

MONDO:0013119.name: autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss 77
MONDO:0013119.def: any autosomal recessive nonsyndromic deafness in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the loxhd1 gene.

MONDO:0013123.name: atrial septal defect 6
MONDO:0013123.def: any atrial heart septal defect in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the tll1 gene.

MONDO:0013125.name: clapo syndrome
MONDO:0013125.def: clapo syndrome is a newly described syndrome consisting of capillary malformation of the lower lip (c), lymphatic malformation of the face and neck (l), asymmetry of face and limbs (a) and partial or generalized overgrowth (o).

MONDO:0013127.name: asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy 3
MONDO:0013127.def: an asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy that has material basis in homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the dync2h1 gene on chromosome 11q22.

MONDO:0013128.name: familial juvenile hyperuricemic nephropathy type 2
MONDO:0013128.def: familial juvenile hyperuricemic nephropathy type 2 is a rare autosomal dominantly inherited disease of childhood characterized by hypoproliferative anemia, hyperuricemia and slowly progressing kidney failure due to dysregulation of the renin-angiotensin system (ras).

MONDO:0013129.name: cone dystrophy 4
MONDO:0013129.def: any cone dystrophy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the pde6c gene.

MONDO:0013130.name: isolated microphthalmia 4
MONDO:0013130.def: any isolated microphthalmia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the gdf6 gene.

MONDO:0013131.name: polycystic kidney disease 2
MONDO:0013131.def: autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease caused by a mutation in pkd2.
MONDO:0013131.synonym: polycystic kidney disease, adult, type ii

MONDO:0013132.name: hereditary spastic paraplegia 36
MONDO:0013132.def: autosomal dominant spastic paraplegia type 36 (spg36) is a complex form of hereditary spastic paraplegia, characterized by an onset in childhood or adulthood of progressive spastic paraplegia (with spastic gait, spasticity, lower limb weakness, pes cavus and urinary urgency) associated with the additional manifestation of peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy.

MONDO:0013134.name: glaucoma 1, open angle, o
MONDO:0013134.def: any open-angle glaucoma in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ntf4 gene.
MONDO:0013134.synonym: open-angle glaucoma caused by mutation in ntf4

MONDO:0013135.name: familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis 5
MONDO:0013135.def: any genetic hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the stxbp2 gene.

MONDO:0013136.name: hereditary hypotrichosis with recurrent skin vesicles
MONDO:0013136.def: hereditary hypotrichosis with recurrent skin vesicles is a very rare inherited hair loss disorder described in a family and characterized by sparse, fragile or absent hair on the scalp, eyebrows, eyelashes, axillae and rest of the body, associated with vesicle formation on various parts of the scalp and body which regularly burst and release watery fluid.

MONDO:0013137.name: choroidal dystrophy, central areolar 2
MONDO:0013137.def: any central areolar choroidal dystrophy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the prph2 gene.

MONDO:0013139.name: neutropenia, severe congenital, 2, autosomal dominant
MONDO:0013139.def: any autosomal dominant severe congenital neutropenia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the gfi1 gene.

MONDO:0013140.name: candidiasis, familial, 4
MONDO:0013140.def: any familial chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the clec7a gene.
MONDO:0013140.synonym: familial chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis caused by mutation in clec7a

MONDO:0013142.name: neuropathy, hereditary sensory and autonomic, type 2b
MONDO:0013142.def: any hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type 2 in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the retreg1 gene.
MONDO:0013142.synonym: retreg1 hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type 2

MONDO:0013143.name: hereditary thrombophilia due to congenital histidine-rich (poly-l) glycoprotein deficiency
MONDO:0013143.synonym: thrombophilia due to histidine-rich glycoprotein deficiency

MONDO:0013144.name: hereditary antithrombin deficiency
MONDO:0013144.def: a rare, genetic, hematological disease characterized by decreased levels of antithrombin activity in plasma resulting in impaired inactivation of thrombin and factor xa. patients have an increased risk for venous thromboembolism, usually in the deep veins of the arms, legs and pulmonary system and, on occasion, in other venous territories (e.g. cerebral veins or sinus, mesenteric, portal, hepatic, renal and/or retinal veins).
MONDO:0013144.synonym: thrombophilia due to antithrombin iii deficiency

MONDO:0013145.name: brugada syndrome 6
MONDO:0013145.def: any brugada syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the kcne3 gene.

MONDO:0013146.name: brugada syndrome 7
MONDO:0013146.def: any brugada syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the scn3b gene.

MONDO:0013147.name: dilated cardiomyopathy 1cc
MONDO:0013147.def: any familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the nexn gene.

MONDO:0013148.name: brugada syndrome 8
MONDO:0013148.def: any brugada syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the hcn4 gene.

MONDO:0013149.name: hydrops fetalis, nonimmune, with gracile bones and dysmorphic features
MONDO:0013149.synonym: hydrops fetalis, nonimmune, with gracile bones and dysmorphic features

MONDO:0013150.name: parkinsonism-dystonia, infantile
MONDO:0013150.def: infantile dystonia-parkinsonism (ipd) is an extremely rare inherited neurological syndrome that presents in early infancy with hypokinetic parkinsonism and dystonia and that can be fatal.

MONDO:0013151.name: choroidal dystrophy, central areolar, 3
MONDO:0013151.synonym: choroidal dystrophy, central areolar, with or without drusen

MONDO:0013153.name: inflammatory bowel disease 28
MONDO:0013153.def: any inflammatory bowel disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the il10ra gene.
MONDO:0013153.synonym: inflammatory bowel disease, early-onset, autosomal recessive

MONDO:0013154.name: muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy (congenital with brain and eye anomalies), type a2
MONDO:0013154.def: an autosomal recessive muscular dystrophy caused by mutations in the pomt2 gene. it is associated with characteristic brain and eye malformations and profound mental retardation.
MONDO:0013154.synonym: walker-warburg syndrome or muscle-eye-brain disease, pomt2-related

MONDO:0013155.name: muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy (congenital with intellectual disability), type b3
MONDO:0013155.synonym: muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy (congenital with mental retardation), type b, 3

MONDO:0013156.name: muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy (congenital without intellectual disability), type b4
MONDO:0013156.synonym: muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy (congenital without mental retardation), type b, 4

MONDO:0013157.name: muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy (congenital with brain and eye anomalies), type a5
MONDO:0013157.synonym: walker-warburg syndrome or muscle-eye-brain disease, fkrp-related

MONDO:0013158.name: muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy (congenital with brain and eye anomalies), type a6
MONDO:0013158.def: an autosomal recessive muscular dystrophy caused by mutations in the large gene. it is associated with characteristic brain and eye malformations, profound mental retardation, and death usually in the first years of life.
MONDO:0013158.synonym: walker-warburg syndrome or muscle-eye-brain disease, large-related

MONDO:0013159.name: muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy (congenital with intellectual disability), type b1
MONDO:0013159.synonym: muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy (congenital with mental retardation), type b, 1

MONDO:0013160.name: muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy (congenital with intellectual disability), type b2
MONDO:0013160.def: an autosomal recessive inherited congenital muscular dystrophy caused by mutations in the pomt2 gene. it is characterized by mental retardation and mild structural brain abnormalities resulting from defective glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan.
MONDO:0013160.synonym: muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy (congenital with mental retardation), type b, 2

MONDO:0013161.name: autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2o
MONDO:0013161.def: autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2o (lgmd2o) is a form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy characterized by an onset in childhood or adolescence of rapidly progressive proximal limb muscle weakness (particularly affecting the neck, hip girdle, and shoulder abductors), hypertrophy in the calves and quadriceps, ankle contractures, and myopia.
MONDO:0013161.synonym: pomgnt1 autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy

MONDO:0013162.name: autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2n
MONDO:0013162.def: autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2n (lgmd2n) is a form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy characterized by proximal weakness (manifesting as slowness in running) presenting in infancy, along with calf hypertrophy, mild lordosis, scapular winging and normal intelligence or mild intellectual disability.
MONDO:0013162.synonym: pomt2 autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy

MONDO:0013163.name: nephronophthisis-like nephropathy 1
MONDO:0013163.def: any nephronophthisis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the xpnpep3 gene.

MONDO:0013164.name: beta-ureidopropionase deficiency
MONDO:0013164.def: beta-ureidopropionase deficiency is a very rare pyrimidine metabolism disorder described in fewer than 10 patients to date with an extremely wide clinical picture ranging from asymptomatic cases to neurological (epilepsy, autism) and developmental disorders (urogenital, colorectal).

MONDO:0013165.name: hereditary spastic paraplegia 45
MONDO:0013165.def: autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia type 45 is a rare, pure or complex form of hereditary spastic paraplegia characterized by onset in infancy of progressive lower limb spasticity, abnormal gait, increased deep tendon reflexes and extensor plantar responses, that may be associated with intellectual disability. additional signs, such as contractures in the lower limbs, amyotrophy, clubfoot and optic atrophy, have also been reported.

MONDO:0013166.name: gaba aminotransaminase deficiency
MONDO:0013166.def: gamma-aminobutyric acid transaminase (gaba-t) deficiency is an extremely rare disorder of gaba metabolism characterized by a severe neonatal-infantile epileptic encephalopathy (manifesting with symptoms such as seizures, hypotonia, hyperreflexia and developmental delay) and growth acceleration.

MONDO:0013168.name: dilated cardiomyopathy 1dd
MONDO:0013168.def: any familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the rbm20 gene.

MONDO:0013169.name: chromosome 5p13 duplication syndrome
MONDO:0013169.def: 5p13 microduplication syndrome is a rare partial autosomal trisomy/tetrasomy characterized by global developmental delay, intellectual disability, autistic behavior, muscular hypotonia, macrocephaly and facial dysmorphism (frontal bossing, short palpebral fissures, low set, dysplastic ears, short or shallow philtrum, high arched or narrow palate, micrognathia). other associated clinical features include sleep disturbances, seizures, aplasia/hypoplasia of the corpus callosum, skeletal abnormalities (large hands and feet, long fingers and toes, talipes).

MONDO:0013170.name: cutis laxa with severe pulmonary, gastrointestinal and urinary anomalies
MONDO:0013170.def: a autosomal recessive cutis laxa type i that has material basis in homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the ltbp4 gene on chromosome 19q13

MONDO:0013171.name: purine nucleoside phosphorylase deficiency
MONDO:0013171.def: purine nucleoside phosphorylase (pnp) deficiency is a disorder of purine metabolism characterized by progressive immunodeficiency leading to recurrent and opportunistic infections, autoimmunity and malignancy as well as neurologic manifestations.

MONDO:0013172.name: polymicrogyria with optic nerve hypoplasia
MONDO:0013172.def: a rare genetic syndrome with central nervous system malformations characterized by severe developmental delay, neonatal hypotonia, seizures, optic nerve hypoplasia and distinct central nervous system malformations including extensive bilateral polymicrogyria, dysplastic or absent corpus callosum and malformed brainstem with loss of demarcation of the pontomedullary junction.

MONDO:0013173.name: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 13
MONDO:0013173.def: any autosomal recessive non-syndromic intellectual disability in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the trappc9 gene.
MONDO:0013173.synonym: trappc9 autosomal recessive non-syndromic intellectual disability

MONDO:0013174.name: primary ciliary dyskinesia 13
MONDO:0013174.def: any primary ciliary dyskinesia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the dnaaf1 gene.

MONDO:0013175.name: retinitis pigmentosa 50
MONDO:0013175.def: any retinitis pigmentosa in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the best1 gene.

MONDO:0013177.name: congenital muscular dystrophy due to integrin alpha-7 deficiency
MONDO:0013177.def: congenital muscular dystrophy with integrin alpha-7 deficiency is a rare, genetic, congenital muscular dystrophy due to extracellular matrix protein anomaly characterized by early motor development delay and muscle weakness with mild elevation of serum creatine kinase, that may be followed by progressive disease course with predominantly proximal muscle weakness and atrophy, motor development regress, scoliosis and respiratory insufficiency.
MONDO:0013177.synonym: myopathy, congenital, due to integrin alpha-7 deficiency

MONDO:0013178.name: congenital muscular dystrophy due to lmna mutation
MONDO:0013178.def: congenital muscular dystrophy due to lmna mutation is a rare congenital muscular dystrophy characterized by prominent axial hypotonia, dropped head syndrome, predominantly proximal muscle weakness in upper limbs/distal in lower limbs (with absent, poor or lost motor development), joint contractures (initially distal, later proximal), spine rigidity, and early respiratory insufficiency, in the presence of moderately elevated serum creatine kinase. cardiac arrhythmias and sudden death have been also reported.

MONDO:0013179.name: hereditary spastic paraplegia 44
MONDO:0013179.def: a very rare, complex form of hereditary spastic paraplegia characterized by a late-onset, slowly progressive spastic paraplegia associated with mild ataxia and dysarthria, upper extremity involvement (i.e. loss of finger dexterity, dysmetria), and mild cognitive impairment, without the presence of nystagmus. a hypomyelinating leukodystrophy and thin corpus callosum is observed in all cases and psychomotor development is normal or near normal. spg44 is caused by mutations in the gjc2 gene (1q41-q42) encoding the gap junction gamma-2 protein.

MONDO:0013181.name: amelogenesis imperfecta hypomaturation type 2a3
MONDO:0013181.def: any amelogenesis imperfecta in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the wdr72 gene.

MONDO:0013182.name: chromosome 17p13.3 duplication syndrome
MONDO:0013182.def: 17p13.3 microduplication syndrome is characterized by variable psychomotor delay and dysmorphic features.

MONDO:0013183.name: congenital stationary night blindness 1c
MONDO:0013183.def: any congenital stationary night blindness in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the trpm1 gene.

MONDO:0013184.name: congenital diarrhea 5 with tufting enteropathy
MONDO:0013184.def: congenital tufting enteropathy is a rare congenital enteropathy presenting with early-onset severe and intractable diarrhea that leads to irreversible intestinal failure.

MONDO:0013185.name: leprosy, susceptibility to, 5
MONDO:0013185.def: any leprosy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the tlr1 gene.

MONDO:0013186.name: noonan syndrome 6
MONDO:0013186.def: any noonan syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the nras gene.

MONDO:0013187.name: factor xiii, a subunit, deficiency of
MONDO:0013187.synonym: hereditary factor xiii type ii deficiency

MONDO:0013188.name: cerebellar ataxia, intellectual disability, and dysequilibrium syndrome 3
MONDO:0013188.def: any dysequilibrium syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ca8 gene.
MONDO:0013188.synonym: dysequilibrium syndrome caused by mutation in ca8

MONDO:0013189.name: trichotillomania
MONDO:0013189.def: a disorder characterized by repetitive pulling out of one's hair resulting in noticeable hair loss; the individual experiences a rising subjective sense of tension before pulling out the hair and a sense of gratification or relief when pulling out the hair.

MONDO:0013190.name: factor xiii, b subunit, deficiency of

MONDO:0013191.name: focal segmental glomerulosclerosis 5
MONDO:0013191.def: any focal segmental glomerulosclerosis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the inf2 gene.

MONDO:0013193.name: thyrotoxic periodic paralysis, susceptibility to, 2
MONDO:0013193.def: any thyrotoxic periodic paralysis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the kcnj18 gene.

MONDO:0013195.name: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy 13
MONDO:0013195.def: any hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the tnnc1 gene.

MONDO:0013196.name: lynch syndrome 8
MONDO:0013196.def: any hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the epcam gene.

MONDO:0013197.name: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy 14
MONDO:0013197.def: any hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the myh6 gene.

MONDO:0013198.name: dilated cardiomyopathy 1ee
MONDO:0013198.def: any familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the myh6 gene.

MONDO:0013199.name: tuberous sclerosis 2
MONDO:0013199.def: tuberous sclerosis mapped to chromosome 16p13.3 (tsc2 gene).

MONDO:0013200.name: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy 15
MONDO:0013200.def: any hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the vcl gene.

MONDO:0013201.name: waardenburg syndrome type 4b
MONDO:0013201.def: a subtype of waardenburg syndrome type 4 (waardenburg-shah syndrome) caused by mutations in edn3.

MONDO:0013202.name: waardenburg syndrome type 4c
MONDO:0013202.def: a subtype of waardenburg syndrome type 4 (waardenburg-shah syndrome) caused by mutations in sox10.

MONDO:0013203.name: corneal dystrophy, fuchs endothelial, 3
MONDO:0013203.def: any fuchs' endothelial dystrophy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the tcf4 gene.

MONDO:0013204.name: corneal dystrophy, fuchs endothelial, 4
MONDO:0013204.def: any fuchs' endothelial dystrophy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the slc4a11 gene.

MONDO:0013206.name: corneal dystrophy, fuchs endothelial, 6
MONDO:0013206.def: any fuchs' endothelial dystrophy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the zeb1 gene.

MONDO:0013208.name: cirrhosis - dystonia - polycythemia - hypermanganesemia syndrome
MONDO:0013208.synonym: hypermanganesemia with dystonia, polycythemia, and cirrhosis

MONDO:0013209.name: non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
MONDO:0013209.def: a term referring to fatty replacement of the hepatic parenchyma which is not related to alcohol use.

MONDO:0013210.name: autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss 25
MONDO:0013210.def: any autosomal recessive nonsyndromic deafness in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the grxcr1 gene.

MONDO:0013211.name: dilated cardiomyopathy 1ff
MONDO:0013211.def: a dilated cardiomyopathy that has material basis in mutation in the tnni3 gene on chromosome 19q13.42.

MONDO:0013212.name: charcot-marie-tooth disease axonal type 2n
MONDO:0013212.def: autosomal dominant charcot-marie-tooth disease type 2n (cmt2n) is a mild form of axonal charcot-marie-tooth disease, a peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy, characterized by distal legs sensory loss and weakness that can be asymmetric. tendon reflexes are reduced in the knees and absent in ankles. progression is slow.

MONDO:0013215.name: autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss 79
MONDO:0013215.def: any autosomal recessive nonsyndromic deafness in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the tprn gene.

MONDO:0013216.name: diamond-blackfan anemia 9
MONDO:0013216.def: any diamond-blackfan anemia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the rps10 gene.

MONDO:0013217.name: diamond-blackfan anemia 10
MONDO:0013217.def: any diamond-blackfan anemia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the rps26 gene.

MONDO:0013218.name: exudative vitreoretinopathy 5
MONDO:0013218.def: any exudative vitreoretinopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the tspan12 gene.

MONDO:0013219.name: hypophosphatemic rickets, autosomal recessive, 2
MONDO:0013219.def: any autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the enpp1 gene.

MONDO:0013220.name: hemochromatosis type 2b
MONDO:0013220.def: any hemochromatosis type 2 in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the hamp gene.

MONDO:0013223.name: autosomal recessive spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, megarbane type
MONDO:0013223.def: any spondylodysplastic dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the pam16 gene.

MONDO:0013224.name: rhabdoid tumor predisposition syndrome 2
MONDO:0013224.def: any familial rhabdoid tumor in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the smarca4 gene.

MONDO:0013225.name: congenital generalized lipodystrophy type 4
MONDO:0013225.def: any congenital generalized lipodystrophy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the cavin1 gene.

MONDO:0013226.name: combined immunodeficiency with faciooculoskeletal anomalies
MONDO:0013226.def: combined immunodeficiency with faciooculoskeletal anomalies is an extremely rare combined immunodeficiency disorder characterized by primary immunodeficiency manifesting with repeated bacterial, viral and fungal infections, in association with neurological manifestations (hypotonia, cerebellar ataxia, myoclonic seizures), developmental delay, optic atrophy, facial dysmorphism (high forehead, hypoplastic supraorbital ridges, palpebral edema, hypertelorism, flat nasal bridge, broad nasal root and tip, anteverted nares, thin lower lip overlapped by upper lip, square chin) and skeletal anomalies (short metacarpals/metatarsals with cone-shaped epiphyses, osteopenia).

MONDO:0013227.name: congenital plasminogen activator inhibitor type 1 deficiency
MONDO:0013227.def: congenital plasminogen activator inhibitor type 1 (pai-1) deficiency is a rare genetic bleeding disorder characterized by premature lysis of hemostatic clots and a moderate bleeding tendency.

MONDO:0013229.name: hot water reflex epilepsy
MONDO:0013229.def: hot water reflex epilepsy is a rare neurologic disease characterized by the onset of generalized or focal seizures following immersion of the head in hot water, or with hot water being poured over the head. primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures have been reported in rare cases.

MONDO:0013231.name: leber congenital amaurosis 14
MONDO:0013231.def: any leber congenital amaurosis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the lrat gene.

MONDO:0013232.name: brachydactylous dwarfism, mseleni type
MONDO:0013232.def: mseleni joint disease (mjd) is a rare and crippling chondrodysplasia, reported mainly in the maputaland region in northern kwazulu natal, south africa, characterized by a bilateral and uniform arthropathy of the joints that primarily and most severely affects the hip but that can also affect many other joints (i.e. knees, ankles, wrists, shoulders, elbows), and that manifests with pain and stiffness that progressively limits joint movement, eventually compromising a patient's ability to walk. severe short staure and brachydactyly have been reported in a few patients with mjd.

MONDO:0013233.name: spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia, handigodu type
MONDO:0013233.def: a rare, genetic, primary bone dysplasia characterized by three distinct phenotypes, namely: 1) patients of average height with painful, osteoarthritic changes of the hip joints and no spinal abnormalities, 2) short-statured patients with predominantly truncal shortening, arm span exceeding height, dyspalstic changes of hips and varying degrees of platyspondyly, and 3) patients with dwarfism, various associated skeletal abnormalities (particularly of the knees and hands) and severe epiphyseal dysplasia (of hips, knees, hands, wrists) associated with significant platyspondyly. most patients cannot walk long distances, and many have decreased joint spaces and sclerotic and cystic changes on imaging.

MONDO:0013235.name: pancreatic cancer, susceptibility to, 2
MONDO:0013235.def: any familial pancreatic carcinoma in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the brca2 gene.

MONDO:0013236.name: pancreatic cancer, susceptibility to, 3
MONDO:0013236.def: any familial pancreatic carcinoma in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the palb2 gene.

MONDO:0013237.name: susceptibility to mononeuropathy of the median nerve, mild
MONDO:0013237.synonym: mononeuropathy of the median nerve, mild

MONDO:0013238.name: chromosome 17q23.1-q23.2 deletion syndrome
MONDO:0013238.def: 17q23.1q23.2 microdeletion syndrome is a recently described syndrome characterized by developmental delay, microcephaly, short stature, heart defects and limb abnormalities.

MONDO:0013239.name: hereditary spastic paraplegia 41
MONDO:0013239.def: autosomal dominant spastic paraplegia type 41 is a pure form of hereditary spastic paraplegia characterized by onset in adolescence or early adulthood of slowly progressive spastic paraplegia, proximal muscle weakness of the lower extremities and small hand muscles, hyperreflexia, spastic gait and mild urinary compromise.

MONDO:0013240.name: maturity-onset diabetes of the young type 10
MONDO:0013240.def: any maturity-onset diabetes of the young in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ins gene.

MONDO:0013241.name: spinocerebellar ataxia type 30
MONDO:0013241.def: spinocerebellar ataxia type 30 (sca30) is a very rare subtype of autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia type iii (adca type iii) characterized by a slowly progressive and relatively pure ataxia.

MONDO:0013242.name: maturity-onset diabetes of the young type 11
MONDO:0013242.def: any maturity-onset diabetes of the young in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the blk gene.

MONDO:0013243.name: neuronopathy, distal hereditary motor, type 2c
MONDO:0013243.def: any neuronopathy, distal hereditary motor in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the hspb3 gene.

MONDO:0013244.name: brachydactyly type e2
MONDO:0013244.def: any brachydactyly type e in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the pthlh gene.

MONDO:0013245.name: syndromic multisystem autoimmune disease due to itch deficiency
MONDO:0013245.synonym: syndromic multisystem autoimmune disease due to itch deficiency

MONDO:0013246.name: fatty liver disease, nonalcoholic, susceptibility to, 2

MONDO:0013247.name: fanconi renotubular syndrome 2
MONDO:0013247.def: any fanconi syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the slc34a1 gene.

MONDO:0013248.name: fanconi anemia complementation group o
MONDO:0013248.def: any fanconi anemia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the rad51c gene.

MONDO:0013249.name: autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss 84a
MONDO:0013249.def: any autosomal recessive nonsyndromic deafness in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ptprq gene.

MONDO:0013250.name: autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss 85
MONDO:0013250.def: an autosomal recessive nonsyndromic deafness that has material basis in variation in the chromosome region 17p12-q11.2.

MONDO:0013252.name: warsaw breakage syndrome
MONDO:0013252.def: a syndrome mainly characterized by severe growth retardation and microcephaly. it is a new form of cohesinopathy showing defects in sister chromatid cohesion and hypersensitivity to chemicals that induce replication stress, thus combining distinct cytogenetic features seen in roberts syndrome and fanconi anemia, respectively. it has material basis in homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the ddx11 gene on chromosome 12p11.

MONDO:0013253.name: breast-ovarian cancer, familial, susceptibility to, 3
MONDO:0013253.def: any hereditary breast ovarian cancer syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the rad51c gene.

MONDO:0013255.name: arthrogryposis, renal dysfunction, and cholestasis 2
MONDO:0013255.def: any arthrogryposis-renal dysfunction-cholestasis syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the vipas39 gene.

MONDO:0013256.name: chromosome 15q24 deletion syndrome
MONDO:0013256.def: 15q24 microdeletion syndrome is a rare chromosomal anomaly characterized cytogenetically by a 1.7-6.1 mb deletion in chromosome 15q24 and clinically by pre- and post-natal growth retardation, intellectual disability, distinct facial features, and genital, skeletal, and digital anomalies.

MONDO:0013259.name: oguchi disease-2
MONDO:0013259.def: any oguchi disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the grk1 gene.

MONDO:0013261.name: dilated cardiomyopathy 1r
MONDO:0013261.def: any familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the actc1 gene.

MONDO:0013262.name: dilated cardiomyopathy 1s
MONDO:0013262.def: any familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the myh7 gene.

MONDO:0013263.name: retinitis pigmentosa 54
MONDO:0013263.def: any retinitis pigmentosa in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the pcare gene.

MONDO:0013264.name: amyotrophic lateral sclerosis type 12
MONDO:0013264.def: any amyotrophic lateral sclerosis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the optn gene.

MONDO:0013266.name: intellectual disability, autosomal dominant 20
MONDO:0013266.def: any autosomal dominant non-syndromic intellectual disability in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the mef2c gene.
MONDO:0013266.synonym: neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia, stereotypic hand movements, and impaired language

MONDO:0013267.name: distal 16p11.2 microdeletion syndrome
MONDO:0013267.def: distal 16p11.2 microdeletion syndrome is a rare chromosomal anomaly syndrome resulting from the partial deletion of the short arm of chromosome 16 with a highly variable phenotype typically characterized by developmental delay, mild intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder. macrocephaly (apparent by 2 years of age), structural brain malformations, epilepsy, vertebral anomalies and obesity are frequently associated.

MONDO:0013268.name: frontonasal dysplasia with alopecia and genital anomaly
MONDO:0013268.def: frontonasal dysplasia with alopecia and genital anomaly is a new phenotype of frontonasal dysplasia associated with total alopecia and hypogonadism.
MONDO:0013268.synonym: frontonasal dysplasia with alopecia and genital abnomality

MONDO:0013269.name: autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss 91
MONDO:0013269.def: any autosomal recessive nonsyndromic deafness in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the serpinb6 gene.

MONDO:0013271.name: frontonasal dysplasia - severe microphthalmia - severe facial clefting syndrome

MONDO:0013272.name: chromosome 14q11-q22 deletion syndrome
MONDO:0013272.def: 14q11.2 microdeletion syndrome is a recently described syndrome characterized by developmental delay, hypotonia and facial dysmorphism.

MONDO:0013273.name: chromosome 16p13.3 duplication syndrome
MONDO:0013273.def: 16p13.3 microduplication syndrome is a rare chromosomal anomaly syndrome resulting from a partial duplication of the short arm of chromosome 16 and manifesting with a variable phenotype which is mostly characterized by: mild to moderate intellectual deficit and developmental delay (particularly speech), normal growth, short, proximally implanted thumbs and other hand and feet malformations (such as camptodactyly, syndactyly, club feet), mild arthrogryposis and characteristic facies (upslanting, narrow palpebral fissures, hypertelorism, mid face hypoplasia, bulbous nasal tip and low set ears). other reported manifestations include cryptorchidism, inguinal hernia and behavioral problems.

MONDO:0013274.name: retinitis pigmentosa 51
MONDO:0013274.def: any retinitis pigmentosa in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ttc8 gene.

MONDO:0013275.name: hemolytic anemia due to glucophosphate isomerase deficiency
MONDO:0013275.def: glucosephosphate isomerase (gpi) deficiency is an erythroenzymopathy characterized by chronic nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia.
MONDO:0013275.synonym: hemolytic anemia, nonspherocytic, due to glucose phosphate isomerase deficiency

MONDO:0013276.name: reynolds syndrome
MONDO:0013276.def: an autoimmune disorder characterized by the association of primary biliary cirrhosis (pbc) with limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcssc).

MONDO:0013277.name: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 5
MONDO:0013277.def: any early infantile epileptic encephalopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the sptan1 gene.

MONDO:0013278.name: lymphatic malformation 3
MONDO:0013278.def: any hereditary lymphedema in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the gjc2 gene.

MONDO:0013279.name: long qt syndrome 13
MONDO:0013279.def: any long qt syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the kcnj5 gene.

MONDO:0013280.name: myxoid liposarcoma
MONDO:0013280.def: a liposarcoma characterized by the presence of round non-lipogenic primitive mesenchymal cells and small signet ring lipoblasts within a myxoid stoma with a branching vascular pattern. this category includes hypercellular lesions with round cell morphology, formerly known as round cell liposarcoma.

MONDO:0013281.name: cog4-congenital disorder of glycosylation
MONDO:0013281.def: cog4-cdg is an extremely rare form of cdg syndrome characterized clinically in the single reported case to date by seizures, some dysmorphic features, axial hyponia, slight peripheral hypertonia and hyperreflexia.
MONDO:0013281.synonym: congenital disorder of glycosylation, type iij

MONDO:0013282.name: alpha 1-antitrypsin deficiency
MONDO:0013282.def: alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency is a hereditary disease that develops in adulthood and is characterized by chronic liver disorders (cirrhosis), respiratory disorders (emphysema), and rarely panniculitis.
MONDO:0013282.synonym: hemorrhagic diathesis due to antithrombin pittsburgh

MONDO:0013285.name: immunodeficiency, common variable, 5
MONDO:0013285.def: any common variable immunodeficiency in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ms4a1 gene.

MONDO:0013286.name: immunodeficiency, common variable, 6
MONDO:0013286.def: any common variable immunodeficiency in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the cd81 gene.

MONDO:0013287.name: agammaglobulinemia 2, autosomal recessive
MONDO:0013287.def: any autosomal agammaglobulinemia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the igll1 gene.

MONDO:0013288.name: agammaglobulinemia 3, autosomal recessive
MONDO:0013288.def: any autosomal agammaglobulinemia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the cd79a gene.

MONDO:0013289.name: agammaglobulinemia 4, autosomal recessive
MONDO:0013289.def: any autosomal agammaglobulinemia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the blnk gene.

MONDO:0013290.name: agammaglobulinemia 5, autosomal dominant
MONDO:0013290.def: any autosomal agammaglobulinemia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the lrrc8a gene.

MONDO:0013291.name: glycogen storage disease xv
MONDO:0013291.def: glycogen storage disease type 15 is an extremely rare genetic glycogen storage disease reported in one patient to date. clinical signs included muscle weakness, cardiac arrhythmia associated with accumulation of abnormal storage material in the heart and glycogen depletion in skeletal muscle.

MONDO:0013292.name: chromosome 4q21 deletion syndrome
MONDO:0013292.def: the 4q21 microdeletion syndrome is a newly described syndrome associated with facial dysmorphism, progressive growth restriction, severe intellectual deficit and absent or severely delayed speech.

MONDO:0013293.name: isolated microphthalmia 6
MONDO:0013293.def: any isolated microphthalmia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the prss56 gene.

MONDO:0013294.name: dermatitis, atopic, 8
MONDO:0013294.def: an inherited susceptibility or predisposition to developing atopic dermatitis that is associated with variation in the region 4q22.1.

MONDO:0013295.name: dermatitis, atopic, 9
MONDO:0013295.def: an inherited susceptibility or predisposition to developing atopic dermatitis that is associated with variation in the region 3p24.

MONDO:0013296.name: myeloid neoplasm associated with fgfr1 rearrangement
MONDO:0013296.def: hematologic neoplasms characterized by the rearrangement of the fgfr1 gene, resulting in translocations with an 8p11 breakpoint. patients present with a myeloproliferative neoplasm, acute myeloid leukemia, lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia of t or b-cell lineage, or acute leukemia of mixed phenotype.

MONDO:0013297.name: autosomal dominant limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 1h
MONDO:0013297.def: autosomal dominant limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 1h (lgmd1h) is a subtype of autosomal dominant limb-girdle muscular dystrophy characterized by slowly progressive proximal muscular weakness initially affecting the lower limbs (and later involving the upper limbs), hypotrophy of upper and lower limb-girdle muscles, hyporeflexia, calf hypertrophy, and increased serum creatine kinase. there is no involvement of oculo-facial-bulbar muscles and cardiac muscle.

MONDO:0013298.name: chromosome 17q21.31 duplication syndrome
MONDO:0013298.def: the newly described 17q21.31 microduplication syndrome is associated with a broad clinical spectrum, of which behavioral disorders and poor social interaction seem to be the most consistent.

MONDO:0013300.name: commissural facial cleft
MONDO:0013300.def: greatly exaggerated width of the mouth, resulting from failure of union of the maxillary and mandibular processes, with extension of the oral orifice toward the ear. the defect may be unilateral or bilateral. (dorland, 27th ed)

MONDO:0013301.name: aromatase deficiency
MONDO:0013301.def: aromatase deficiency disrupts the synthesis of estradiol, resulting in hirsutism of mothers during gestation of an affected child; pseudohermaphroditism and virilization in women; and tall stature, osteoporosis and obesity in men.
MONDO:0013301.synonym: pseudohermaphroditism, female, due to placental aromatase deficiency

MONDO:0013302.name: nephronophthisis 11
MONDO:0013302.def: a nephronophthisis that has material basis in homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the tmem67 gene on chromosome 8q22.1.

MONDO:0013303.name: autoimmune disease, susceptibility to, 6
MONDO:0013303.def: any autoimmune disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the siae gene.

MONDO:0013304.name: von willebrand disease 2
MONDO:0013304.def: type 2 von willebrand disease (type 2 vwd) is a form of vwd characterized by a bleeding disorder associated with a qualitative deficiency and functional anomalies of the willebrand factor (von willebrand factor; vwf).

MONDO:0013305.name: autosomal dominant nonsyndromic hearing loss 51
MONDO:0013305.def: an autosomal dominant nonsyndromic deafness that is characterized by postlingual onset in the fourth decade of life with high frequency progressive hearing loss and has material basis in a 269-kb duplication of chromosome 9q21.11 involving the tjp2 and fam189a2 genes.

MONDO:0013306.name: combined oxidative phosphorylation defect type 7
MONDO:0013306.def: combined oxidative phosphorylation defect type 7 is a rare mitochondrial disease due to a defect in mitochondrial protein synthesis characterized by a variable phenotype that includes onset in infancy or early childhood of failure to thrive and psychomotor regression (after initial normal development), as well as ocular manifestations (such as ptosis, nystagmus, optic atrophy, ophthalmoplegia and reduced vision). additional manifestations include bulbar paresis with facial weakness, hypotonia, difficulty chewing, dysphagia, mild dysarthria, ataxia, global muscle atrophy, and areflexia. it has a relatively slow disease progression with patients often living into the third decade of life.

MONDO:0013307.name: myopathy, lactic acidosis, and sideroblastic anemia 2
MONDO:0013307.def: any mitochondrial myopathy and sideroblastic anemia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the yars2 gene.
MONDO:0013307.synonym: yars2 mitochondrial myopathy and sideroblastic anemia

MONDO:0013308.name: cbl-related disorder
MONDO:0013308.def: cbl-related disorder is a genetic condition caused by pathogenic variants in the cbl ubiquitin ligase gene, (cbl; hgnc:1541). due to the proposed mechanism indicating the cbl gene's relationship to the ras-mapk pathway and the phenotypic presentation similar to that of the rasopathies, cbl-related disorder should be considered a rasopathy disorder. though there is a wide spectrum of phenotypic variability, broadly, patients with cbl-related disorder have presented with developmental delay, intellectual disability, neurodevelopmental alterations, prenatal lymphatic anomalies, cardiac malformations as well as vascular anomalies particularly affecting the brain (e.g. moya-moya arteriopathies), craniofacial features indicative of a rasopathy, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, edema of the legs, musculoskeletal and respiratory thorax abnormalities, ectodermal features including cafe-au-lait spots, immunological and hematological disorders and susceptibility to tumors diagnosed as juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia (jmml) that is usually self-remitting. note tumor risk beyond jmml has not yet been thoroughly assessed. due to the clinical presentation of a broad spectrum of these and other phenotypes in patients with variants in cbl, these conditions are currently defined by experts in reference to the causal gene, cbl.

MONDO:0013310.name: congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to cytochrome p450 oxidoreductase deficiency
MONDO:0013310.def: congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to cytochrome p450 oxidoreductase deficiency is a unique form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia (cah) characterized by glucocorticoid deficiency, severe sexual ambiguity in both sexes and skeletal (especially craniofacial) malformations.

MONDO:0013311.name: ectodermal dysplasia-syndactyly syndrome
MONDO:0013311.def: ectodermal dysplasia-syndactyly syndrome is a rare, genetic ectodermal dysplasia syndrome characterized by sparse to absent scalp hair, eyebrows, and eyelashes (with pili torti when present), widely spaced, conical-shaped teeth with peg-shaped, conical crowns and enamel hypoplasia and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, associated with partial cutaneous syndactyly in hands and feet.

MONDO:0013312.name: retinitis pigmentosa 55
MONDO:0013312.def: any retinitis pigmentosa in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the arl6 gene.

MONDO:0013314.name: retinitis pigmentosa 56
MONDO:0013314.def: any retinitis pigmentosa in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the impg2 gene.

MONDO:0013315.name: retinitis pigmentosa 57
MONDO:0013315.def: any retinitis pigmentosa in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the pde6g gene.

MONDO:0013316.name: occult macular dystrophy
MONDO:0013316.def: occult macular dystrophy is a rare, genetic retinal dystrophy disease characterized by bilateral progressive decline of visual acuity, due to retinal dysfunction confined only to the macula, associated with normal fundus and fluorescein angiograms and severly attenuated focal macular and multifocal electroretinograms.

MONDO:0013317.name: torsade-de-pointes syndrome with short coupling interval
MONDO:0013317.def: torsade-de-pointes (tdp) syndrome with short coupling interval is a very rare variant of torsade de pointes, a polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, which is characterized by a short coupling interval of the first tdp beat on electrocardiogram in the absence of any structural heart disease. it manifests in early adulthood with syncope, often results in ventricular fibrillation and shows a high risk of sudden cardiac death.

MONDO:0013318.name: early repolarization associated with ventricular fibrillation

MONDO:0013320.name: chromosome 16p12.2-p11.2 deletion syndrome
MONDO:0013320.def: 16p11.2-p12.2 microdeletion syndrome is a recently described syndrome characterized by developmental delay and facial dysmorphism.

MONDO:0013321.name: forsythe-wakeling syndrome
MONDO:0013321.synonym: microcephaly and growth retardation with childhood-onset nephrotic syndrome and thrombocytopenia

MONDO:0013323.name: cranioectodermal dysplasia 2
MONDO:0013323.def: any cranioectodermal dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the wdr35 gene.

MONDO:0013325.name: cog5-congenital disorder of glycosylation
MONDO:0013325.def: cog5-cdg is an extremely rare form of cdg syndrome characterized clinically in the single reported case to date by moderate mental retardation with slow and inarticulate speech, truncal ataxia, and mild hypotonia.
MONDO:0013325.synonym: congenital disorder of glycosylation, type iii

MONDO:0013326.name: senior-loken syndrome 7
MONDO:0013326.def: any senior-loken syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the sdccag8 gene.

MONDO:0013327.name: primary hyperoxaluria type 3
MONDO:0013327.def: primary hyperoxaluria type 3 (ph3) is a disorder of glyoxylate metabolism that can be asymptomatic or characterized by oxalate nephrolithiasis.

MONDO:0013328.name: retinitis pigmentosa 58
MONDO:0013328.def: any retinitis pigmentosa in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the znf513 gene.

MONDO:0013329.name: familial clubfoot due to 17q23.1q23.2 microduplication
MONDO:0013329.def: 17q23.1-q23.2 microduplication is a newly described cause of familial isolated clubfoot.

MONDO:0013330.name: agenesis of the corpus callosum and congenital lymphedema
MONDO:0013330.synonym: agenesis of the corpus callosum and congenital lymphedema

MONDO:0013331.name: factor 5 and factor viii, combined deficiency of, 2
MONDO:0013331.def: any combined deficiency of factor v and factor viii in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the mcfd2 gene.
MONDO:0013331.synonym: mcfd2 combined deficiency of factor v and factor viii

MONDO:0013332.name: brachydactyly, type a1, with short stature, scoliosis, microcephaly, ptosis, hearing loss, and intellectual disability

MONDO:0013333.name: odontoid hypoplasia
MONDO:0013333.def: an often asymptomatic developmental abnormality of the cervical spine. it is characterized by the hypoplasia of the odontoid which appears as a stubby peg of an odontoid process. symptoms may develop after minor trauma and include localized neck pain, atlantoaxial instability, and transient or permanent neurologic manifestations.

MONDO:0013334.name: cocoon syndrome
MONDO:0013334.def: fetal encasement syndrome is a rare, lethal developmental defect during embryogenesis characterized by severe fetal malformations, including craniofacial dysmorphism (abnormal cyst in the cranial region, hypoplastic eyeballs, two orifices in the nasal region separated by a nasal septum, abnormal orifice replacing the mouth), omphalocele and immotile, hypoplastic limbs encased under an abnormal, transparent, membrane-like skin. additional features include absence of adnexal structures of the skin on the outer aspect of the limbs, as well as underdeveloped skeletal muscles and bones. association with tetralogy of fallot, horse-shoe kidneys and diaphragm and lung lobulation defects is reported.

MONDO:0013335.name: tuberculin skin test reactivity, absence of
MONDO:0013335.synonym: tuberculin skin test reactivity, absence of

MONDO:0013336.name: chromosome 19p13.13 deletion syndrome
MONDO:0013336.def: 19p13.13 microdeletion syndrome is a rare partial autosomal monosomy characterized by global developmental delay, moderate intellectual disability, macrocephaly, overgrowth, hypotonia, and facial dysmorphism (frontal bossing, down-slanting palpebral fissures). other associated features variably include ataxia, seizures, ventriculomegaly, ocular abnormalities (strabismus, optic nerve hypoplasia) and gastrointestinal problems (abdominal pain, vomiting, constipation).

MONDO:0013337.name: neuropathy, hereditary sensory and autonomic, type 1c
MONDO:0013337.def: a hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type 1 that has material basis in heterozygous mutation in the sptlc2 gene on chromosome 14q24.

MONDO:0013338.name: charcot-marie-tooth disease recessive intermediate b
MONDO:0013338.def: autosomal recessive intermediate charcot-marie-tooth disease type b is an extremely rare subtype of autosomal recessive intermediate charcot-marie-tooth (cmt) disease characterized by a cmt neuropathy associated with developmental delay, self-abusive behavior, dysmorphic features and vestibular schwannoma. motor nerve conduction velocities demonstrate features of both demyelinating and axonal pathology.

MONDO:0013339.name: dilated cardiomyopathy 1gg
MONDO:0013339.def: any familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the sdha gene.

MONDO:0013340.name: parkinson disease 5, autosomal dominant, susceptibility to
MONDO:0013340.def: an inherited susceptibility or predisposition to developing young-onset parkinson disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the uchl1 gene.
MONDO:0013340.synonym: young-onset parkinson disease caused by mutation in uchl1

MONDO:0013341.name: methylmalonic acidemia due to transcobalamin receptor defect
MONDO:0013341.def: methylmalonic aciduria due to transcobalamin receptor defect is a rare metabolite absorption and transport disorder characterized by a moderate increase of methylmalonic acid (mma) in the blood and urine due to decreased cellular uptake of cobalamin resulting from decreased transcobalamin receptor function. patients are usually asymptomatic however, screening reveals increased c3-acylcarnitine and mma in plasma. serum homocysteine levels may vary from normal to moderately elevated and retinal vascular occlusive disease, resulting in severe visual loss, has been reported.
MONDO:0013341.synonym: methylmalonic aciduria, transient, due to transcobalamin receptor defect

MONDO:0013342.name: hereditary spastic paraplegia 48
MONDO:0013342.def: autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia type 48 (spg48) is a form of hereditary spastic paraplegia usually characterized by a pure phenotype of a slowly progressive spastic paraplegia associated with urinary incontinence with an onset in mid- to late-adulthood. a complex phenotype, with the additional findings of cognitive impairment, sensorimotor polyneuropathy, ataxia and parkinsonism, as well as thin corpus callosum and white matter lesions (seen on magnetic resonance imaging), has also been reported.

MONDO:0013343.name: c1q deficiency
MONDO:0013343.def: c1q deficiency is a rare disorder associated with recurrent skin lesions, chronic infections, systemic lupus erythematosus (sle) or sle-like diseases. it has also been associated with a kidney disease known as mesangial proliferative glomerulonephritis. c1q is a complex and together with other proteins, c1r and c1s, it forms the c1 complex. this complex is important for the activation of the complement system (a group of proteins that work with the immune system). it also disposes cells that are dead. c1q deficiency presents in 2 different forms, absent c1q protein or abnormal c1q protein. symptoms include infections (ear infections (otitis media), meningitis, urinary tract infections, oral infections); skin lesions (small blisters (vesicles), dark patches, and atrophic areas) that get worse upon light exposure; cataracts; loss of eyelashes, eyebrows, and scalp hair; blood in urine; and glomerulonephritis. about 93% of cases are associated with systemic lupus erythematosus. it can be caused by mutations in the c1qa, c1qb or c1qc genes and is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern. treatment depends on the symptoms. recently, it was shown that c1q production can be restored by allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, a procedure in which a person receives blood-forming stem cells (cells from which all blood cells develop) from a genetically similar, but not identical donor.

MONDO:0013344.name: migraine, with or without aura, susceptibility to, 13
MONDO:0013344.def: any migraine disorder in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the kcnk18 gene.
MONDO:0013344.synonym: susceptibility to migraine with or without aura 13

MONDO:0013345.name: d-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria 2
MONDO:0013345.def: any d-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the idh2 gene.

MONDO:0013348.name: cone-rod dystrophy 15
MONDO:0013348.def: any cone-rod dystrophy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the cdhr1 gene.

MONDO:0013349.name: alg11-congenital disorder of glycosylation
MONDO:0013349.def: a form of congenital disorders of n-linked glycosylation characterized by facial dysmorphism (microcephaly, high forehead, low posterior hairline, strabismus), hypotonia, failure to thrive, intractable seizures, developmental delay, persistent vomiting and gastric bleeding. additional features that may be observed include fat pads anomalies, inverted nipples, and body temperature oscillation. the disease is caused by mutations in the gene alg11 (13q14.3).
MONDO:0013349.synonym: congenital disorder of glycosylation, type ip

MONDO:0013351.name: infantile cerebral and cerebellar atrophy with postnatal progressive microcephaly
MONDO:0013351.def: infantile cerebral and cerebellar atrophy with postnatal progressive microcephaly is a rare, central nervous system malformation syndrome characterized by progressive microcephaly with profound motor delay and intellectual disability, associated with hypertonia, spasticity, clonus, and seizures, with brain imaging revealing severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, and poor myelination.
MONDO:0013351.synonym: postnatal progressive microcephaly, seizures, and brain atrophy

MONDO:0013352.name: intellectual disability-severe speech delay-mild dysmorphism syndrome
MONDO:0013352.def: intellectual disability-severe speech delay-mild dysmorphism syndrome, also known as intellectual disability with language impairment and with or without autistic features, is adisorder characterized by global developmental delay with moderate to severe speech delay thataffects expressive speech. most patients have difficulty articulating words. common signs and symptoms include broad forehead, downslanting palpebral fissures, short nose with broad tip, head appearing too large for the body, frontal hair upsweep, and bulging digit pads anddelatyed gross motor skills. some patients have autistic features and/or behavioral problems. congenital malformations may be associated. all reported cases have occurred de novo (without any cases in the family). it is caused by alterations (mutations) in the caused by heterozygous mutation in the foxp1 gene.
MONDO:0013352.synonym: mental retardation with language impairment and with or without autistic features

MONDO:0013353.name: intellectual disability, anterior maxillary protrusion, and strabismus

MONDO:0013354.name: spastic ataxia 4
MONDO:0013354.def: any autosomal recessive spastic ataxia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the mtpap gene.

MONDO:0013355.name: congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type 4
MONDO:0013355.def: congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type iv (cda iv) is a newly discovered form of cda characterized by ineffective erythropoiesis and hemolysis that leads to severe anemia at birth.

MONDO:0013356.name: vesicoureteral reflux 3
MONDO:0013356.def: any vesicoureteral reflux in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the sox17 gene.

MONDO:0013357.name: chromosome 17q11.2 deletion syndrome, 1.4mb
MONDO:0013357.def: a rare severe form of neurofibromatosis type 1 (nf1) characterized by mild facial dysmorphism, developmental delay, intellectual disability, increased risk of malignancies, and a large number of neurofibromas.

MONDO:0013358.name: seckel syndrome 4
MONDO:0013358.def: any seckel syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the cenpj gene.

MONDO:0013359.name: familial hyperaldosteronism type iii
MONDO:0013359.def: familial hyperaldosteronism type iii (fh-iii) is a rare heritable form of primary aldosteronism (pa) that is characterized by early-onset severe hypertension, non glucocorticoid-remediable hyperaldosteronism, overproduction of 18-oxocortisol and 18-hydroxycortisol, and profound hypokalemia.

MONDO:0013360.name: brachyolmia, maroteaux type
MONDO:0013360.def: autosomal recessive brachyolmia, maroteaux type is a relatively mild form of brachyolmia, a group of rare genetic skeletal disorders, characterized by short trunk/short stature, generalized platyspondyly and rounding of vertebral bodies. it remains unknown whether the phenotype represents a single disease entity or a heterogeneous group of mild skeletal dysplasias.

MONDO:0013361.name: congenital prothrombin deficiency
MONDO:0013361.def: congenital factor ii deficiency is an inherited bleeding disorder due to reduced activity of factor ii (fii, prothrombin) and characterized by mucocutaneous bleeding symptoms.

MONDO:0013362.name: thoc6-related developmental delay-microcephaly-facial dysmorphism syndrome

MONDO:0013364.name: rubinstein-taybi syndrome due to ep300 haploinsufficiency
MONDO:0013364.def: any rubinstein-taybi syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ep300 gene.

MONDO:0013365.name: autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss 83
MONDO:0013365.def: an autosomal recessive nonsyndromic deafness that has material basis in variation in the chromosome region 9p23-p21.2.

MONDO:0013366.name: spondylocostal dysostosis 4, autosomal recessive
MONDO:0013366.def: any autosomal recessive spondylocostal dysostosis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the hes7 gene.

MONDO:0013367.name: long qt syndrome 2
MONDO:0013367.def: an autosomal dominant condition caused by mutation(s) in the kcnh2 gene, encoding potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily h member 2. it is characterized by a prolonged qt interval that may result in torsade de pointes, ventricular fibrillation and/or sudden cardiac death.

MONDO:0013368.name: mammary-digital-nail syndrome
MONDO:0013368.def: mammary-digital-nail syndrome is a syndromic limb malformation characterized by congenital onychodystrophy/anonychia, brachydactyly of the fifth finger, digitalization of the thumbs, with absence or hypoplasia of the distal phalanges of the hands and feet in association with juvenile hypertrophy of the breast with gigantomastia in peripubertal females.

MONDO:0013381.name: neuropathy, hereditary sensory, type 1d

MONDO:0013382.name: progressive demyelinating neuropathy with bilateral striatal necrosis
MONDO:0013382.def: progressive polyneuropathy with bilateral striatal necrosis is a rare, genetic disorder of thiamine metabolism and transport characterized by the childhood-onset of recurrent episodes of flaccid paralysis and encephalopathy, associated with bilateral striatal necrosis and chronic progressive axonal polyneuropathy with proximal and distal muscle weakness, areflexia, contractures and foot deformities.

MONDO:0013384.name: hirschsprung disease, susceptibility to, 4
MONDO:0013384.def: an inherited susceptibility or predisposition to developing hirschsprung disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the edn3 gene.

MONDO:0013385.name: treacher collins syndrome 2

MONDO:0013385.synonym: treacher-collins syndrome caused by mutation in polr1d

MONDO:0013386.name: autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss 74
MONDO:0013386.def: any autosomal recessive nonsyndromic deafness in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the msrb3 gene.

MONDO:0013387.name: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 7
MONDO:0013387.def: kcnq2-related epileptic encephalopathy is a severe form of neonatal epilepsy that usually manifests in newborns during the first week of life with seizures (that affect alternatively both sides of the body), often accompanied by clonic jerking or more complex motor behavior, as well as signs of encephalopathy such as diffuse hypotonia, limb spasticity, lack of visual fixation and tracking and mild to moderate intellectual deficiency. the severity can range from controlled to intractable seizures and mild/moderate to severe intellectual disability.

MONDO:0013388.name: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 11
MONDO:0013388.def: any early infantile epileptic encephalopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the scn2a gene.

MONDO:0013389.name: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 12
MONDO:0013389.def: an extremely rare nervous system disorder. infants with eiee12 develop very frequent epileptic seizures. seizures present within the first days to months of life. seizures may trigger eye rolling, eyelid fluttering, lip smacking, drooling, bluish coloring around the mouth, limpness, or muscle stiffening (particularly those in his or her back, legs, and arms). the seizures associated with this disease are difficult to treat and the syndrome is severely progressive. eiee12 occurs when a child inherits two mutations in the plcb1 gene (one from each parent). eiee12 is inherited in an autosomal recessive fashion.

MONDO:0013390.name: autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2q
MONDO:0013390.def: autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2q (lgmd2q) is a form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy characterized by proximal muscle weakness presenting in early childhood (with occasional falls and difficulties in climbing stairs) and a progressive course resulting in loss of ambulation in early adulthood. muscle atrophy and multiple contractures have also been reported in rare cases.

MONDO:0013391.name: sterol carrier protein 2 deficiency
MONDO:0013391.def: a peroxisomal neurodegenerative disorder characterized by spasmodic torticollis, dystonic head tremor, intention tremor, nystagmus, hyposmia, and hypergonadotrophic hypogonadism with azoospermia. slight cerebellar signs (left-sided intention tremor, balance and gait impairment) are also noted. magnetic resonance imaging (mri) shows bilateral hyperintense signals in the thalamus, butterfly-like lesions in the pons, and lesions in the occipital region, whereas nerve conduction studies of the lower extremities shows a predominantly motor and slight sensory neuropathy.

MONDO:0013392.name: autosomal recessive spinocerebellar ataxia 10
MONDO:0013392.def: any autosomal recessive cerebellar ataxia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ano10 gene.

MONDO:0013393.name: distal 7q11.23 microdeletion syndrome
MONDO:0013393.def: distal 7q11.23 microdeletion syndrome is a rare chromosomal anomaly characterized by epilepsy, neurodevelopmental disorder variably including developmental delays and intellectual disabilities of variable severity, learning disability and neurobehavioral abnormalities (autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, impulsivity, aggression, self-abusive behaviors, depression).

MONDO:0013395.name: retinitis pigmentosa 4
MONDO:0013395.def: any retinitis pigmentosa in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the rho gene.

MONDO:0013396.name: chromosome 1p32-p31 deletion syndrome
MONDO:0013396.def: 1p31p32 microdeletion syndrome is a rare chromosomal anomaly syndrome, resulting from the partial deletion of the short arm of chromosome 1, characterized by developmental delay, corpus callosum agenesis/hypoplasia and craniofacial dysmorphism, such as macrocephaly (caused by hydrocephalus or ventriculomegaly), low-set ears, anteverted nostrils and micrognathia. urinary tract defects (e.g. vesicoureteral reflux, urinary incontinence) are also frequently associated. other reported variable manifestations include hypotonia, tethered spinal cord, chiari type i malformation and seizures.

MONDO:0013400.name: congenital adrenal insuffiency with 46, xy sex reversal or 46,xy disorder of sex development-adrenal insufficiency due to cyp11a1 deficiency
MONDO:0013400.def: a rare, genetic, developmental defect during embryogenesis disorder characterized by severe, early-onset, salt-wasting adrenal insufficiency and ambiguous/female external genitalia (irrespective of chromosomal sex) due to mutations in the cyp11a1 gene. milder cases may present delayed onset of adrenal gland dysfunction and genitalia phenotype may range from normal male to female in individuals with 46,xy karyotype. imaging studies reveal hypoplastic/absent adrenal glands and biochemical findings include low serum cortisol, mineralocorticoids, androgens, and sodium, with elevated potassium levels.

MONDO:0013404.name: hypermethioninemia with deficiency of s-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase

MONDO:0013404.synonym: psychomotor retardation due to s-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase deficiency

MONDO:0013405.def: any retinitis pigmentosa in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the cnga1 gene.

MONDO:0013408.name: fadd-related immunodeficiency
MONDO:0013408.def: a rare genetic immunological disease reported in a single consanguineous pakistani family with several affected members presenting with severe bacterial and viral infections, recurrent hepatopathy (portal inflammation, fibrosis), and recurrent, stereotypical febrile episodes, sometimes lasting several days, with encephalopathy and difficult-to-control seizures. variable cardiac malformations were also reported. although there were autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (alps)-like biological features, clinical alps was not present. a homozygous missense mutation in the fadd gene (11q13.3) was found in the family and the disease is thought to follow an autosomal recessive pattern of inheritance.
MONDO:0013408.synonym: infections, recurrent, with encephalopathy, hepatic dysfunction, and cardiovascular malformations

MONDO:0013417.name: complement component 3 deficiency
MONDO:0013417.def: a rare genetic disorder with an autosomal recessive pattern of inheritance. it is caused by the ineffective or decreased biosynthesis of the third complement component, c3. c3 deficiency may also be acquired acutely post-infection or chronically from co-morbid autoimmune disorders. if c3 is adequately synthesized, its rapid depletion may result in a functional deficiency. clinical signs of the inherited deficiency present within the first decade of life and are consistent with the signs of recurrent systemic infection or immune complex disease. deficiency of serum c3 and its major cleavage product, c3b, will decrease the effective humoral immune response to encapsulated bacteria. deficiency of c3 also impairs clearance of circulating immune complexes and therefore predisposes to rheumatic and renal disease.

MONDO:0013419.name: complement component c1s deficiency

MONDO:0013424.name: 3p- syndrome
MONDO:0013424.def: distal monosomy 3p is a rare chromosomal anomaly syndrome, resulting from a partial deletion of the short arm of chromosome 3, with a highly variable phenotype typically characterized by pre- and post-natal growth retardation, intellectual disability, developmental delay and craniofacial dysmorphism (microcephaly, trigonocephaly, downslanting palpebral fissures, telecanthus, ptosis, micrognathia). postaxial polydactyly, hypotonia, renal anomalies and congenital heart defects (e.g. atrioventricular septal defect) may be associated.
