MONDO:0020635.name: anaplastic meningioma
MONDO:0020635.def: a who grade iii meningioma characterized by the presence of malignant morphologic features, including malignant cytology and a very high mitotic index (20 or more mitoses per ten high power fields).

MONDO:0020636.name: mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial diseases due to a complete deficiency

MONDO:0020637.name: mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial diseases due to a partial deficiency

MONDO:0020638.name: superficial spreading melanoma
MONDO:0020638.def: a type of melanoma that typically occurs in light-skinned individuals ranging in age from young adults to the elderly. risk factors include extensive sun exposure during childhood, a family history of melanoma, and the presence of dysplastic nevi.
MONDO:0020638.synonym: superficial spreading melanoma of the skin

MONDO:0020639.name: monosomy
MONDO:0020639.def: a chromosomal abnormality consisting of the absence of one chromosome from the normal diploid number.

MONDO:0020640.name: autoimmune encephalitis
MONDO:0020640.def: inflammation of the brain secondary to an immune response triggered by the body itself.

MONDO:0020641.name: respiratory tract neoplasm
MONDO:0020641.def: a benign or malignant, primary or metastatic neoplasm involving the respiratory tract.

MONDO:0020642.name: polycystic kidney disease
MONDO:0020642.def: a usually autosomal dominant and less frequently autosomal recessive genetic disorder characterized by the presence of numerous cysts in the kidneys leading to end-stage renal failure. the autosomal dominant trait is associated with abnormalities on the short arm of chromosome 16. symptoms in patients with the autosomal dominant trait usually appear at middle age and include abdominal pain, hematuria, and high blood pressure. patients may develop brain aneurysms and liver cysts. patients with the autosomal recessive trait present with progressive renal failure early in life and symptoms resulting from hepatic fibrosis. the autosomal recessive trait is associated with abnormalities of chromosome 6. polycystic kidney disease may also result as a side effect in patients on renal dialysis.

MONDO:0020644.name: lung non-hodgkin lymphoma
MONDO:0020644.def: a rare non-hodgkin lymphoma that arises in and is confined to the lung at the time of diagnosis. representative examples include bronchial mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma and diffuse large b-cell lymphoma.

MONDO:0020646.name: ocular adnexal lymphoma
MONDO:0020646.def: a non-hodgkin lymphoma arising from the conjunctiva, lacrimal gland, lacrimal drainage apparatus, eyelids, or other orbital tissues around the eye. the vast majority of cases are extranodal marginal zone lymphomas of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue, however, other histologic types of lymphomas can originate from ocular adnexal tissues, including rare cases of nk/t-cell lymphomas of nasal type.

MONDO:0020647.name: microcephaly, facial dysmorphism, renal agenesis, and ambiguous genitalia syndrome
MONDO:0020647.synonym: microcephaly, facial dysmorphism, renal agenesis, and ambiguous genitalia syndrome

MONDO:0020649.name: warty carcinoma of the penis
MONDO:0020649.def: a squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the penis. it is characterized by a papillary growth pattern, hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis. koilocytotic atypia is present. human papillomavirus types 16 and 6 have been identified in some cases.
MONDO:0020649.synonym: warty squamous cell carcinoma of the penis

MONDO:0020650.name: germ cell tumor of the vulva

MONDO:0020651.name: mixed germ cell tumor of vulva

MONDO:0020653.name: vaginal adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0020653.def: an adenocarcinoma arising from the vagina. morphologic variants include the clear cell, endometrioid, mesonephric, and mucinous adenocarcinoma.

MONDO:0020654.name: renal pelvis/ureter urothelial carcinoma
MONDO:0020654.def: a transitional cell carcinoma that arises from the renal pelvis and ureter.
MONDO:0020654.synonym: urothelial carcinoma of the renal pelvis and ureter

MONDO:0020656.name: human papillomavirus-related penile squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0020656.def: a squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the penis and is caused by human papillomavirus infection. morphologic variants include basaloid carcinoma and warty carcinoma.
MONDO:0020656.synonym: human papillomavirus-related penile squamous cell carcinoma

MONDO:0020660.name: osteoblastic osteosarcoma
MONDO:0020660.def: a conventional osteosarcoma characterized by the predominance of osteoid matrix.

MONDO:0020661.name: undifferentiated round cell sarcoma
MONDO:0020661.def: an undifferentiated soft tissue sarcoma characterized by the presence of uniform round or ovoid malignant cells with a high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio.

MONDO:0020662.name: borderline ovarian serous tumor
MONDO:0020662.def: a low grade serous epithelial neoplasm arising from the ovary. it is characterized by an atypical proliferation of serous-type epithelial cells without evidence of stromal invasion. it is often asymptomatic but rarely it may present with abdominal pain or abdominal enlargement due to rupture or torsion.
MONDO:0020662.synonym: serous tumour of the ovary with low malignant potential

MONDO:0020663.name: malignant spindle cell neoplasm
MONDO:0020663.def: a malignant neoplasm characterized by the presence of atypical spindle cells.

MONDO:0020664.name: spindle cell neoplasm
MONDO:0020664.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm characterized by the presence of neoplastic spindle cells.

MONDO:0020666.name: löfgren syndrome
MONDO:0020666.def: a sarcoidosis characterized by the triad of erythema nodosum, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy on chest radiograph, and joint pain.

MONDO:0020667.name: antley-bixler syndrome without genital anomalies or disordered steroidogenesis

MONDO:0020669.name: paranasal sinus cancer
MONDO:0020669.def: a primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm involving the paranasal sinuses.
MONDO:0020669.synonym: malignant tumour of the paranasal sinus

MONDO:0020672.name: vascular occlusion disorder
MONDO:0020672.def: a disorder characterized by occlusion of blood vessels. it differs from thrombosis in that it can be used to describe any form of blockage, not just one formed by a clot.

MONDO:0020673.name: arterial occlusion
MONDO:0020673.def: complete closure of the normally patent lumen of the blood vessels which carry blood away from the heart.

MONDO:0020675.name: ischemic bowel disorder
MONDO:0020675.def: disease of the large or small intestine that is caused by inadequate blood supply.

MONDO:0020676.name: obsolete disorder of central nervous system or retinal vasculature

MONDO:0020678.name: sensorineural hearing loss disorder
MONDO:0020678.def: hearing loss in which the root cause lies in the inner ear or sensory organ (cochlea and associated structures) or the vestibulocochlear nerve (cranial nerve viii).

MONDO:0020679.name: conductive hearing loss disorder
MONDO:0020679.def: hearing loss caused by impaired transmission of signals from the external auditory canal or middle ear to the cochlea.

MONDO:0020680.name: acute bronchiolitis
MONDO:0020680.def: acute inflammation of the bronchioles usually caused by the respiratory syncytial virus.

MONDO:0020683.name: acute disease
MONDO:0020683.def: disease having a short and relatively severe course.

MONDO:0020685.name: infratentorial ependymal tumor
MONDO:0020685.def: an ependymal tumor arising from the infratentorial region of the brain.

MONDO:0020686.name: acute tonsillitis
MONDO:0020686.def: an acute inflammation of the tonsils caused by viruses or bacteria. signs and symptoms include fever, enlargement of the tonsils, difficulty swallowing, and enlargement of the regional lymph nodes.

MONDO:0020687.name: supratentorial ependymal tumor
MONDO:0020687.def: an ependymal tumor arising from the supratentorial region of the brain.

MONDO:0020688.name: spinal cord ischemia
MONDO:0020688.def: reduced blood flow to the spinal cord which is supplied by the anterior spinal artery and the paired posterior spinal arteries. this condition may be associated with arteriosclerosis, trauma, emboli, diseases of the aorta, and other disorders. prolonged ischemia may lead to infarction of spinal cord tissue.

MONDO:0020689.name: aids dementia complex
MONDO:0020689.def: a neurologic condition associated with the acquired immunodeficiency syndrome and characterized by impaired concentration and memory, slowness of hand movements, ataxia, incontinence, apathy, and gait difficulties associated with hiv-1 viral infection of the central nervous system. pathologic examination of the brain reveals white matter rarefaction, perivascular infiltrates of lymphocytes, foamy macrophages, and multinucleated giant cells. (from adams et al., principles of neurology, 6th ed, pp760-1; n engl j med, 1995 apr 6;332(14):934-40)

MONDO:0020693.name: glycogen storage disease due to liver phosphorylase kinase deficiency
MONDO:0020693.def: a benign form of phosphorylase kinase deficiency caused by variants in phka2 or phkg2 and characterized by hepatomegaly, growth retardation, and mild delay in motor development during childhood.

MONDO:0020694.name: salivary gland epithelial myoepithelial carcinoma
MONDO:0020694.def: a carcinoma that arises from the salivary glands, most often the parotid gland. it presents as a slow growing and painless mass. it is characterized by the presence of duct-like structures lined by two layers of cells, an inner layer composed of epithelial-type cells and an outer layer composed of clear, myoepithelial-type cells.

MONDO:0020695.name: hypotonic cerebral palsy
MONDO:0020695.def: a type of cerebral palsy characterized by decreased muscle tone.

MONDO:0020696.name: vitamin b12 deficiency
MONDO:0020696.def: a disease characterized by low serum levels of vitamin b12, either inherited or acquired.

MONDO:0020697.name: lung epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma
MONDO:0020697.def: a lung carcinoma arising within the bronchi or bronchial tubes. it is characterized by the presence of myoepithelial cells, spindle cells, clear cells, and duct-forming epithelial cells. surgical resection may be curative.

MONDO:0020699.name: biotin metabolic disease
MONDO:0020699.def: a deficiency in biotin through either inherited or acquired causes.

MONDO:0020700.name: obsolete microcephaly, short stature, and impaired glucose metabolism

MONDO:0020704.name: inherited rippling muscle disease
MONDO:0020704.def: a rare, genetic, neuromuscular disorder characterized by muscle hyperirritability triggered by stretch, percussion or movement. patients present wave-like, electrically-silent muscle contractions (rippling), muscle mounding, painful muscle stiffness and muscle hypertrophy, usually with elevated serum creatine kinase.

MONDO:0020706.name: heberden's node
MONDO:0020706.def: osteophytes that most commonly develop on the distal interphalangeal joints, often in the setting of osteoarthritis.

MONDO:0020707.name: central hearing loss
MONDO:0020707.def: hearing loss resulting from disorders of the central nervous system auditory pathways.

MONDO:0020708.name: brachial amyotrophic diplegia
MONDO:0020708.def: a neurodegenerative condition characterized by asymmetric weakness in the upper extremities resulting from segmental lower motor neuron dysfunction.

MONDO:0020709.name: majocchi granuloma
MONDO:0020709.def: an inflammatory and granulomatous, dermatophytic infection that is classified into two forms, depending on the affected individual’s health situation and clinical picture. the first form is mainly observed in healthy individuals and is defined as a perifollicular, papular form induced by penetrating trauma that is mostly observed in the lower extremities. the second form is granulomatous, related to immunosuppression, seen in a nodular form, and usually appears on the upper extremities.

MONDO:0020711.name: selective peripheral resistance to thyroid hormone
MONDO:0020711.def: a thyroid hormone resistance syndrome characterized by resistance in peripheral tissues but not in the pituitary.

MONDO:0020714.name: mitochondrial myopathy, episodic, with optic atrophy and reversible leukoencephalopathy

MONDO:0020718.name: congenital short bowel syndrome, autosomal recessive

MONDO:0020724.name: cerebral cavernous malformation 1
MONDO:0020724.synonym: hyperkeratotic cutaneous capillary-venous malformations associated with cerebral capillary malformations

MONDO:0020725.name: anemia due to chronic disorder
MONDO:0020725.def: anemia due to a disorder that is persistent or long-standing in nature.

MONDO:0020726.name: tubulointerstitial kidney disease, autosomal dominant, 2
MONDO:0020726.def: an inherited disorder that causes a gradual loss of kidney function, caused by a mutation in the muc1 gene that leads to production of an abnormal mucin 1 protein, which deposits in the kidney and leads to slow loss of kidney function.

MONDO:0020731.name: arbovirus infection
MONDO:0020731.def: a viral infection that is transmitted by an arthropod.

MONDO:0020735.name: acth-independent macronodular adrenal hyperplasia 1
MONDO:0020735.synonym: cushing syndrome, adrenal, due to aimah

MONDO:0020737.name: optic atrophy 10 with or without ataxia, intellectual disability, and seizures
MONDO:0020737.synonym: optic atrophy 10 with or without ataxia, mental retardation, and seizures

MONDO:0020738.name: multiple benign circumferential skin creases on limbs 1

MONDO:0020741.name: pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy caused by aldh7a1 mutant
MONDO:0020741.synonym: pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy caused by aldh7a1 mutant

MONDO:0020742.name: obsolete cataract, microcephaly, failure to thrive, kyphoscoliosis syndrome

MONDO:0020743.name: mixed phenotype acute leukemia
MONDO:0020743.def: an acute leukemia of ambiguous lineage. it is characterized by the presence of either separate populations of blasts of more than one lineage, or one population of blasts co-expressing markers of more than one lineage.

MONDO:0020744.name: mobitz type i atrioventricular block
MONDO:0020744.def: a disorder characterized by an electrocardiographic finding of intermittent failure of atrial electrical impulse conduction to the ventricles, characterized by a progressively lengthening pr interval prior to the block of an atrial impulse. (cdisc)

MONDO:0020745.name: ventricular arrhythmias due to cardiac ryanodine receptor calcium release deficiency syndrome
MONDO:0020745.synonym: ventricular arrhythmias due to cardiac ryanodine receptor calcium release deficiency syndrome

MONDO:0020746.name: contractures, pterygia, and variable skeletal fusions syndrome 1b
MONDO:0020746.synonym: contractures, pterygia, and spondylocarpotarsal fusion syndrome 1b

MONDO:0020749.name: polycystic lipomembranous osteodysplasia with sclerosing leukoencephalopathy 1
MONDO:0020749.synonym: polycystic lipomembranous osteodysplasia with sclerosing leukoencephalopathy 1

MONDO:0020750.name: polycystic lipomembranous osteodysplasia with sclerosing leukoencephalopathy 2

MONDO:0020753.name: orthocoronavirinae infectious disease
MONDO:0020753.def: infectious disease causes by viruses in the subfamily orthocoronavirinae (coronaviruses). in humans, coronaviruses cause respiratory tract infections that can be mild, such as some cases of the common cold (among other possible causes, predominantly rhinoviruses), and others that can be lethal, such as sars, mers, and covid-19.

MONDO:0020757.name: sporadic hemiplegic migraine
MONDO:0020757.def: a migraine disorder characterized by an aura that includes motor weakness and the absence of family history.

MONDO:0020760.name: skin squamous cell carcinoma in situ
MONDO:0020760.def: intraepidermal squamous cell carcinoma, confined to the epidermis. there is no evidence of invasion.
MONDO:0020760.synonym: squamous cell carcinoma in situ of the skin

MONDO:0020761.name: bowen disease of the skin
MONDO:0020761.def: a form of squamous cell carcinoma in situ. it is a distinct clinicopathological entity and arises from the skin or the mucocutaneous junction. it affects predominantly white males in their 6-8th decades of life. exposed and non-exposed skin sites are equally affected. uv damage and ingestion of inorganic arsenic may play a role in the development of the disease. on the skin surface, it presents as a single or multiple erythematous, scaly, keratotic patches or plaques. the clinical entity of erythroplasia of queyrat is regarded as bowen disease of the penis and it presents as an asymptomatic, red, circumscribed plaque. morphologically, bowen disease is characterized by the presence of hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, dyskeratosis, and acanthosis. the keratotic squamous cells are atypical and display hyperchromatism and abnormal mitotic figures. the dermoepidermal basement membrane is intact. complete surgical removal of the lesion may be curative.
MONDO:0020761.synonym: intraepidermal squamous cell carcinoma, bowen type

MONDO:0020762.name: diencephalic-mesencephalic junction dysplasia syndrome 2
MONDO:0020762.synonym: spastic tetraparesis, dystonia, developmental delay, and structural abnormalities of the basal ganglia

MONDO:0020767.name: cauda equina syndrome with neurogenic bladder
MONDO:0020767.def: a rare neurologic disorder caused by impingement of the nerve roots of the cauda equina secondary to disk herniation, spinal stenosis, vertebral fracture, neoplasm or infection. clinical signs may include bladder or bowel dysfunction, paresthesia and weakness of the lower extremities. the development of neurogenic bladder implies that surgical decompression was either ineffective, delayed or not attempted.
MONDO:0020767.synonym: cauda equina syndrome with neurogenic bladder

MONDO:0020770.name: spinocerebellar ataxia, autosomal recessive, with axonal neuropathy 3
MONDO:0020770.synonym: spinocerebellar ataxia, autosomal recessive, with axonal neuropathy 3

MONDO:0020771.name: spinocerebellar ataxia, autosomal recessive, with axonal neuropathy

MONDO:0020773.name: cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea
MONDO:0020773.def: discharge of cerebrospinal fluid through the nose. common etiologies include trauma, neoplasms, and prior surgery, although the condition may occur spontaneously. (otolaryngol head neck surg 1997 apr;116(4):442-9)

MONDO:0020775.name: congenital disorder of glycosylation with defective fucosylation 1
MONDO:0020775.synonym: congenital disorder of glycosylation with defective fucosylation 1

MONDO:0020776.name: chlamydiaceae infections
MONDO:0020776.def: infections with bacteria of the family chlamydiaceae.

MONDO:0020777.name: congenital disorder of glycosylation with defective fucosylation 2
MONDO:0020777.synonym: congenital disorder of glycosylation with defective fucosylation 2

MONDO:0020779.name: cartilage development disorder
MONDO:0020779.def: any dysfunction in the growth of cartilage.

MONDO:0020781.name: encephalopathy, progressive, early-onset, with brain edema and/or leukoencephalopathy, 1

MONDO:0020782.name: chronic gingivitis
MONDO:0020782.def: chronic painless inflammation of the gums. it is characterized by erythema and edema of the gums and bleeding while brushing the teeth.

MONDO:0020790.name: gaze palsy, familial horizontal, with progressive scoliosis 1

MONDO:0020794.name: colorectal medullary carcinoma
MONDO:0020794.def: a rare, invasive colorectal adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of sheets of malignant epithelial cells with vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm. it usually has a favorable prognosis.

MONDO:0020797.name: decompression sickness
MONDO:0020797.def: a condition occurring as a result of exposure to a rapid fall in ambient pressure. gases, nitrogen in particular, come out of solution and form bubbles in body fluid and blood. these gas bubbles accumulate in joint spaces and the peripheral circulation impairing tissue oxygenation causing disorientation, severe pain, and potentially death.

MONDO:0020799.name: basal cell neoplasm
MONDO:0020799.def: a neoplastic proliferation of basal cells in the epidermis (part of the skin) or other anatomic sites (most frequently the salivary glands). the basal cell neoplastic proliferation in the epidermis results in basal cell carcinomas. the basal cell neoplastic proliferation in the salivary glands can be benign, resulting in basal cell adenomas or malignant, resulting in basal cell adenocarcinomas.

MONDO:0020800.name: demyelinating disease of central nervous system
MONDO:0020800.def: any condition in which there is degeneration of the myelin sheath that covers the nerves of the central nervous system.
MONDO:0020800.synonym: demyelinating disorders of the central nervous system

MONDO:0020801.name: rectal medullary carcinoma
MONDO:0020801.def: a rare, invasive rectal adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of sheets of malignant epithelial cells with vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm. it usually has a favorable prognosis.

MONDO:0020802.name: obsolete basal cell cancer
MONDO:0020802.def: obsolete. a neoplasm composed of basal cells that metastasizes to other anatomic sites.

MONDO:0020803.name: obsolete bundle branch block
MONDO:0020803.def: obsolete. a defect of the bundle branches or fascicles in the electrical conduction system of the heart.

MONDO:0020804.name: basal cell carcinoma
MONDO:0020804.def: a carcinoma involving the basal cells.

MONDO:0020805.name: benign basal cell neoplasm
MONDO:0020805.def: a neoplasm composed of basal cells that remains localized and does not metastasize to other anatomic sites.

MONDO:0020806.name: sinoatrial block
MONDO:0020806.def: a heart block that is initiated in the sinoatrial node.

MONDO:0020807.name: ovarian sertoli-stromal cell tumor
MONDO:0020807.def: a sex cord-stromal tumor that arises from the ovary and is composed entirely of, or in various combinations of, sertoli cells, leydig cells, and fibroblast-like cells.

MONDO:0020808.name: testicular sertoli cell tumor
MONDO:0020808.def: a sex cord-stromal tumor that arises from the testis and is characterized by the presence of neoplastic cells with features of sertoli cells. it usually presents as a slow growing testicular mass. the vast majority of cases follow a benign clinical course.

MONDO:0020809.name: benign sertoli cell tumor
MONDO:0020809.def: a sertoli cell tumor of the testis or the ovary which remains localized and does not metastasize to another anatomic site.

MONDO:0020810.name: obsolete congenital multiple café-au-lait macules-increased sister chromatid exchange syndrome

MONDO:0020811.name: mitochondrial complex iii deficiency, nuclear type

MONDO:0020812.name: exposure, dental pulp
MONDO:0020812.def: the result of pathological changes in the hard tissue of a tooth caused by carious lesions, mechanical factors, or trauma, which render the pulp susceptible to bacterial invasion from the external environment.

MONDO:0020813.name: benign testicular sertoli cell tumor
MONDO:0020813.def: a non-metastasizing sex cord-stromal tumor that arises from the testis. morphologically, it is characterized by the presence of sertoli cells forming tubules. leydig cells are rare or absent.

MONDO:0020815.name: dentigerous cyst
MONDO:0020815.def: most common follicular odontogenic cyst. occurs in relation to a partially erupted or unerupted tooth with at least the crown of the tooth to which the cyst is attached protruding into the cystic cavity. may give rise to an ameloblastoma and, in rare instances, undergo malignant transformation.

MONDO:0020818.name: secondary dentine
MONDO:0020818.def: dentin formed by normal pulp after completion of root end formation.

MONDO:0020831.name: congenital vertebral-cardiac-renal anomalies syndrome
MONDO:0020831.synonym: vertebral, cardiac, renal, and limb defects syndrome

MONDO:0020838.name: anterior nasal diphtheria
MONDO:0020838.def: infection of the anterior nasal structures by corynebacterium diphtheriae.

MONDO:0020840.name: pulmonary alveolar proteinosis with hypogammaglobulinemia
MONDO:0020840.def: a primarily a lung disorder characterized by onset of respiratory insufficiency due to pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (pap) in the first months of life. affected individuals may have normal respiratory function at birth. development of the disorder appears to be influenced or triggered by viral infection, manifest as progressive respiratory insufficiency, confluent consolidations on lung imaging, and diffuse collection of periodic acid-schiff (pas)-positive material in pulmonary alveoli associated with small and nonfoamy alveolar macrophages. patients also have hypogammaglobulinemia, leukocytosis, and splenomegaly. many patients die of respiratory failure in infancy or early childhood; hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (hsct) is curative. the pathogenesis may be related to abnormal function of alveolar macrophages, resulting in decreased catabolism of surfactant. the disorder results from a gain-of-function effect that particularly affects b cells and monocytes.

MONDO:0020841.name: neurodevelopmental disorder with cerebellar atrophy and with or without seizures
MONDO:0020841.synonym: neurodevelopmental disorder with cerebellar atrophy and with or without seizures

MONDO:0020842.name: obsolete medullary carcinoma
MONDO:0020842.def: obsolete. medullary carcinoma may refer to one of several different tumors of epithelial origin. as the term 'medulla' is a generic anatomic descriptor for the mid-layer of various organ tissues, a medullary tumor usually arises from the 'mid-layer tissues' of the relevant organ.

MONDO:0020843.name: pseudomembranous diphtheritic conjunctivitis
MONDO:0020843.def: pseudomembranous colitis resulting from infection by corynebacterium diphtheriae.

MONDO:0020845.name: progressive external ophthalmoplegia with mitochondrial dna deletions, autosomal recessive 5

MONDO:0020853.name: encephalitis/encephalopathy, mild, with reversible myelin vacuolization

MONDO:0020854.name: liddle syndrome 2
MONDO:0020854.def: any liddle syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the scnn1g gene.

MONDO:0020858.name: mitochondrial complex 5 (atp synthase) deficiency nuclear type 5
MONDO:0020858.synonym: mitochondrial complex v (atp synthase) deficiency, nuclear type 5

MONDO:0020860.name: faucial diphtheria
MONDO:0020860.def: infection of the fauces by corynebacterium diphtheriae.

MONDO:0020863.name: laryngeal diphtheria
MONDO:0020863.def: infection of the larynx by corynebacterium diphtheriae.

MONDO:0020866.name: nasopharyngeal diphtheria
MONDO:0020866.def: infection of the nasopharynx by corynebacterium diphtheriae.

MONDO:0020920.name: escherichia coli infection
MONDO:0020920.def: infection with the organism escherichia coli.

MONDO:0020937.name: contractures, pterygia, and variable skeletal fusions syndrome

MONDO:0020944.name: fungal infection of eye
MONDO:0020944.def: infection by a variety of fungi, usually through four possible mechanisms: superficial infection producing conjunctivitis, keratitis, or lacrimal obstruction; extension of infection from neighboring structures - skin, paranasal sinuses, nasopharynx; direct introduction during surgery or accidental penetrating trauma; or via the blood or lymphatic routes in patients with underlying mycoses.

MONDO:0020947.name: parasitic eye infection
MONDO:0020947.def: mild to severe infections of the eye and its adjacent structures (adnexa) by adult or larval protozoan or metazoan parasites.

MONDO:0020950.name: viral eye infection
MONDO:0020950.def: infections of the eye caused by minute intracellular agents. these infections may lead to severe inflammation in various parts of the eye - conjunctiva, iris, eyelids, etc. several viruses have been identified as the causative agents. among these are herpesvirus, adenovirus, poxvirus, and myxovirus.

MONDO:0020959.name: mansonella ozzardi infection
MONDO:0020959.def: an infection that is caused by the organism mansonella ozzardi.

MONDO:0020971.name: gonococcal urethritis
MONDO:0020971.def: inflammation of the urethra secondary to infection with neisseria gonorrhoeae; this infection is spread through sexual contact.

MONDO:0020974.name: laryngeal granuloma
MONDO:0020974.def: a tumor-like nodule or mass of inflammatory granulation tissue projecting into the lumen of the larynx.

MONDO:0020977.name: granulomatous prostatitis
MONDO:0020977.def: an infectious or non-infectious inflammatory process that affects the prostate gland. infectious causative agents include bacteria, parasites, fungi, and viruses. it is characterized by the formation of granulomas in the prostatic tissue.

MONDO:0020979.name: pilosebaceous hamartoma
MONDO:0020979.def: a hamartoma characterized by localized pilosebaceous apparatus malformation.

MONDO:0020980.name: hair nevus
MONDO:0020980.def: a usually benign congenital skin growth that is often pigmented and sometimes develop coarse surface hair. there is a lifetime risk of transformation to malignant melanoma which varies depending on the size of the lesion.

MONDO:0020983.name: myocardial rupture
MONDO:0020983.def: disease-related laceration or tearing of tissues of the heart, including the free-wall myocardium; heart septum; papillary muscles; chordae tendineae; and any of the heart valves. pathological rupture usually results from myocardial infarction (heart rupture, post-infarction).

MONDO:0020989.name: hereditary persistence of fetal hemoglobin
MONDO:0020989.def: the persistence of substantial fetal hemoglobin production into adulthood, usually associated with hemoglobinopathies due to mutations in the alpha and/or beta chain of hemoglobin.
MONDO:0020989.synonym: hpfh - hereditary persistence of foetal haemoglobin

MONDO:0020999.name: obsolete genetic chronic primary adrenal insufficiency

MONDO:0021001.name: hemochromatosis type 1
MONDO:0021001.def: hemochromatosis type 1 (classic) is the most common form of hereditary hemochromatosis (hh), a group of diseases characterized by excessive tissue iron deposition. due to its incidence (1/200-1/1000), it is not considered as a rare disease, unlike the other subforms of the disease
MONDO:0021001.synonym: symptomatic form of hfe-related hereditary hemochromatosis

MONDO:0021002.name: syndactyly
MONDO:0021002.def: a disease characterized by the presence of syndactyly, including syndromic and non-syndromic forms.

MONDO:0021003.name: polydactyly
MONDO:0021003.def: a disease characterized by the presence of polydactyly, including syndromic and non-syndromic forms.

MONDO:0021004.name: brachydactyly
MONDO:0021004.def: a disease characterized by the presence of brachydactyly, including syndromic and non-syndromic forms.

MONDO:0021005.name: faciodigitogenital syndrome
MONDO:0021005.def: a rare developmental disorder characterized by facial, limbs and genital features, and a disproportionate acromelic short stature. this includes x-linked, ar and ad forms of aarskog syndrome.

MONDO:0021008.name: secondary antiphospholipid syndrome
MONDO:0021008.def: an antiphospholipid syndrome that occurs alongside another autoimmune disorder.

MONDO:0021009.name: salivary gland mucoepidermoid carcinoma
MONDO:0021009.def: a carcinoma that arises from the salivary glands. it is the most common primary carcinoma of the salivary glands and usually presents as a firm and painless mass. it is characterized by the presence of epidermoid cells, mucus producing cells, and cells of intermediate type. the majority of cases have a favorable outcome.

MONDO:0021010.name: skin lymphangiosarcoma
MONDO:0021010.def: a malignant vascular neoplasm of the skin arising from the lymphatic vessels.

MONDO:0021013.name: trichothiodystrophy 4, nonphotosensitive
MONDO:0021013.def: a subtype of trichothiodystrophy caused by mutation(s) in the mplkip gene, encoding m-phase-specific plk1-interacting protein.

MONDO:0021016.name: obsolete channelopathy
MONDO:0021016.def: obsolete. a disease caused by disturbed function of ion channel subunits or the proteins that regulate them.

MONDO:0021017.name: synaptopathy
MONDO:0021017.def: a disease caused by dysfunction of synapses.

MONDO:0021018.name: autosomal dominant limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 1d (dnajb6)
MONDO:0021018.def: autosomal dominant limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 1d (lgmd1d) is a subtype of autosomal dominant limb-girdle muscular dystrophy characterized by an adult-onset of slowly progressive, proximal pelvic girdle weakness, with none, or only minimal, shoulder girdle involvement, and absence of cardiac and respiratory symptoms. mild to moderate elevated creatine kinase serum levels and gait abnormalities are frequently observed. lgmd1d is caused by heterozygous missense mutations in the dnajb6 gene at chr. 7q36.3.

MONDO:0021019.name: x-linked recessive ocular albinism
MONDO:0021019.def: x-linked recessive ocular albinism (xloa) is a rare disorder characterized by ocular hypopigmentation, foveal hypoplasia, nystagmus, photodysphoria, and reduced visual acuity in males.

MONDO:0021020.name: crigler-najjar syndrome type 1
MONDO:0021020.def: crigler-najjar syndrome type 1 (cns1) is the most severe form of cns, a hereditary disorder of hepatic bilirubin conjugation, characterized by severe neonatal unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia due to a complete absence of hepatic bilirubin glucuronosyltransferase (bgt).

MONDO:0021022.name: hereditary hyperekplexia
MONDO:0021022.def: hereditary hyperekplexia is a hereditary neurological disorder characterized by excessive startle responses.

MONDO:0021023.name: complete androgen insensitivity syndrome
MONDO:0021023.def: complete androgen insensitivity syndrome (cais) is a form of androgen insensitivity syndrome (ais), a disorder of sex development (dsd), characterized by the presence of female external genitalia in a 46,xy individual with normal testis development but undescended testes and unresponsiveness to age-appropriate levels of androgens.

MONDO:0021024.name: malaria, susceptibility to
MONDO:0021024.synonym: resistance to malaria due to g6pd deficiency

MONDO:0021026.name: hereditary epidermal appendage anomaly
MONDO:0021026.def: an instance of epidermal appendage anomaly that is caused by a modification of the individual's genome.

MONDO:0021027.name: obsolete genetic hair anomaly
MONDO:0021027.def: obsolete. an instance of hair anomaly that is caused by a modification of the individual's genome.

MONDO:0021028.name: obsolete genetic nail anomaly
MONDO:0021028.def: obsolete. an instance of nail anomaly that is caused by a modification of the individual's genome.

MONDO:0021029.name: hereditary sebaceous gland anomaly
MONDO:0021029.def: an instance of sebaceous gland anomaly that is caused by a modification of the individual's genome.

MONDO:0021032.name: herpes zoster with dermatitis of eyelid
MONDO:0021032.def: a form of herpes zoster infection characterized by dermatitis of the skin of the eyelid due to reactivation of latent virus associated with the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve.
MONDO:0021032.synonym: herpes zoster with dermatitis of eyelid

MONDO:0021033.name: herpes zoster dermatitis
MONDO:0021033.def: painful, localized rash caused by reactivation of latent varicella zoster virus residing in nerve cell bodies, with resulting infection of the skin in the region supplied by the affected nerve.

MONDO:0021034.name: hereditary alopecia
MONDO:0021034.def: an instance of alopecia that is caused by a modification of the individual's genome.

MONDO:0021036.name: keratosis pilaris
MONDO:0021036.def: a form of dry skin characterized by hair follicles plugged by scale.

MONDO:0021037.name: obsolete genetic neurodegenerative disease with dementia
MONDO:0021037.def: obsolete. an instance of neurodegenerative disease with dementia that is caused by a modification of the individual's genome.

MONDO:0021038.name: ewing sarcoma/peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor
MONDO:0021038.def: a spectrum of malignant tumors, affecting mostly males under age 20, characterized morphologically by the presence of small round cells. ewing sarcoma and peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor represent the ends of a spectrum, with ewing sarcoma lacking evidence of neural differentiation and the markers that characterize the peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor. ewing sarcoma and peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor may share cytogenetic abnormalities, proto-oncogene expression, cell culture and immunohistochemical abnormalities. these tumors may occur in the soft tissues or the bones. pain and the presence of a mass are the most common clinical symptoms.

MONDO:0021039.name: extraskeletal ewing sarcoma/peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor
MONDO:0021039.def: a spectrum of malignant tumors arising from the soft tissues, characterized morphologically by the presence of small round cells. ewing sarcoma and peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor represent the ends of a spectrum, with ewing sarcoma lacking evidence of neural differentiation and the markers that characterize the peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor. ewing sarcoma and peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor may share cytogenetic abnormalities, proto-oncogene expression, cell culture and immunohistochemical abnormalities. pain and the presence of a mass are the most common clinical symptoms.
MONDO:0021039.synonym: extraskeletal ewing sarcoma/peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor

MONDO:0021040.name: pancreatic neoplasm
MONDO:0021040.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm involving the pancreas.

MONDO:0021041.name: pleural solitary fibrous tumor
MONDO:0021041.def: a localized neoplasm of probable fibroblastic derivation, that arises from the pleura. it is characterized by the presence of round to spindle-shaped cells, hylanized stroma formation, thin-walled branching blood vessels, and thin bands of collagen.
MONDO:0021041.synonym: solitary fibrous tumour of the pleura

MONDO:0021042.name: glioma
MONDO:0021042.def: a benign or malignant brain and spinal cord tumor that arises from glial cells (astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, ependymal cells). tumors that arise from astrocytes are called astrocytic tumors or astrocytomas. tumors that arise from oligodendrocytes are called oligodendroglial tumors. tumors that arise from ependymal cells are called ependymomas.

MONDO:0021043.name: mixed neoplasm
MONDO:0021043.def: a neoplasm composed of at least two distinct cellular populations.

MONDO:0021044.name: obsolete wilms tumor
MONDO:0021044.def: obsolete. an embryonal neoplasm characterized by the presence of epithelial, mesenchymal, and blastema components. the vast majority of cases arise from the kidney. a small number of cases with morphologic features resembling wilms tumor of the kidney have been reported arising from the ovary and the cervix.

MONDO:0021045.name: fibroepithelial neoplasm
MONDO:0021045.def: a benign, borderline, or malignant neoplasm characterized by the presence of an epithelial and a fibrous component. representative examples are fibroadenoma and phyllodes tumor.

MONDO:0021046.name: breast fibroepithelial neoplasm
MONDO:0021046.def: a benign or malignant biphasic neoplasm that arises from the breast parenchyma. it is characterized by the presence of an epithelial and a mesenchymal (stromal) component. the typical examples are fibroadenoma and phyllodes tumor.

MONDO:0021047.name: breast phyllodes tumor
MONDO:0021047.def: a benign, malignant, or borderline circumscribed biphasic neoplasm that arises from the breast. it usually affects middle-aged women. it is characterized by the presence of a double layer of epithelial cells that are arranged in clefts, surrounded by a spindle cell mesenchymal (stromal) component.

MONDO:0021048.name: benign mastocytoma
MONDO:0021048.def: a localized mast cell neoplasm without metastatic potential.

MONDO:0021049.name: vulvar neoplasm
MONDO:0021049.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the vulva. representative examples include bartholin gland adenoma, vulvar nodular hidradenoma, vulvar carcinoma, and vulvar melanoma.

MONDO:0021050.name: vaginal neoplasm
MONDO:0021050.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm affecting the vagina. representative examples of benign neoplasms include squamous papilloma and melanocytic nevus. representative examples of malignant neoplasms include carcinoma, melanoma, and sarcoma.

MONDO:0021052.name: parasympathetic paraganglioma
MONDO:0021052.def: a benign or malignant, usually non-functioning, extra-adrenal paraganglioma that arises from paraganglia located along the parasympathetic nerves. representative examples include aorticopulmonary, carotid body, jugulotympanic, and mediastinal paragangliomas.

MONDO:0021053.name: carotid body paraganglioma
MONDO:0021053.def: a benign or malignant extra-adrenal parasympathetic paraganglioma arising from paraganglia adjacent to or in the bifurcation of the common carotid artery. most patients present with a slow growing, painless mass in the neck.

MONDO:0021054.name: bone sarcoma
MONDO:0021054.def: a sarcoma that arises from the bone. representative examples are osteosarcoma and chondrosarcoma.

MONDO:0021055.name: classic familial adenomatous polyposis
MONDO:0021055.def: familial adenomatous polyposis (fap) is characterized by the development of hundreds to thousands of adenomas in the rectum and colon during the second decade of life.

MONDO:0021056.name: familial adenomatous polyposis 1
MONDO:0021056.def: any attenuated familial adenomatous polyposis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the apc gene.

MONDO:0021057.name: classic or attenuated familial adenomatous polyposis
MONDO:0021057.def: an inherited diseases haracterized by the development of adenomas in the rectum and colon; classified into classic fap and attenuated fap.

MONDO:0021058.name: neoplastic syndrome
MONDO:0021058.def: a broad classification for disorders in which the development of neoplasms typically occur in association with a characteristic set of signs or symptoms. these disorders may be inherited or acquired.

MONDO:0021059.name: obsolete head or neck disorder/disorder
MONDO:0021059.def: obsolete. any disease or disorder affecting the head and/or neck region.

MONDO:0021060.name: rasopathy
MONDO:0021060.def: developmental syndromes caused by germline mutations (or in rare cases by somatic mosaicism) in genes that alter the ras subfamily and mitogen-activated protein kinases that control signal transduction.

MONDO:0021061.name: neurofibromatosis
MONDO:0021061.def: a hereditary neoplastic syndrome in which tumors grow in the nervous system. there are typically 3 main types recognized, but other forms with uncertain etiology exist.

MONDO:0021062.name: obsolete hereditary acrokeratotic poikiloderma of kindler-weary

MONDO:0021063.name: malignant colon neoplasm
MONDO:0021063.def: a primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm that affects the colon. representative examples include carcinoma, lymphoma, and sarcoma.

MONDO:0021064.name: jugulotympanic paraganglioma
MONDO:0021064.def: a benign or malignant extra-adrenal parasympathetic paraganglioma arising from paraganglia in the base of the skull and middle ear.

MONDO:0021065.name: pleural neoplasm
MONDO:0021065.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm that involves the serous membrane that lines the lungs and thoracic cavity. most pleural neoplasms are metastatic. diffuse malignant mesothelioma is the most common primary malignant neoplasm of the pleura.

MONDO:0021066.name: urinary system neoplasm
MONDO:0021066.def: a benign or malignant, primary or metastatic neoplasm involving the urinary system. --2003

MONDO:0021067.name: mediastinal germ cell tumor
MONDO:0021067.def: a germ cell tumor that arises from the mediastinum. representative examples include seminoma, embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumor, teratoma, and mixed germ cell tumor.

MONDO:0021068.name: ovarian neoplasm
MONDO:0021068.def: a benign, borderline, or malignant neoplasm involving the ovary.

MONDO:0021069.name: malignant endocrine neoplasm
MONDO:0021069.def: a malignant neoplasm affecting the endocrine glands. representative examples include thyroid gland carcinoma, parathyroid gland carcinoma, pituitary gland carcinoma, and adrenal cortex carcinoma.

MONDO:0021070.name: sublingual gland carcinoma
MONDO:0021070.def: a carcinoma that arises from the sublingual gland. representative examples include cystadenocarcinoma and mucoepidermoid carcinoma.

MONDO:0021071.name: laryngeal neoplasm
MONDO:0021071.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm involving the larynx.

MONDO:0021072.name: sympathetic paraganglioma
MONDO:0021072.def: a benign or malignant paraganglioma arising from the chromaffin cells of the paraganglia that are located along the sympathetic nerves. it includes extra-adrenal paragangliomas and paragangliomas that arise from the adrenal medulla. the latter are commonly referred to as pheochromocytomas. representative examples of extra-adrenal sympathetic paragangliomas include the bladder, and superior and inferior paraaortic paragangliomas. clinical signs are related to the secretion of catecholamines resulting in hypertension.

MONDO:0021073.name: paraneoplastic syndrome
MONDO:0021073.def: a classification for rare disorders of diverse organ systems (endocrine, neuromuscular, gastrointestinal, renal, dermatologic, rheumatologic, hematologic) that are affected by substances secreted by a distant neoplasm but not by the action of the neoplasm itself metastasizing to that organ or tissue. less than 1 % of neoplasms are associated with these syndromes. an immune-mediated response to neoplasm-elaborated proteins may be the cause of these syndromes. additionally, their manifestation may signal the presence of an occult neoplasm, potentially at an earlier stage of disease thereby leading to a better clinical outcome. constitutional signs may include fever, night sweats, anorexia and cachexia. clinical course is usually progressive. prognosis is variable depending on the effective treatment of the underlying neoplasm.

MONDO:0021074.name: precancerous condition
MONDO:0021074.def: a pathological process with signs indicating it may become cancerous. representative examples include leukoplakia, dysplastic nevus, actinic keratosis, xeroderma pigmentosum, and intraepithelial neoplasia.

MONDO:0021076.name: pancreatic exocrine neoplasm
MONDO:0021076.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm that arises from the epithelial cells of the exocrine pancreatic tissue.

MONDO:0021077.name: cystic neoplasm
MONDO:0021077.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm that contains a single or multiple cystic spaces. examples include cystadenoma, mucinous cystadenocarcinoma, and serous cystadenocarcinoma.

MONDO:0021079.name: childhood neoplasm
MONDO:0021079.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm arising during childhood.

MONDO:0021080.name: blood vessel neoplasm
MONDO:0021080.def: a neoplasm arising from arteries or veins.

MONDO:0021081.name: anti-nmda receptor encephalitis
MONDO:0021081.def: an autoimmune acute encephalitis caused by antibodies against the glutamate nmda receptor. it usually affects females and in the majority of cases it is associated with the presence of a tumor, most commonly an ovarian teratoma. the presence of a tumor in patients with this form of encephalitis implies that the latter is a paraneoplastic syndrome. it is manifested with psychiatric symptoms and epileptic seizures. it is a potentially lethal disorder; however, it is usually reversible with the prompt removal of the tumor.
MONDO:0021081.synonym: limbic encephalitis with nmda receptor antibodies

MONDO:0021082.name: meckel diverticulum neoplasm
MONDO:0021082.def: a neoplasm involving a meckel's diverticulum.

MONDO:0021083.name: congenital fibrosis of extraocular muscles type 1
MONDO:0021083.def: any congenital fibrosis of extraocular muscles in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the kif21a gene.

MONDO:0021085.name: gastric neoplasm
MONDO:0021085.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm involving the stomach.

MONDO:0021086.name: gingival neoplasm
MONDO:0021086.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the upper or lower gingiva.

MONDO:0021088.name: papillary meningioma
MONDO:0021088.def: a who grade iii meningioma characterized by the predominance of a perivascular pseudopapillary pattern.

MONDO:0021089.name: peripheral nervous system cancer
MONDO:0021089.def: malignant growth of cells in the peripheral nervous system (pns)or autonomic nervous system (ans), without specification as to location

MONDO:0021090.name: lipid-rich breast carcinoma
MONDO:0021090.def: an invasive breast carcinoma characterized by the presence of cytoplasmic neutral lipids in the vast majority of the malignant cells.

MONDO:0021091.name: papillary cystadenoma
MONDO:0021091.def: a serous or mucinous benign or low malignant potential cystic epithelial neoplasm. it is characterized by the presence of glandular epithelial cells forming papillary structures.

MONDO:0021092.name: fallopian tube neoplasm
MONDO:0021092.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm affecting the fallopian tube. representative examples of benign neoplasms include papilloma, adenofibroma, and leiomyoma. representative examples of malignant neoplasms include carcinoma, carcinosarcoma, and adenosarcoma.

MONDO:0021093.name: cranioectodermal dysplasia 1
MONDO:0021093.def: any cranioectodermal dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ift122 gene.

MONDO:0021094.name: immunodeficiency disease
MONDO:0021094.def: disease in which there is a deficiency or defect in the mechanisms of immunity, either cellular or humoral.

MONDO:0021095.name: parkinsonian disorder
MONDO:0021095.def: a group of disorders which feature impaired motor control characterized by bradykinesia, muscle rigidity; tremor; and postural instability. parkinsonian diseases are generally divided into primary parkinsonism (see parkinson disease), secondary parkinsonism (see parkinson disease, secondary) and inherited forms. these conditions are associated with dysfunction of dopaminergic or closely related motor integration neuronal pathways in the basal ganglia.

MONDO:0021097.name: intraductal breast papilloma
MONDO:0021097.def: a benign papillary neoplasm that arises anywhere in the ductal system of the breast. it is characterized by fibrovascular structures lined by benign epithelial and myoepithelial proliferations. intraductal breast papillomas are classified as central, when they arise in large ducts, or peripheral, when they arise in the terminal ductal lobular units.

MONDO:0021098.name: papillomatosis
MONDO:0021098.def: glandular or squamous cell neoplastic proliferations characterized by the formation of multiple papillary structures diffusely involving a specific anatomic site.

MONDO:0021099.name: intraductal papillomatosis
MONDO:0021099.def: a neoplastic process characterized by the presence of multiple intraductal papillomas.

MONDO:0021100.name: breast neoplasm
MONDO:0021100.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm of the breast parenchyma. it can originate from the ducts, lobules or the breast adipose tissue. breast neoplasms are much more common in females than males.

MONDO:0021101.name: appendix l-cell glucagon-like peptide-producing neuroendocrine tumor
MONDO:0021101.def: a neuroendocrine tumor arising from the wall of the appendix, producing glucagon-like peptides. morphologically, it is characterized by the presence of neoplastic cells forming tubular or trabecular patterns.
MONDO:0021101.synonym: vermiform appendix l-cell glucagon-like peptide-producing neuroendocrine tumour

MONDO:0021102.name: prostate phyllodes tumor
MONDO:0021102.def: an unusual, biphasic benign or malignant neoplasm that arises from the prostate gland. it is characterized by the presence of an epithelial glandular component and a proliferating stroma.

MONDO:0021103.name: obsolete collagen diseases
MONDO:0021103.def: obsolete. historically, a heterogeneous group of acute and chronic diseases, including rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, progressive systemic sclerosis, dermatomyositis, etc. this classification was based on the notion that 'collagen' was equivalent to 'connective tissue', but with the present recognition of the different types of collagen and the aggregates derived from them as distinct entities, the term 'collagen diseases' now pertains exclusively to those inherited conditions in which the primary defect is at the gene level and affects collagen biosynthesis, post-translational modification, or extracellular processing directly. (from cecil textbook of medicine, 19th ed, p1494)

MONDO:0021104.name: alcoholic fatty liver disease
MONDO:0021104.def: lipid infiltration of the hepatic parenchymal cells that is due to alcohol abuse. the fatty changes in the alcoholic fatty liver may be reversible, depending on the amounts of triglycerides accumulated.

MONDO:0021106.name: laminopathy
MONDO:0021106.def: a rare genetic disorder caused by mutations in genes encoding proteins of the nuclear lamina.

MONDO:0021107.name: narcolepsy
MONDO:0021107.def: a sleep disorder characterized by a tendency for excessive sleepiness during the day which occurs even after adequate sleep in the nighttime. the persons who suffer from this condition experience fatigue and may fall asleep at inappropriate times during the day.

MONDO:0021108.name: meningitis
MONDO:0021108.def: a disorder characterized by acute inflammation of the meninges of the brain and/or spinal cord.

MONDO:0021109.name: inverted urothelial papilloma
MONDO:0021109.def: an endophytic lesion in the urinary tract which shares several morphologic features with urothelial papilloma. this lesion may recur after complete excision. transitional cell carcinomas may arise within inverted urothelial papillomas.

MONDO:0021110.name: sweat gland adenoma
MONDO:0021110.def: a benign epithelial neoplasm arising from the sweat glands. representative examples include tubular apocrine adenoma, syringofibroadenoma, and hidradenoma.

MONDO:0021111.name: ureter neoplasm
MONDO:0021111.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the ureter.

MONDO:0021112.name: scrotum cancer
MONDO:0021112.def: a primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm affecting the scrotum.

MONDO:0021113.name: respiratory failure
MONDO:0021113.def: the significant impairment of gas exchange within the lungs resulting in hypoxia, hypercarbia, or both, to the extent that organ tissue perfusion is severely compromised. causes include chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, asthma, emphysema, acute respiratory distress syndrome, pneumonia, pulmonary edema, pneumothorax, and congestive heart failure. treatment requires intubation and mechanical ventilation until the time the lungs recover sufficient function.

MONDO:0021114.name: bartholin gland neoplasm
MONDO:0021114.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the bartholin gland. representative examples include adenoma, adenomyoma, adenocarcinoma, and squamous cell carcinoma.

MONDO:0021115.name: luminal b breast carcinoma
MONDO:0021115.def: a biologic subset of breast carcinoma defined by low to moderate expression of genes characteristic of luminal epithelial cells including estrogen receptor (er), and high expression of ggh, laptm4b, and ccne1. this subtype of breast cancer is associated with a good prognosis, although not as favorable as the luminal a subtype.
MONDO:0021115.synonym: luminal b subtype of breast carcinoma

MONDO:0021116.name: luminal a breast carcinoma
MONDO:0021116.def: a biologic subset of breast carcinoma defined by high expression of genes characteristic of luminal epithelial cells, including estrogen receptor (er), estrogen regulated protein liv-1, and the transcription factors hepatocyte nuclear factor 3, hnf3a, xbp1, and gata 3. this subtype of breast cancer is associated with a good prognosis.
MONDO:0021116.synonym: luminal a subtype of breast carcinoma

MONDO:0021117.name: lung neoplasm
MONDO:0021117.def: a benign or malignant, primary or metastatic neoplasm involving the lungs. representative examples of benign neoplasms include adenoma, papilloma, chondroma, and endobronchial lipoma. representative examples of malignant neoplasms include carcinoma, carcinoid tumor, sarcoma, and lymphoma.

MONDO:0021118.name: intestinal neoplasm
MONDO:0021118.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm involving the small or large intestine.

MONDO:0021119.name: non-functioning endocrine neoplasm
MONDO:0021119.def: a hormone producing or non-producing endocrine neoplasm, not associated with a hormonal syndrome.

MONDO:0021120.name: functioning endocrine neoplasm
MONDO:0021120.def: a hormone producing endocrine neoplasm, associated with a hormonal syndrome.

MONDO:0021121.name: hemangioendothelioma
MONDO:0021121.def: a vascular proliferation characterized by the presence of prominent endothelial cells and the formation of vascular channels. hemangioendotheliomas may display borderline or low grade characteristics.

MONDO:0021123.name: ewing sarcoma/peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor of bone
MONDO:0021123.def: a spectrum of malignant tumors arising from the bone and characterized morphologically by the presence of small round cells. ewing sarcoma and peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor represent the ends of a spectrum, with ewing sarcoma lacking evidence of neural differentiation and the markers that characterize the peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor. ewing sarcoma and peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor may share cytogenetic abnormalities, proto-oncogene expression, cell culture and immunohistochemical abnormalities. pain and the presence of a mass are the most common clinical symptoms.
MONDO:0021123.synonym: ewing's sarcoma/peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumour of bone

MONDO:0021124.name: female infertility
MONDO:0021124.def: diminished or absent ability of a female to achieve conception.

MONDO:0021126.name: syndromic or isolated
MONDO:0021126.def: an characteristic of a disease that varies depending on whether the disease appears as an isolated feature or whether the disease is a syndrome consisting of multiple features.

MONDO:0021127.name: has a syndromic presentation
MONDO:0021127.def: an characteristic of a disease in which the disease is not manifested as an isolated feature but has multiple distinct features.

MONDO:0021128.name: has an isolated presentation
MONDO:0021128.def: an characteristic of a disease in which the disease is manifested as an isolated feature.

MONDO:0021129.name: microphthalmia
MONDO:0021129.def: congenital or developmental anomaly in which the eyeballs are abnormally small.

MONDO:0021130.name: disorder of sphingolipid biosynthesis
MONDO:0021130.def: an inherited metabolic disease that is has its basis in the disruption of sphingolipid biosynthetic process.
MONDO:0021130.synonym: rare inborn error of sphingolipid biosynthetic process

MONDO:0021131.name: frontal lobe ependymal tumor
MONDO:0021131.def: an ependymal tumor affecting the frontal lobe of the brain.

MONDO:0021132.name: tertiary hyperparathyroidism
MONDO:0021132.def: an overproduction of parathyroid hormone that is autonomous and often associated with chronic secondary hyperparathyroidism.

MONDO:0021133.name: acquired factor xiii deficiency
MONDO:0021133.def: an acquired coagulation disorder due to reduced levels and activity of factor xiii.

MONDO:0021134.name: acquired factor x deficiency
MONDO:0021134.def: an bleeding disorder with a decreased antigen and/or activity of factor x (fx) that is acquired. acquired factor x deficiency is a rare disorder, commonly associated with a preceding viral illness and a circulating fx inhibitor. although multiple treatment modalities have been described with variable success, in many cases, it is a self-limited condition.

MONDO:0021136.name: rare
MONDO:0021136.def: a disease or disorder is defined as rare in europe when it affects fewer than 1 in 2000. a disease or disorder is defined as rare in the usa when it affects fewer than 200,000 persons at any given time. here we take the european definition to be consistent with orphanet.

MONDO:0021138.name: bone marrow cancer
MONDO:0021138.def: malignant neoplasms that either originate from the bone marrow (e.g. myeloid leukemias) or involve the bone marrow as secondary-metastatic tumors (e.g. metastatic carcinomas to the bone marrow). --2003

MONDO:0021140.name: congenital
MONDO:0021140.def: a characteristic of a disease in which the disease is present at birth, regardless of cause.

MONDO:0021142.name: acquired rippling muscle disease
MONDO:0021142.def: the acquired form of rmd. although rmd most often is reported with autosomal dominant inheritance, some sporadic cases are found, and an association with other diseases such as myasthenia gravis has also been reported.

MONDO:0021144.name: ovarian clear cell tumor
MONDO:0021144.def: a benign, borderline, or malignant epithelial tumor of the ovary that is characterized by a predominance of clear and hobnail cells.

MONDO:0021145.name: obsolete disorder of genitourinary system
MONDO:0021145.def: obsolete. a disease that involves the genitourinary system.

MONDO:0021146.name: headache disorder
MONDO:0021146.def: various conditions with the symptom of headache. headache disorders are classified into major groups, such as primary headache disorders (based on characteristics of their headache symptoms) and secondary headache disorders (based on their etiologies). (international classification of headache disorders, 2nd ed. cephalalgia 2004: suppl 1)

MONDO:0021147.name: disorder of development or morphogenesis
MONDO:0021147.def: any disease or disorder that disrupts the process development of an anatomical structure. can be due to genetic or environmental causes. typically happens during embryogenesis, but also includes post-embryonic development.

MONDO:0021148.name: female reproductive system neoplasm
MONDO:0021148.def: a benign, precancerous, or malignant neoplasm that affects the female reproductive system. representative examples include uterine corpus leiomyoma, endocervical polyp, ovarian carcinoma, cervical carcinoma, and endometrial carcinoma.
MONDO:0021148.synonym: tumour of the female reproductive system

MONDO:0021152.name: inherited
MONDO:0021152.def: a characteristic of a disease in which the cause of the disease is a genetic problem inherited from either or both parents.

MONDO:0021154.name: dermis disorder
MONDO:0021154.def: a disease that involves the dermis.

MONDO:0021159.name: gonococcal salpingitis
MONDO:0021159.def: an salpingitis caused by infection with neisseria gonorrhoeae.

MONDO:0021160.name: gonococcal cystitis
MONDO:0021160.def: an cystitis caused by infection with neisseria gonorrhoeae.

MONDO:0021161.name: gonococcal prostatitis
MONDO:0021161.def: an prostatitis (disease) caused by infection with neisseria gonorrhoeae.

MONDO:0021163.name: kidney neoplasm
MONDO:0021163.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm affecting the kidney. representative examples of benign renal neoplasms include fibroma, lipoma, oncocytoma, and juxtaglomerular cell tumor. representative examples of malignant renal neoplasms include renal cell carcinoma, renal pelvis carcinoma, wilms tumor, rhabdoid tumor, sarcoma, and lymphoma.

MONDO:0021164.name: posthitis
MONDO:0021164.def: an inflammatory disease involving a pathogenic inflammatory response in the prepuce of penis.

MONDO:0021165.name: paget disease
MONDO:0021165.def: a malignant neoplasm composed of large cells with large nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and abundant pale cytoplasm (paget cells). paget cell neoplasms include paget disease of the nipple and extramammary paget disease which may affect the vulva, penis, anus, skin and scrotum.

MONDO:0021166.name: inflammatory disease
MONDO:0021166.def: a disease involving a pathogenic inflammatory response in the anatomical structure.

MONDO:0021167.name: myositis disease
MONDO:0021167.def: an inflammatory disease involving a pathogenic inflammatory response in the muscle tissue.

MONDO:0021168.name: hibernoma
MONDO:0021168.def: a rare benign slow growing adipose tissue tumor, characterized by the presence of polygonal brown fat cells with multivacuolated and/or granular cytoplasm. the tumor is usually painless and is most often seen in young adults.

MONDO:0021169.name: epithelioid hemangioma
MONDO:0021169.def: a hemangioma characterized by the presence of epithelioid endothelial cells.

MONDO:0021171.name: timothy syndrome, classic type
MONDO:0021171.def: classic form of timothy syndrome, includes all features of generic.

MONDO:0021172.name: timothy syndrome, atypical type
MONDO:0021172.def: atypical form of timothy syndrome, causes a more severe form of long qt syndrome and a greater risk of arrhythmia and sudden death.

MONDO:0021175.name: herpetic vulvovaginitis
MONDO:0021175.def: infection of the vulva and the vagina caused by herpes simplex virus.

MONDO:0021176.name: autoimmune hepatitis type 2
MONDO:0021176.def: autoimmune hepatitis characterized by the presence of anti-liver kidney microsomal antibody type 1 (anti-lkm1) and/or anti-liver cytosol type 1 (anti-lc1) autoantibodies.

MONDO:0021177.name: autoimmune hepatitis type 3
MONDO:0021177.def: autoimmune hepatitis characterized by the presence of antibodies to soluble liver or liver-pancreas antigens.

MONDO:0021178.name: injury
MONDO:0021178.def: damage inflicted on the body as the direct or indirect result of an external force, with or without disruption of structural continuity.

MONDO:0021179.name: proteostasis deficiencies
MONDO:0021179.def: disorders caused by imbalances in the protein homeostasis network - synthesis, folding, and transport of proteins; post-translational modifications; and degradation or clearance of misfolded proteins.

MONDO:0021180.name: acquired xanthinuria
MONDO:0021180.def: acquired xanthinuria is generally iatrogenic. allopurinol treatment, administered to block xor and prevent uric acid overproduction, leads to the accumulation of xanthine. rarely, in the setting of aggressive chemotherapy with rapid tumor lysis or in patients with hprt deficiency on allopurinol therapy, complications of renal failure can develop from xanthine crystal nephropathy.

MONDO:0021181.name: inherited blood coagulation disorder
MONDO:0021181.def: hemorrhagic and thrombotic disorders that occur as a consequence of inherited abnormalities in blood coagulation.

MONDO:0021184.name: deltaretrovirus infections
MONDO:0021184.def: infections caused by the htlv or blv deltaretroviruses. they include human t-cell leukemia-lymphoma (leukemia-lymphoma, t-cell, acute, htlv-i-associated).

MONDO:0021189.name: intestinal motility disease
MONDO:0021189.def: a disease that has its basis in the disruption of intestinal motility.

MONDO:0021190.name: dna repair disease
MONDO:0021190.def: a disease that has its basis in the disruption of dna repair.

MONDO:0021192.name: odontogenic neoplasm
MONDO:0021192.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm arising from tooth-forming tissues. it occurs in the maxillofacial skeleton or the gingiva. benign tumors are slow growing and are not associated with specific clinical symptoms. pain is absent or slight. malignant tumors are usually associated with rapid swelling and pain.

MONDO:0021193.name: neuroepithelial neoplasm
MONDO:0021193.def: a neoplasm of the nervous system that arises from the neuroepithelial tissues. representative examples include astrocytic tumors, oligodendroglial tumors, ependymal tumors, and primitive neuroectodermal tumors.

MONDO:0021194.name: obsolete disease by subcellular system affected
MONDO:0021194.def: obsolete. a grouping of diseases based on molecular activity, cellular process or subcellular component.

MONDO:0021195.name: obsolete disease by cellular process disrupted

MONDO:0021196.name: obsolete disease by molecular activity disrupted

MONDO:0021197.name: obsolete disease by cellular component affected

MONDO:0021199.name: obsolete disease by anatomical system
MONDO:0021199.def: obsolete. a disease that disrupts the functioning of an organ system.

MONDO:0021200.name: obsolete rare disease
MONDO:0021200.def: obsolete. any of the forms of disease that have a rare incidence.

MONDO:0021201.name: skin infection
MONDO:0021201.def: an inflammatory process affecting the skin, caused by bacteria, viruses, parasites, or fungi. examples of bacterial infection include carbuncles, furuncles, impetigo, erysipelas, and abscesses. examples of viral infection include shingles, warts, molluscum contagiosum, and pityriasis rosea. examples of parasitic infection include scabies and lice. examples of fungal infection include athlete's foot, yeast infection, and ringworm.

MONDO:0021202.name: allergic otitis media
MONDO:0021202.def: a otitis media (disease) with a basis in a pathological type i hypersensitivity reaction.

MONDO:0021576.name: fallopian tube endometrioid tumor
MONDO:0021576.def: a benign, borderline, or malignant epithelial tumor of the fallopian tube that is characterized by the presence of glands and/or cysts lined by neoplastic cells that resemble endometrial cells.

MONDO:0021578.name: sternal neoplasm
MONDO:0021578.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the sternum.

MONDO:0021580.name: neoplasm of jaw
MONDO:0021580.def: a neoplasm (disease) that involves the jaw skeleton.

MONDO:0021581.name: connective tissue neoplasm
MONDO:0021581.def: neoplasms composed of connective tissue, including elastic, mucous, reticular, osseous, and cartilaginous tissue. the concept does not refer to neoplasms located in connective tissue.

MONDO:0021582.name: lentigo
MONDO:0021582.def: a flat, benign, pigmented spot on the skin caused by excessive deposition of melanin from an increased number of melanocytes in the cell layer directly above the basement membrane of the epidermis. formation is usually related to sun exposure during youth, and the lesions do not typically progress to malignancy.

MONDO:0021583.name: melanocytic skin neoplasm
MONDO:0021583.def: a melanocytic neoplasm that involves the zone of skin.

MONDO:0021588.name: eyelid sebaceous gland carcinoma
MONDO:0021588.def: a sebaceous gland carcinoma affecting the eyelid. it arises from the meibomian glands, glands of zeis, or glands associated with the caruncle. it usually affects elderly women and is characterized by high rate of local recurrence, regional, and distant metastases.

MONDO:0021605.name: benign eyelid neoplasm
MONDO:0021605.def: a non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the upper or lower eyelid.

MONDO:0021607.name: eyelid seborrheic keratosis
MONDO:0021607.def: a seborrheic keratosis that involves the eyelid.

MONDO:0021627.name: eyelid capillary hemangioma
MONDO:0021627.def: a capillary hemangioma arising from the eyelid.

MONDO:0021629.name: uterine ligament neoplasm
MONDO:0021629.def: a benign, borderline, or malignant neoplasm that affects the uterine ligaments. representative examples include wolffian adnexal tumor, papillary cystadenoma, and adenocarcinoma.

MONDO:0021630.name: lipoma of face
MONDO:0021630.def: a lipoma that involves the face.

MONDO:0021631.name: brain astrocytoma
MONDO:0021631.def: a astrocytoma (excluding glioblastoma) that involves the brain.

MONDO:0021633.name: cerebral astrocytoma
MONDO:0021633.def: an astrocytoma that arises from the cerebral hemispheres.

MONDO:0021634.name: epithelial skin neoplasm
MONDO:0021634.def: a epithelial neoplasm that involves the zone of skin.

MONDO:0021635.name: neurocristopathy
MONDO:0021635.def: that disease that arises from defects in the development of tissues containing cells commonly derived from the embryonic neural crest cell lineage.

MONDO:0021636.name: astrocytic tumor
MONDO:0021636.def: a glial tumor of the brain or spinal cord showing astrocytic differentiation. it includes the following clinicopathological entities: pilocytic astrocytoma, diffuse astrocytoma, anaplastic astrocytoma, pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma, subependymal giant cell astrocytoma, and glioblastoma.

MONDO:0021637.name: low grade glioma
MONDO:0021637.def: a grade i or grade ii glioma arising from the central nervous system. this category includes pilocytic astrocytoma, diffuse astrocytoma, subependymal giant cell astrocytoma, ependymoma, oligodendroglioma, oligoastrocytoma, and angiocentric glioma.

MONDO:0021638.name: low grade astrocytic tumor
MONDO:0021638.def: a grade i or grade ii astrocytic tumor. this category includes pilocytic astrocytoma (grade i), subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (grade i), and diffuse astrocytoma (grade ii).

MONDO:0021639.name: grade ii glioma
MONDO:0021639.def: a glioma arising from the central nervous system. this category includes diffuse astrocytoma, ependymoma, oligodendroglioma, and oligoastrocytoma.

MONDO:0021640.name: grade iii glioma
MONDO:0021640.def: a group of malignant gliomas that includes anaplastic astrocytoma, anaplastic oligodendroglioma, anaplastic oligoastrocytoma, and anaplastic ependymoma.

MONDO:0021641.name: bunyaviridae infectious disease
MONDO:0021641.def: virus diseases caused by the bunyaviridae.

MONDO:0021642.name: vulval varices
MONDO:0021642.def: a varicose disease that involves the mammalian vulva.

MONDO:0021643.name: mesenteric varices
MONDO:0021643.def: a varicose disease that involves the mesentery.

MONDO:0021650.name: uterine corpus neuroendocrine neoplasm
MONDO:0021650.def: an epithelial neoplasm with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the uterine corpus. it includes carcinoid tumor, small cell carcinoma pulmonary type, and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma.

MONDO:0021651.name: synpolydactyly
MONDO:0021651.def: a joint presentation of syndactyly (fusion of digits) and polydactyly (production of supernumerary digits).

MONDO:0021652.name: diffuse type adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0021652.def: an adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of a diffuse cellular infiltrate which is composed of poorly cohesive cells with minimal or no glandular formations. representative example is the gastric diffuse adenocarcinoma.

MONDO:0021656.name: nongerminomatous germ cell tumor
MONDO:0021656.def: a term that refers to teratoma, embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumor, choriocarcinoma, or mixed forms of these tumors.

MONDO:0021657.name: ovarian sex cord-stromal tumor
MONDO:0021657.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm that arises from the ovary and is composed of granulosa cells, sertoli cells, leydig cells, theca cells, and fibroblasts. representative examples include thecoma, fibroma, sertoli cell tumor, and granulosa cell tumor.
MONDO:0021657.synonym: sex cord-stromal tumour of the ovary

MONDO:0021659.name: combined carcinoid and adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0021659.def: a malignant epithelial neoplasm composed of a mixture of neuroendocrine cells with morphologic and immunohistochemical characteristics of carcinoid tumor and malignant glandular cells.

MONDO:0021660.name: deep seated dermatophytosis
MONDO:0021660.def: a deep folliculitis due to a cutaneous dermatophyte infection, usually on the legs. it is most commonly caused by trichophyton rubrum and is characterized by the formation of spongy granulomas which persist for three to four months and leaves deep scars.

MONDO:0021662.name: bile duct neoplasm
MONDO:0021662.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the intrahepatic or extrahepatic bile ducts. representative examples of benign neoplasms include bile duct adenoma and extrahepatic bile duct lipoma. representative examples of malignant neoplasms include intrahepatic and extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.

MONDO:0021663.name: sarcomatoid squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0021663.def: a poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma characterized by the presence of malignant cells with spindle cell features.

MONDO:0021665.name: obsolete refsum disease
MONDO:0021665.def: obsolete. a rare autosomal recessive condition caused by mutation(s) in the phyh gene, encoding phytanoyl-coa dioxygenase, peroxisomal. it is characterized by abnormalities in the breakdown of phytanic acid and impaired growth of myelin sheaths. signs and symptoms include neurologic damage, cerebellar degeneration, and neuropathy.

MONDO:0021666.name: ear infection
MONDO:0021666.def: a viral or bacterial infection that affects the external, middle, or inner ear. it may follow an upper respiratory infection. signs and symptoms include pain, ear discharge, ear fullness, hearing loss, vertigo, nausea, and vomiting.

MONDO:0021667.name: neuralgia
MONDO:0021667.def: a pain disorder characterize by pain in the distribution of a nerve or nerves

MONDO:0021669.name: post-infectious disorder
MONDO:0021669.def: a disorder that follows infection but is distinct from the infection itself and its usual manifestations.

MONDO:0021674.name: post-viral disorder
MONDO:0021674.def: a post-infectious disorder that follows viral infection but is distinct from the viral infection itself and its usual manifestations.

MONDO:0021678.name: gram-negative bacterial infections
MONDO:0021678.def: infections caused by bacteria that show up as pink (negative) when treated by the gram-staining method.

MONDO:0021679.name: gram-positive bacterial infections
MONDO:0021679.def: infections caused by bacteria that retain the crystal violet stain (positive) when treated by the gram-staining method.

MONDO:0021680.name: streptococcal infection
MONDO:0021680.def: any of the several infectious disorders caused by members of streptococcus, a genus of gram positive bacteria belonging to the family streptococcaceae. streptococcal infections are classified into groups a, b, c, d and g.

MONDO:0021681.name: sexually transmitted disease
MONDO:0021681.def: a disease due to or propagated by sexual contact.

MONDO:0021682.name: viral sexually transmitted disease
MONDO:0021682.def: viral diseases which are potentially transmitted or propagated by sexual conduct.

MONDO:0021683.name: obsolete transmissible disease
MONDO:0021683.def: obsolete a disease that can be transmitted from one organism to another, typically but not always by an infectious process.

MONDO:0021684.name: obsolete infectious disease of central nervous system

MONDO:0021690.name: obsolete congenital left ventricular aneurysm
MONDO:0021690.def: obsolete. a rare congenital non-syndromic heart malformation characterized by a bulging of the left ventricular wall, connected to the left ventricle by a wide neck (with a ratio of the connection to the body of the anomaly >1). the dimensions of described aneurysms range from 0.5 cm in diameter up to a size of 8x9 cm. most frequent locations are the left ventricular apex and the perivalvular area. aneurysms can be a- or dyskinetic or show almost normal contractility. patients may remain asymptomatic or present with systemic embolization, congestive heart failure, valvular regurgitation, ventricular wall rupture, ventricular tachycardia, or sudden cardiac death. [orphanet:1055]

MONDO:0021697.name: chlamydia infectious disease
MONDO:0021697.def: infections with bacteria of the genus chlamydia.

MONDO:0021698.name: alcohol-related disorders
MONDO:0021698.def: disorders related to or resulting from abuse or mis-use of alcohol.

MONDO:0021699.name: alcohol-induced disorders
MONDO:0021699.def: disorders stemming from the misuse and abuse of alcohol.

MONDO:0021702.name: alcohol amnestic disorder
MONDO:0021702.def: a mental disorder associated with chronic ethanol abuse (alcoholism) and nutritional deficiencies characterized by short term memory loss, confabulations, and disturbances of attention. (adams et al., principles of neurology, 6th ed, p1139)

MONDO:0021722.name: vulvodynia
