MONDO:0023305.def: heavy metal poisoning refers to when excessive exposure to a heavy metal affects the normal function of the body. examples of heavy metals that can cause toxicity include lead, mercury, arsenic, cadmium, and chromium. exposure may occur through the diet, from medications, from the environment, or in the course of work or play. heavy metals can enter the body through the skin, or by inhalation or ingestion. toxicity can result from sudden, severe exposure, or from chronic exposure over time. symptoms can vary depending on the metal involved, the amount absorbed, and the age of the person exposed. for example, young children are more susceptible to the effects of lead exposure because they absorb more compared with adults and their brains are still developing. nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain are common symptoms of acute metal ingestion. chronic exposure may cause various symptoms resulting from damage to body organs, and may increase the risk of cancer. treatment depends on the circumstances of the exposure.

MONDO:0023368.name: ho-kaufman-mcalister syndrome
MONDO:0023368.def: cleft palate, micrognathia, wormian bones, congenital heart disease, dislocated hips, absent tibiae, bowed fibulae, preaxial polydactyly of the feet

MONDO:0023369.name: disorder of facial skeleton
MONDO:0023369.def: a disease that involves the facial skeleton.

MONDO:0023370.name: neoplastic disease or syndrome
MONDO:0023370.def: either an isolated neoplasm or a syndrome with neoplasm as a major feature.

MONDO:0023388.name: pityriasis rotunda
MONDO:0023388.def: pityriasis rotunda is a rare skindisease characterized by round, scaly, pigmented patches that mainly occur on the trunk, arms and legs. there are two types of pityriasis rotunda.

MONDO:0023415.name: congenital candidiasis
MONDO:0023415.def: a fungal infection by any of the candida species that is present at birth.

MONDO:0023419.name: hyperprolinemia
MONDO:0023419.def: hyperprolinemia is when there isan excess of a particular protein building block (amino acid), called proline, in the blood. this condition generally occurs when proline is not broken down properly by the body. there are two inherited forms:hyperprolinemia type1 and hyperprolinemia type 2. people with hyperprolinemia type i often do not show any symptoms, although they have proline levels in their blood between 3 and 10 times the normal level. less commonly, affected individuals can experience seizures, intellectual disability, or other neurological or psychiatric problems. hyperprolinemia is caused by mutations in the prodh gene and is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.

MONDO:0023472.name: chondrodysplasia situs inversus imperforate anus polydactyly

MONDO:0023483.name: infectious myositis
MONDO:0023483.def: an infectious process affecting the skeletal muscles. it can be caused by viruses (including hiv), bacteria, fungi, and parasites. symptoms include muscle weakness and muscle pain.

MONDO:0023521.name: judge misch wright syndrome
MONDO:0023521.synonym: palmoplantar and perioroficial keratoderma with corneal epithelial dysplasia

MONDO:0023528.name: kshv inflammatory cytokine syndrome
MONDO:0023528.def: a syndrome caused by kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (kshv) infection. it manifests with fever, weight loss, and fluid retention in the legs or abdomen. patients are at risk of developing kshv-related cancers including kaposi sarcoma and lymphoma.

MONDO:0023551.name: c1q nephropathy
MONDO:0023551.def: c1q nephropathy is a kidney disease in which a large amount of protein is lost in the urine. it is one of the many diseases that can cause the nephrotic syndrome.

MONDO:0023554.name: acquired testicular failure
MONDO:0023554.def: testicular failure, the cause of which is not present at birth.

MONDO:0023557.name: infective vaginitis
MONDO:0023557.def: an infectious process affecting the vagina. symptoms include pain and purulent discharge.

MONDO:0023563.name: kotzot-richter syndrome
MONDO:0023563.synonym: oculocutaneous albinism, immunodeficiency, hematological disorders, and minor anomalies

MONDO:0023567.name: kozlowski brown hardwick syndrome
MONDO:0023567.synonym: unusual facies, hooked clavicles, 13 pairs of ribs, widened metaphyses, square shaped vertebral bodies and communicating hydrocephalus

MONDO:0023569.name: kozlowski ouvrier syndrome
MONDO:0023569.synonym: agenesis of the corpus callosum with mental retardation and osseous lesions

MONDO:0023571.name: kozlowski rafinski klicharska syndrome
MONDO:0023571.synonym: metaphyseal and epiphyseal dysplasia with unusual facies and cataract

MONDO:0023575.name: krauss herman holmes syndrome
MONDO:0023575.synonym: telecanthus, hypertelorism, strabismus, and pes cavus syndrome

MONDO:0023577.name: krieble bixler syndrome
MONDO:0023577.synonym: autosomal dominant blepharophimosis with multiple congenital anomalies

MONDO:0023579.name: kuster majewski hammerstein syndrome
MONDO:0023579.synonym: alopecia, macular degeneration, and growth retardation

MONDO:0023581.name: kuster syndrome
MONDO:0023581.synonym: cleft lip palate lip pits limb deficiency

MONDO:0023595.name: congenital myotonic dystrophy
MONDO:0023595.def: myotonic dystrophy that is present at birth.

MONDO:0023597.name: laryngeal papillomatosis
MONDO:0023597.def: laryngeal papillomatosis is a form of recurrent respiratory papillomatosis where tumors (papillomas) grow in the larynx (voice box).symptoms usually begin with hoarseness and/or a change in the voice.some people mayexperience difficulty breathing (dyspnea) and/or experience other life-threatening complications if the papillomas block the airway. the tumors may vary in size and grow very quickly. they often grow back even when removed.laryngeal papillomatosisis caused by two types of human papilloma virus (hpv), called hpv 6 and hpv 11.

MONDO:0023599.name: mesomelic dysplasia
MONDO:0023599.def: a form of skeletal dysplasia characterized by shortening of the bones of the middle segments of the limbs (i.e., the radii, ulnae, tibiae and fibulae).

MONDO:0023601.name: non-classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia
MONDO:0023601.def: a milder form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia characterized by decreased activity of an enzyme in the steroidogenic pathway, typically presenting later in life, that does not require life-long cortisol replacement.

MONDO:0023603.name: hereditary disorder of connective tissue
MONDO:0023603.def: an inherited genetic disorder that affects the connective tissues. representative examples include ehlers-danlos syndrome and marfan syndrome.

MONDO:0023607.name: laurence-prosser-rocker syndrome
MONDO:0023607.synonym: hirschsprung's disease associated with ulnar polydactyly, polysyndactyly of big toes and ventricular septal defect

MONDO:0023619.name: lentigo maligna melanoma
MONDO:0023619.def: lentigo maligna melanoma (lmm) is a type of skin cancer that usually develops in older, fair-skinnedadults. the average age of diagnosis is65. lmm is thought to be caused by a history of sun exposure to the affected area. treatment includes surgery to remove as much of the lmm as possible.

MONDO:0023628.name: levator syndrome
MONDO:0023628.def: levator syndrome is characterized by sporadic pain in the rectum caused by spasm of a muscle near the anus (the levator ani muscle). the muscle spasm causes pain that typically is not related to defecation. the pain usually lasts less than 20 minutes. pain may be brief and intense or a vague ache high in the rectum. it may occur spontaneously or with sitting and can waken a person from sleep. the pain may feel as if it would be relieved by the passage of gas or a bowel movement. in severe cases, the pain can persist for many hours and can recur frequently. a person may have undergone various unsuccessful rectal operations to relieve these symptoms.

MONDO:0023644.name: lip and oral cavity carcinoma
MONDO:0023644.def: a carcinoma arising in the lip or oral cavity. most oral cavity carcinomas are squamous cell carcinomas of the tongue, buccal mucosa, or gums. less frequent morphologic variants include mucoepidermoid carcinoma and adenocarcinoma. lip carcinomas are usually basal cell or squamous cell carcinomas.

MONDO:0023646.name: lipodermatosclerosis
MONDO:0023646.def: lipodermatosclerosis refers to changes in the skin of the lower legs. it is a form of panniculitis (inflammation of the layer of fat under the skin). signs and symptoms include pain, hardening of skin, change in skin color (redness), swelling, and a tapering of the legs above the ankles. the exact underlying cause is unknown; however, it appears to be associated with venous insufficiency and/or obesity. treatment usually includes compression therapy.

MONDO:0023650.name: littoral cell angioma of the spleen
MONDO:0023650.def: littoral cell angioma is a rare primary vascular neoplasm of the spleen, composed of littoral cells that line the splenic sinuses of the red pulp. it was thought to be a benign, incidental lesion. however, many recent reports have described it to be a malignant lesion with congenital and immunological associations. the definitive diagnosis can only be made after histology and immunohistochemistry studies.

MONDO:0023663.name: obsolete macrocephaly mesodermal hamartoma spectrum
MONDO:0023663.synonym: partial gigantism of hands and feet, nevi, hemihypertrophy, macrocephaly

MONDO:0023679.name: hematohidrosis
MONDO:0023679.def: hematohidrosis is a rare condition characterized by blood oozing from intact skin and mucosa. signs and symptoms include sweating blood, crying bloody tears, bleeding from the nose, bleeding from the ears, or oozing bloodfrom other skin surfaces. the episodes are usually self-limiting.

MONDO:0023682.name: tympanic paraganglioma
MONDO:0023682.def: a benign or malignant middle ear paraganglioma arising from paraganglia around the tympanum. signs and symptoms include a mass behind the tympanum, tinnitus, and conductive hearing loss.

MONDO:0023691.name: maple syrup urine disease type 1a
MONDO:0023691.def: a maple syrup urine disease caused by mutations in bckdha.

MONDO:0023692.name: maple syrup urine disease type 1b
MONDO:0023692.def: a maple syrup urine disease caused by mutations in bckdhb.

MONDO:0023693.name: maple syrup urine disease type 2
MONDO:0023693.def: a maple syrup urine disease caused by mutations in dbt.

MONDO:0023696.name: marinesco-sjogren-like syndrome
MONDO:0023696.def: a disease with similar features to marinesco-sjogren syndrome.

MONDO:0023704.name: martinez monasterio pinheiro syndrome
MONDO:0023704.def: a form of blepharo-cheilo-dontic syndrome with with cleft lip and palate, complete absence of deciduous teeth, hypodontia of permanent teeth, hair alterations, hypertelorism, midface hypoplasia, abnormal eeg, syndactyly, and other findings. this is an n-of-1 use case where only one patient or family has been described with this disorder.
MONDO:0023704.synonym: cleft lip/palate oligodontia syndactyly hair alterations

MONDO:0023726.name: mediastinal yolk sac tumor
MONDO:0023726.def: an extragonadal non-seminomatous malignant germ cell tumor that arises from the mediastinum. it is characterized by the presence of small pale cells with small amount of cytoplasm and round to oval nuclei with small nucleoli forming a variety of patterns, including microcystic, macrocystic, pseudopapillary, myxomatous, hepatoid, polyvesicular vitelline, and solid. it manifests with respiratory distress, thoracic pain, fever, and superior vena cava syndrome.
MONDO:0023726.synonym: yolk sac tumour of the mediastinum

MONDO:0023757.name: meralgia paresthetica
MONDO:0023757.def: meralgia paresthetica is a condition characterized by tingling, numbness and burning pain in the outer thigh. these symptoms may become worse after walking or standing. the condition generally only affects one side of the body, although both sides may be involved in up to 20% of cases. meralgia paresthetica is caused by compression of the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (a sensory nerve to the skin on the outer thigh). this may be associated with a variety of causes such as tight clothing, obesity, and/or pregnancy. treatment is based on the signs and symptoms present in each person and may include medications to manage pain. in most cases, conservative treatment by wearing looser clothing and/or losing weight generally resolves symptoms.

MONDO:0023820.name: moebius axonal neuropathy hypogonadism
MONDO:0023820.synonym: moebius syndrome with hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism and progressive peripheral neuropathy axonal and demyelinating type

MONDO:0023833.name: multifocal choroiditis
MONDO:0023833.def: multifocal choroiditis (mfc) is an inflammatory disorder characterized by swelling of the eye (called uveitis) and multiple lesions in the choroid, a layer of blood vessels between the white of the eye and the retina. symptoms include blurry vision, floaters, sensitivity to light, blind spots and mild eye discomfort. though the cause is unknown, multifocal choroiditis is seen most frequently in women ages 20 to 60, and usually affects both eyes. mfc is generally treated with steroid medication that can be taken orally or injected into the eye. multifocal choroiditis is a chronic condition, thus symptoms may return or worsen even after successful treatment.

MONDO:0023865.name: corneal infection
MONDO:0023865.def: a viral or bacterial infectious process affecting the cornea. symptoms include pain and redness in the eye, photophobia and eye watering.

MONDO:0023868.name: melanoma associated retinopathy
MONDO:0023868.def: melanoma-associated retinopathy (mar) is a rare autoimmune condition that occurs in some people with melanoma (a type of skin cancer) and can affect the vision.

MONDO:0023873.name: obsolete noonan-like/multiple giant cell lesion syndrome
MONDO:0023873.def: obsolete. noonan-like/multiple giant cell lesion syndrome (ns/mgcls) is a term used to describe a subgroup of people with noonan syndrome who also have giant cell lesions (benign tumor-like lesions that most frequently occur in the jaws but may also affect other bones or soft tissues) and resemble individuals who have cherubism. although ns/mgcls was once believed to be a separate condition, it is now known to bepart of the noonan syndrome spectrum. mutations in the ptpn11 and sos1 genes have been associated with ns/mgcls; however, mutations in these genes do not always cause giant cell lesions. one family with ns/mgcls has been found to have a mutation in the ptpn11 gene butno giant cell lesions, suggesting that other genetic factors may be involved in leading to giant cell development. multiple giant cell lesions associated with ns may resolve after puberty with variable restoration of the facial structure.

MONDO:0024145.name: obsolete pierre robin syndrome associated with collagen disease

MONDO:0024147.name: obsolete pierre robin syndrome associated with a chromosomal anomaly

MONDO:0024148.name: obsolete pierre robin syndrome associated with branchial archs anomalies

MONDO:0024149.name: obsolete pierre robin syndrome associated with bone disease

MONDO:0024189.name: neurologic, endocrine, and pancreatic disease, multisystem, infantile-onset

MONDO:0024227.name: miliaria pustulosa
MONDO:0024227.def: a miliaria that is characterized by pustules resulting from inflammation and bacterial infection.

MONDO:0024228.name: miliaria profunda
MONDO:0024228.def: a miliaria that is characterized by ductal occlusion of the papillary dermis causing the gland's secretions to leak between the superficial and deep layers of the skin resulting in a rapidly-spreading flesh-colored rash.

MONDO:0024229.name: miliaria crystallina
MONDO:0024229.def: a miliaria that is characterized by clear, superficial, noninflammed, subcorneal vesicles that easily rupture when rubbed and is located in the stratum corneum.

MONDO:0024235.name: brenner tumor
MONDO:0024235.def: a usually benign tumor composed of solid and cystic nests of epithelial cells resembling transitional epithelium; it is surrounded by an abundant stromal component that is dense and fibroblastic in nature.

MONDO:0024236.name: obsolete degenerative disorder
MONDO:0024236.def: obsolete. a disorder characterized by the progressive loss of function and/or structure of the affected tissues.

MONDO:0024237.name: inherited neurodegenerative disorder
MONDO:0024237.def: an inherited disorder characterized by progressive degeneration and atrophy of the nervous system.

MONDO:0024238.name: cerebral degeneration
MONDO:0024238.def: a neurodegenerative disease that involves the telencephalon.

MONDO:0024239.name: congenital anomaly of cardiovascular system
MONDO:0024239.def: a disease that has its basis in the disruption of cardiovascular system development.

MONDO:0024240.name: eccrine carcinoma
MONDO:0024240.def: an adenocarcinoma with eccrine differentiation arising from the sweat glands. it includes the following subtypes: ductal eccrine adenocarcinoma, papillary eccrine carcinoma, and eccrine porocarcinoma.

MONDO:0024245.name: ductal eccrine adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0024245.synonym: sweat gland carcinoma of the hand

MONDO:0024246.name: syringofibroadenoma
MONDO:0024246.def: a rare, benign eccrine neoplasm usually arising on acral areas as a solitary papular or nodular lesion. multiple lesions are referred as syringofibroadenomatosis. it is characterized by the presence of epithelial cuboidal cells forming anastomosing cords in a fibrovascular stroma.

MONDO:0024247.name: benign eccrine neoplasm
MONDO:0024247.def: a non-metastasizing eccrine appendage sweat gland neoplasm. representative examples include hidrocystoma, syringoma, and syringofibroadenoma.

MONDO:0024248.name: obsolete pityriasis
MONDO:0024248.def: obsolete. a name originally applied to a group of skin diseases characterized by the formation of fine, branny scales, but now used only with a modifier. (dorland, 27th ed)

MONDO:0024249.name: pityriasis lichenoides
MONDO:0024249.def: a rare cutaneous disorder of unknown etiology that can present either as an acute condition, with multiple papular lesions which become vesicular and necrotic (pityriasis lichenoides et varioliformis acuta) or chronic, with small, scaling papules (pityriasis lichenoides chronica).

MONDO:0024251.name: minamata disease
MONDO:0024251.def: a neurological syndrome caused by severe mercury poisoning.

MONDO:0024252.name: global developmental delay-neuro-ophthalmological abnormalities-seizures-intellectual disability syndrome

MONDO:0024257.name: hereditary motor neuron disease
MONDO:0024257.def: an instance of motor neuron disease that is caused by an inherited modification of the individual's genome.

MONDO:0024263.name: neonatal aspiration syndrome
MONDO:0024263.def: aspiration of meconium, blood, amniotic fluid or gastric contents around the time of delivery resulting in clinical symptoms from airway obstruction, parenchymal injury, and ventilation-perfusion mismatch. this may lead to persistent pulmonary hypertension in the newborn.

MONDO:0024264.name: hypothyroidism, congenital, nongoitrous, 2
MONDO:0024264.def: a congenital hypothyroidism that has material basis in heterozygous mutation in the pax8 gene on chromosome 2q13.

MONDO:0024265.name: duane syndrome type 1
MONDO:0024265.def: duane syndrome type 1 is the most common type of duane syndrome, an eye movement disorder that is present at birth. people with duane syndrome have restricted ability to move the affected eye(s) outward toward the ear (abduction) and/or inward toward the nose (adduction). the different types are distinguished by the eye movements that are most restricted. duane syndrome type 1 is characterized by absent to very restricted abduction and normal to mildly restricted adduction. the eye opening (palpebral fissure) narrows and the eyeball retracts into the orbit with adduction. with abduction, the reverse occurs. one or both eyes may be affected. the majority of cases are sporadic (not inherited), while about 10% are familial. 70% of affected people do not have any other abnormalities at birth (isolated duane syndrome). treatment is mainly supportive and may include glasses or contact lenses for vision correction, eye patches, or surgery.

MONDO:0024266.name: patent ductus arteriosus 3
MONDO:0024266.def: any patent ductus arteriosus in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the prdm6 gene.

MONDO:0024268.name: superficial mycosis
MONDO:0024268.def: a mycosis that is limited to the stratum corneum and essentially elicits no inflammation.
MONDO:0024268.synonym: stratum corneum of epidermis fungal infectious disease

MONDO:0024270.name: parasitic intestinal disorder
MONDO:0024270.def: infections of the intestines with parasites, commonly involving parasitic worms. infections with roundworms (nematode infections) and tapeworms (cestode infections) are also known as helminthiasis.

MONDO:0024271.name: intestinal helminthiasis
MONDO:0024271.def: a parasitic helminthiasis infectious disease that involves the intestine.

MONDO:0024275.name: amebic dysentery
MONDO:0024275.def: dysentery caused by intestinal amebic infection, chiefly with entamoeba histolytica. this condition may be associated with amebic infection of the liver and other distant sites.

MONDO:0024278.name: proctocolitis
MONDO:0024278.def: inflammation of the rectum and colon.

MONDO:0024279.name: chronic endometritis
MONDO:0024279.def: a non-granulomatous or granulomatous chronic inflammation of the endometrium. causes include sexually transmitted pathogens and gynecological procedures. patients may present with irregular bleeding.

MONDO:0024280.name: polyarticular arthritis
MONDO:0024280.def: an arthritis affecting five or more separate joints.

MONDO:0024281.name: juvenile chronic polyarthritis
MONDO:0024281.def: a group of conditions used to describe polyarthritis occurring in children.

MONDO:0024282.name: mucinous ovarian cancer
MONDO:0024282.def: an invasive malignant neoplasm that arises from the ovary and is characterized by the presence of malignant epithelial cells that contain intracytoplasmic mucin and may resemble the epithelial cells of the endocervix or gastrointestinal tract. it includes mucinous adenocarcinoma and mucinous adenocarcinofibroma.

MONDO:0024283.name: demodex folliculitis
MONDO:0024283.def: a demodicidosis that involves the hair follicle.

MONDO:0024284.name: demodicidosis of sebaceous gland
MONDO:0024284.def: a demodicidosis that involves the sebaceous gland.

MONDO:0024286.name: benign blood vessel neoplasm
MONDO:0024286.def: a benign neoplasm arising from arteries or veins.

MONDO:0024287.name: congenital vascular malformation
MONDO:0024287.def: a congenital abnormality of the arteries and veins, lymph vessels or veins and lymph vessels.

MONDO:0024288.name: hyperbilirubinemia
MONDO:0024288.def: a disease characterized by elevated level of the pigment bilirubin in the blood.

MONDO:0024290.name: enuresis
MONDO:0024290.def: an elimination disorder characterized by urinary incontinence, whether involuntary or intentional, which is not due to a medical condition and which occurs at or beyond an age at which continence is expected (usually 5 years).

MONDO:0024291.name: vascular malformation
MONDO:0024291.def: a non-neoplastic disorder that is the result of defects of vascular morphogenesis.

MONDO:0024292.name: gastrointestinal polyp
MONDO:0024292.def: a polypoid tumor that arises from any part of the gastrointestinal tract and protrudes into the lumen. representative examples include adenomatous polyps, hyperplastic polyps, and hamartomatous polyps.

MONDO:0024293.name: obsolete polyposis, gastric, dos santos and de magalhaes 1980

MONDO:0024294.name: skin disorder caused by infection
MONDO:0024294.def: skin diseases caused by bacteria, fungi, parasites, or viruses.

MONDO:0024295.name: skin disease caused by bacterial infection

MONDO:0024296.name: vascular neoplasm
MONDO:0024296.def: a benign, intermediate, or malignant neoplasm arising from vascular tissue including arteries, veins, venous sinuses, lymphatic vessels, arterioles and capillaries. it may occur in essentially any body location and is characterized by the presence of vascular channel formation and endothelial cells.

MONDO:0024297.name: obsolete nutritional or metabolic disease
MONDO:0024297.def: obsolete. a collective term for nutritional disorders resulting from poor absorption or nutritional imbalance, and metabolic disorders resulting from defects in biosynthesis (anabolism) or breakdown (catabolism) of endogenous substances.

MONDO:0024298.name: vitamin deficiency disorder
MONDO:0024298.def: a disorder that is caused by the deficiency of a vitamin. the deficiency may result from either suboptimal vitamin intake or conditions that prevent the vitamin's use or absorption in the body. representative examples include beriberi caused by thiamine deficiency, scurvy caused by vitamin c deficiency, and rickets caused by vitamin d deficiency.

MONDO:0024300.name: hypophosphatemic rickets
MONDO:0024300.def: rickets due to low serum phosphate concentrations, the cause of which can be nutritional or genetic. this condition is characterized by normal parathyroid hormone concentrations, usually caused by renal phosphate wasting occurring in isolation or as part of a renal tubular disorder, and characterized by resistance to treatment with ultraviolet radiation or vitamin d.

MONDO:0024301.name: acquired mineral metabolism disease
MONDO:0024301.def: an instance of mineral metabolism disease that is acquired during the lifetime of the individual.

MONDO:0024302.name: internal hirudiniasis
MONDO:0024302.def: a condition resulting from accidental ingestion of leeches in drinking water. they may attach themselves to the wall of the pharynx, nasal cavity, or larynx.

MONDO:0024303.name: external hirudiniasis
MONDO:0024303.def: the attachment of leeches to the skin. after the leeches drop off, bleeding may continue as a result of the action of hirudin. bites may become infected or ulcerate.

MONDO:0024304.name: ichthyosis vulgaris
MONDO:0024304.def: the most common form of ichthyosis. it is an autosomal dominant inherited or acquired disorder characterized by scaling and desquamation of the skin.

MONDO:0024305.name: acquired hyperprolactinemia
MONDO:0024305.def: an instance of hyperprolactinemia (disease) that is acquired during the lifetime of the individual.

MONDO:0024306.name: acquired lactic acidosis
MONDO:0024306.def: an instance of lactic acidosis that is acquired during the lifetime of the individual.

MONDO:0024308.name: pseudoxanthoma elasticum (inherited or acquired)
MONDO:0024308.def: an inherited disorder that causes calcium and other minerals to accumulate in the elastic fibers of the skin, eyes, and blood vessels, and less frequently in other areas such as the digestive tract.

MONDO:0024309.name: neuropathy, hereditary sensory and autonomic, type 2a
MONDO:0024309.def: a hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type 2 characterized by progressive sensory neuropathy with onset in childhood that has material basis in mutation in the hsn2 isoform of the wnk1 gene on chromosome 12p13

MONDO:0024310.name: angiodysplasia of stomach
MONDO:0024310.def: a angiodysplasia that involves the stomach.

MONDO:0024311.name: cancer affecting bone of limb skeleton
MONDO:0024311.def: a cancer that involves the limb bone.

MONDO:0024312.name: cancer of short bone of upper limb

MONDO:0024314.name: parasitemia
MONDO:0024314.def: the presence of parasites (especially malarial parasites) in the blood. (dorland, 27th ed)

MONDO:0024315.name: parasitic endophthalmitis
MONDO:0024315.def: infection of the epicondyles by a parasite.

MONDO:0024316.name: physiological malfunction arising from mental factor
MONDO:0024316.def: a dysfunction in biological function that is due to a psychological process.
MONDO:0024316.synonym: physiological malfunction arising from mental factor

MONDO:0024317.name: chronic pain syndrome
MONDO:0024317.def: chronic form of disorder involving pain.

MONDO:0024318.name: viral infection of central nervous system
MONDO:0024318.synonym: viral infection of central nervous system

MONDO:0024320.name: inner ear neoplasm
MONDO:0024320.def: a rare neoplasm that arises from the inner ear. representative examples include lipoma and acoustic schwannoma.

MONDO:0024321.name: disorder of gpi anchor biosynthesis
MONDO:0024321.def: a disease that has its basis in the disruption of gpi anchor biosynthetic process.

MONDO:0024322.name: disorder of glycosylation
MONDO:0024322.def: a disease that has its basis in the disruption of glycosylation.

MONDO:0024323.name: glomangiomyoma
MONDO:0024323.def: a morphologic variant of the glomus tumor with architectural features similar to solid glomus tumor. it is characterized by the presence of elongated glomus cells which resemble mature smooth muscle.

MONDO:0024325.name: cutaneous glomangiomyoma
MONDO:0024325.def: a glomangiomyoma that involves the zone of skin.

MONDO:0024326.name: pleural adenomatoid tumor
MONDO:0024326.def: a rare benign neoplasm that arises from the mesothelial cells of the pleura. it is characterized by a proliferation of epithelioid cells forming glandular and tubular patterns in a fibrous stroma.

MONDO:0024327.name: chronic renal failure syndrome
MONDO:0024327.def: impairment of the renal function due to chronic kidney damage.

MONDO:0024330.name: infectious otitis media
MONDO:0024330.def: inflammation of the anatomical structures of the middle ear secondary to an infectious process. bacterial etiology is most common, but both viral and fungal pathogens are also possible. symptoms include erythema and edema of the tympanic membrane, pain, and possibly fever. in severe infections, inflammation and edema of the structures of the middle ear can lead to perforation of the tympanic membrane secondary to the buildup of pressure in the narrow space.

MONDO:0024331.name: colorectal carcinoma
MONDO:0024331.def: a malignant epithelial neoplasm that arises from the colon or rectum and invades through the muscularis mucosa into the submucosa. the vast majority are adenocarcinomas.

MONDO:0024332.name: perennial allergic rhinitis
MONDO:0024332.def: allergic rhinitis caused by indoor allergens and lasting year round.

MONDO:0024333.name: sciatica
MONDO:0024333.def: a condition characterized by pain radiating from the back into the buttock and posterior/lateral aspects of the leg. sciatica may be a manifestation of sciatic neuropathy; radiculopathy (involving the spinal nerve roots; l4, l5, s1, or s2, often associated with intervertebral disk displacement); or lesions of the cauda equina.

MONDO:0024336.name: vulvar adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0024336.def: an adenocarcinoma that arises from the vulva. representative examples include bartholin gland adenocarcinoma, eccrine adenocarcinoma, apocrine adenocarcinoma, and sebaceous carcinoma.

MONDO:0024339.name: lymph node neoplasm
MONDO:0024339.def: a neoplasm involving a lymph node.

MONDO:0024340.name: retinal neuroblastoma
MONDO:0024340.def: a neuroblastoma arising from the retina.

MONDO:0024341.name: retinal cell neoplasm
MONDO:0024341.def: a neoplasm arising from the neural retina. this category includes retinoblastoma and retinocytoma.

MONDO:0024352.name: viral respiratory tract infection
MONDO:0024352.def: a respiratory tract infection caused by a virus. viruses represent the most common causes of upper and lower respiratory tract infections and include rhinoviruses, influenza viruses, parainfluenza viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus.

MONDO:0024354.name: cytomegalovirus pneumonia
MONDO:0024354.def: pneumonia caused by cytomegalovirus. most humans are exposed to cytomegalovirus. healthy individuals do not develop signs and symptoms of infection. patients with weakened immune system (e.g., aids patients, cancer patients who are being treated with chemotherapy, and patients who have received bone marrow or solid organ transplants) develop signs and symptoms of infection. they include cough, shortness of breath, fatigue, malaise, fever, muscle and joint pain, and excessive sweating.

MONDO:0024355.name: respiratory tract infectious disorder
MONDO:0024355.def: invasion of the host respiratory system by microorganisms, usually leading to pathological processes or diseases.

MONDO:0024358.name: complex sleep apnea
MONDO:0024358.def: a distinct form of sleep-disordered breathing characterized as central sleep apnea (csa), and presents in obstructive sleep apnea (osa) patients during initial treatment with a continuous positive airway pressure (cpap) device.

MONDO:0024359.name: central sleep apnea due to periodic breathing
MONDO:0024359.synonym: central sleep apnea due to periodic breathing

MONDO:0024360.name: central sleep apnea caused by high altitude
MONDO:0024360.synonym: central sleep apnea due to high altitude

MONDO:0024361.name: circadian rhythm sleep disorder
MONDO:0024361.def: a persistent or recurrent pattern of sleep disruption that is primarily due to an alteration of the circadian system or to a misalignment between the endogenous circadian rhythm and the sleep-wake schedule required by an individual's physical environment or social or professional schedule.(dsm iv)

MONDO:0024363.name: rapid eye movement sleep disorder
MONDO:0024363.synonym: repeated rapid eye movement sleep interruptions

MONDO:0024376.name: sleep disorder, initiating and maintaining sleep
MONDO:0024376.synonym: disorders of initiating and maintaining sleep

MONDO:0024377.name: circadian rhythm sleep disorder, delayed sleep phase type
MONDO:0024377.def: a circadian sleep disorder in which the individual's internal body clock is delayed with respect to the external day/night cycle.

MONDO:0024378.name: circadian rhythm sleep disorder, advanced sleep phase type
MONDO:0024378.def: a circadian sleep disorder characterized by bedtime and wake-up time much earlier than normal, although sleep quality is normal.
MONDO:0024378.synonym: sleep-wake schedule disorder, advanced phase type

MONDO:0024379.name: circadian rhythm sleep disorder, irregular sleep wake type
MONDO:0024379.def: a circadian sleep disorder characterized by at least three sleep episodes per 24-hour period, irregularly from day to day.

MONDO:0024381.name: circadian rhythm sleep disorder, jet lag type
MONDO:0024381.def: a circadian sleep disorder that results from traveling across time zones.

MONDO:0024382.name: circadian rhythm sleep disorder, shift work type
MONDO:0024382.def: a circadian sleep disorder that occurs when work schedules force people to be awake when their circadian rhythms dictate that they should be sleeping. it is classified as a circadian rhythm disorder (crd) and is extrinsic, i.e. caused by external behavioral factors.

MONDO:0024386.name: large cell lung carcinoma, clear cell variant
MONDO:0024386.def: a morphologic variant of large cell lung carcinoma characterized by a predominance of clear cells that may or may not contain glycogen.
MONDO:0024386.synonym: large cell lung carcinoma, clear cell variant

MONDO:0024387.name: benign ovarian sex cord-stromal tumor
MONDO:0024387.def: a sex cord-stromal tumor arising from the ovary, without metastatic potential.

MONDO:0024388.name: clostridium infectious disease
MONDO:0024388.def: infections with bacteria of the genus clostridium.

MONDO:0024404.name: obsolete meningitis caused by anaerobic bacteria

MONDO:0024410.name: infection caused by bifidobacterium
MONDO:0024410.def: a disease caused by infection with bifidobacterium.

MONDO:0024412.name: peptostreptococcus infectious disease
MONDO:0024412.def: a disease caused by infection with peptostreptococcus.

MONDO:0024416.name: neorickettsia infectious disease
MONDO:0024416.def: a disease caused by infection with neorickettsia.

MONDO:0024417.name: perceptual disorders
MONDO:0024417.def: cognitive disorders characterized by an impaired ability to perceive the nature of objects or concepts through use of the sense organs. these include spatial neglect syndromes, where an individual does not attend to visual, auditory, or sensory stimuli presented from one side of the body.

MONDO:0024419.name: enthesitis
MONDO:0024419.def: inflammation at the site of insertion of ligaments, tendons, and other fibrous structures into bone.

MONDO:0024422.name: auditory perceptual disorders
MONDO:0024422.def: acquired or developmental cognitive disorders of auditory perception characterized by a reduced ability to perceive information contained in auditory stimuli despite intact auditory pathways. affected individuals have difficulty with speech perception, sound localization, and comprehending the meaning of inflections of speech.

MONDO:0024429.name: alice in wonderland syndrome
MONDO:0024429.def: a disorienting neuropsychological condition that affects perception. people experience size distortion such as micropsia, macropsia, pelopsia, or teleopsia. size distortion may occur of other sensory modalities.

MONDO:0024430.name: allesthesia
MONDO:0024430.def: a neurological disorder in which a sensory stimulus, usually tactile but more rarely other sensory modalities, is misperceived in a location distant from the original stimulus.

MONDO:0024432.name: nerve plexus disorder
MONDO:0024432.def: a disease that involves the nerve plexus.

MONDO:0024454.name: sacral nerve plexus disorder
MONDO:0024454.def: a disease that involves the sacral nerve plexus.

MONDO:0024455.name: autosomal dominant robinow syndrome 1
MONDO:0024455.def: any autosomal dominant robinow syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the wnt5a gene.

MONDO:0024456.name: anterior segment dysgenesis 3
MONDO:0024456.def: an iridogoniodysgenesis that results from alterations in the forkhead transcription factor gene (foxc1)

MONDO:0024458.name: disorder of visual system
MONDO:0024458.def: a disease that involves the visual system.

MONDO:0024459.name: aeromonas hydrophila intestinal disease
MONDO:0024459.synonym: intestinal infection due to aeromonas hydrophila

MONDO:0024461.name: angiomatosis
MONDO:0024461.def: a benign diffuse vascular proliferation usually occurring in young adults. it is characterized by the formation of capillary-sized and cavernous vascular spaces. patients present with diffuse persistent swelling.

MONDO:0024462.name: familial cutaneous melanoma
MONDO:0024462.def: an instance of cutaneous melanoma (disease) that is caused by an inherited modification of the individual's genome.

MONDO:0024464.name: pituitary hormone deficiency, combined, 1
MONDO:0024464.def: any combined pituitary hormone deficiencies, genetic form in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the pou1f1 gene.
MONDO:0024464.synonym: pou1f1 combined pituitary hormone deficiencies, genetic form

MONDO:0024467.name: apocrine sweat gland disorder
MONDO:0024467.def: a disease that involves the apocrine sweat gland.

MONDO:0024468.name: anterior pituitary gland disorder
MONDO:0024468.def: a disease that involves the adenohypophysis.

MONDO:0024469.name: chondrogenic neoplasm
MONDO:0024469.def: a benign, intermediate, or malignant cartilaginous matrix-producing neoplasm. representative examples include osteochondroma, chondroblastoma, and chondrosarcoma.

MONDO:0024470.name: benign chondrogenic neoplasm
MONDO:0024470.def: a non-metastasizing cartilaginous matrix-producing neoplasm characterized by the presence of neoplastic chondrocytes. representative examples include osteochondroma and chondroma.

MONDO:0024472.name: boutonneuse fever
MONDO:0024472.def: an infectious disease of the mediterranean area, the crimea, africa, and india, caused by infection with rickettsia conorii subsp. coronorii.
MONDO:0024472.synonym: tick typhus due to rickettsia conorii

MONDO:0024473.name: astrakhan spotted fever
MONDO:0024473.def: an infectious disease of the astrakhan region, chad, kosovo, caused by infection with rickettsia conorii subsp. caspia.

MONDO:0024474.name: intraepithelial neoplasia
MONDO:0024474.def: a precancerous neoplastic process that affects the squamous, glandular, or transitional cell epithelium without evidence of invasion. according to the degree of nuclear atypia, number of mitotic figures, and presence of architectural distortion, it is classified as low grade (mild dysplasia) or high grade (moderate or severe dysplasia).

MONDO:0024476.name: epithelial neoplasm of rectum
MONDO:0024476.def: a epithelial neoplasm that involves the rectum.

MONDO:0024477.name: liver and intrahepatic bile duct neoplasm
MONDO:0024477.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the liver parenchyma or intrahepatic bile ducts. representative examples of benign neoplasms include hepatocellular adenoma, and bile duct adenoma. representative examples of malignant neoplasms include hepatocellular carcinoma, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, and lymphoma.

MONDO:0024479.name: epithelial tumor of colon
MONDO:0024479.def: a epithelial neoplasm that involves the colon.

MONDO:0024481.name: skin appendage disorder
MONDO:0024481.def: a disease that involves the cutaneous appendage.

MONDO:0024482.name: eccrine sweat gland hamartoma
MONDO:0024482.def: a hamartoma characterized by localized eccrine sweat gland malformation.
MONDO:0024482.synonym: hamartoma of the eccrine sweat gland

MONDO:0024483.name: urothelial hyperplasia
MONDO:0024483.def: hyperplasia of the transitional epithelium of the urinary tract. morphologically it is subdivided into flat and papillary hyperplasia. -- 2003

MONDO:0024485.name: papillary urothelial hyperplasia
MONDO:0024485.def: a type of hyperplasia that is characterized by variable thickening of the urinary tract epithelium and a slight papillary growth. the latter is not associated with the presence of fibrovascular cores. there is no evidence of atypia. the relationship between this lesion and papillary urothelial neoplasia is not clear. -- 2003

MONDO:0024487.name: nail infection
MONDO:0024487.def: an infectious process affecting the nail.

MONDO:0024488.name: tumor grading characteristic
MONDO:0024488.def: a modifier that can be applied to a tumor class describing abnormal tumor histology or morphology. it is an indicator of how quickly a tumor is likely to grow and spread

MONDO:0024489.name: general tumor grading characteristic
MONDO:0024489.def: a term that refers to the cellular differentiation of a malignant cellular infiltrate. a cancer is defined through grades i-iv (or 1-4), or as well, moderately, poorly differentiated or undifferentiated.

MONDO:0024490.name: tumor grade x, general grading system

MONDO:0024491.name: tumor grade 1, general grading system
MONDO:0024491.def: a morphologic qualifier indicating that a cancerous lesion is well differentiated.

MONDO:0024492.name: tumor grade 2, general grading system
MONDO:0024492.def: a morphologic qualifier indicating that a cancerous lesion is moderately differentiated.

MONDO:0024493.name: tumor grade 3, general grading system
MONDO:0024493.def: a morphologic qualifier indicating that a cancerous lesion is poorly differentiated.

MONDO:0024494.name: tumor grade 4, general grading system
MONDO:0024494.def: a morphologic qualifier indicating that a cancerous lesion is undifferentiated.

MONDO:0024495.name: tumor grade 1 or 2, general grading system

MONDO:0024496.name: tumor grade 2 or 3, general grading system
MONDO:0024496.def: a morphologic qualifier indicating that a neoplastic lesion is moderately to poorly differentiated.

MONDO:0024497.name: tumor grade 3 or 4, general grading system
MONDO:0024497.def: used to describe tumor samples that exhibit poorly differentiated or undifferentiated cells. they are generally expected to be fast growing and aggressive.

MONDO:0024499.name: vascular bone neoplasm
MONDO:0024499.def: a benign, intermediate, or malignant vascular neoplasm that arises from the bone.

MONDO:0024500.name: duodenal neuroendocrine neoplasm
MONDO:0024500.def: a neuroendocrine neoplasm that involves the duodenum.

MONDO:0024501.name: appendix neuroendocrine neoplasm
MONDO:0024501.def: a neoplasm with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the appendix. it includes well differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (low and intermediate grade) and poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (high grade).

MONDO:0024502.name: gallbladder neuroendocrine neoplasm
MONDO:0024502.def: a neoplasm with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the gallbladder. it includes well differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (low and intermediate grade) and poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (high grade).

MONDO:0024503.name: digestive system neuroendocrine neoplasm
MONDO:0024503.def: a neoplasm with neuroendocrine differentiation arising from the digestive system. it includes neuroendocrine tumors (well-differentiated endocrine tumors or carcinoid tumors and well differentiated endocrine carcinomas) and neuroendocrine carcinomas (poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas, small cell carcinomas, and large cell neuroendocrine carcinomas).

MONDO:0024504.name: enterochromaffin cell serotonin-producing pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor
MONDO:0024504.def: a usually slow-growing, grade 1 pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor that secretes serotonin. when it metastasizes to the liver, it produces the clinical symptoms of the carcinoid syndrome.

MONDO:0024505.name: obsolete disorder by anatomical region
MONDO:0024505.def: obsolete. a broad grouping of diseases based on major body subdivisions.

MONDO:0024506.name: adams-oliver syndrome 1
MONDO:0024506.def: any adams-oliver syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the arhgap31 gene.
MONDO:0024506.synonym: congenital scalp defects with distal limb reduction anomalies

MONDO:0024507.name: aniridia 1
MONDO:0024507.synonym: cataract, congenital, with late-onset corneal dystrophy

MONDO:0024516.name: familial acne inversa
MONDO:0024516.def: an instance of hidradenitis suppurativa that is caused by an inherited modification of the individual's genome.

MONDO:0024518.name: reactive thrombocytosis
MONDO:0024518.def: a thrombocytosis caused by an underlying condition, such as an infection.

MONDO:0024522.name: amyloidosis, primary localized cutaneous, 1
MONDO:0024522.def: any primary cutaneous amyloidosis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the osmr gene.
MONDO:0024522.synonym: primary cutaneous amyloidosis caused by mutation in osmr

MONDO:0024523.name: aortic valve disease 1
MONDO:0024523.def: any aortic valve disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the notch1 gene.

MONDO:0024526.name: zimmermann-laband syndrome 1
MONDO:0024526.def: any zimmermann-laband syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the kcnh1 gene.

MONDO:0024528.name: progressive external ophthalmoplegia with mitochondrial dna deletions, autosomal dominant 1
MONDO:0024528.def: any autosomal dominant progressive external ophthalmoplegia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the polg gene.

MONDO:0024531.name: myopathy, tubular aggregate, 1
MONDO:0024531.def: any tubular aggregate myopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the stim1 gene.
MONDO:0024531.synonym: tubular aggregate myopathy caused by mutation in stim1

MONDO:0024532.name: otofaciocervical syndrome 1
MONDO:0024532.def: any otofaciocervical syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the eya1 gene.
MONDO:0024532.synonym: otofaciocervical syndrome caused by mutation in eya1

MONDO:0024533.name: pulmonary hypertension, primary, 1
MONDO:0024533.def: any primary pulmonary hypertension in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the bmpr2 gene.

MONDO:0024534.name: dowling-degos disease 1
MONDO:0024534.def: any dowling-degos disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the krt5 gene.

MONDO:0024535.name: singleton-merten syndrome 1
MONDO:0024535.def: any singleton-merten dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ifih1 gene.

MONDO:0024536.name: glucocorticoid deficiency 1
MONDO:0024536.def: any familial glucocorticoid deficiency in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the mc2r gene.

MONDO:0024537.name: brown-vialetto-van laere syndrome 1
MONDO:0024537.def: any brown-vialetto-van laere syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the slc52a3 gene.

MONDO:0024539.name: choroidal dystrophy, central areolar, 1
MONDO:0024539.def: any central areolar choroidal dystrophy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the gucy2d gene.

MONDO:0024540.name: jervell and lange-nielsen syndrome 1
MONDO:0024540.def: any jervell and lange-nielsen syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the kcnq1 gene.

MONDO:0024541.name: trichohepatoenteric syndrome 1
MONDO:0024541.def: any tricho-hepato-enteric syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ttc37 gene.

MONDO:0024542.name: cerebellar ataxia, intellectual disability, and dysequilibrium syndrome 1
MONDO:0024542.def: any dysequilibrium syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the vldlr gene.

MONDO:0024543.name: brittle cornea syndrome 1
MONDO:0024543.def: any brittle cornea syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the znf469 gene.

MONDO:0024545.name: miyoshi muscular dystrophy 1
MONDO:0024545.def: any miyoshi myopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the dysf gene.
MONDO:0024545.synonym: muscular dystrophy, distal, late-onset, autosomal recessive

MONDO:0024546.name: hypertrophic osteoarthropathy, primary, autosomal recessive, 1
MONDO:0024546.def: any primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the hpgd gene.

MONDO:0024547.name: pancreatic agenesis 1
MONDO:0024547.def: any pancreatic agenesis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the pdx1 gene.

MONDO:0024548.name: peeling skin syndrome 1
MONDO:0024548.def: any peeling skin syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the cdsn gene.

MONDO:0024550.name: frontometaphyseal dysplasia 1
MONDO:0024550.def: any frontometaphyseal dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the flna gene.
MONDO:0024550.synonym: frontometaphyseal dysplasia caused by mutation in flna

MONDO:0024551.name: x-linked lymphoproliferative disease due to sh2d1a deficiency
MONDO:0024551.def: a rare, genetic, primary immunodeficiency disorder characterized by an abnormal immune response to epstein-barr virus (ebv) infection, caused by hemizygous mutations in the x-linked sh2d1a gene, resulting in b cell lymphoproliferation and manifesting with various phenotypes which include ebv-driven severe or fulminant mononucleosis, hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (presenting with fulminant hepatitis, hepatic necrosis, bone marrow hypoplasia, and neurological involvement), hypogammaglobulinemia, and b-cell lymphoma. additional variable manifestations include vasculitis, lymphomatoid granulomatosis, aplastic anemia, and chronic gastritis. occasionally, t-cell lymphoma may be observed. laboratory findings include normal or increased activated t cells and reduced memory b cells.

MONDO:0024552.name: linear skin defects with multiple congenital anomalies 1
MONDO:0024552.def: any microphthalmia with linear skin defects syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the hccs gene.

MONDO:0024553.name: myopathy, lactic acidosis, and sideroblastic anemia 1
MONDO:0024553.def: any myopathy, lactic acidosis, and sideroblastic anemia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the pus1 gene.
MONDO:0024553.synonym: pus1 myopathy, lactic acidosis, and sideroblastic anemia

MONDO:0024554.name: d-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria 1
MONDO:0024554.def: any d-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the d2hgdh gene.

MONDO:0024556.name: epilepsy, familial focal, with variable foci 1
MONDO:0024556.def: any epilepsy, familial focal, with variable foci in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the depdc5 gene.

MONDO:0024557.name: ataxia-telangiectasia-like disorder 1
MONDO:0024557.def: any ataxia-telangiectasia-like disorder in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the mre11 gene.

MONDO:0024558.name: radioulnar synostosis with amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia 1
MONDO:0024558.def: any radio-ulnar synostosis-amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the hoxa11 gene.

MONDO:0024561.name: vitelliform macular dystrophy 3
MONDO:0024561.def: any vitelliform macular dystrophy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the prph2 gene.

MONDO:0024562.name: sick sinus syndrome 1
MONDO:0024562.def: any sick sinus syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the scn5a gene.

MONDO:0024563.name: herpes simplex encephalitis, susceptibility to, 1
MONDO:0024563.def: a mendelian susceptibility or predisposition to herpes simplex infection induced encephalitis in which the cause of the diseas is a mutation in the unc93b1 gene.

MONDO:0024564.name: cerebroretinal microangiopathy with calcifications and cysts 1
MONDO:0024564.def: any coats plus syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ctc1 gene.

MONDO:0024565.name: ectodermal dysplasia-syndactyly syndrome 1
MONDO:0024565.def: any ectodermal dysplasia-syndactyly syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the nectin4 gene.

MONDO:0024567.name: hypotonia, infantile, with psychomotor retardation and characteristic facies 1
MONDO:0024567.def: any hypotonia, infantile, with psychomotor retardation and characteristic facies in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the nalcn gene.
MONDO:0024567.synonym: nalcn hypotonia, infantile, with psychomotor retardation and characteristic facies

MONDO:0024568.name: infantile liver failure syndrome 1
MONDO:0024568.def: any infantile liver failure in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the lars gene.

MONDO:0024570.name: hyperparathyroidism 4
MONDO:0024570.def: any familial isolated hyperparathyroidism in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the gcm2 gene.

MONDO:0024571.name: aids-related disorder
MONDO:0024571.def: a non-neoplastic or neoplastic disorder arising as a result of the immunologic defects caused by autoimmune deficiency syndrome.

MONDO:0024572.name: immunodeficiency-related disorder
MONDO:0024572.def: a non-neoplastic or neoplastic disorder that develops in a patient with immunodeficiency. representative examples include aids-related disorders and disorders that develop following organ transplantation.

MONDO:0024573.name: familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
MONDO:0024573.def: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy caused by mutations in the genes encoding components of the sarcomere, in the absence of predisposing conditions.

MONDO:0024574.name: von willebrand disease (hereditary or acquired)
MONDO:0024574.def: hereditary or acquired coagulation disorder characterized by a qualitative or quantitative deficiency of the von willebrand factor. the latter plays an important role in platelet adhesion. signs and symptoms include bruises, nose bleeding, gum bleeding following a dental procedure, heavy menstrual bleeding, and gastrointestinal bleeding.

MONDO:0024575.name: pregnancy disorder
MONDO:0024575.def: a disorder that is related to pregnancy. representative examples include ectopic pregnancy, toxemia of pregnancy, and gestational trophoblastic tumor.

MONDO:0024582.name: male reproductive system neoplasm
MONDO:0024582.def: a benign, borderline, or malignant neoplasm that affects the male reproductive system. representative examples include benign prostate phyllodes tumor, benign testicular sertoli cell tumor, prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia, prostate carcinoma, testicular seminoma, and testicular embryonal carcinoma.
MONDO:0024582.synonym: tumour of the male reproductive system

MONDO:0024583.name: obsolete hernia
MONDO:0024583.def: obsolete. the protrusion of part of an organ or fibroadipose tissue through an abnormal opening.

MONDO:0024607.name: congenital muscular dystrophy with cataracts and intellectual disability
MONDO:0024607.def: a congenital muscular dystrophy characterized by onset of progressive muscle weakness in early childhood with autosomal recessive inheritance that has material basis in homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the inpp5k gene (607875) on chromosome 17p13.
MONDO:0024607.synonym: muscular dystrophy, congenital, with cataracts and intellectual disability

MONDO:0024608.name: dientamoebiasis
MONDO:0024608.def: gastrointestinal infection with organisms of the genus dientamoeba.

MONDO:0024609.name: vulvar squamous cell carcinoma
MONDO:0024609.def: an invasive squamous cell carcinoma arising from the vulva. risk factors include the human papilloma virus and cigarette smoking. precursor lesions include the vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia, lichen sclerosus with associated squamous cell hyperplasia, and chronic granulomatous vulvar disease such as granuloma inguinale. symptoms include vulvar pruritus or irritation, discharge, bleeding, and pain. the following morphologic variants have been identified: keratinizing, non-keratinizing, basaloid, warty, verrucous, keratoacanthoma-like, and squamous cell carcinoma with tumor giant cells. risk factors for recurrence include advanced stage, tumor diameter greater than 2.5 cm, multifocality, capillary-like space involvement, associated vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia grades 2 or 3, and margins of resection involved by tumor. (who, 2003)

MONDO:0024610.name: parasitic skin disorder
MONDO:0024610.def: skin diseases caused by arthropods; helminths; or other parasites.

MONDO:0024611.name: orbit neoplasm
MONDO:0024611.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the orbit.

MONDO:0024612.name: manic bipolar affective disorder
MONDO:0024612.def: the manic phase of bipolar disorder.

MONDO:0024613.name: bipolar depression
MONDO:0024613.def: the depressive stage of bipolar disorder.

MONDO:0024614.name: neurotic depression
MONDO:0024614.def: a term used for any state of depression that is not psychotic.

MONDO:0024616.name: tympanitis
MONDO:0024616.def: an inflammatory disease involving a pathogenic inflammatory response in the tympanic membrane.

MONDO:0024618.name: poliovirus infection
MONDO:0024618.def: an disease or disorder caused by infection with enterovirus c.

MONDO:0024619.name: central nervous system infectious disorder
MONDO:0024619.def: an infectious process that affects the brain and/or spinal cord. representative examples include encephalitis, poliomyelitis, arachnoiditis, and meningitis.
MONDO:0024619.synonym: infectious disease of central nervous system

MONDO:0024621.name: serous cystadenocarcinoma
MONDO:0024621.def: a malignant serous cystic neoplasm usually involving the ovary or the pancreas. it is characterized by the presence of invasive malignant glandular epithelial cells which often form papillary structures.

MONDO:0024622.name: thyroid gland adenocarcinoma
MONDO:0024622.def: an adenocarcinoma arising from the follicular cells of the thyroid gland. according to the degree of differentiation, it is classified either as differentiated carcinoma (extensive evidence of follicular cell differentiation), or poorly differentiated carcinoma (limited evidence of follicular cell differentiation).

MONDO:0024623.name: otorhinolaryngologic disease
MONDO:0024623.def: pathological processes of the ear, the nose, and the throat, also known as the ent diseases.

MONDO:0024624.name: obsolete atrophy of lacrimal gland
MONDO:0024624.def: obsolete. a degenerative disorder that involves the lacrimal gland.

MONDO:0024625.name: disorder of lacrimal gland
MONDO:0024625.def: a disease that involves the lacrimal gland.

MONDO:0024633.name: hypertensive nephropathy
MONDO:0024633.def: kidney damage that results from chronically elevated blood pressure; complications include glomerular damage resulting in proteinuria and hematuria.

MONDO:0024634.name: large intestine disorder
MONDO:0024634.def: a disease that involves the large intestine.

MONDO:0024635.name: small intestine disorder
MONDO:0024635.def: a disease that involves the small intestine.

MONDO:0024636.name: inflammation of heart layer
MONDO:0024636.def: an inflammatory disease involving a pathogenic inflammatory response in the heart layer.

MONDO:0024637.name: malignant soft tissue neoplasm
MONDO:0024637.def: a malignant neoplasm arising exclusively from the soft tissues.
MONDO:0024637.synonym: malignant tumour of the soft tissue

MONDO:0024638.name: pancreatic gastrinoma
MONDO:0024638.def: a neuroendocrine tumor arising from the pancreas. it is characterized by inappropriate secretion of gastrin and associated with zollinger ellison syndrome. the latter is characterized by the presence of peptic ulcer, gastroesophageal reflux disease, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and malabsorption.

MONDO:0024639.name: gastric enterochromaffin cell serotonin-producing neuroendocrine tumor
MONDO:0024639.def: a well differentiated neuroendocrine tumor that arises from the stomach. it produces serotonin and it may occasionally be found in association with a carcinoid syndrome.
MONDO:0024639.synonym: gastric enterochromaffin cell serotonin-producing neuroendocrine tumor

MONDO:0024642.name: gastric neuroendocrine tumor g2
MONDO:0024642.def: a well differentiated, intermediate grade tumor with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the stomach. the mitotic count is 2-20 per 10 hpf and/or the ki67 index is 3 to 20 percent.

MONDO:0024643.name: myocardial disorder
MONDO:0024643.def: a disorder that affects the muscle tissue of the heart. representative examples include myocardial infarction, myocarditis, and cardiomyopathy.

MONDO:0024644.name: myocardial ischemia
MONDO:0024644.def: a disorder of cardiac function caused by insufficient blood flow to the muscle tissue of the heart. the decreased blood flow may be due to narrowing of the coronary arteries (coronary artery disease), to obstruction by a thrombus (coronary thrombosis), or less commonly, to diffuse narrowing of arterioles and other small vessels within the heart. severe interruption of the blood supply to the myocardial tissue may result in necrosis of cardiac muscle (myocardial infarction).

MONDO:0024645.name: retroperitoneal neoplasm
MONDO:0024645.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the retroperitoneum.

MONDO:0024648.name: optic tract meningioma
MONDO:0024648.def: a meningioma that affects the visual pathway.

MONDO:0024649.name: optic tract astrocytoma
MONDO:0024649.def: an astrocytoma that affects the optic tract. this condition can be seen in association with neurofibromatosis 1. it is most commonly seen in the pediatric age group.

MONDO:0024653.name: skull neoplasm
MONDO:0024653.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the bones and structures of the skull.

MONDO:0024654.name: skull disorder
MONDO:0024654.def: a non-neoplastic or neoplastic disorder that affects structures of the skull.

MONDO:0024656.name: colorectal lymphoma
MONDO:0024656.def: an extranodal lymphoma that arises from the colon or rectum. the majority are b-cell non-hodgkin lymphomas.

MONDO:0024658.name: extrahepatic bile duct sarcoma
MONDO:0024658.def: a malignant soft tissue neoplasm that arises from the extrahepatic bile ducts. representative examples include kaposi sarcoma, leiomyosarcoma, and rhabdomyosarcoma.
MONDO:0024658.synonym: sarcoma of the extrahepatic bile duct

MONDO:0024659.name: colorectal kaposi sarcoma
MONDO:0024659.def: a kaposi sarcoma that arises from the colon or rectum.

MONDO:0024660.name: tubular adenoma
MONDO:0024660.def: a usually polypoid neoplasm arising from the glandular epithelium. it is characterized by a tubular architectural pattern. the neoplastic glandular cells have dysplastic features. representative examples include the tubular adenomas of the colon and rectum.

MONDO:0024661.name: tubulovillous adenoma
MONDO:0024661.def: an epithelial neoplasm morphologically characterized by the presence of a villous and a tubular architectural pattern. most often it occurs in the large intestine, small intestine, and the stomach in which the neoplastic epithelial cells show dysplastic features.

MONDO:0024662.name: colorectal tubulovillous adenoma
MONDO:0024662.def: a neoplasm that arises from the glandular epithelium of the colonic and rectal mucosa. it is characterized by tubular and villous architectural patterns. the neoplastic glandular cells have dysplastic features.
MONDO:0024662.synonym: tubulovillous adenoma of the large bowel

MONDO:0024664.name: hypertension, pregnancy-induced
MONDO:0024664.def: a hypertensive disorder that develops during pregnancy.

MONDO:0024666.name: benign epithelial skin neoplasm
MONDO:0024666.def: a form of epithelial skin neoplasm without malignant characteristics.

MONDO:0024673.name: skin lymphangioma
MONDO:0024673.def: a lymphangioma arising from the skin.

MONDO:0024674.name: pancoast syndrome
MONDO:0024674.def: a rare neoplastic syndrome characterized by obstruction of the thoracic outlet leading to compression of the brachial plexus and vessels within. it is usually caused by a malignant neoplasm in the superior pulmonary sulcus. the most commonly involved neoplasms are non-small cell lung carcinomas. clinical signs include horner's syndrome, shoulder pain radiating down the arm in the ulnar distribution followed by edema and atrophy of the affected extremity. clinical course usually leads to early local invasion of the bony thoracic structures. prognosis is highly stage-dependent.

MONDO:0024675.name: adult kidney wilms tumor
MONDO:0024675.def: wilms tumor of the kidney which occurs in adults.

MONDO:0024676.name: childhood kidney wilms tumor
MONDO:0024676.def: a wilms tumor of the kidney which occurs in children.

MONDO:0024677.name: pancreatic insulinoma
MONDO:0024677.def: an insulin-producing neuroendocrine tumor arising from the beta cells of the pancreas. patients exhibit symptoms related to hypoglycemia due to inappropriate secretion of insulin.

MONDO:0024686.name: tenosynovial giant cell tumor, diffuse type
MONDO:0024686.def: a locally aggressive, diffusely infiltrating tumor, arising in the tendon sheath. it is composed of synovial-like mononuclear cells, hemosiderin-laden macrophages, foam cells, and inflammatory cells. multinucleated osteoclast-like giant cells are usually present, although in a minority of cases they may be absent or rare. it predominantly affects young adults. symptoms include joint swelling, pain, and joint effusion.

MONDO:0024711.name: malignant mixed epithelial stromal tumor of the kidney
MONDO:0024711.def: a mixed epithelial stromal tumor of the kidney with malignant stromal features.
MONDO:0024711.synonym: mixed epithelial stromal tumour of the kidney, malignant

MONDO:0024715.name: benign synovial neoplasm
MONDO:0024715.def: a benign neoplasm arising from the synovial membrane. examples include the diffuse giant cell tumor of tendon sheath and localized giant cell tumor of tendon sheath.

MONDO:0024744.name: childhood choroid plexus neoplasm
MONDO:0024744.def: a neoplasm that arises from the choroid plexus in the brain and occurs during childhood.

MONDO:0024746.name: immature teratoma
MONDO:0024746.def: a teratoma composed of immature, fetal-type tissues.

MONDO:0024757.name: cardiovascular neoplasm
MONDO:0024757.def: a benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the heart and/or vessels. representative examples of benign neoplasms include atrial myxoma, hemangioma, and lymphangioma. representative examples of malignant neoplasms include pericardial malignant mesothelioma and angiosarcoma.

MONDO:0024772.name: intellectual developmental disorder, x-linked, syndromic, pilorge type

MONDO:0024777.name: immunodeficiency 98 with autoinflammation, x-linked
MONDO:0024777.def: an immunodeficiency disease characterized by onset of recurrent infections associated with lymphoproliferation and autoinflammation in the first decade of life. mostly males are affected; carrier females may have mild symptoms. laboratory studies show evidence of immune dysregulation, including hypogammaglobulinemia with reduced memory b cells, skewed t-cell subsets, increased levels of proinflammatory cytokines, activated t cells and monocytes, and autoimmune cytopenias, including neutropenia.

MONDO:0024781.name: immunodeficiency 102
MONDO:0024781.def: an x-linked recessive immunologic disorder characterized by the onset of recurrent sinopulmonary, mucosal, and other infections in early childhood, usually accompanied by refractory autoimmune cytopenias. affected individuals have bacterial, viral, and fungal infections, as well as hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, lymphopenia, and decreased nk cells. laboratory studies show defective t-cell proliferation and function, likely due to signaling abnormalities. the disorder may also manifest as a hyperinflammatory state with immune dysregulation.

MONDO:0024797.name: adult brain stem neoplasm
MONDO:0024797.def: a brainstem neoplasm that occurs in an adult.

MONDO:0024813.name: pulmonary sulcus neoplasm
MONDO:0024813.def: a neoplasm originating from the apical lung. most superior sulcus neoplasms are bronchogenic carcinomas. this tumor may be associated with pancoast syndrome. it is also known as pancoast tumor.

MONDO:0024857.name: immature extragonadal teratoma
MONDO:0024857.def: an immature teratoma that develops as a primary tumor in an anatomic site other than the testis or ovary.

MONDO:0024868.name: metastatic carcinoma in the adrenal medulla
MONDO:0024868.def: a carcinoma that has spread to the adrenal medulla from an adjacent or distant anatomic site.
MONDO:0024868.synonym: metastatic carcinoma to the adrenal medulla

MONDO:0024873.name: clitoral carcinoma
MONDO:0024873.def: a carcinoma that arises from the clitoris.

MONDO:0024876.name: tendon sheath disorder
MONDO:0024876.def: a disease that involves the tendon sheath.

MONDO:0024878.name: secondary carcinoma
MONDO:0024878.def: a carcinoma that arises from a pre-existing lower grade epithelial lesion, or as a result of a primary carcinoma that has spread to secondary sites, or due to a complication of a cancer treatment.

MONDO:0024879.name: metastatic carcinoma
MONDO:0024879.def: a carcinoma which has spread from the original site of growth to another anatomic site.

MONDO:0024880.name: metastatic malignant neoplasm
MONDO:0024880.def: a malignant tumor that has spread from its original (primary) site of growth to another site close to or distant from the primary site.

MONDO:0024881.name: secondary malignant neoplasm
MONDO:0024881.def: a malignant neoplasm that arises from a pre-existing lower grade lesion, or as a result of a primary lesion that has spread to secondary sites, or due to a complication of a cancer treatment.

MONDO:0024882.name: secondary neoplasm
MONDO:0024882.def: a neoplasm that arises from a pre-existing lower grade lesion, or as a result of a primary lesion that has spread to secondary sites, or due to a complication of a cancer treatment.

MONDO:0024883.name: metastatic neoplasm
MONDO:0024883.def: a tumor that has spread from its original (primary) site of growth to another site, close to or distant from the primary site. metastasis is characteristic of advanced malignancies, but in rare instances can be seen in neoplasms lacking malignant morphology.

MONDO:0024884.name: metastatic carcinoma in the bone
MONDO:0024884.def: a carcinoma that has spread to the bone from another, primary anatomic site. bone is one of the most frequent sites of metastatic carcinoma. common sites of origin include lung, breast, and prostate.

MONDO:0024885.name: malignant ovarian serous tumor
MONDO:0024885.def: an invasive malignant neoplasm that arises from the ovary and is characterized by the presence of malignant epithelial cells that, in well differentiated tumors, resemble the epithelium of the fallopian tube or, in poorly differentiated tumors, show anaplastic features and marked nuclear atypia. it includes serous adenocarcinoma and serous adenocarcinofibroma.

MONDO:0024886.name: serous adenofibroma
MONDO:0024886.def: a benign adenofibroma characterized by the presence of serous secretory cells and minute cystic spaces filled with watery fluid. a representative example is the ovarian serous adenofibroma. cases with epithelial atypia described in the ovary lacking stromal invasion are designated as borderline serous adenofibromas and have a low grade malignant potential.

MONDO:0024888.name: mesonephric neoplasm
MONDO:0024888.def: an epithelial neoplasm of the female reproductive system arising from mesonephric remnants.

MONDO:0024889.name: benign mesonephroma
MONDO:0024889.def: a benign epithelial neoplasm of the female reproductive system arising from mesonephric remnants.

MONDO:0024890.name: pineal parenchymal cell neoplasm
MONDO:0024890.def: a neoplasm arising from the pineocyte, a cell with photosensory and neuroendocrine functions. it may be composed of mature elements or primitive, immature cells. the cellular composition determines the biological behavior and clinical outcome. three types are recognized: pineoblastoma, pineocytoma, and pineal parenchymal tumor of intermediate differentiation (adapted from who.)

MONDO:0024892.name: soft tissue amyloid neoplasm
MONDO:0024892.def: a soft tissue neoplasm composed of acellular amyloid material.

MONDO:0024905.name: bird disease
MONDO:0024905.def: diseases of birds not considered poultry, therefore usually found in zoos, parks, and the wild. the concept is differentiated from poultry diseases which is for birds raised as a source of meat or eggs for human consumption, and usually found in barnyards, hatcheries, etc.

MONDO:0024912.name: cat disease
MONDO:0024912.def: diseases of the domestic cat (felis catus or f. domesticus). this term does not include diseases of the so-called big cats such as cheetahs; lions; tigers, cougars, panthers, leopards, and other felidae for which the heading carnivora is used.

MONDO:0024913.name: cattle disease
MONDO:0024913.def: diseases of domestic cattle of the genus bos. it includes diseases of cows, yaks, and zebus.

MONDO:0024919.name: dog disease
MONDO:0024919.def: diseases of the domestic dog (canis familiaris). this term does not include diseases of wild dogs, wolves; foxes; and other canidae for which the heading carnivora is used.

MONDO:0024934.name: fish disease
MONDO:0024934.def: diseases of freshwater, marine, hatchery or aquarium fish. this term includes diseases of both teleosts (true fish) and elasmobranchs (sharks, rays and skates).

MONDO:0024935.name: foot rot
MONDO:0024935.def: a disease of the horny parts and of the adjacent soft structures of the feet of cattle, swine, and sheep. it is usually caused by corynebacterium pyogenes or bacteroides nodosus (see dichelobacter nodosus). it is also known as interdigital necrobacillosis. (from black's veterinary dictionary, 18th ed)

MONDO:0024945.name: hepatitis, non-human animal
MONDO:0024945.def: inflammation of the liver in non-human animals.

MONDO:0024950.name: horse disease
MONDO:0024950.def: diseases of domestic and wild horses of the species equus caballus.

MONDO:0024953.name: lameness, non-human animal
MONDO:0024953.def: a departure from the normal gait in animals.

MONDO:0024954.name: larva migrans, visceral
MONDO:0024954.def: a condition produced in humans by the prolonged migration of animal nematode larvae in extraintestinal tissues other than skin; characterized by persistent hypereosinophilia, hepatomegaly, and frequently pneumonitis, commonly caused by toxocara canis and toxocara cati.

MONDO:0024969.name: parasitic disease, non-human animal
MONDO:0024969.def: infections or infestations with parasitic organisms. the infestation may be experimental or veterinary.

MONDO:0024971.name: parturient paresis
MONDO:0024971.def: a disease of pregnant and lactating cows and ewes leading to generalized paresis and death. the disease, which is characterized by hypocalcemia, occurs at or shortly after parturition in cows and within weeks before or after parturition in ewes.

MONDO:0024973.name: pneumonia, atypical interstitial, of cattle
MONDO:0024973.def: a cattle disease of uncertain cause, probably an allergic reaction.

MONDO:0024981.name: rodent disease
MONDO:0024981.def: diseases of rodents of the order rodentia. this term includes diseases of sciuridae (squirrels), geomyidae (gophers), heteromyidae (pouched mice), castoridae (beavers), cricetidae (rats and mice), muridae (old world rats and mice), erethizontidae (porcupines), and caviidae (guinea pigs).

MONDO:0024982.name: salmonella infections, animal
MONDO:0024982.def: infections in animals with bacteria of the genus salmonella.

MONDO:0024985.name: sheep disease
MONDO:0024985.def: diseases of domestic and mountain sheep of the genus ovis.

MONDO:0024988.name: sex cord-stromal benign neoplasm
MONDO:0024988.def: a reproductive organ benign neoplasm that arises in the ovary or testis and that is composed of granulosa cells, leydig cells, sertoli cells, and/or fibroblasts.

MONDO:0024990.name: swine disease
MONDO:0024990.def: diseases of domestic swine and of the wild boar of the genus sus.

MONDO:0025003.name: goat disease
MONDO:0025003.def: diseases of the domestic or wild goat of the genus capra.

MONDO:0025013.name: non-human primate disease
MONDO:0025013.def: diseases of animals within the order primates. this term includes diseases of haplorhini and strepsirhini.

MONDO:0025028.name: vesicular stomatitis
MONDO:0025028.def: a viral disease caused by at least two distinct species (serotypes) in the vesiculovirus genus: vesicular stomatitis indiana virus and vesicular stomatitis new jersey virus. it is characterized by vesicular eruptions on the oral mucosa in cattle, horses, pigs, and other animals. in humans, vesicular stomatitis causes an acute influenza-like illness.

MONDO:0025030.name: digital dermatitis in cattle
MONDO:0025030.def: highly contagious infectious dermatitis with lesions near the interdigital spaces usually in cattle. it causes discomfort and often severe lameness (lameness, animal). lesions can be either erosive or proliferative and wart-like with papillary growths and hypertrophied hairs. dichelobacter nodosus and treponema are the most commonly associated causative agents for this mixed bacterial infection disease.

MONDO:0025061.name: edema disease of swine
MONDO:0025061.def: an acute disease of young pigs that is usually associated with weaning. it is characterized clinically by paresis and subcutaneous edema.

MONDO:0025062.name: encephalomyelitis, enzootic porcine
MONDO:0025062.def: a picornavirus infection producing symptoms similar to poliomyelitis in pigs.

MONDO:0025066.name: epidermitis, exudative, of swine
MONDO:0025066.def: an acute generalized dermatitis of pigs which occurs from 5 to 35 days of age, characterized by sudden onset, with morbidity of 10 to 90% and mortality of 5 to 90%. the lesions are caused by staphylococcus hyos but the bacterial agent is unable to penetrate the intact skin. abrasions on the feet and legs or lacerations on the body frequently precede infection. in acute cases, a vesicular-type virus may be the predisposing factor. the causative organism is inhibited by most antibiotics. (merck veterinary manual, 5th ed)

MONDO:0025082.name: helminthiasis, animal
MONDO:0025082.def: infestation of animals with parasitic worms of the helminth class. the infestation may be experimental or veterinary.

MONDO:0025085.name: hepatitis, viral, animal
MONDO:0025085.def: inflammation of the liver in animals due to viral infection.

MONDO:0025086.name: hip dysplasia, canine
